paper_title: On the Space Complexity of Online Convolution
statement_tex:
A streaming algorithm is a sequence of maps $m^{(t)}$ and $u^{(t)}$ as follows.
Let $\beta : \{-1\} \cup \N \to \N$ be a buffer size function with $\beta(-1) = 1$.
Denote the state at time $t$ by
$\state{t} \in \R^{\beta(t)}$.
Initially, the state is $\state{-1} = 0 \in \R$.
Upon receiving $z_{t}$, 
the algorithm updates its internal state:
    \begin{equation*}
        \state{t} = \smap{t}(\state{t-1}, z_{t}),
    \end{equation*}
    where $\smap{t} : \mathbb{R}^{\beta(t-1)} \times \R \to \R^{\beta(t)}$.
The algorithm then outputs 
    \begin{equation*}
m^{(t)}(\state{t})
    \end{equation*}
    where $\outmap{t}: \R^{\beta(t)} \to \R$.
    We assume that the state maps are continuous; for each $t$,
   the map $(z_0,\ldots,z_t) \mapsto \state{t}$ is assumed to be continuous.
    The algorithm solves the streaming problem defined by 
$M\in\mathbb{R}^{\N \times \N}$ if for every $z$ and every $t$,
$$m^{(t)}(\state{t}) = (M z)_t\,.$$
statement_text: A streaming algorithm is a sequence of maps m^ (t) and u^ (t) as follows. Let β : {-1} ∪ N → N be a buffer size function with β(-1) = 1 . Denote the state at time t by s^ (t) ∈ R ^ β(t) . Initially, the state is s^ (-1) = 0 ∈ R . Upon receiving z_ t , the algorithm updates its internal state: s^ (t) = u^ (t) (s^ (t-1) , z_ t ), where u^ (t) : R ^ β(t-1) × R → R ^ β(t) . The algorithm then outputs m^ (t) (s^ (t) ) where m^ (t) : R ^ β(t) → R . We assume that the state maps are continuous; for each t , the map (z_0, ... ,z_t) mapsto s^ (t) is assumed to be continuous. The algorithm solves the streaming problem defined by M ∈ R ^ N × N if for every z and every t , m^ (t) (s^ (t) ) = (M z)_t .
title: streaming model

statement_tex:
A polynomial $Q(x)$ of degree $d$ is an expression of the form
$Q(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{d} q_k x^k$ where $q_d \neq 0$.
The polynomial $Q(x)$ is invertible if $q_0 \neq 0$.
The generating function $G$ is a rational function of degree at most $d$ if there are polynomials $P,Q$ with $Q$ invertible 
so that $Q(x) \cdot G(x) = P(x)$
where $\deg(Q) \leq d$ and $\deg(P) \leq d-1$. 
We say that $G$ has degree $d$
if it is of degree at most $d$ but not of degree at most $d-1$.
We say that $G$ is irrational if it is not rational (of any degree).
statement_text: A polynomial Q(x) of degree d is an expression of the form Q(x) = Σ _ k=0 ^ d q_k x^k where q_d ≠ 0 . The polynomial Q(x) is invertible if q_0 ≠ 0 . We say that G has degree d if it is of degree at most d but not of degree at most d-1 . We say that G is irrational if it is not rational (of any degree).

       \hat{u}^{(t)} : \mathbb{R}^{\beta(t-1)} \times \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R}^{\beta(t)},
       \quad\hat{m}^{(t)} : \mathbb{R}^{\beta(t)} \times \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R},
   \end{equation*}
   where the state is updated via $\hat{s}^{(t)} = \hat{u}^{(t)}(\hat{s}^{(t-1)}, z_{\geq t})$ where $\hat{s}^{(-1)} = 0$ and the algorithm outputs $\hat{m}^{(t)}(\hat{s}^{(t)}, z_{>t})$.
The map $\hat{s}^{(t)}$ is assumed continuous as a function in $z_{\leq t}$
(that is, for every fixed $z_{>t}$, the map
$z_{\leq t} \mapsto \hat{s}^{(t)}(z)$ is continuous).

label: thm:shearer-KL

statement_tex:
\label{thm:shearer-KL}
For a finite set $\mathcal{X}$, let $Q=(Q_1,Q_2,\ldots,Q_N)$ be the uniform distribution on $\mathcal{X}^N = \mathcal{X} \times \ldots \times \mathcal{X}$, and let $P=(P_1,\ldots,P_N)$ be another distribution on $\mathcal{X}^N$. Let
$\Qcal_1,\Qcal_2,\ldots,\Qcal_m$ be subsets of $[N]$, such that each $i \in [N]$ belongs to at most $k$ of them. Then
$$k\cdot\KL( P \| Q ) \geq \sum_{j \in [m]} \KL( P_{\Qcal_j} \| Q_{\Qcal_j}),$$
where for $\Qcal =\{i_1,\dots i_\ell\} \subset [N]$, $P_{\Qcal}=(P_{i_1},\ldots,P_{i_\ell})$ is the marginal distribution of $P$ on $\mathcal{X}^{\ell}$, and analogously for $Q$.

Let U _1, U _2, ... , U _m be subsets of [N] , such that each i ∈ [N] belongs to at most k of them. Then k · D_ KL ( P | Q ) ≥ Σ _ j ∈ [m] D_ KL ( P_ U _j | Q_ U _j ), where for U ={i_1, ... i_ell } ⊂ [N] , P_ U =(P_ i_1 , ... ,P_ i_ell ) is the marginal distribution of P on X ^ ell , and analogously for Q .

label: thm:Gavinsky-perm

statement_tex:
\label{thm:Gavinsky-perm}
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a set of size $N$. Let $Q_X = Q_{X_1,\ldots,X_N}$ be the uniform distribution over bijections from $[N]$ to $\mathcal{X}$,
and let $P_X = P_{X_1,\ldots,X_N}$ be another distribution over such bijections. 
Let $\{ f_j \}_{j \in [m]}$ be a read-$k$ family of functions, with $f_j:\mathcal{X}^N \mapsto [0,1]$ for all $j$. Denote $p_j = \E_{P_X}[f_j(X)]$ and let $p = \frac{1}{m} \cdot \sum_{j \in [m]} p_j$ be the average of the expectations. Similarly, denote $q_j = \E_{Q_X}[f_j(X)]$ and $q = \frac{1}{m} \cdot \sum_{j \in [m]} q_j$.
Then
$$2k \cdot  \KL( P_X \| Q_X ) \geq m \cdot \KL( p \| q ),$$
where $\KL( p \| q ) = p \log(\frac{p}{q}) + (1-p)\log(\frac{1-p}{1-q})$ is the KL-divergence between two Bernoulli distributions with parameters $p$ and $q$.
statement_text: Let X be a set of size N . statement_text: A middle game MID has the same setting as PC , and it differs only in the allowed actions for the adversary. Then a permutation σ:[N] → [N] is sampled uniformly from the set of permutations satisfying σ(I_j) = O_j for all j . widehat A _1 is defined similarly to the algorithm A_1 from PC , but with respect to that permutation σ , and it is allowed to make only outer queries and no inner queries . The outer queries of widehat A _1 may depend on I and O . The rest of the game is defined similarly. The running time T_2 of widehat A _1 is defined as the number of queries it makes, and the total running time of widehat A is defined as T := T_1 + T_2 .

statement_tex:
\label{def:adaptivity}
We say that an oracle algorithm is $k$-round adaptive if the algorithm's oracle queries consist of $k$ sets, 
such that each set of queries
depends on the advice string, the input, and the replies to the previous rounds
of queries. We call a $1$-round adaptive algorithm non-adaptive. Finally, we say
that an algorithm is strongly non-adaptive if it issues a single set of queries that
only depends on the algorithm’s input, but not on the advice string. In all of the
above cases, when referring to the number of queries made by the algorithm, we
account for the sum over all rounds.
statement_text: We say that an oracle algorithm is k -round adaptive if the algorithm's oracle queries consist of k sets, such that each set of queries depends on the advice string, the input, and the replies to the previous rounds of queries. We call a 1 -round adaptive algorithm non-adaptive. Finally, we say that an algorithm is strongly non-adaptive if it issues a single set of queries that only depends on the algorithm’s input, but not on the advice string. In all of the above cases, when referring to the number of queries made by the algorithm, we account for the sum over all rounds.

label: def:sum-of-squares

statement_tex:
\label{def:sum-of-squares} 
Given a set of $m$ polynomial equality constraints $\Axioms$ over the reals, a Sum of Squares (SoS) refutation is a sequence of polynomials $\Proof = (t_1, \dots, t_m; s_1, \dots, s_a)$ such that

\[ h \Def \sum_{i \in [m]} t_ip_i+ \sum_{i \in [a]} s_i^2 = -1\]

The degree of a proof $\Proof$ is

\[ \Degree{\Proof} \Def \max\left\{\max_{i \in [m]} \Degree{t_i} + \Degree{p_i}, \max_{i \in [a]} 2\Degree{s_i}\right\}\]
statement_text: Given a set of m polynomial equality constraints Q over the reals, a Sum of Squares (SoS) refutation is a sequence of polynomials π = (t_1, ... , t_m; s_1, ... , s_a) such that \[ h = Σ _ i ∈ [m] t_ip_i+ Σ _ i ∈ [a] s_i^2 = -1\] The degree of a proof π is \[ Deg (π ) = max {max _ i ∈ [m] Deg (t_i ) + Deg (p_i ), max _ i ∈ [a] 2 Deg (s_i ) }\]
title: Sum Of Squares Refutation

The degree of the proof is given by $\Degree{\Proof} = \max_{i \in l}\Degree{t_i}$. If we let $\Pi$ denote the set of all PC refutations of $\Axioms$, then

\[ \Degree{\Axioms \PC \bot} \Def \min_{\Proof \in \Pi}\Degree{\Proof}\]

statement_tex:
\label{thm:AM-original}
    For every CNF formula $\varphi$ over $n$ variables and every size parameter $s \in \bbN$, if $\varphi$ is unsatisfiable and $\pi$ is a correct Resolution refutation of $\Reff_s(\varphi)$, then $|\pi| \geq 2^{\Omega(s/n)}$.
statement_text: For every CNF formula φ over n variables and every size parameter s ∈ N , if φ is unsatisfiable and π is a correct Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) , then |π| ≥ 2^ Ω(s/n) .
title: Atserias--Müller lower bound

label: thm:ub-in-res-informal
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:ub-in-res-informal}
    There is a polynomial-size depth-2 Boolean circuit~$P(\alpha, \varphi, s)$ of fan-in 2 that given a CNF formula $\varphi$, a satisfying assignment $\alpha$, and $s \in \bbN$, outputs a Resolution refutation $\pi$ of $\Reff_s(\varphi)$. Furthermore, the correctness of this circuit $P$ has polynomial-size proofs in Resolution.
statement_text: There is a polynomial-size depth-2 Boolean circuit P(α, φ, s) of fan-in 2 that given a CNF formula φ , a satisfying assignment α , and s ∈ N , outputs a Resolution refutation π of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) . Furthermore, the correctness of this circuit P has polynomial-size proofs in Resolution.
title: Pudlák's upper bound in Resolution, informal

label: thm:characterization-informal
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let S be a reasonable propositional proof system that simulates Extended Frege. Then, for every sequence { φ_n }_ n ∈ N of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, \[ S vdash _ poly ¬ φ_n qquad if and only if qquad Svdash _ poly ¬ normal scshape Ref (normal scshape Ref (φ_n)).\]
title: Propositional fragments of Atserias--Müller, informal

label: thm:aut-for-Ref-informal
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: For every reasonable proof system S that simulates Extended Frege as well as for Resolution itself, sep=0pt S is automatable if, and only if, S is automatable exclusively on normal scshape Ref formulas; S is weakly automatable if, and only if, S is weakly automatable exclusively on normal scshape Ref formulas.
title: Automatability in terms of normal scshape Ref formulas, informal

label: thm:prop-unprovable-informal
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let Q be a reasonable propositional proof system that simulates Resolution. If { φ_n}_ n ∈ N is a sequence of hard unsatisfiable CNF formulas for Q , where φ_n has n variables and size |φ_n|= poly (n) , then sep=0pt the formulas normal scshape Ref _ n^2 (φ_n) over N = poly (n) variables are all unsatisfiable and require size 2^ N^ Ω(1) to be refuted in Resolution; yet, Q does not have polynomial-size refutations of the formulas normal scshape Ref _ N^2 (normal scshape Ref _ n^2 (φ_n)) stating quadratic lower bounds on normal scshape Ref _ n^2 (φ_n) .
title: Propositional unprovability of Resolution lower bounds, informal

label: cor:PHP-Ref-ACO-informal
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{cor:PHP-Ref-ACO-informal}
    For every $d\leq O(\log n / \log \log n)$, the formulas $\Reff(\Reff(\PHP_n))$ are all unsatisfiable but require size $\exp({\Omega(n^{1/(2d+1)})})$ to be refuted in depth-$d$ Frege systems.
statement_text: For every d ≤ O( log n / log log n) , the formulas normal scshape Ref (normal scshape Ref (normal scshape PHP _n)) are all unsatisfiable but require size exp ( Ω(n^ 1/(2d+1) ) ) to be refuted in depth- d Frege systems.
title: Hard normal scshape Ref formulas for bounded-depth Frege, informal

label: thm:fo-unprovable-informal
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let T be a consistent first-order theory extending Robinson Arithmetic by a set of polynomial-time recognizable axioms. Then, there exists a sequence of unsatisfiable propositional formulas { ψ_ N }_ N ∈ N described uniformly by a polynomial-time algorithm, where ψ_N has N variables, such that sep=0pt Resolution refutations of the formula ψ_ N require size 2^ N^ Ω(1) ; there exists c > 0 such that the theory T cannot prove Ω(N^c) lower bounds on the Resolution size of these refutations; that is, there is N_0 ∈ N such that the lower bound expressed by the first-order sentence ∀ N ∀ π (N > N_0 ∧ Ref _ Res (ψ_N,π) → |π| > N^c ) is unprovable in T .
title: First-order unprovability of Resolution lower bounds, informal

label: thm:Hastad-PHP
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:Hastad-PHP}
    For every $d \leq O(\log n / \log \log n)$, depth-$d$ Frege systems require size at least $\exp({\Omega(n^{1/(4d-2)})})$ to prove $\neg \PHP_n$.
statement_text: For every d ≤ O( log n / log log n) , depth- d Frege systems require size at least exp ( Ω(n^ 1/(4d-2) ) ) to prove ¬ normal scshape PHP _n .

label: thm:buss-witnessing
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:buss-witnessing}
    Let $\varphi(x, y)$ be a $\Sigma^b_1$ formula. If $\SOT \vdash \forall x\exists y\varphi(x, y)$, then there exists a $\PV$ function $w$ such that $\SOT \vdash \forall x\varphi(x, w(x))$.
statement_text: Let φ(x, y) be a Σ^b_1 formula. If S^1_2 vdash ∀ x ∃ yφ(x, y) , then there exists a PV function w such that S^1_2 vdash ∀ xφ(x, w(x)) .
title: Buss's witnessing theorem

label: thm:translation
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: The theory PV_1 and the proof system Extended Frege correspond to each other. That is, sep=0pt PV_1 proves the soundness of EF ; if φ(x) is a quantifier-free formula in the language L _ BA ( PV ) and PV_1 vdash ∀ xφ(x) , then there exists a polynomial-time computable function f such that for every n ∈ N , it holds that f(1^n) : EF vdash llbracket φrrbracket _n .
title: Cook's correspondence theorem

label: def:Reff-formulas
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let n, m, s ∈ N , and let Lit _n coloneq {x_1, ... , x_n, ¬ x_1, ... , ¬ x_n} denote the of possible literals over n variables. The normal scshape Ref _s(φ) formula is built from the variables defined above, together with the conjunction of the following clauses: allowdisplaybreaks 2 Ref & ( enable ^B ∧ res ^B_ x_i ∧ lpoint ^B_ B' ∧ lit ^ B' _ell ) → lit ^ B _ell &&quad for B, B' ∈ [s], B' < B, i ∈ [n], ell ∈ Lit _n \ { x_i}, & ( enable ^B ∧ res ^B_ x_i ∧ rpoint ^B_ B' ∧ lit ^ B' _ell ) → lit ^ B _ell &&quad for B, B' ∈ [s], B' < B, i ∈ [n], ell ∈ Lit _n \ { ¬ x_i}, & ( enable ^B ∧ weak ^B_A ∧ a sf - lit ^A_ell ) → lit ^B_ell &&quad for B ∈ [s], A ∈ [m], ell ∈ Lit _n, & ( enable ^B ∧ derived ^B ) → vee_ i ∈ [n] res ^B_ x_i &&quad for B ∈ [s], & ( enable ^B ∧ derived ^B ) → vee_ substack B' ∈ [s] B' < B lpoint ^B_ B' &&quad for B ∈ [s], & ( enable ^B ∧ derived ^B ) → vee_ substack B' ∈ [s] B' < B rpoint ^B_ B' &&quad for B ∈ [s], & ( enable ^B ∧ ¬ derived ^B ) → vee_ A ∈ [m] weak ^B_A &&quad for B ∈ [s], & ( enable ^B ∧ lpoint ^B_ B' ) → enable ^ B' &&quad for B, B' ∈ [s], B' < B & ( enable ^B ∧ rpoint ^B_ B' ) → enable ^ B' &&quad for B, B' ∈ [s], B' < B & ¬ lit ^s_ell &&quad for ell ∈ Lit _n , & enable ^s. &&
title: The normal scshape Ref formulas

label: def:satf
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let n, m ∈ N , let φ denote the set of variables of the form a sf - lit ^A_ell as above and let α denote the set of variables α_i as above. The formula normal scshape Sat (φ, α) is the CNF formula over the variables in φ , α and additionally all the variables sat ^A_ell above consisting of the conjunction of the following clauses, allowdisplaybreaks 2 Sat & ¬ sat ^A_ell ∨ a sf - lit _ell ^A &&quad for all A ∈ [m] and ell ∈ {x_1, ... , x_n, ¬ x_1, ... , ¬ x_n}, & ¬ sat ^A_ x_i ∨ α_i &&quad for all A ∈ [m] and i ∈ [n], & ¬ sat ^A_ ¬ x_i ∨ ¬ α_i &&quad for all A ∈ [m] and i ∈ [n], & vee_ i ∈ [n] sat ^A_ x_i ∨ sat ^A_ ¬ x_i &&quad for all A ∈ [m].
title: The normal scshape Sat formulas

label: prop:sat-to-native-Res
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: For every CNF formula φ , the following statements hold: sep=0pt if φ has a Resolution refutation of length s , then normal scshape Sat _ restriction φ has a Resolution refutation of length O(s) ; if normal scshape Sat _ restriction φ has a Resolution refutation of length s , then φ has a Resolution refutation of length O(s) .

label: def:refl-formulas
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{def:refl-formulas}
Let $Q$ be a Cook--Reckhow propositional proof system and let $n, m, s \in \bbN$. We define $\Reflf^Q_{n, m, s} \coloneq \neg\Satf(\varphi, \alpha)  \lor \neg \Reff^Q(\varphi, \pi)$ where the $\Satf$ instance is for CNF formulas with $n$ variables and $m$ clauses and the $\Reff^Q$ instance is for $Q$-refutations of such formulas of size $s$, and refer to the sequence of tautologies $\Reflf^Q \coloneq \{\Reflf^Q_{n, m, s}\}_{n, m, s \in \bbN}$ as the \emph{reflection principle for $Q$}.
statement_text: Let Q be a Cook--Reckhow propositional proof system and let n, m, s ∈ N . We define normal scshape Refl ^Q_ n, m, s coloneq ¬ normal scshape Sat (φ, α) ∨ ¬ normal scshape Ref ^Q(φ, π) where the normal scshape Sat instance is for CNF formulas with n variables and m clauses and the normal scshape Ref ^Q instance is for Q -refutations of such formulas of size s , and refer to the sequence of tautologies normal scshape Refl ^Q coloneq {normal scshape Refl ^Q_ n, m, s }_ n, m, s ∈ N as the reflection principle for Q .
title: The normal scshape Refl formulas

label: def:PAP
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{def:PAP}
    Let $Q$ be a propositional proof system. We define the \emph{Proof Analysis Problem for $Q$} to be the language
    \[ \PAP_Q \coloneq \{ (\varphi, \pi, 1^s) \mid \varphi \in \SAT \text{ and } \pi : {Q \vdash \neg \Reff_s(\varphi)} \}.\]
    We denote by $\PAP_Q[s(n)]$ the problem where the size parameter $s$ is restricted to be at least $s(n)$ and $n$ denotes the number of variables of $\varphi$.
statement_text: Let Q be a propositional proof system. We define the Proof Analysis Problem for Q to be the language \[ PAP _Q coloneq { (φ, π, 1^s) mid φ ∈ SAT and π : Q vdash ¬ normal scshape Ref _s(φ) }.\] We denote by PAP _Q[s(n)] the problem where the size parameter s is restricted to be at least s(n) and n denotes the number of variables of φ .
title: The Proof Analysis Problem, PAP _Q

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex: We say that a propositional proof system $Q$ is \emph{analyzable} if there exists some constant $c > 0$ such that $\PAP_Q[n^c] \in \P$.
statement_text: We say that a propositional proof system Q is analyzable if there exists some constant c > 0 such that PAP _Q[n^c] ∈ P .
title: Analyzability

label: prop:PAP_
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{prop:PAP_}
    It holds that $\PAP_\Res[n^2]$ is in $\P$-uniform $\ComplexityFont{AC}^0$. That is, Resolution is analyzable.
statement_text: It holds that PAP _ Res [n^2] is in P -uniform AC ^0 . That is, Resolution is analyzable.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: For a propositional proof system Q , we denote by FPAP _Q the search version of the Proof Analysis Problem for Q , defined as follows. mylen @ l > RaggedRight X @ toprule multicolumn 2 @ > Centering p mylen @ FPAP _Q (search version of PAP _Q ) midrule bf Input & A CNF formula φ , a size parameter s in unary and a proof π such that π : Q vdash ¬ normal scshape Ref _s(φ) . addlinespace bf Output & Either a satisfying assignment for φ , if φ ∈ SAT , or 0 otherwise. bottomrule Similarly to PAP _Q[s(n)] , we define FPAP _Q[s(n)] to be the search problem where the size parameter is at least s(n) .
title: Search version of PAP

label: prop:aut-anal-duality
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{prop:aut-anal-duality}
    Let $Q \geq \Res$. If $Q$ is both analyzable and automatable, then $\P = \NP$.
statement_text: Let Q ≥ Res . If Q is both analyzable and automatable, then P = NP .

label: def:disabling-restriction
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{def:disabling-restriction}
    We say that a restriction $\rho\in\{0,1, *\}^N$ to the $N$ variables of $\Reff_s(\varphi)$ is \emph{$d$-disabling} if it satisfies that (i) exactly $d$ blocks are disabled, and the rest are all enabled, (ii) every variable belonging to a disabled block is assigned a value, and (iii) no other variable is assigned.
statement_text: We say that a restriction ρ ∈ {0,1, *}^N to the N variables of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) is d -disabling if it satisfies that (i) exactly d blocks are disabled, and the rest are all enabled, (ii) every variable belonging to a disabled block is assigned a value, and (iii) no other variable is assigned.
title: Disabling restrictions

label: lemma:rand-wr
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let p ∈ [0, 1) and let N be the number of variables of the normal scshape Ref _s(φ) formula for some CNF formula φ over n variables. There exists a randomized algorithm R taking as input 1^N , and outputting an lfloor s/2 rfloor -disabling restriction ρ ∈ {0, 1, * }^ N , such that for every Resolution refutation π of the formula normal scshape Ref _s(φ) , the following properties hold: sep=0pt the restriction ρ does not falsify normal scshape Ref _s(φ) ; with probability at least p , the block-width of π_ restriction ρ is at most O ( log |π| - log (1 - p) ) ; the running time of R(1^N) is O(N) .
title: Randomized block-width reduction

label: lemma:det-wr
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: There exists a constant c > 0 and a deterministic algorithm taking as input a Resolution refutation π of the formula normal scshape Ref _s(φ) over N variables and outputting a d -disabling restriction ρ ∈ {0,1, *}^ N with d ≤ c/2 · ( sqrt s log |π| ) such that sep=0pt the restriction ρ does not falsify normal scshape Ref _s(φ) ; the block-width of π_ restriction ρ is at most c · ( sqrt s log |π| ) ; the algorithm runs in time poly (|π|, s) .
title: Deterministic block-width reduction

label: fact:weakening
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{fact:weakening}
    Let $\varphi$ be CNF formula over $n$ variables. If $C$ is a non-tautological width-$n$ clause over the variables of $\varphi$ that is not the weakening of any clause of $\varphi$, then the unique assignment that falsifies $C$ is a satisfying assignment for $\varphi$.
statement_text: Let φ be CNF formula over n variables. If C is a non-tautological width- n clause over the variables of φ that is not the weakening of any clause of φ , then the unique assignment that falsifies C is a satisfying assignment for φ .

label: lemma:extraction
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: There exists a deterministic algorithm E such that for every s ∈ N , every π a purported Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) for a CNF formula φ(x_1, ... , x_n) with m clauses, and every ρ ∈ { 0,1,*}^N a d -disabling restriction to the N variables in normal scshape Ref _s(φ) , it holds that E(φ, ρ, s, π) terminates in time poly (|π|, s, n, m) and provides exactly one of the following outputs: sep=0pt an incorrect derivation step in π ; a clause C ∈ π_ restriction ρ of block-width at least 1/3 lfloor (s-d - n)/nrfloor ; a satisfying assignment for φ .
title: Assignment extraction

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: The following hold at the beginning of each iteration of the algorithm, when dealing with the clause C in the traversal of π : sep=0pt the reservation α falsifies C ; a block B ∉ D is only reserved in α if it is either mentioned in C or its parent according to α is mentioned in C , and, in particular, bw (α) - d ≤ 3 bw (C) ; if α encodes any information about a block B from layer i , and B ∉ D , then α also determines that B contains exactly i literals over the variables x_1, ... , x_i and no two literals for the same variable; the reservation α does not falsify any axiom of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) .
title: Invariant

label: thm:det-algo
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:det-algo}
It holds that ${\FPAP_{\Res}}[n^3] \in \FP$. That is, there exists a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm solving the search version of the Proof Analysis problem for Resolution whenever the lower bound parameter satisfies $s \geq n^3$.
statement_text: It holds that FPAP _ Res [n^3] ∈ FP . That is, there exists a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm solving the search version of the Proof Analysis problem for Resolution whenever the lower bound parameter satisfies s ≥ n^3 .

label: thm:rand-algo
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:rand-algo}
   There exists a zero-error randomized polynomial-time algorithm solving the search version of the Proof Analysis problem for Resolution whenever the lower bound parameter satisfies $s \geq n^2$. That is, ${\FPAP_{\Res}}[n^2] \in \ComplexityFont{FZPP}$.
statement_text: There exists a zero-error randomized polynomial-time algorithm solving the search version of the Proof Analysis problem for Resolution whenever the lower bound parameter satisfies s ≥ n^2 . That is, FPAP _ Res [n^2] ∈ FZPP .

label: cor:Levin-NP-hard
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{cor:Levin-NP-hard}
    There is a polynomial-time Levin reduction from the search problem for $\TSAT$ to the Proof Size Problem for Resolution.
statement_text: There is a polynomial-time Levin reduction from the search problem for TSAT to the Proof Size Problem for Resolution.

label: thm:info-efficiency
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:info-efficiency}
    For every CNF formula $\varphi$ over $n$ variables and $\poly(n)$ clauses and every $s \geq n^3$, if $\varphi$ is satisfiable, then
        \[\info_\Res(\neg \Reff_s(\varphi))  = \Theta\left( \min \{ \Kt(\alpha \mid \varphi)   \mid \varphi(\alpha)=1 \}\right).\]
    On the other hand, if $\varphi$ is unsatisfiable, then $\info_\Res(\neg \Reff_s(\varphi)) = \Omega(n)$.
statement_text: For every CNF formula φ over n variables and poly (n) clauses and every s ≥ n^3 , if φ is satisfiable, then \[ info _ Res ( ¬ normal scshape Ref _s(φ)) = Θ ( min { Kt (α mid φ) mid φ(α)=1 } ).\] On the other hand, if φ is unsatisfiable, then info _ Res ( ¬ normal scshape Ref _s(φ)) = Ω(n) .
title: Assignment extraction as information efficiency

label: thm:CP90-PHP
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: There exist a positive ε_0 ∈ Q and n_0 ∈ N such that \[ PV_1 vdash ∀ n ∀ π( Ref _ Res (normal scshape PHP ^n_ n-1 , π) ∧ n ≥ n_0 → ||π|| > ε_0 n).\]

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
Let $\varphi = C_1 \land \cdots \land C_k$ and $\psi = D_1 \land \cdots \land D_m$ be two CNF formulas over the variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$. We denote by $\disj(\varphi, \psi)$ the formula
    \[  \disj(\varphi, \psi) \coloneq \bigwedge_{i=1}^k (\neg y \lor C_i) \land \bigwedge_{i=1}^m (y \lor D_i),\]
    where $y$ is a fresh variable not present in $\varphi$ or $\psi$.
statement_text: Let φ = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_k and ψ = D_1 ∧ ... ∧ D_m be two CNF formulas over the variables x_1, ... , x_n . We denote by Disj (φ, ψ) the formula \[ Disj (φ, ψ) coloneq wedge_ i=1 ^k ( ¬ y ∨ C_i) ∧ wedge_ i=1 ^m (y ∨ D_i),\] where y is a fresh variable not present in φ or ψ .

label: thm:lwb-for-Disj
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: For every positive constant c ∈ N , there exist n_0 ∈ N such that \[ S^1_2 vdash ∀ φ ∀ π ∀ n ≤ φ ∀ m ≤ φ (n ≥ n_0 ∧ 3-CNF (φ, n, m) ∧ |π| ≤ n^ c → ¬ Ref _ Res ( Disj (φ, normal scshape PHP _n) ), π) ) .\]

label: cor:EF-proofs
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: For every positive constant c ∈ N , there exists a polynomial-time computable function t such that for every 3-CNF formula φ over a large enough number n of variables, t(φ) outputs an Extended Frege proof π such that \[ π: EF vdash ¬ normal scshape Ref _ n^ c ( Disj (φ, normal scshape PHP _n) ).\]

label: thm:PAP-EF-reduction
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:PAP-EF-reduction}
For every positive constant $c \in \bbN$, the language $\TSAT$ reduces to $\PAP_{\EF}[n^c]$ under polynomial-time many-one Levin reductions.
statement_text: For every positive constant c ∈ N , the language TSAT reduces to PAP _ EF [n^c] under polynomial-time many-one Levin reductions.

label: cor:PAPS-hard-above-EF
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{cor:PAPS-hard-above-EF}
    For every propositional proof system $Q$ that p-simulates Extended Frege and every polynomial $s(n)$, the problem $\PAP_Q[s(n)]$ is $\NP$-complete under polynomial-time many-one Levin reductions.
statement_text: For every propositional proof system Q that p-simulates Extended Frege and every polynomial s(n) , the problem PAP _Q[s(n)] is NP -complete under polynomial-time many-one Levin reductions.

label: cor:general-NP-hardness
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{cor:general-NP-hardness}
    Let $S$ be a propositional proof system constructively closed under \emph{modus ponens} and proving that Resolution is closed under restrictions and suppose there exists a constant $c > 0$ and a $\P$-uniform sequence of unsatisfiable formulas $\{ \psi_n\}_{n\in \bbN}$ such that $\psi_n$ has $n$ variables and $\poly(n)$ clauses and there exists a $\P$-uniform sequence of $S$-proofs $\{ \pi_n\}_{n\in\bbN}$ such that $\pi_n :S \vdash \neg\Reff_{n^c}(\psi_n)$.  Then, the problem $\PAP_S[n^c]$ is $\NP$-complete.
statement_text: Let S be a propositional proof system constructively closed under modus ponens and proving that Resolution is closed under restrictions and suppose there exists a constant c > 0 and a P -uniform sequence of unsatisfiable formulas { ψ_n}_ n ∈ N such that ψ_n has n variables and poly (n) clauses and there exists a P -uniform sequence of S -proofs { π_n}_ n ∈ N such that π_n :S vdash ¬ normal scshape Ref _ n^c (ψ_n) . Then, the problem PAP _S[n^c] is NP -complete.

label: conj:analyzability-requires-lbs
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{conj:analyzability-requires-lbs}
    For every propositional proof system $Q$, if $Q$ is analyzable, then $Q$ is not optimal.
statement_text: For every propositional proof system Q , if Q is analyzable, then Q is not optimal.

label: conj:original
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{conj:original}
    For every propositional proof system $Q$, if $Q$ is analyzable, then $Q$ is not p-optimal.
statement_text: For every propositional proof system Q , if Q is analyzable, then Q is not p-optimal.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: The following hold: sep=0pt Cref conj:analyzability-requires-lbs is true if, and only if, NP ≠ coNP ; Cref conj:original is true if, and only if, P ≠ NP .

label: thm:equivalence-PAP-AM
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let S be a propositional proof system that simulates Resolution, is constructively closed under modus ponens and contrapositions, and proves that Resolution is closed under restrictions. Assuming there exists a constant δ >0 such that TSAT ∉ io SIZE [2^ δ n ] , the following are equivalent: sep=0pt the proof system S is analyzable; there are constants c > 0 , n_0 ≥ 1 and ε > 0 such that for every unsatisfiable 3-CNF formula φ over n ≥ n_0 variables, every S -proof of the formula ¬ normal scshape Ref _ n^ c (φ) requires size at least 2^ ε n .

label: def:most-killing
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: We will say that a restriction ρ enjoys the most-killing property with respect to a trace τ = ((b_1, X_1), ... , (b_ell , X_ell )) if it holds that for every k ∈ [ell ] , the block i ∈ [s] \ { b_1, ... , b_ k-1 } that is the most frequent block mentioned in W_ restriction ρ_ k-1 happens to be precisely b_k and ρ_k satisfies the following conditions. sep=0pt If e_i appears positively in at least 1/3 of all the clauses in W_ restriction ρ_ k-1 that mention block i , then ρ_k(e_i) = 1 and ρ_k(x) = * for every other variable x ≠ e_i in block i . If e_i does not appear positively in at least 1/3 of all the clauses in W_ restriction ρ_ k-1 that mention block i , then ρ_k(e_i) = 0 and for every other variable in block i , ρ_k assigns values to them respecting the ordering in X_i = ( e_i, x_ i,1 , x_ i, 2 , ... ) and with the following priority. For j = 1, ... , |X_i|-1 , sep=0pt if x_ i, j appears positively more often than negatively in W_ restriction ρ_ k-1, {e_i, x_ i, 1 , ... , x_ i, j-1 } , then ρ_k(x_ i, j ) = 1 ; if x_ i, j appears negatively more often than positively in W_ restriction ρ_ k-1, {e_i, x_ i, 1 , ... , x_ i, j-1 } , then ρ_k(x_ i, j ) = 0 .
title: Most-killing property

label: lemma:induction-restriction-PV
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let c ∈ N . The following is provable in S^1_2 . For every CNF formula φ over n variables and π a correct Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) , let w coloneq c · lceil sqrt s log |π| rceil and let W denote the set of clauses in π of block-width larger than w . Then, for every ell , the formula Ψ(φ, π, s, ell ) defined as follows holds: if ell ≤ w/2 , then there exists a restriction ρ ∈ { 0,1,*}^N , where N is the number of variables of the normal scshape Ref _s(φ) formula, a trace τ = ((b_1, X_1), ... , (b_ell , X_ell )) and d ≤ ell such that: sep=0pt ρ is d -disabling; ρ has the most-killing property according to τ ; (3s)^ell · |W_ restriction ρ | ≤ |W| · (3s- w + ell )^ell .

label: lemma:exp-bound-PV
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: In PV_1 , for all n,m,p ∈ Log , if n < m and p ≥ 1 , it holds that \[ gl( 1 - frac n m gr)^p ≤ 2^ -frac n m p . \]

label: fact-in-PV

statement_text: Let φ be a Boolean formula in CNF over n variables. If C is a width- n clause over the variables of φ that is not the weakening of any clause of φ , then ¬ C encodes a satisfying assignment for φ .

label: def:reservation-invariant
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let π be a Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) for some CNF formula φ(x_1, ... , x_n) , let N be the number of variables of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) , d ≤ depth (π) , and let C = (C_1, ... , C_d) be a length- d path in π starting from C_1 = bot . Let the s blocks of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) be arranged in a layered manner, so that there are n layers, each containing lfloor s/nrfloor blocks, with the remainder blocks left from the flooring operations collected all in the last layer, plus one additional layer on top with a single block corresponding to the root. We say that C satisfies the reservation invariant with respect to a sequence A = (α_1, ... , α_d) of restrictions α_i ∈ { 0,1,*}^N if, for every i ∈ [d] , sep=0pt the restriction α_i falsifies C_i ; a block is only mentioned in α_i if it is either mentioned in C_i or its parent according to α_i is mentioned in C_i , and, in particular, bw (α_i) ≤ 3 bw (C_i) ; if α_i restricts some variable in block B from layer ell , then it does so in the following way: B must contain exactly ell literals over the variables x_1, ... , x_ell and no two literals for the same variable; the restriction α_i does not falsify any clause of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) ; the path determined by C corresponds to A in the following way: if C_i was derived from C_ i+1 by resolving over variable v , then α_ i+1 (v) is defined and v appears in C_ i+1 with polarity 1- α_ i+1 (v) .
title: Reservation invariant

label: lemma:induction-width-PV
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: The following is provable in S^1_2 . For every CNF formula φ over n variables and π a correct Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) , for every d , the formula Ψ(φ, π, s, d) defined as follows holds: if 1 ≤ d ≤ depth (π) , then there exists a sequence C = (C_1, ... , C_d) of clauses of π and a sequence A = (α_1, ... , α_d) of restrictions such that at least one of the following conditions holds: sep=0pt there is C_i ∈ C that satisfies bw (C_i) ≥ 1/3 (lfloor s/n rfloor - 1 ) ; there is C_i in and its corresponding restriction α_i that contain a satisfying assignment to φ ; the sequence C is a path in π starting at C_1 = bot and the reservation invariant holds for C with respect to A .

label: thm:ub-in-Res
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:ub-in-Res}
    For every $n, m, s \in \bbN$, 
    there is some $\tau=\Theta(s(m+sn^2))$ such that for $t\geq \tau$
    there exist uniform polynomial-size Resolution derivations of the form
    \[ \Satf(\varphi, \alpha) \land \pi =P(\varphi, \alpha, s)  \vdash_{\Res}  \Reff_t(\Reff_s(\varphi), \pi) \,,\]
    where the $\Satf$ formula is for CNF formulas with $n$ variables and $m$ clauses, and $\pi = P(\varphi, \alpha, s)$ stands for the conjunction of clauses describing the upper bound construction, as per \Cref{subsec:Pudlak-as-ckt}. Moreover, the derivations can be described uniformly in polynomial time.
statement_text: For every n, m, s ∈ N , there is some τ=Θ(s(m+sn^2)) such that for t ≥ τ there exist uniform polynomial-size Resolution derivations of the form \[ normal scshape Sat (φ, α) ∧ π =P(φ, α, s) vdash _ Res normal scshape Ref _t(normal scshape Ref _s(φ), π) ,\] where the normal scshape Sat formula is for CNF formulas with n variables and m clauses, and π = P(φ, α, s) stands for the conjunction of clauses describing the upper bound construction, as per Cref subsec:Pudlak-as-ckt . Moreover, the derivations can be described uniformly in polynomial time.
title: Pudlák's upper bound in Resolution

label: thm:lb-formal
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
\label{thm:lb-formal}
    There exists a uniform family of polynomial-size circuits $\{ E_{n,m,s,t} \}_{n,m,s,t \in \bbN}$ such that for every CNF formula $\varphi$ over $n$ variables and $m$ clauses, if $\varphi$ is satisfiable and $\pi$ is a Resolution refutation of $\Reff_s(\varphi)$ for $s \geq n^3$, then the circuit $E_{n,m,s,t}(\varphi, \pi)$ outputs a satisfying assignment for $\varphi$. Furthermore, this is provable in Extended Frege, that is,  there exists a polynomial $\ell(n, m, s, t)$ such that
    \[ \EF \vdash_{\ell(n,m,s,t)} \Reff_{t}(\Reff_s(\varphi), \pi) \to \Satf(\varphi, E_{n,m,s,t}(\varphi, \pi)) \,,\]
    and these proofs can be generated uniformly in polynomial time.
statement_text: There exists a uniform family of polynomial-size circuits { E_ n,m,s,t }_ n,m,s,t ∈ N such that for every CNF formula φ over n variables and m clauses, if φ is satisfiable and π is a Resolution refutation of normal scshape Ref _s(φ) for s ≥ n^3 , then the circuit E_ n,m,s,t (φ, π) outputs a satisfying assignment for φ . Furthermore, this is provable in Extended Frege, that is, there exists a polynomial ell (n, m, s, t) such that \[ EF vdash _ ell (n,m,s,t) normal scshape Ref _ t (normal scshape Ref _s(φ), π) → normal scshape Sat (φ, E_ n,m,s,t (φ, π)) ,\] and these proofs can be generated uniformly in polynomial time.
title: Extraction algorithm in EF

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex: Suppose Resolution is automatable by a sequence of circuits $A = \{ A_{n,m, s}\}_{n,m,s \in \bbN}$, and suppose $\EF \vdash_{\mathrm{poly}} \Autf^A_{n, m, s}$. Then, there exists a family of circuits $C =\{C_{n}\}_{n\in\bbN}$ of size $n^{O(1)}$ such that $\EF \vdash_{n^{O(1)}} \Satf^C_{n}$.
statement_text: Suppose Resolution is automatable by a sequence of circuits A = { A_ n,m, s }_ n,m,s ∈ N , and suppose EF vdash _ poly normal scshape Aut ^A_ n, m, s . Then, there exists a family of circuits C ={C_ n }_ n ∈ N of size n^ O(1) such that EF vdash _ n^ O(1) normal scshape Sat ^C_ n .
title: Resolution is NP -hard to automate, in EF

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex: We say that a proof system $S$ is \emph{reasonably strong} if it is polynomially equivalent to $\EF + A$ for some set $A$ of tautologies recognizable in polynomial time.
statement_text: We say that a proof system S is reasonably strong if it is polynomially equivalent to EF + A for some set A of tautologies recognizable in polynomial time.

label: prop:mild-properties
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: The following hold for every reasonably strong proof system S : sep=0pt the system S is constructively closed under formula substitutions, i.e., given a proof of φ(x_1, ... , x_n) in size s and formulas ψ_1, ... , ψ_n , we can obtain a proof of φ(ψ_1, ... , ψ_n) in time poly (s, n, |ψ_1|, ... , |ψ_n|) ; the system S is constructively closed under modus ponens , i.e., given an S -proof of φ in size s and an S -proof of φ → ψ in size t , we can obtain an S -proof of ψ in time poly (s, t) ; the system S is constructively closed under contrapositions, i.e., given an S -proof of ¬ ψ in size s and an S -proof of φ → ψ in size t , we can obtain an S -proof of ¬ φ in time poly (s, t) ; the system S implicationally simulates Resolution : for every two CNF formulas φ and ψ such that Resolution performs the derivation φ vdash _ Res ψ in size s , there is an S -proof of φ → ψ in size poly (s) .

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex:
Let $\varphi(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be a CNF formula and let $ 1 \leq k \leq n$. We define $\varphi[k]$ to be the CNF formula $\varphi \land \mathsf{Ext}^k_n$, where $\mathsf{Ext}^k_n$ consists of all clauses encoding the extensions
    \[ y_{\{\ell_1, \dots, \ell_k\}} \leftrightarrow \ell_1 \land \dots \land \ell_k \]
    for every set of literals $\{\ell_1, \dots, \ell_k\}$ over the variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$, where the $y$-variables are fresh variables.
statement_text: Let φ(x_1, ... , x_n) be a CNF formula and let 1 ≤ k ≤ n . We define φ[k] to be the CNF formula φ ∧ Ext ^k_n , where Ext ^k_n consists of all clauses encoding the extensions \[ y_ {ell _1, ... , ell _k} ↔ ell _1 ∧ ... ∧ ell _k \] for every set of literals {ell _1, ... , ell _k} over the variables x_1, ... , x_n , where the y -variables are fresh variables.

label: lemma:UB-consequence-basic
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let S ≥ Res be a propositional proof system closed under literal substitutions, modus ponens, contrapositions, and implicationally simulating Resolution. Then, there exists p(n, m, s) = poly (n,m, s) such that for every n -variate CNF formula φ with m clauses, and every t ≥ p(n,m,s) if S vdash ¬ normal scshape Ref _ t (normal scshape Ref _s(φ)) in size ell , then S vdash ¬ φ[2] in size poly (n, m, s, t, ell ) .

label: thm:fragment-characterization
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let S be a reasonably strong proof system. There is p(n, m, s) = poly (n,m, s) such that for every CNF formula φ(x_1, ... , x_n) with m clauses, every t ∈ N , and every s ≥ n^3 , sep=0pt if S vdash ¬ φ in size ell , then S vdash ¬ normal scshape Ref _t(normal scshape Ref _ s (φ_n)) in size poly (n, m, s, t, ell ) ; if S vdash ¬ normal scshape Ref _ p(n,m,s) (normal scshape Ref _s(φ_n)) in size ell , then S vdash ¬ φ_n in size poly (n, m, s, ell ) . Furthermore, in both cases, given an S -proof of the left-hand side statement, one can obtain a proof of the right-hand side statement in polynomial time.

paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_tex: For every $d \leq O(\log n / \log \log n)$, there are polynomials $p(n)$ and $q(n)$ such that the formulas in the sequence $ \{ \neg \Reff_{p(n)} (\Reff_{q(n)}(\PHP_n)) \}_{n\in \bbN} $ are all tautological but require size $\exp(\Omega({n^{1/(4d-2)}}))$ to be proven in depth-$d$ Frege systems.

label: cor:prop-unprovability
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: For every propositional proof system S ≥ Res implicationally simulating Resolution and closed under contrapositions and clause substitutions, if S is not polynomially bounded, there exists a family of unsatisfiable CNF formulas {ψ_n}_ n ∈ N on N = poly (n) variables and of size |ψ_n| = poly (n) such that they require size at least 2^ N^ Ω(1) to be refuted in Resolution; there is a polynomial p(n) such that the formulas { ¬ normal scshape Ref _ p(n) (ψ_n)}_ n ∈ N are tautological but do not have polynomial-size proofs in S .

label: thm:fo-unprovable
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let T be a consistent first-order extending S^1_2 with a set of axioms recognizable in polynomial time and admitting N as a model. Then, there exits a sequence of unsatisfiable propositional formulas { ψ_ k, s }_ k, s ∈ N described uniformly by a polynomial-time algorithm given k and s in unary, where ψ_ k,s has N = poly (k, s) variables, and such that sep=0pt Resolution refutations of the formula ψ_ k, s require size 2^ N^ Ω(1) ; there are constants c >0 and N_0 ∈ N such that the lower bound expressed by the first-order sentence ∀ k ∀ s ∀ π ( N > N_0 ∧ Ref _ Res (ψ_ k, s , π) → |π| > N^ c ) is independent of T .

label: cor:fo-unprovable
paper_title: The Proof Analysis Problem
statement_text: Let T be a consistent first-order extending Q with a set of axioms recognizable in polynomial time. Then, there exits a sequence of unsatisfiable propositional formulas { ψ_ k, s }_ k, s ∈ N described uniformly by a polynomial-time algorithm given k and s in unary, where ψ_ k,s has N = poly (k, s) variables, and such that sep=0pt Resolution refutations of the formula ψ_ k, s require size 2^ N^ Ω(1) ; there is a constant c > 0 and N_0 ∈ N such that the lower bound expressed by the first-order sentence ∀ k ∀ s ∀ π (N > N_0 ∧ Ref _ Res (ψ_ k, s , π) → |π| > N^ c ) is unprovable in T , but true in N .

label: thm:intro_algo
paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
\label{thm:intro_algo}
    Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language over some domain $D$ that has the dual discriminator operation as its polymorphism. Then $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma)$ can be $|D|$-approximated in polynomial time.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language over some domain D that has the dual discriminator operation as its polymorphism. Then sc MinCostCSP (Γ) can be |D| -approximated in polynomial time.

label: thm:intro_necessary
paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
\label{thm:intro_necessary}
    Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language such that $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma)$ has a constant-factor approximation, then $\Gamma$ has a NU polymorphism, unless P = NP.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language such that sc MinCostCSP (Γ) has a constant-factor approximation, then Γ has a NU polymorphism, unless P = NP.

label: thm:intro_perm
paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
\label{thm:intro_perm}
    Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language over some domain $D$ that contains all permutation relations over $D$. Then $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma)$ can be $|D|$-approximated if $\Gamma$ has an NU polymorphism, and is NP-hard to approximate within any constant factor otherwise.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language over some domain D that contains all permutation relations over D . Then sc MinCostCSP (Γ) can be |D| -approximated if Γ has an NU polymorphism, and is NP-hard to approximate within any constant factor otherwise.

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language. An instance of $\CSP(\Gamma)$ is a tuple $I = (V, \mathcal{C})$, where $V$ is a finite set of variables and $\mathcal{C}$ a finite set of constraints. Each constraint $C \in \mathcal{C}$ is of the form $(R, S)$, where $R$ is a relation in $\Gamma$ with some arity $k$ and $S \in V^k$ a $k$-tuple of variables.
    An \emph{assignment} for $I$ is a function $A: V \to D$. We say that $A$ satisfies a constraint $C = (R, (x_1, \ldots, x_k))$ if $(A(x_1), \ldots, A(x_k)) \in R$, and we say that $A$ is a satisfying assignment for $I = (V, \mathcal{C})$ if $A$ satisfies every constraint in $\mathcal{C}$.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language. An instance of sc CSP (Γ) is a tuple I = (V, C ) , where V is a finite set of variables and C a finite set of constraints. Each constraint C ∈ C is of the form (R, S) , where R is a relation in Γ with some arity k and S ∈ V^k a k -tuple of variables. An assignment for I is a function A: V → D . We say that A satisfies a constraint C = (R, (x_1, ... , x_k)) if (A(x_1), ... , A(x_k)) ∈ R , and we say that A is a satisfying assignment for I = (V, C ) if A satisfies every constraint in C .

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex: Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language. An instance of $\ListCSP(\Gamma)$ is a tuple $I = (V, \mathcal{C}, \{R_x\}_{x \in V})$, where $V$ is a finite set of variables and $\mathcal{C}$ a finite set of constraints, as in the definition of $\CSP(\Gamma)$. In addition to $V$ and $\mathcal{C}$, we are also given a subset $R_x \subseteq D$ for every variable $x \in V$. We say that $A$ is a satisfying assignment for $I = (V, \mathcal{C}, \{R_x\}_{x \in V})$ if $A$ satisfies every constraint in $\mathcal{C}$ and $A(x) \in R_x$ for every $x \in V$.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language. An instance of sc ListCSP (Γ) is a tuple I = (V, C , {R_x}_ x ∈ V ) , where V is a finite set of variables and C a finite set of constraints, as in the definition of sc CSP (Γ) . In addition to V and C , we are also given a subset R_x ⊆ D for every variable x ∈ V . We say that A is a satisfying assignment for I = (V, C , {R_x}_ x ∈ V ) if A satisfies every constraint in C and A(x) ∈ R_x for every x ∈ V .

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex: Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language. An instance of $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma)$ is a tuple $I = (V, \mathcal{C}, \cost)$, where $V$ and $\mathcal{C}$ are the same as they are in the definition of $\CSP(\Gamma)$, and we are also given a function $\cost: V \times D \to \mathbb{R}^{\geq 0} \cup \{+\infty\}$. For any assignment $A$ for $I$, the cost of $A$ is defined to be $\cost_I(A) = \sum_{x \in V}\cost(x, A(x))$. The goal is find a satisfying assignment with the minimum cost.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language. An instance of sc MinCostCSP (Γ) is a tuple I = (V, C , mathtt cost ) , where V and C are the same as they are in the definition of sc CSP (Γ) , and we are also given a function mathtt cost : V × D → R ^ ≥ 0 ∪ {+ ∞ } . For any assignment A for I , the cost of A is defined to be mathtt cost _I(A) = Σ _ x ∈ V mathtt cost (x, A(x)) . The goal is find a satisfying assignment with the minimum cost.

label: obs:mincost_unary
paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
\label{obs:mincost_unary}
    Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language over some domain $D$ and $\Gamma' = \Gamma \cup \{S \subseteq D \mid S \neq \varnothing\}$. Then $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma)$ and $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma')$ are equivalent. Namely, any instance of $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma)$ can be solved as an instance of $\MinCostCSP(\Gamma')$ and vice versa.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language over some domain D and Γ' = Γ ∪ {S ⊆ D mid S ≠ varnothing } . Then sc MinCostCSP (Γ) and sc MinCostCSP (Γ') are equivalent. Namely, any instance of sc MinCostCSP (Γ) can be solved as an instance of sc MinCostCSP (Γ') and vice versa.

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex: Let $f: D^k \to D$ be a $k$-ary operation on the domain $D$, and $R$ some $m$-ary relation over the same domain. We say that $f$ preserves $R$ (or $f$ is a \emph{polymorphism} of $R$) if for every $(a_{1,1}, \ldots, a_{1,m}), \ldots, (a_{k,1}, \ldots, a_{k,m}) \in R$ we have $(b_1, \ldots, b_m) \in R$, where $b_i = f(a_{1, i}, \ldots, a_{k, i})$ for every $i \in [m]$. Given a constraint language $\Gamma$ we say that $f$ preserves $\Gamma$ (or $f$ is a \emph{polymorphism} of $\Gamma$) if $f$ preserves every $R \in \Gamma$. We use $\Pol(R)$ to denote the set of all polymorphisms of $R$, and (abusing notation slightly) $\Pol(\Gamma) = \bigcap_{R \in \Gamma} \Pol(R)$ to denote the set of all polymorphisms of $\Gamma$.
statement_text: Let f: D^k → D be a k -ary operation on the domain D , and R some m -ary relation over the same domain. We say that f preserves R (or f is a polymorphism of R ) if for every (a_ 1,1 , ... , a_ 1,m ), ... , (a_ k,1 , ... , a_ k,m ) ∈ R we have (b_1, ... , b_m) ∈ R , where b_i = f(a_ 1, i , ... , a_ k, i ) for every i ∈ [m] . Given a constraint language Γ we say that f preserves Γ (or f is a polymorphism of Γ ) if f preserves every R ∈ Γ . We use Pol (R) to denote the set of all polymorphisms of R , and (abusing notation slightly) Pol (Γ) = cap_ R ∈ Γ Pol (R) to denote the set of all polymorphisms of Γ .

label: def:clone
paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_text: A clone over D is a set of operations F ⊆ cup_ n ≥ 1 {f: D^n → D} for which the following holds: F contains the projection operation proj ^n_i for every n ≥ 1 , i ∈ [n] . For every m -ary g ∈ F and n -ary f_1, ... , f_m ∈ F , the n -ary function g' defined by \[ g': (x_1, ... , x_n) mapsto g(f_1(x_1, ... , x_n), ... , f_m(x_1, ... , x_n)) \] is also in F .

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
Let $f: D^k \to D$ be a $k$-ary operation for some $k \geq 3$. We say that $f$ is a \emph{near-unanimity (NU)} operation if for every $a, b \in D$, 
    \[
    f(a, a, \ldots, a, b) = f(a, a, \ldots, b, a) = \cdots = f(b, a, \ldots, a, a) = a.
    \]
    In other words, if all but one inputs are equal to some $a \in D$, then $f$ outputs $a$. If $k = 3$, then $f$ is also called a \emph{majority} operation.
statement_text: Let f: D^k → D be a k -ary operation for some k ≥ 3 . We say that f is a near-unanimity (NU) operation if for every a, b ∈ D , \[ f(a, a, ... , a, b) = f(a, a, ... , b, a) = ... = f(b, a, ... , a, a) = a. \] In other words, if all but one inputs are equal to some a ∈ D , then f outputs a . If k = 3 , then f is also called a majority operation.

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
Let \emph{the dual discriminator operation} $d: D^3 \to D$ be defined by
    \[
    d(x_1, x_2, x_3) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
        a & \text{if } |\{i \mid x_i = a\}| \geq 2, \\
        x_1 & \text{otherwise.}
    \end{array}\right.
    \]
    Then $d$ is a majority operation. This operation will be featured heavily in our algorithmic results.
statement_text: Let the dual discriminator operation d: D^3 → D be defined by \[ d(x_1, x_2, x_3) = { ll a & if |{i mid x_i = a}| ≥ 2, x_1 & otherwise. . \] Then d is a majority operation. This operation will be featured heavily in our algorithmic results.

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
Let $R$ be a $n$-ary relation. Let $S_{n, k} = \{(i_1, \ldots, i_k) \mid 1 \leq i_1 < \cdots < i_k \leq n\}$ be the set of $k$-tuples whose entries are in $[n]$ and in increasing order. For any $s = (i_1, \ldots, i_k) \in S_{n,k}$ and $x = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)$, let $\Pi_{s} x = (x_{i_1}, \ldots, x_{i_k})$ and $\Pi_{s}R = \{\Pi_{s} x \mid x \in R\}$. We say that $R$ is $k$-decomposable if for every $x = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)$, we have
    \[
    x \in R \quad\Leftrightarrow\quad \forall s \in S_{n, k}, \Pi_s x \in \Pi_s R.
    \] 
    We say that $\Gamma$ is $k$-decomposable if every $R \in \Gamma$ is $k$-decomposable.

label: def:pp_def
paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex:
\label{def:pp_def}
    Let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language over $D$ and $R$ a $k$-ary relation over the same domain. We say that $\Gamma$ \emph{pp-defines} $R$, if there exist some $m > 0$ and a conjunction $\mathfrak{C}$ over variables $x_1, \ldots, x_k, y_1, \ldots, y_m$ consisting of relations in $\Gamma$ and the equality relation ($\eq_D := \{(u, v) \in D^2 \mid u = v\}$) over $D$, such that
    \[
    R(x_1, \ldots, x_k) \equiv \exists y_1\cdots \exists y_m \mathfrak{C}.
    \]
    If $\Gamma'$ is another constraint language over the same domain $D$, then we say that $\Gamma$ pp-defines $\Gamma'$ if $\Gamma$ pp-defines every relation in $\Gamma'$.
statement_text: Let Γ be a constraint language over D and R a k -ary relation over the same domain. We say that Γ pp-defines R , if there exist some m > 0 and a conjunction C over variables x_1, ... , x_k, y_1, ... , y_m consisting of relations in Γ and the equality relation ( eq _D := {(u, v) ∈ D^2 mid u = v} ) over D , such that \[ R(x_1, ... , x_k) equiv ∃ y_1 ... ∃ y_m C . \] If Γ' is another constraint language over the same domain D , then we say that Γ pp-defines Γ' if Γ pp-defines every relation in Γ' .

statement_tex:
Let $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ be constraint languages over domains $D$ and $E$ respectively. We say that $\Gamma_1$ pp-interprets $\Gamma_2$ if there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $F \subseteq D^n$, and a surjective function $f: F \to E$ such that $\Gamma_1$ pp-defines the following relations:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $F$ as an $n$-ary relation over $D$.
    \item For every $R \in \Gamma_2$ with some arity $k$, the relation 
    \[
    f^{-1}(R) = \{(x^{(1)}, x^{(2)}, \ldots, x^{(k)}) \in D^{kn} \mid x^{(i)} \in F \text{ for } i = 1, 2, \ldots, k, (f(x^{(1)}), \ldots, f(x^{(k)})) \in R\}
    \]
    Here each $x^{(i)}$ is a $n$-tuple over $D$ and we are thinking of $(x^{(1)}, x^{(2)}, \ldots, x^{(k)})$ as a flattened $kn$-tuple over $D$.
    \item The relation 
    \[
    f^{-1}(\mathrm{eq}_{E}) = \left\{(x^{(1)}, x^{(2)}) \in D^{2n} \mid x^{(i)} \in F \text{ for } i = 1, 2,\, f(x^{(1)}) = f(x^{(2)})\right\}
    \]
    Here again $x^{(1)}$ and $x^{(2)}$ are $n$-tuples over $D$ and $(x^{(1)}, x^{(2)})$ is a flattened $2n$-tuple.
\end{itemize}

For every R ∈ Γ_2 with some arity k , the relation \[ f^ -1 (R) = {(x^ (1) , x^ (2) , ... , x^ (k) ) ∈ D^ kn mid x^ (i) ∈ F for i = 1, 2, ... , k, (f(x^ (1) ), ... , f(x^ (k) )) ∈ R} \] Here each x^ (i) is a n -tuple over D and we are thinking of (x^ (1) , x^ (2) , ... , x^ (k) ) as a flattened kn -tuple over D . The relation \[ f^ -1 ( eq _ E ) = {(x^ (1) , x^ (2) ) ∈ D^ 2n mid x^ (i) ∈ F for i = 1, 2, f(x^ (1) ) = f(x^ (2) ) } \] Here again x^ (1) and x^ (2) are n -tuples over D and (x^ (1) , x^ (2) ) is a flattened 2n -tuple.

paper_title: On the Constant-Factor Approximability of Minimum Cost Constraint Satisfaction Problems
statement_tex: Let $(D, \mathcal{F})$ and $(D', \mathcal{F}')$ be two algebras with the same signature. A function $f: D \to D'$ is called a homomorphism from  $(D, \mathcal{F})$ to $(D', \mathcal{F}')$, if $f$ commutes with all basic operations. That is, for every $k$-ary function symbol $t$ in the signature, we have $t_{D'}(f(a_1), \ldots, f(a_k)) = f(t_D(a_1, \ldots, a_k))$, where $t_D$ and $t_{D'}$ are the functions $t$ represents in $(D, \mathcal{F})$ and $(D', \mathcal{F}')$ respectively. When $(D, \mathcal{F})=(D', \mathcal{F}')$, we also say that $f$ is an \emph{automorphism}.

    Let $D$ be a finite domain such that $|D| \geq 5$. Let $(D, \mathcal{F})$ be a homogeneous algebra, then either the dual discriminator operation $d$ is a term operation, or its clone of term operations $\langle \mathcal{F} \rangle$ is equal to one of the followings:

statement_tex:
{definition}{factors}\label{def:factors}
For rooted forest $T$ we define the following three kinds of factors:
\begin{description}[topsep=0pt,noitemsep]
\item[Tree Factor] A \emph{tree factor} is a set $V(T_x)$ for some $x \in V(T)$. We call $x$ \emph{the root} of the factor.
    \item[Forest Factor] 
    A forest factor is a {\bf nonempty} 
union of tree factors whose roots are siblings. In particular, 
a tree factor is also a forest factor but the empty set is not. 
The set of roots of the tree factors included in the union are 
called the \emph{roots} of the 

factor. 
If they are not roots of components of $T$, we define their 
joint parent as the \emph{parent} of the factor. Note that We consider two nodes of $T$  siblings when they
have a joint parent or if they both roots of components of $T$. This convention is chosen to remain consistent with the notation of~\cite{DBLP:journals/lmcs/BojanczykP22}.
\item[Context Factor] A context factor is a set $U=X \setminus Y$ where $X$ is a 
tree factor and $Y$ is a forest factor whose roots are strict
descendants of the root of $X$. The \emph{root} of $U$, denoted by $rt(U)$, is the root of $X$
and the roots of $Y$ are called the \emph{appendices} of $U$. 
Note that a tree factor is {\bf not} a context factor. 
We will sometimes refer to
$X$ as the \emph{base tree factor} of $U$ and to $Y$ as the \emph{removed forest} of $U$.  For clarity we sometimes denote $X$ and $Y$ as $X(U)$ and $Y(U)$.
We also denote the parent of the appendices by $pr(U)$ and let 
the \emph{spine} of $U$, denoted by $spine(U)$, be the path 
from $rt(U)$ to $pr(U)$
\end{description}

statement_tex:
{definition}{managewidth}\label{def:manageablewidth}
We call a width function $f$ \emph{manageable} if it satisfies all of the following.

\begin{description}[topsep=0pt,noitemsep]
\item[Weak monotone separability.]
$f$ is weakly monotone separable, as in Definition~\ref{def:weaksep}.

\item[Bounded size.]
There exists a computable function $\beta$ such that for every $k\ge 0$, every hypergraph $H$,
and every $U\subseteq V(H)$, if $f_H(U)\le k$, then
\(
  |U|\le \beta\bigl(k,\rank(H)\bigr).
\)
We refer to any such $\beta$ as a \emph{size bound} for $f$.

\item[Invariant locality.]
For all hypergraphs $H_1,H_2$ and all $U_1\subseteq V(H_1)$, $U_2\subseteq V(H_2)$, if
$H_1[U_1]\cong H_2[U_2]$, then $f_{H_1}(U_1)=f_{H_2}(U_2)$.

\item[Automatizability.]
There exists an algorithm that, given a hypergraph $H$, computes $f_H(V(H))$ in time at most
$t(|V(H)|)$ for some computable function $t$.
\end{description}

\label{def:singleswap}
Continuing on Definition \ref{def:contmono}, 
assume that $q \geq 4$. 
Let $1<i<q-1$. 
Let $(u_1,u_2)$ be the edge from the last vertex of $P_{i-1}$ to
the first vertex of $P_i$. 
Let $(v_1,v_2)$ be the edge from the last vertex 
of $P_i$ to the first vertex of $P_{i+1}$.
Finally, let $(w_1,w_2)$ be the edge connecting the
last vertex of $P_{i+1}$ and the first vertex of $P_{i+2}$. 
Let $F'$ be obtained from $F$ by removal of edges 
$(u_1,u_2)$ , $(v_1,v_2)$, and $(w_1,w_2)$
and adding edges $(u_1,v_2)$, $(w_1,u_2)$, $(v_1,w_2)$. 
We call $F'$ a \emph{swap} of $F$ and the \emph{intervals
being swapped} are $P_i$ and $P_{i+1}$. 

We say that the swap is \emph{neutral} if $\fwidth(F') \leq \fwidth(F)$.
In particular, in this case that $U$ \emph{admits} a neutral swap
(of intervals $P_{i}$ and $P_{i+1}$).

label: lem:singleswap

statement_tex:
\label{lem:singleswap}
Let $F$ be a reduced elimination forest. Let $B$ be a context factor of $F$
with the spine $P$ and appendices $W$. 
Let $P_1, \dots, P_q$ be the colour intervals of $P$. 
Let $1 \leq i \leq q-4$.
Let $F'$ be the elimination forest obtained from $F$ by swapping $P_{i+1}$ and $P_{i+2}$.
Then the following statements hold regarding $F'$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F'$ is a reduced elimination forest. 
\item Each monochromatic factor of $F$ remains a monochromatic factor of $F'$ in
the same capacity (that is a tree factor remains a tree factor, a
forest factor remains a forest factor, and a context factor remains a context factor). 
\item Each context factor of $F$ disjoint with $B$ remains a context factor in $F'$
with the same spine and appendices. 
\item $B$ remains a context factor of $F'$ with the same appendices but with the spine
obtained from $P$ by swapping $P_{i+1}$ and $P_{i+2}$ as in Definition \ref{def:singleswap}.
In particular, the number of colour intervals of $B$ w.r.t. $B$ reduces by $2$.  
\end{enumerate}

Each context factor of F disjoint with B remains a context factor in F' with the same spine and appendices. label: def:transdtuple

statement_tex:
\label{def:transdtuple}
Let $({\bf t}=(T,B),F)$ be a \textsc{tf} pair of a hypergraph $H$. 
A \emph{transduction tuple} $({\bf C},{\bf D}, {\bf K}, {\bf f}, {\bf h})$ is defined as follows. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\bf C}$ is a partition of $V(H)$ into independent sets of $\mathsf{CG}({\bf t},F)$.
To put it differently ${\bf C}$ determines a proper colouring of $\mathsf{CG}({\bf t},F)$.
\item ${\bf D}$ is a weak partition of $V(H)$. 
\item ${\bf K}$ is a family of subgraphs. 
\item ${\bf f}$ is a mapping from ${\bf C}$ to ${\bf D}$ defined as follows. 
     \begin{enumerate}
		 \item There is exactly one element $D_0 \in {\bf D}$ such that ${\bf f}^{-1}(D_0)=\emptyset$. 
		 \item For each $C \in {\bf C}$, ${\bf f}(C)$ is the set of all children (in $F$) of the non-leaf elements of $C$. 
		 \end{enumerate}
\item ${\bf g}$ is a surjective mapping from ${\bf C}$ such that for each 
$C \in {\bf C}$, ${\bf g}(C)=\bigcup_{u \in C} T[\Stain(u,({\bf t},F))]$. 
\end{enumerate}

We also introduce additional related terminology. 
In particular, for each  $u \in V(H)$, $C(u)$ is the element of ${\bf C}$ containing $u$. 
Also, for each $C \in {\bf C}$, we define a function ${\bf h}_C$ on $C$ such that,
for each $u \in C$, ${\bf h}_C(u)$ is the connected component of ${\bf g}(C)$ containing $u$.

statement_tex:
\label{th:adaptauxapp}
There is an algorithm $\mathcal{A}(H,{\bf t}, k,\delta)$ (where $H$ is  a hypergraph,
${\bf t}$ is a tree decomposition of $H$,
$k$ is a non-negative rational, and $\delta \in \mathbb{N}$)
that returns an MSO formula $\varphi_1(U_1,\dots,U_\delta)$
where $U_0,\dots,U_\delta$ are free set variables
so that the following holds under assumption that $U_1, \dots, U_\delta$ weakly
partition $H$. 

Let $M=M(H,{\bf t})$ be a model over $\tau_{td}$. 
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $f_1[U_1, \dots, U_\delta]$ is not an independent set function then
    $M \models \varphi_1(U_1, \dots, U_\delta)$
    \item If $f_1=f_1[U_1, \dots, U_\delta]$ is an independent set function and
    and the $f_1$-width of $H$ is at most $k$ then 
    $M \models \varphi_1(U_1, \dots, U_\delta)$. 
    \item If $f_1=f_1[U_1, \dots, U_\delta]$ is an independent set function and
    and the $f_1$-width of $H$ is greater than $k$ then 
    $M \not\models \varphi_1(U_1, \dots, U_\delta)$.
\end{enumerate}
The runtime of the algorithm is FPT parameterized 
by the  treewidth of ${\bf t}$, $k$, $rank(H)$, $\Delta(H)$ and $\delta$
and the size of the resulting formula is upper-bounded by a function depending 
on these parameters.

being free set variables. Then there is an algorithm 
that transforms $\psi_0(V_1, \dots, V_r)$ to an MSO
formula $\psi_1(V_0, \dots, V_r)$ over the same signature $\tau$ 
where $V_0$ is also a free set variable
so that the following holds.

Then for each model $M$ over $\tau$, $M \models \psi_1(V'_0, \dots, V'_r)$
if and only if $M \setminus V'_0 \models \psi_0(V'_1, \dots, V'_r)$.

statement_tex:
Consider the quantity $(|V(G)|-1)^{2} = (n-1)^{2} \geq 0$ for $n$-vertex graphs $G$. This is nonnegative and, in fact, a graph motif parameter: 
Abbreviating $\#H = \indsub HG$, we have $n = \#{K_{1}}$ and $1 = \#{K_{0}}$, and  $(n-1)^{2}=\#{K_{1}}^{2}-2\#{K_{1}}+\#{K_{0}}$. Moreover, the quadratic term $\#{K_{1}}^2$ can be linearized\footnote{
This holds because $\#{K_{1}}^2$ counts the pairs $(u,v)\in V(G)^2$, and so does the linear combination $2 \#{K_{2}} + 2 \#{I_2} + \#{K_{1}}$, whose summands correspond to the isomorphism type of $G[\{u,v\}]$, which is either $K_2$, $I_2$, or $K_1$.
As we will elaborate later, graph motif parameters enjoy a general linearization property: Any polynomial combination of induced subgraph counts can be expressed as a unique linear combination. This holds even for ``subobject'' counts under more general notions of objects; see Lemma~\ref{lem:cat:linearize} and Corollary~\ref{cor:cat:lin}. This motivates our focus on \emph{linear} combinations.}
, i.e., expressed as the linear combination $\#{K_{1}}^{2} = 2 \#{K_{2}} + 2 \#{I_2} + \#{K_{1}}$.
Thus, we have
\[
0 \leq (\#K_1 - 1)^2 = 2\, \#K_2 + 2\,  \#I_2 - \# K_1 + \# K_0,
\]
and have constructed a linear combination of induced subgraph counts evaluating to a nonnegative value for every graph $G$, even though the term $\indsub {K_1}{\starpad}$ appears with coefficient $-1$.

statement_tex:
For a fixed graph $H$, we consider the problem of finding an induced $H$-copy in a large graph $G$. The graph $G$ is given as $(x, O)$ where $O: \Sigma^\ast \to \{0,1\}$ is an oracle encoding the edge relation and $x$ is the number of nodes of $G$ written in binary. The nodes of $G$ are $0,\dots,x-1$, written as bit strings of fixed length~$n$.
Given two nodes $u$ and $v$ of $G$, there is an edge between $u$ and $v$ iff $O(uv) = 1$. (Since we consider strings of fixed length $n$, no separation symbol is needed.) 
In this representation, most of the information about $G$ is stored in the oracle; the input $x$ only encodes the size of the graph, and the running time of oracle Turing machines is measured in terms of $x$.

paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_tex:
In our example of finding an induced copy of $H$ in the graph $G$, we start with a binary
type-2 relation $\IsIndSub_H(x,y,O)$. The relation interprets $y$ as an encoding of a set $Y$ of $k$ distinct nodes of $G$ with $k$ being the number of nodes of $H$. 
The relation then queries the oracle $O$ to obtain the induced subgraph $G[Y]$.
It then checks by brute force whether $G[Y]$ and $H$ are isomorphic. If yes, it returns the value $1$ and otherwise $0$. This is clearly polynomial-time computable in $|x|$. The relation $\exists \IsIndSub_H(x,O)$ now returns $1$ if $G$ contains an induced copy of $H$ \emph{somewhere}, and $0$ if $G$ does not contain such a copy. See also Lemma~\ref{lem:graphs_lower} for a more formal proof.

It then checks by brute force whether G[Y] and H are isomorphic. If yes, it returns the value 1 and otherwise 0 . This is clearly polynomial-time computable in |x| . The relation ∃ IsIndSub _H(x,O) now returns 1 if G contains an induced copy of H somewhere , and 0 if G does not contain such a copy. See also Lemma for a more formal proof.

label: def:Msub
paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_tex:
\label{def:Msub}
    Let $C$ be a locally small category and let $\cM$ be some class of morphisms in $C$ that contains all isomorphisms and is closed under composition.
    For any objects $a, b$ we call morphisms $a \to b$ from $\cM$ the $\cM$-subobjects of $a$ under $b$.
    We identify morphisms $f, f': a \to b$ if there is an isomorphism $g: a \to a$ with $f' = gf$.
    The set of all $\cM$-subobjects of $a$ under $b$ is denoted by $\Msub{a}{b}$, while the class of all $\cM$-subobjects under $b$ is denoted by $\poset{b}$.
    If all such $\poset{b}$ are small (i.e.\ a set), then we call $C$ $\cM$-well-powered and if they are all finite $C$ is called finitely $\cM$-well-powered.
    For notational convenience, we write $\domain \poset{b} := \{\domain f \,:\, f \in \poset{b}\}$.

    Let $f: a \to b$ and $f': a' \to b$ be $\cM$-subobjects under $b$.
    We write $f' \prec f$ if there is some morphism $g$ with $f' = gf$.
statement_text: Let C be a locally small category and let M be some class of morphisms in C that contains all isomorphisms and is closed under composition. For any objects a, b we call morphisms a → b from M the M -subobjects of a under b . We identify morphisms f, f': a → b if there is an isomorphism g: a → a with f' = gf . The set of all M -subobjects of a under b is denoted by Sub _ M (a mathop → b) , while the class of all M -subobjects under b is denoted by P (b) . If all such P (b) are small (i.e.\ a set), then we call C M -well-powered and if they are all finite C is called finitely M -well-powered. For notational convenience, we write mathop dom P (b) := {mathop dom f : f ∈ P (b)} . Let f: a → b and f': a' → b be M -subobjects under b . We write f' prec f if there is some morphism g with f' = gf .

label: def:factorization_system
paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_text: Let C be a category and let E and M be some classes of morphisms in C . We call ( E , M ) a factorization system if they fulfil the following properties: Every morphism f: a → b factors as f = me with e ∈ E and m ∈ M . This factorization is unique, up to a unique isomorphism, i.e.\ if there is some other factorization f = m'e' with e' ∈ E and m' ∈ M , then there is a unique isomorphism g such that the following diagramm commutes: a arrow [r, "e" description] arrow [d, "e'" description] & bullet arrow [d, "m" description] bullet arrow [r, "m'" description] arrow [ru, "g" description, dotted] & b Both E and M contain all isomorphisms and are closed under composition. A factorization system is called proper, if all morphisms in E are epi and all morphisms in M are mono.

\label{def:cat_setinstantiator}
Let $C$ and $P$ be locally small, finitely $\cM$-well-powered categories with a compatible ($\cE$, $\cM$)-factorization system and where $P$ is a full subcategory of $C$ that is closed under isomorphism.

Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine,
let $c \in C$ and
let $\varphi$ be a $P$-pure motif parameter.

Let  $\top$  be a symbolic top element above the $\cM$-subobject poset $\poset{c}$, i.e., $\top \not\prec f$ for all $\cM$-subobjects $f \in \poset{c}$.
A  \defn{set-instantiator}  $\SI$  is a triple of

$\circ$ \ some $j \in \IN$, 

$\circ$ \ an instantiation function  $\inst_\SI : \poset{c} \to \catsize{C}{j}$,   and

$\circ$ \  a perception function  $\perc_\SI : \{0,1\}^* \to \poset{c} \cup \{\top\}$,

\smallskip

such that the following property holds for all $\cM$-subobjects $f \in \poset{c}$.

\smallskip
$\bu$ \ $\tau\in\{0,1\}^*$ is an accepting path for the computation  $\#\acc_{M^{\inst_\SI(f)}}(j)$
iff $\perc_\SI(\tau) \prec f$, and 

$\bu$ \ $\varphi(\inst_\SI(f))) = \varphi(\domain f)$.

label: def:cat_ramsey_prop
paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_tex:
\label{def:cat_ramsey_prop}
    A locally small category $C$ with a ($\cE$, $\cM$)-factorization system is called $\cM$-Ramsey, if for every $a, b \in C$ and $t \in \IN$, there is some $c \in C$, such that for every $\Phi: \Msub{a}{c} \to \{0, \ldots, t\}$, there is a $f_\Phi \in \Msub{b}{c}$ with the property that $\Phi$ is constant when restricted to inputs from $\{g \in \Msub{a}{c} \,: \, g \prec f_\Phi\}$.
statement_text: A locally small category C with a ( E , M )-factorization system is called M -Ramsey, if for every a, b ∈ C and t ∈ N , there is some c ∈ C , such that for every Φ: Sub _ M (a mathop → c) → {0, ... , t} , there is a f_Φ ∈ Sub _ M (b mathop → c) with the property that Φ is constant when restricted to inputs from {g ∈ Sub _ M (a mathop → c) : g prec f_Φ} .

label: pro:cat_ramseyposet
paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_tex:
\label{pro:cat_ramseyposet}
    Let $C$ be an $\cM$-Ramsey, locally small and finitely $\cM$-well-powered category with a ($\cE$, $\cM$)-factorization system.
    
    Let $b \in C$ and let $t \in \IN$ be fixed.
    Then there is a $c \in C$, such that for every $\Phi: \poset{c} \to \{0, \ldots, t\}$ there is a $f_\Phi \in \Msub{b}{c}$ with the property, if $g, h \prec f_\Phi$ with $\domain g \cong \domain h$, then $\Phi(g) = \Phi(h)$.
statement_text: Let C be an M -Ramsey, locally small and finitely M -well-powered category with a ( E , M )-factorization system. Let b ∈ C and let t ∈ N be fixed. Then there is a c ∈ C , such that for every Φ: P (c) → {0, ... , t} there is a f_Φ ∈ Sub _ M (b mathop → c) with the property, if g, h prec f_Φ with mathop dom g cong mathop dom h , then Φ(g) = Φ(h) .
title: Ramsey Theorem

label: lem:cat_forceGood
paper_title: Which graph motif parameters count?
statement_tex:
\label{lem:cat_forceGood}
    Let $C$ and $P$ be locally small and finitely $\cM$-well-powered categories with a compatible ($\cE$, $\cM$)-factorization system, where $P$ is a full subcategory of $C$ that is closed under isomorphisms and where $C$ is $\cM$-Ramsey.

\label{lem:cat:prop}
    \label{lem:cat_seperate}
    Let $C$ and $P$ be two categories with the following properties:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $P$ is a full subcategory of $C$, closed under isomorphism.
        \item $C$ and $P$ have a compatible proper ($\cE$, $\cM$)-factorization system.
        \item $C$ and $P$ are both locally small.
        \item $C$ and $P$ are both finitely $\cM$-well-powered.
        \item $C$ and $P$ both have the joint $\cM$-embedding property.
        \item $C$ is $\cM$-Ramsey.
        \item $C$ and $P$ fulfill the blowup property.

    Let $M$ be any nondeterministic polynomial-time Turing machine computing $\eval{\varphi}$ for some bad $P$-pure motif parameter $\varphi$.
