Each gate is replaced by constant-radius ( r=1 ) SoS gadgets arranged as layered-wires or time × tape tiles. bf Complexity. For every M ∈ DTIME (n^t) , the compiled polynomial has size n^ O(1) and contextual entanglement width \[ CEW (P_ M,n ) = O( log n). \] bf Rank bound. For κ', ell ' = Θ( log n) , \[ Γ_ κ',ell ' (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \]
title: Self-Contained Deterministic Compiler

label: lem:machine-exact-verifier-norm
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:machine-exact-verifier-norm}
For every uniform decider $M$ of 3SAT (time $n^c$), the compiler can be extended---without changing acceptance---to an instrumented machine $M'$ that prepends a static clause-gadget sheet consisting of $O(m)$ disjoint, radius-$1$ blocks with coupling selectors, computing the coupled verifier polynomial
\[
V_C(x) = \mathrm{OR}(\ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3), \quad Q_\Phi^{\times}(x,z) = \prod_{C \in \Phi} (1 - z_C \cdot V_C(x)^2).
\]
Compilation preserves polylog CEW and polynomial rank:
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',n}) \leq n^{O(1)}.
\]

label: lem:instance-uniform-extraction
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:instance-uniform-extraction}
For each instance $\Phi$ of 3SAT, there exists a block-local transformation
\[
T_\Phi = (\text{basis}) \circ (\text{affine relabel}) \circ (\text{restriction}) \circ (\text{projection})
\]
computable in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time from $\Phi$ alone, such that
\[
T_\Phi(P_{M',|\rho(\Phi)|}) = Q_{\Phi,\mathcal{S}}^{\times} \quad\text{and}\quad \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q_{\Phi,\mathcal{S}}^{\times}) \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',|\rho(\Phi)|}),
\]
where $\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}(n)$ is the activated clause-set from the God-Move projection.
Each stage is rank-preserving or non-increasing by the Monotonicity Lemmas (Section~\ref{sec:components}); see Lemma~\ref{lem:god-move-properties} for the combined properties.

label: lem:coupled-sheet-extraction
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:coupled-sheet-extraction}
The instrumented polynomial $P_{M',n}$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:machine-exact-verifier-norm} admits an extraction to the coupled verifier sheet: there exists a deterministic local wiring $z=\zeta(u,v)$ such that for all inputs $(u, v)$ where $u$ represents clause variables and $v$ represents computation variables,
\[
P_{M',n}(u, v) = Q_\Phi^{\times}(u,z)\Big|_{z=\zeta(u,v)} + R_{M',\Phi}(v),
\]
where $Q_\Phi^{\times}(u,z) = \prod_{C\in\Phi}(1-z_C \cdot V_C(u)^2)$ is the coupled verifier sheet (Definition~\ref{def:Qphi-times}) and $R_{M',\Phi}$ depends only on $v$ (the TM tableau).

For the activated clause-set $\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}(n)$ from the God-Move projection, this yields $Q_{\Phi,\mathcal{S}}^{\times}(u) = \prod_{C\in\mathcal{S}}(1-V_C(u)^2)$, and the SPDP submatrix induced by the $u$-blocks satisfies
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q_{\Phi,\mathcal{S}}^{\times}) \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',n}).
\]

label: thm:global-god-move-pnp
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:global-god-move-pnp}
Assume the premises above.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose for contradiction $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP}$.
\item Then a polytime decider $M$ for 3SAT exists.
\item By Theorem~\ref{thm:self-contained-det-compiler} and Lemma~\ref{lem:machine-exact-verifier-norm} we obtain $P_{M',n}$ with
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',n}) \leq n^{O(1)}.
\]
\item Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:instance-uniform-extraction} yields for each $\Phi_n$:
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}) \leq n^{O(1)}.
\]
\item However, by the NP-side identity-minor lower bound (Section~\ref{sec:perm-lower-bound}),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}) \geq n^{\Theta(\log n)},
\]
a contradiction. Hence
\[
\boxed{\mathsf{P} \neq \mathsf{NP}.}
\]
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: Assume the premises above. Suppose for contradiction P = NP . Then a polytime decider M for 3SAT exists. By Theorem and Lemma we obtain P_ M',n with \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] Applying Lemma yields for each Φ_n : \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] However, by the NP-side identity-minor lower bound (Section ), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) , \] a contradiction. Hence \[ boxed P ≠ NP . \]
title: Global God Move (Global gauge projection map) ⇒ P ≠ NP

label: thm:universal-p-to-polyspdp
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:universal-p-to-polyspdp}
Fix any deterministic Turing machine $M\in\mathrm{DTIME}(n^t)$.
There exists a \emph{uniform}, \emph{input-independent} compiler
$\Compdet$ producing a multilinear polynomial $P_{M,n}$ over a field $\F$
(of characteristic $0$, or prime $p$ sufficiently large), such that:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item (\textbf{Uniformity}) $P_{M,n}$ is computable from the finite description of $M$
and $n$ in time $\poly(n)$ (no dependence on the particular input $x$).
\item (\textbf{Locality}) $P_{M,n}$ is assembled from constant-radius ($r=1$) local gadgets
arranged in a time$\times$tape (or layered-wire) layout.
\item (\textbf{Bounded interface types by construction}) in every canonical window,
only $O(1)$ gadget types occur, so the induced profile alphabet is finite and
\emph{independent of the window length} $\kappa$.
\item (\textbf{CEW bound}) $\CEW(P_{M,n}) = O(\log n)$.
\item (\textbf{SPDP rank bound}) for $\kappa'=\alpha\log n$ and $\ell'=\beta\log n$
(with fixed constants $\alpha,\beta>0$),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa',\ell'}(P_{M,n})\ \le\ n^{O(1)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, every language in $P$ admits a polynomial-SPDP-rank representation.
statement_text: Fix any deterministic Turing machine M ∈ DTIME (n^t) . There exists a uniform , input-independent compiler C _ det producing a multilinear polynomial P_ M,n over a field F (of characteristic 0 , or prime p sufficiently large), such that: (bf Uniformity ) P_ M,n is computable from the finite description of M and n in time poly (n) (no dependence on the particular input x ). (bf Locality ) P_ M,n is assembled from constant-radius ( r=1 ) local gadgets arranged in a time × tape (or layered-wire) layout. (bf Bounded interface types by construction ) in every canonical window, only O(1) gadget types occur, so the induced profile alphabet is finite and independent of the window length κ . (bf CEW bound ) CEW (P_ M,n ) = O( log n) . (bf SPDP rank bound ) for κ'=α log n and ell '=β log n (with fixed constants α,β>0 ), \[ Γ_ κ',ell ' (P_ M,n )\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . \] Consequently, every language in P admits a polynomial-SPDP-rank representation.
title: Universal P → poly--SPDP bridge

\label{lem:uniform-bounded-profile-diversity}

$\Delta=O(1)$ and bounded arity/width $w=O(1)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:compiler-bounded-degree}).

derivative parameter $\kappa$.

label: thm:universal-p-to-spdp-consolidated
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:universal-p-to-spdp-consolidated}
For every deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine
$M \in \mathrm{DTIME}(n^t)$, the self-contained deterministic compiler
of Theorem~\ref{thm:self-contained-det-compiler}
produces an SPDP polynomial $P_{M,n}$ such that:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Object identity:} $P_{M,n}$ coincides with the SPDP polynomial object used in the
Codimension/Collapse Theorem (the compiled polynomial is the same mathematical object
analyzed for rank bounds).

\item \textbf{CEW implies SPDP-admissibility:} The CEW bound $\mathrm{CEW}(P_{M,n}) = O(\log n)$
implies $P_{M,n}\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}(n)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:cew-to-admissible}.

\[

\]
\end{enumerate}

Thus, the universal inclusion
\[
P \subseteq \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}
\]
holds in ZFC, with all quantifiers discharged by explicit uniform construction.

statement_tex:

\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p \circ U) = \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p).

statement_text: If U is block-diagonal invertible, then \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p ∘ U) = Γ_ κ,ell (p). \]
title: Block-Local Basis Invariance

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model

\label{lem:mono-formal}

label: def:template-partition

statement_tex:
\label{def:template-partition}
The compiler template library is partitioned as

\mathcal{T} \;=\; \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{ver}} \;\dot{\cup}\; \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{comp}},
\]
where every $T\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{ver}}$ uses only verification/interface variables
(e.g.\ $u,z$) and every $T\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{comp}}$ uses only computation variables

label: lem:additive-separability
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:additive-separability}
For every compiled instance $P_{M,n}$ there exist polynomials $V_{M,n}$ and $R_{M,n}$
such that
\[
P_{M,n}(u,z,v) \;=\; V_{M,n}(u,z) \;+\; R_{M,n}(v),
\]
and $V_{M,n}$ contains no $v$-variables while $R_{M,n}$ contains no $(u,z)$-variables.
In particular, $P_{M,n}$ has no mixed monomials involving both $(u,z)$ and $v$.
statement_text: For every compiled instance P_ M,n there exist polynomials V_ M,n and R_ M,n such that \[ P_ M,n (u,z,v) = V_ M,n (u,z) + R_ M,n (v), \] and V_ M,n contains no v -variables while R_ M,n contains no (u,z) -variables. In particular, P_ M,n has no mixed monomials involving both (u,z) and v .

label: thm:tphi-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:tphi-formal}
For every 3SAT instance $\Phi$ with $n$ variables,
there exists a block-local transformation
\[
T_\Phi = (\text{basis}) \circ (\text{affine relabeling}) \circ (\text{restriction}) \circ (\text{projection})
\]
such that
\[
T_\Phi(P_{M^*,|\rho(\Phi)|}) = Q^{\times}_\Phi,
\quad
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(T_\Phi(\cdot)) \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(\cdot).
\]
Moreover, $T_\Phi$ is \textbf{uniformly computable} with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Time bound:} The description of $T_\Phi$ can be computed from $\Phi$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n)$.
\item \textbf{Description length:} The representation of $T_\Phi$ has size $\mathrm{poly}(n)$.
\item \textbf{Instance-independence:} The structure of $T_\Phi$ depends only on the size $n$ and parameters $(\kappa,\ell)$, not on the specific satisfying assignment or accepting computation. The map is determined entirely by the clause structure of $\Phi$ and the fixed compiler templates from Section~\ref{sec:tm-arithmetization}.
\item \textbf{Rank monotonicity:} Each stage (basis change, affine relabeling, restriction, projection) preserves or decreases SPDP rank by Lemma~\ref{lem:monotonicity-suite}; see also Lemma~\ref{lem:god-move-properties} for the combined God-move properties.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: For every 3SAT instance Φ with n variables, there exists a block-local transformation \[ T_Φ = ( basis ) ∘ ( affine relabeling ) ∘ ( restriction ) ∘ ( projection ) \] such that \[ T_Φ(P_ M^*,|ρ(Φ)| ) = Q^ × _Φ, quad Γ_ κ,ell (T_Φ( · )) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell ( · ). \] Moreover, T_Φ is bf uniformly computable with the following properties: bf Time bound: The description of T_Φ can be computed from Φ in time poly (n) . bf Description length: The representation of T_Φ has size poly (n) . bf Instance-independence: The structure of T_Φ depends only on the size n and parameters (κ,ell ) , not on the specific satisfying assignment or accepting computation. The map is determined entirely by the clause structure of Φ and the fixed compiler templates from Section . bf Rank monotonicity: Each stage (basis change, affine relabeling, restriction, projection) preserves or decreases SPDP rank by Lemma ; see also Lemma for the combined God-move properties.
title: Instance-Uniform Extraction

statement_tex:
\label{lem:sheet-formal}
In the compiled machine-exact polynomial $P_{M',|x|}$,
verifier-sheet variables $(u,z)$
and compute variables $v$ factor block-locally:
\[
P_{M',|x|}(u,z,v) = Q^{\times}_\Phi(u,z) + R_{M',\Phi}(v),
\]
where $Q^{\times}_\Phi(u,z) = \prod_C (1 - z_C \cdot V_C(u)^2)$ is the coupled verifier sheet (Definition~\ref{def:Qphi-times}),

label: def:spdp-admissible-feature-scheme
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_text: A polynomial p over N= poly (n) variables admits an SPDP-admissible feature scheme if it satisfies: bf Bounded local degree: p decomposes into local gadgets of degree O(1) , uniformly across all canonical windows; bf Canonical window structure / bounded incidence: there is a canonical windowing rule producing windows of radius R=Θ( log n) in the clause--variable (or gadget-interaction) incidence graph, and this incidence graph has maximum degree Δ=O(1) ; bf Bounded profile diversity: the number of distinct interface-anonymous profiles (Definition ) realized within any canonical window is at most N^ O(1) , independent of the derivative parameter κ ; bf Parameter compatibility: for κ,ell =Θ( log n) , all shifted partials used to form M_ κ,ell (p) remain within the degree regime required by the collapse theorem; equivalently, the effective degree after |S| ≤ κ differentiation and ell -shift is O( log n) . These conditions ensure that the SPDP Codimension/Collapse Theorem (Theorem ) applies with parameters κ,ell =Θ( log n) .
title: SPDP-admissible feature scheme

label: def:collapsing-class
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{def:collapsing-class}
Fix parameters $\kappa=\lceil \alpha \log n\rceil$ and $\ell=\lceil \beta \log n\rceil$.
A multilinear polynomial $p$ over $N=\poly(n)$ variables is in
$\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}(n)$ if there exists a \emph{canonical window}
decomposition and \emph{interface-anonymous profile} representation satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Local canonical windows:} $p$ decomposes into local windows of
radius $O(1)$ after the canonicalization map of
Section~\ref{sec:canonical-windows}.

\item \textbf{Bounded interface diversity:} within each window, the number of
realizable interface-anonymous profiles is at most $n^{O(1)}$ (equivalently,
profile compression removes any $\kappa$-dependence as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-compression-removes-k}).

\item \textbf{SPDP-admissibility:} the induced feature scheme is SPDP-admissible
in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:spdp-admissible-feature-scheme}
(and hence satisfies the Codimension/Collapse hypotheses).

\end{enumerate}
statement_text: Fix parameters κ=lceil α log nrceil and ell =lceil β log nrceil . A multilinear polynomial p over N= poly (n) variables is in C _ coll (n) if there exists a canonical window decomposition and interface-anonymous profile representation satisfying: bf Local canonical windows: p decomposes into local windows of radius O(1) after the canonicalization map of Section . bf Bounded interface diversity: within each window, the number of realizable interface-anonymous profiles is at most n^ O(1) (equivalently, profile compression removes any κ -dependence as in Lemma ). bf SPDP-admissibility: the induced feature scheme is SPDP-admissible in the sense of Definition (and hence satisfies the Codimension/Collapse hypotheses).

statement_tex:
\label{lem:tm-to-uniform-circuit}
Fix $c\ge 1$. For every deterministic $M\in \mathrm{DTIME}(n^c)$ there exists a

\[

label: thm:uniform-p-to-spdp
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:uniform-p-to-spdp}
There exists a \emph{uniform} polynomial-time compilation map
\[
\Comp:\ (M,1^n)\ \mapsto\ p_{M,n}
\]
such that for every deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine $M$ deciding a
language $L\in P$ and for all input lengths $n$:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Soundness of representation:} $p_{M,n}$ is the SPDP polynomial
associated to the computation of $M$ on length-$n$ inputs under the compiler
semantics of Section~\ref{sec:compiler} (i.e.\ the compiler is machine-exact).

\item \textbf{Membership in the collapsing class:} $p_{M,n}\in
\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}(n)$.

\item \textbf{Uniform rank collapse:} consequently,
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\bigl(p_{M,n}\bigr)\ \le\ n^{O(1)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

Equivalently, under the same fixed parameters $\kappa=\Theta(\log n)$ and
$\ell=\Theta(\log n)$,
\[
P\ \subseteq\ \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}.
\]
statement_text: There exists a uniform polynomial-time compilation map \[ C :\ (M,1^n)\ mapsto \ p_ M,n \] such that for every deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine M deciding a language L ∈ P and for all input lengths n : bf Soundness of representation: p_ M,n is the SPDP polynomial associated to the computation of M on length- n inputs under the compiler semantics of Section (i.e.\ the compiler is machine-exact). bf Membership in the collapsing class: p_ M,n ∈ C _ coll (n) . bf Uniform rank collapse: consequently, \[ Γ_ κ,ell l(p_ M,n r)\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . \] Equivalently, under the same fixed parameters κ=Θ( log n) and ell =Θ( log n) , \[ P\ ⊆ \ C _ coll . \]

label: lem:np-complete-witness-bookkeeping
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:np-complete-witness-bookkeeping}
Let $\mathrm{3SAT}\subseteq\{0,1\}^\ast$ denote the standard NP-complete
language of satisfiable 3-CNF formulas under the usual binary encoding
(e.g.\ listing clauses as triples of signed variable indices). Let
$\{\Phi_n\}$ be the explicit 3-CNF family used in
Section~\ref{sec:godmove} (e.g.\ the expander/Tseitin/Ramanujan--Tseitin
construction), with $|\Phi_n|=\poly(n)$ and each $\Phi_n$ a bona fide 3-CNF
formula over $n$ primary variables and $\poly(n)$ auxiliary variables.

Then:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{$\Phi_n$ is a standard 3SAT instance.}
For every $n$, the formula $\Phi_n$ is a syntactically valid 3-CNF formula,
and its encoding length satisfies $|\enc(\Phi_n)|=\poly(n)$.

\item \textbf{Uniform constructibility.}
The map $n\mapsto \enc(\Phi_n)$ is computable in time $\poly(n)$ (indeed
logspace/uniform, if desired), so $\{\Phi_n\}$ forms an explicit uniform family
of inputs to $\mathrm{3SAT}$.

\item \textbf{Same encoding regime for SPDP objects.}
Let $\Comp$ be the uniform compiler/encoding map fixed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform-p-to-spdp} (or Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-p-to-spdp-consolidated}).
Define the NP-side SPDP object by
\[
q_n \;:=\; \Comp(\Phi_n).
\]
Then $q_n$ is exactly the SPDP polynomial associated to the standard 3SAT input
$\Phi_n$ under the \emph{same} compilation/feature-scheme/canonical-window
regime used on the P-side.

\item \textbf{NP-complete witness role.}
Consequently, any claimed separation that proves a rank lower bound for the
family $\{q_n\}$ (e.g.\ $\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(q_n)\ge n^{\Omega(\log n)}$ for
$\kappa,\ell=\Theta(\log n)$) is a rank lower bound for a uniform family of
\emph{standard 3SAT instances} under the paper's fixed encoding.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: Let 3SAT ⊆ {0,1}^ast denote the standard NP-complete language of satisfiable 3-CNF formulas under the usual binary encoding (e.g.\ listing clauses as triples of signed variable indices). Let {Φ_n} be the explicit 3-CNF family used in Section (e.g.\ the expander/Tseitin/Ramanujan--Tseitin construction), with |Φ_n|= poly (n) and each Φ_n a bona fide 3-CNF formula over n primary variables and poly (n) auxiliary variables. Then: bf Φ_n is a standard 3SAT instance. For every n , the formula Φ_n is a syntactically valid 3-CNF formula, and its encoding length satisfies | enc (Φ_n)|= poly (n) . bf Uniform constructibility. The map nmapsto enc (Φ_n) is computable in time poly (n) (indeed logspace/uniform, if desired), so {Φ_n} forms an explicit uniform family of inputs to 3SAT . bf Same encoding regime for SPDP objects. Let C be the uniform compiler/encoding map fixed in Theorem (or Theorem ). Define the NP-side SPDP object by \[ q_n := C (Φ_n). \] Then q_n is exactly the SPDP polynomial associated to the standard 3SAT input Φ_n under the same compilation/feature-scheme/canonical-window regime used on the P-side. bf NP-complete witness role. Consequently, any claimed separation that proves a rank lower bound for the family {q_n} (e.g.\ Γ_ κ,ell (q_n) ≥ n^ Ω( log n) for κ,ell =Θ( log n) ) is a rank lower bound for a uniform family of standard 3SAT instances under the paper's fixed encoding.
title: NP-completeness bookkeeping for the witness family

label: thm:godmove-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:godmove-formal}
Fix $\kappa=\lceil K\log n\rceil$ and $\ell=\lceil \beta\log n\rceil$ for constants $K,\beta>0$.

Assume for contradiction that $P=NP$. Then for the verifier-restricted machine $M'$
deciding 3SAT, the compiled polynomial satisfies

\noindent\textbf{Guard (no extraction from $\Phi$ alone).}
The extraction operator $T_{\Phi}$ is applied only to the \emph{compiled machine-exact} polynomial
$P_{M',n}$ produced by the assumed polytime decider $M'$ on input length $n$; it is not an
operator that outputs $Q^{\times}_{\Phi}$ from $\Phi$ in isolation.

The compiled polynomial satisfies
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',n}) \le n^{O(1)}
\]
by the P-side width$\Rightarrow$rank upper bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:width-to-rank-formal}).

By the coupled extraction map (Lemma~\ref{lem:additive-separability}),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}\big)
\ \le\ \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',n})
\ \le\ n^{O(1)}.
\]

On the other hand, by the coefficient-space identity minor for coupled sheets
(Theorem~\ref{thm:np-identity-minor-formal}, which applies to $Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}$),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}\big)\ \ge\ n^{\Theta(\log n)},
\]
a contradiction for large $n$. Hence $P\neq NP$.
statement_text: Fix κ=lceil K log nrceil and ell =lceil β log nrceil for constants K,β>0 . Assume for contradiction that P=NP . Then for the verifier-restricted machine M' deciding 3SAT, the compiled polynomial satisfies bf Guard (no extraction from Φ alone). The extraction operator T_ Φ is applied only to the compiled machine-exact polynomial P_ M',n produced by the assumed polytime decider M' on input length n ; it is not an operator that outputs Q^ × _ Φ from Φ in isolation. The compiled polynomial satisfies \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) \] by the P-side width ⇒ rank upper bound (Theorem ). By the coupled extraction map (Lemma ), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) \ ≤ \ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M',n ) \ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . \] On the other hand, by the coefficient-space identity minor for coupled sheets (Theorem , which applies to Q^ × _ Φ_n ), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n )\ ≥ \ n^ Θ( log n) , \] a contradiction for large n . Hence P ≠ NP .
title: Global God-Move ⇒ P ≠ NP (coupled-sheet form)

label: thm:uniform-extraction-verifier-sos
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:uniform-extraction-verifier-sos}
There exists a deterministic, instance-uniform map
\[
\mathcal{E} : (\Phi, M) \longmapsto (Q^{\times}_\Phi, P_{M,n})
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{P-side compilation.} For any polytime decider $M$ of 3SAT, the compiler produces $P_{M,n}$ with
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M,n}) \leq n^{O(1)}, \quad \kappa, \ell = \Theta(\log n).
\]

\item \textbf{Verifier extraction.} For each 3SAT instance $\Phi$ with $n$ variables and $m$ clauses, the map extracts $Q^{\times}_\Phi$ (the coupled clause-gadget SoS polynomial, Definition~\ref{def:Qphi-times}) such that
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_\Phi) \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M,n}) \leq n^{O(1)}.
\]

\item \textbf{Block-locality.} The extraction $T_\Phi : P_{M,n} \mapsto Q^{\times}_\Phi$ decomposes as a finite composition of block-local operations (restriction, projection, affine relabeling, basis change), each operating within radius $O(1)$ blocks.

\item \textbf{NP-side lower bound.} For sufficiently hard 3SAT instances $\Phi_n$ (derived from the permanent via Valiant--Vazirani reduction or direct construction),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}) \geq n^{\Theta(\log n)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: There exists a deterministic, instance-uniform map \[ E : (Φ, M) longmapsto (Q^ × _Φ, P_ M,n ) \] with the following properties: bf P-side compilation. For any polytime decider M of 3SAT, the compiler produces P_ M,n with \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) , quad κ, ell = Θ( log n). \] bf Verifier extraction. For each 3SAT instance Φ with n variables and m clauses, the map extracts Q^ × _Φ (the coupled clause-gadget SoS polynomial, Definition ) such that \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _Φ) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] bf Block-locality. The extraction T_Φ : P_ M,n mapsto Q^ × _Φ decomposes as a finite composition of block-local operations (restriction, projection, affine relabeling, basis change), each operating within radius O(1) blocks. bf NP-side lower bound. For sufficiently hard 3SAT instances Φ_n (derived from the permanent via Valiant--Vazirani reduction or direct construction), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) . \]
title: Uniform Block-Local Extraction of the Verifier SoS

label: lem:sheet-extract
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:sheet-extract}
In the instrumented compilation, the coupled verifier sheet occupies disjoint blocks tagged \textsf{VER}.
Selecting rows whose derivatives touch only \textsf{VER} variables (including coupling selectors $z$) and projecting to columns supported on \textsf{VER} blocks yields a block-supported submatrix.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:submatrix}, this projection cannot increase rank, and after the instance-uniform affine relabeling of literal pads, the extracted polynomial equals $Q^{\times}_\Phi$ exactly.
statement_text: In the instrumented compilation, the coupled verifier sheet occupies disjoint blocks tagged sf VER . Selecting rows whose derivatives touch only sf VER variables (including coupling selectors z ) and projecting to columns supported on sf VER blocks yields a block-supported submatrix. By Lemma , this projection cannot increase rank, and after the instance-uniform affine relabeling of literal pads, the extracted polynomial equals Q^ × _Φ exactly.

label: thm:oracle-invariance
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:oracle-invariance}
Let $p \in \mathbb{F}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be any polynomial and $\kappa,\ell \geq 0$. For any oracle $O \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ (or any Turing-relativized model), define the ``relativized'' SPDP rank $\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}^O(p)$ to be the rank of the same shifted partial-derivative matrix $M_{\kappa,\ell}(p)$ computed over $\mathbb{F}$ (i.e., the definition does not refer to oracle answers). Then
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}^O(p) = \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p) \quad\text{for all } O.
\]
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... ,x_n] be any polynomial and κ,ell ≥ 0 . For any oracle O ⊆ {0,1}^* (or any Turing-relativized model), define the ``relativized'' SPDP rank Γ_ κ,ell ^O(p) to be the rank of the same shifted partial-derivative matrix M_ κ,ell (p) computed over F (i.e., the definition does not refer to oracle answers). Then \[ Γ_ κ,ell ^O(p) = Γ_ κ,ell (p) quad for all O. \]

\]

label: def:compiler-equivalence-moves
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_text: Fix the compiler template family Comp (radius-- 1 blocks, diagonal basis, and Π^+ ). We write p equiv _ comp p' (or p p' ) if p' is obtained from p by a finite sequence of the following moves (and their inverses where applicable): bf (E1) Block-local invertible changes. Blockwise invertible linear changes of variables within blocks, and block-local variable renamings (permutations) consistent with the block partition B . bf (E2) Tag specialization / administrative normalization. Deterministic specialization, coalescing, or elimination of administrative tags introduced by the compiler front-end, in a way that preserves the Boolean semantics of the compiled instance. bf (E3) Deletion of identically-zero components (only). Removal of constraints/cells whose compiled polynomial is identically 0 after deterministic normalization. No other notion of ``semantically inactive'' is permitted. bf (E4) Commutation / reordering of independent cells. Reordering (permutation) of commuting factors, independent cells, or disjoint local constraints, including deterministic tie-breaking conventions. bf (E6) Positive-cone closure Π^+ . Applying the canonical ``positive-cone'' linear map Π^+ used in the final canonicalization layer. By definition of the compiler, Π^+ is chosen block-local and invertible on each block, hence is a special case of (E1) (recorded separately because it is used repeatedly in the narrative).
title: Compiler equivalence moves

statement_tex:
\label{lem:hoeffding-bernstein}

\[

\]

statement_tex:
\label{def:spdp-appg}
Let $p\in\Bbb F[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ and let $\mathcal B=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}$ be a partition of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ into blocks of size $\le b=O(1)$.
Fix $\kappa,\ell\in\Bbb N$. Rows are indexed by pairs $(\tau,u)$ with multi-index $\tau\in\Bbb N^N$ of weight $|\tau|=\kappa$ whose block support
$\,\mathrm{supp}_{\mathcal B}(\tau):=\{j:\exists i\in B_j,\ \tau_i>0\}$ satisfies $|\mathrm{supp}_{\mathcal B}(\tau)|\le \kappa$, and $u$ a monomial of degree $\le \ell$.
Columns are monomials $x^\beta$ with $\deg x^\beta \le \deg(p)-\kappa+\ell$ (empty set if negative).
Define
\[
M^{\mathcal B}_{\kappa,\ell}(p)\big[(\tau,u),x^\beta\big]
:= \mathrm{coeff}_{x^\beta}\!\big(u\cdot \partial^\tau p\big),
\qquad
\Gamma^{\mathcal B}_{\kappa,\ell}(p):=\mathrm{rank}_\Bbb F\big(M^{\mathcal B}_{\kappa,\ell}(p)\big).
\]
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and let B={B_1, ... ,B_m} be a partition of {1, ... ,N} into blocks of size ≤ b=O(1) . Fix κ,ell ∈ Bbb N . Rows are indexed by pairs (τ,u) with multi-index τ ∈ Bbb N^N of weight |τ|=κ whose block support supp _ B (τ):={j: ∃ i ∈ B_j,\ τ_i>0} satisfies | supp _ B (τ)| ≤ κ , and u a monomial of degree ≤ ell . Columns are monomials x^β with deg x^β ≤ deg (p)-κ+ell (empty set if negative). Define \[ M^ B _ κ,ell (p) [(τ,u),x^β ] := coeff _ x^β (u · partial ^τ p ), qquad Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p):= rank _Bbb F (M^ B _ κ,ell (p) ). \]

label: lem:isolator
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:isolator}
Let $N$ be the number of clause--blocks/variable--pads in $Q_{\Phi_n}$ and let $\kappa=\alpha\log n$ for a fixed $\alpha>0$.
There exists a family $\mathcal{H}$ of $\kappa$-perfect hash functions $h:[N]\to[\kappa]$ of size
\[
|\mathcal{H}| \;\le\; C_0\, \kappa^\kappa \log N \;=\; n^{O(1)}
\]
with the following property: for every $\kappa$-subset $S\subseteq[N]$ there is an $h\in\mathcal{H}$ that is injective on $S$.
For each $S$ choose the unique monomial $x^{\beta(S)}$ that selects, in the SoS clause gadget for $Q_{\Phi_n}$, exactly the $\kappa$ literal--wires indexed by $S$ and no others (feasible because each block exposes private pads and the gadgets are block-separable). Then the SPDP submatrix with rows indexed by the $\kappa$-tuples $S$ and columns by the $x^{\beta(S)}$ is the identity.
Consequently,
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(Q_{\Phi_n}\big)\;\ge\;\binom{N}{\kappa}
\;=\; n^{\Theta(\log n)} .
\]

statement_tex:
\label{lem:identity-minor-explicit}

expander $G_n = (V_n,E_n)$ with $|V_n| = m$ and $|E_n| = N = \Theta(n)$, and

$\{x_e : e \in E_n\}$ constructed above. For

In particular, rank M(p_n) ≥ binom N κ and there are no cancellations among the corresponding monomials.

label: def:spdp-matrix-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{def:spdp-matrix-formal}\label{def:spdp-matrix}
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and $p \in \mathbb{F}[x_1, \ldots, x_N]$ a polynomial. Fix parameters $\kappa, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$ with $\kappa \leq N$. Define:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathcal{S}_\kappa := \{S \subseteq [N] : |S| = \kappa\}$ (the set of all $\kappa$-subsets of variable indices),
\item $\mathcal{T}_\ell := \{\text{monomials } m \text{ in } x_1, \ldots, x_N : \deg m \leq \ell\}$,
\item For $S \in \mathcal{S}_\kappa$, define the partial derivative operator $\partial_S := \prod_{i \in S} \frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}$,
\item For $m \in \mathcal{T}_\ell$, define the shift operator $x^m : p \mapsto m \cdot p$.
\end{itemize}
The \textbf{SPDP matrix} $M_{\kappa,\ell}(p)$ is the matrix with rows indexed by $(S, m) \in \mathcal{S}_\kappa \times \mathcal{T}_\ell$ and columns indexed by monomials in the standard monomial basis, where the $(S,m)$-th row is the coefficient vector of $m \cdot \partial_S p$ expressed as a linear combination of monomials.

The \textbf{SPDP rank} is defined as
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p) := \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{F}} M_{\kappa,\ell}(p).
\]
statement_text: Let F be a field and p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_N] a polynomial. Fix parameters κ, ell ∈ N with κ ≤ N . Define: S _κ := {S ⊆ [N] : |S| = κ} (the set of all κ -subsets of variable indices), T _ell := { monomials m in x_1, ... , x_N : deg m ≤ ell } , For S ∈ S _κ , define the partial derivative operator partial _S := Π _ i ∈ S frac partial partial x_i , For m ∈ T _ell , define the shift operator x^m : p mapsto m · p . The bf SPDP matrix M_ κ,ell (p) is the matrix with rows indexed by (S, m) ∈ S _κ × T _ell and columns indexed by monomials in the standard monomial basis, where the (S,m) -th row is the coefficient vector of m · partial _S p expressed as a linear combination of monomials. The bf SPDP rank is defined as \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) := rank _ F M_ κ,ell (p). \]
title: SPDP matrix

label: def:cew-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{def:cew-formal}
Let $p$ be a polynomial representing a Boolean function or circuit. The \textbf{Contextual Entanglement Width} $\mathrm{CEW}(p)$ is the minimal $w$ such that after a universal restriction $\rho_\star$ (defined via deterministic switching lemma), the SPDP rank satisfies
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p \!\upharpoonright\! \rho_\star) \leq w
\]
for fixed parameters $(\kappa,\ell) = \Theta(\log n)$.

For compositional systems (e.g., layered circuits), CEW satisfies the \textbf{additive composition law}:
\[
\mathrm{CEW}(f \circ g) \leq \mathrm{CEW}(f) + \mathrm{CEW}(g) + O(1),
\]
where the $O(1)$ accounts for interface gadgets.
statement_text: Let p be a polynomial representing a Boolean function or circuit. The bf Contextual Entanglement Width CEW (p) is the minimal w such that after a universal restriction ρ_star (defined via deterministic switching lemma), the SPDP rank satisfies \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p upharpoonright ρ_star ) ≤ w \] for fixed parameters (κ,ell ) = Θ( log n) . For compositional systems (e.g., layered circuits), CEW satisfies the bf additive composition law : \[ CEW (f ∘ g) ≤ CEW (f) + CEW (g) + O(1), \] where the O(1) accounts for interface gadgets.
title: CEW and additive composition law

label: def:batcher-network
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_text: The bf Batcher sorting network for N inputs is a fixed comparison network defined recursively: bf Base case : For N = 1 , the network is trivial (identity). bf Recursive case : For N > 1 , split into two halves of size lceil N/2 rceil and lfloor N/2 rfloor , recursively sort each half, then merge using the odd--even merge gadget. The network has: bf Depth : D(N) = O( log ^2 N) , bf Width : Constant (each comparison gate operates on exactly 2 wires), bf Size : S(N) = O(N log ^2 N) comparisons.
title: Batcher odd--even merge network

statement_tex:

label: lem:basis-Piplus-invariance
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:basis-Piplus-invariance}\label{lem:affine-map-invariance}
Let $p \in \Bbb F[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ and fix $\kappa,\ell$.
Suppose a block-local change of variables $x \mapsto Ax+b$ acts on each block by an
invertible linear map $A$ (so $\det A \neq 0$ on each block), and let $\Pi^+$ denote the
fixed positive-cone map used in the compilation (acting block-locally and invertibly on the
column space induced by the local basis).
Then left/right multiplication of $M_{\kappa,\ell}(p)$ by the corresponding
block-diagonal change-of-basis matrices is invertible, hence
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p) \;=\; \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(p\circ(Ax+b)\big) \;=\; \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(\Pi^+[p]\big).
\]
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and fix κ,ell . Suppose a block-local change of variables x mapsto Ax+b acts on each block by an invertible linear map A (so det A ≠ 0 on each block), and let Π^+ denote the fixed positive-cone map used in the compilation (acting block-locally and invertibly on the column space induced by the local basis). Then left/right multiplication of M_ κ,ell (p) by the corresponding block-diagonal change-of-basis matrices is invertible, hence \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) = Γ_ κ,ell (p ∘ (Ax+b) ) = Γ_ κ,ell (Π^+[p] ). \]
title: Block-local affine/basis invariance and Π^+

label: lem:private-linear-unique

statement_tex:
\label{lem:private-linear-unique}
For each witness block $B_i$, the local gadget factor has the form
\[
G_i(\ell_i, y_i) = \ell_i + H_i(y_i),
\]

statement_text: For each witness block B_i , the local gadget factor has the form \[ G_i(ell _i, y_i) = ell _i + H_i(y_i), \] where y_i are the remaining variables of the block and H_i does not contain ell _i . label: lem:no-cross-interference

statement_tex:

paper_title: Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs
statement_text: A quantum interactive oracle proof (quantum IOP) system, parameterized by functions q(n) and l(n): Z _+ → Z _+ , consists of a quantum verifier tt V satisfying the following conditions for any input of size n : The verifier interacts with the prover for at most poly (n) rounds. In each round, the prover sends a quantum message to the verifier. The message length may vary between rounds. In each round, the verifier: applies a quantum circuit to his private qubits and to portions of the prover’s message, including qubits received in the current round as well as those retained from previous rounds, stores part of the prover’s message registers for use in later rounds. After each interaction, the verifier returns the remainder of the prover's quantum message (i.e., the part not stored) and may optionally send back part of their own private quantum register. At the end of the protocol, the verifier outputs a single decision bit. The main complexity parameters are: The bf query complexity q(n) : the total number of qubits from the prover's messages accessed by the verifier across all rounds. The bf communication complexity l(n) : the total number of qubits in the prover's messages across all rounds. We refer to such a system as a quantum IOP if q(n) is bounded by a constant. In the formal Definition , we refer to this as the general quantum IOP to distinguish it from the restricted and strong variants. We define the following variants of a quantum IOP : A system is called a restricted quantum IOP if the private register sent back by the verifier is required to be classical . It is called a strong quantum IOP if the verifier must return the entire prover's message register in each round (i.e., does not store any part of the message).
title: Quantum IOP systems; informal version of Definition

paper_title: Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs
statement_tex:
A \emph{quantum interactive oracle proof} (quantum IOP) system for a language $\mathcal{L}$ with completeness $c: \mathbb{Z}_+ \rightarrow [0,1]$ and soundness $s: \mathbb{Z}_+ \rightarrow [0,1]$ satisfies the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item For any \emph{YES-instance} of size $n$, 
There exists a polynomial-time prover such that
the verifier accepts with probability at least $c(n)$.
\item For any \emph{NO-instance} of size $n$, for all provers, the verifier accepts with probability at most $s(n)$.
\end{itemize}
The \emph{completeness-soundness gap} of the system is defined as $c(n) - s(n)$.
statement_text: A quantum interactive oracle proof (quantum IOP) system for a language L with completeness c: Z _+ → [0,1] and soundness s: Z _+ → [0,1] satisfies the following: For any YES-instance of size n , There exists a polynomial-time prover such that the verifier accepts with probability at least c(n) . For any NO-instance of size n , for all provers, the verifier accepts with probability at most s(n) . The completeness-soundness gap of the system is defined as c(n) - s(n) .
title: Quantum IOP systems for a promise problem, informal version of Definition

\label{thm:ourqubits}
Let $n, d \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, $\delta \in (0, 1)$, and $\sigma \in \mathbb{C}^d \otimes \mathbb{C}^d$. 
Let $\mu_1$ be a distribution over ${0,1}^n$. Sample $(b, a) \sim \mu_1$, then sample $r$ uniformly at random from ${0,1}^n$. Define $\mu_2$ as the distribution of $(b + r, a)$.
Let $\rho(\pm X(a)Z(b)) = \pm X(a)Z(b)$. 
Let $f_X, f_Z: \{0,1\}^n \to U(\mathbb{C}^d)$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item $f_X(a)^2 = f_Z(b)^2 = I$, $f_X(a)^\dagger = f_X(a)$, $f_Z(b)^\dagger = f_Z(b)$ for all $a,b\in \{0,1\}^n$,
\item $f_X(a)f_X(b) = f_X(a + b)$, $f_Z(a)f_Z(b) = f_Z(a + b)$, for all $a,b\in \{0,1\}^n$,
\item $\mathbb{E}_{(b,a) \sim \mu_1} \|f_Z(b)f_X(a) - (-1)^{a \cdot b} f_X(a)f_Z(b)\|_\sigma^2 \leq \delta$,
\item $\mathbb{E}_{(b,a) \sim \mu_2} \|f_Z(b)f_X(a) - (-1)^{a \cdot b} f_X(a)f_Z(b)\|_\sigma^2 \leq \delta$,

\[
\mathbb{E}_{(b,a) \sim \mu_1} \|f_X(a)f_Z(b) - V^\dagger g(X(a)Z(b)) V\|_\sigma^2 \leq \Theta(\delta)\;.
\]

paper_title: Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs
statement_text: Let m ∈ Z _+ be the total number of messages, and let h = lfloor m/2 + 1 rfloor . An m -message quantum interactive oracle proof system is defined by a tuple of quantum algorithms with queries tt V = (tt V _1, tt V _2, ... , tt V _h) . The tuple V _x = ( V _ x,1 , ... , V _ x,h ) represents the quantum channels with queries produced by the algorithm tt V _i on input x . Each quantum channel V _ x,i , for i ∈ [h] , acts on a (quantum) witness register ( W _ i-1 , W '_ i-1 ) and (quantum) reference register R , and it returns a message register ( J _i, M _i) where J _i is classical and M _i quantum, together with private registers ( W '_ i , R ) . For the present definition the registers W '_ i are not needed and can be assumed to be trivial without loss of generality. We include them for future consistency. Summarizing, the verifier channel V _ x,i acts on the registers as follows: (( W _ i-1 , W '_ i-1 ), R ) longrightarrow (( M _ i , J _ i ), ( W '_ i , R ) ) . If m is odd, define the index set I = {0, ... , h-1} ; if m is even, let I = {1, ... , h-1} . A prover strategy is specified by a collection of quantum channels { P _i}_ i ∈ I and a quantum register P , where each P _i acts on the registers as follows: \[ (( M _i, J _i), P ) longrightarrow ( W _i, P ). \] Let the first (classical) bit of the register J _ h in the output of V _ x,h represent the verifier's final decision to accept or reject. Let ω( V _x) denote the value of the interactive game defined by V _x . That is, ω( V _x) is the maximum acceptance probability of V _x over all possible prover strategies { P _i}_ i ∈ I . The following properties must be satisfied: normal Consistent: Unless otherwise specified, we initialize W _i , W '_i , R , M _i to ket 0 , whereas P may be initialized in an arbitrary quantum state. The register J _i is initialized to the all-zero string. normal Efficient: Each verifier's algorithm tt V _i must be implementable in polynomial time and have polynomial time complexity as defined in Definition .
title: Quantum interactive proof systems

label: def:gqiop
paper_title: Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs
statement_tex:
\label{def:gqiop}
Let $m \in \mathbb{Z}_+$. 
An $m$-message general quantum interactive oracle proof system consists of an $m$-message quantum interactive proof system $\texttt{V}$ satisfying the same structure as in Definition~\ref{def:qip}, but with the following modifications to the register structure.

As before, in the $i$th round, for $i\in[h]$ where  $h = \lfloor m/2 + 1 \rfloor$, the verifier receives the quantum message register $\mathsf{W}_{i-1}$ from the prover. 
In addition, the verifier has in their possession  a register $\mathsf{W}'_{i-1}$ that stores (parts of) previously received messages from the prover, and a register $\mathsf{R}$ that is their private (reference) register. 
The register  $\mathsf{W}'_{i-1}$ decomposes as 
\[\mathsf{W}'_{i-1}=(\mathsf{W}'_{0,i-1},\mathsf{W}'_{1,i-1}, \ldots, \mathsf{W}'_{i-2,i-1})\;,\] where $\mathsf{W}'_{j,i-1}$ denotes the part of the prover's $j$th message (i.e., $\mathsf{W}_{j}$) that has so far not been sent back to the prover. 

For each $\mathsf{W}'_{j,i-1}$, the verifier sends a subregister $\mathsf{N}_{j,i}$ to the prover in the $i$th round, and keeps the remaining part as $\mathsf{W}'_{j,i}$. 
In addition, the verifier produces a quantum message register $\mathsf{M}'_i$ and a classical message register $\mathsf{J}_i$ . The verifier sends back the total message register $(\mathsf{M}_i, \mathsf{J}_i)$ to the prover, where
\[\mathsf{M}_i =
(\mathsf{M}'_i,(\mathsf{N}_{0,i},\mathsf{N}_{1,i}, \ldots, \mathsf{N}_{i-1,i})).\] 
 

Finally, we define the following resource bounds of the protocol:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Proof length:} The verifier $V$ has proof length $l : \mathbb{Z}_+ \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_+$ if
    \[
    l(n) \geq \sum_{i \in [n]} l_i(n),
    \]
    where $l_i(n)$ is the proof length of $\texttt{V}_i$.

    \item \textbf{Query complexity:} The verifier $V$ has query complexity $q : \mathbb{Z}_+ \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_+$ if
    \[
    q(n) \geq \sum_{i \in [n]} q_i(n),
    \]
    where $q_i(n)$ is the query complexity of $\texttt{V}_i$.
\end{itemize}
statement_text: Let m ∈ Z _+ . An m -message general quantum interactive oracle proof system consists of an m -message quantum interactive proof system tt V satisfying the same structure as in Definition , but with the following modifications to the register structure. As before, in the i th round, for i ∈ [h] where h = lfloor m/2 + 1 rfloor , the verifier receives the quantum message register W _ i-1 from the prover. In addition, the verifier has in their possession a register W '_ i-1 that stores (parts of) previously received messages from the prover, and a register R that is their private (reference) register. The register W '_ i-1 decomposes as \[ W '_ i-1 =( W '_ 0,i-1 , W '_ 1,i-1 , ... , W '_ i-2,i-1 ) ,\] where W '_ j,i-1 denotes the part of the prover's j th message (i.e., W _ j ) that has so far not been sent back to the prover. For each W '_ j,i-1 , the verifier sends a subregister N _ j,i to the prover in the i th round, and keeps the remaining part as W '_ j,i . In addition, the verifier produces a quantum message register M '_i and a classical message register J _i . The verifier sends back the total message register ( M _i, J _i) to the prover, where \[ M _i = ( M '_i,( N _ 0,i , N _ 1,i , ... , N _ i-1,i )).\] Finally, we define the following resource bounds of the protocol: bf Proof length: The verifier V has proof length l : Z _+ → Z _+ if \[ l(n) ≥ Σ _ i ∈ [n] l_i(n), \] where l_i(n) is the proof length of tt V _i . bf Query complexity: The verifier V has query complexity q : Z _+ → Z _+ if \[ q(n) ≥ Σ _ i ∈ [n] q_i(n), \] where q_i(n) is the query complexity of tt V _i .

statement_tex:
\label{def:qpcp_tlp_v}
Under the same setup assumptions as in Definition~\ref{def:qpcp_tlp_hp}, the verifier performs the following actions:
\begin{itemize}
\item For each $i \in [N]$, the verifier samples $l_i \in [m]$ independently and uniformly at random.

\item For each $i \in [m]$, let $H_i = \left(C_i^\dagger (\ketbra{0}{0})^{\otimes 5} C_i\right) \otimes I$. For $j \in [5]$, define
\[
O_{i,j} = \left(C_i^\dagger \cdot (I^{\otimes j-1} \otimes Z \otimes I^{\otimes (5-j)}) \cdot C_i \right) \otimes I,
\]
and let
\[
O_{i,j} = (-1)^{d_{i,j}} X(a_{i,j}) Z(b_{i,j}) Y(c_{i,j})
\]
be its Pauli representation as in Lemma~\ref{lem:clifford_pauli}.

\item For each $i \in [N]$, the verifier measures the register
\[
\mathsf{R'}_i = (\mathsf{R'}_{(i-1)*n + 1}, \ldots, \mathsf{R'}_{(i-1)*n + n})
\]
using the observables $O_{l_i, j}$ for $j = 1$ to $5$, and stores the measurement outcomes in $r_{i, j}$.

\item The verifier constructs the Boolean circuit:
\[
C(x) = \bigoplus_{i \in [N]} \Big(1 \oplus \bigvee_{j \in [5]} \big(r_{l_i,j} \oplus a_{l_i,j} x_{0,i} \oplus b_{l_i,j} x_{1,i} \oplus c_{l_i,j} x_{1,i} \oplus c_{l_i,j} x_{0,i} \big) \Big),
\]
where $x = \left(x_{k, i, j}\right)_{k \in \{0, 1\}, i \in [N], j \in [n]}$.

\item The verifier runs the interactive oracle commitment protocol in Definition~\ref{def:ioc} with the circuit $C $ and $\varepsilon = 0.001$.

\item The verifier accepts if and only if the interactive oracle commitment accepts and its output is $0$.
\end{itemize}

label: thm:3c_code
paper_title: Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs
statement_tex:
\label{thm:3c_code}
The family of Hadamard codes $\{C_k\}$ satisfies the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The code has rate $r=1/\exp(k)$ and relative distance $d=\Theta(1)$.
    \item It is a linear code with generator matrix $G_k \in \mathbb{F}_2^{n(k) \times k}$, where $n(k)$ denotes the length of the encoded message as a function of the message length $k$.
    \item The code admits deterministic encoding and decoding algorithms, denoted by $\texttt{E}$ and $\texttt{D}$ respectively.
\end{enumerate}

Furthermore, there exists $\varepsilon \in (0, 0.001)$, $\kappa, \kappa' \in (0, 1)$, and $q_{\texttt{L}}, q_{\texttt{S}} \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textnormal{Local Testing:}  
For all $n$, the code $C_n$ is $\kappa$-locally testable with query complexity $q_{\texttt{L}}$. That is, there exists a non-adaptive probabilistic polynomial-time oracle machine $\texttt{L}$ with query complexity $q_{\texttt{L}}$, such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $k \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ and $x \in \mathbb{F}_2^k$,
        \[
    \Pr[\texttt{L}^{\texttt{E}(x)}(1^k) = 1] = 1.
        \]
        \item For any $k \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ and $w \in \mathbb{F}_2^{n(k)}$,
        \[
        \Pr[\texttt{L}^w(1^k) = 1] \leq 1 - \kappa \cdot \mathrm{dist}(w, C_n).
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
    
\item \textnormal{Self-Correction:}  
For all $n$, the code $C_n$ is self-correctable with query complexity $q_{\texttt{S}}$. There exists a non-adaptive probabilistic polynomial-time oracle machine $\texttt{S}$ with query complexity $q_{\texttt{S}}$ such that for any $k \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ and any $w \in \mathbb{F}_2^{n(k)}$ satisfying
    \[
    \mathrm{dist}(w, C_n) < \kappa' \cdot d / 2,
    \]
    it holds for all $p \in [n(k)]$ that
    \[
    \Pr[\texttt{S}^w(1^k, p) = (\texttt{E} \circ \texttt{D}(w))_p] \geq 1 - \varepsilon.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: The family of Hadamard codes {C_k} satisfies the following properties: The code has rate r=1/exp (k) and relative distance d=Θ(1) . It is a linear code with generator matrix G_k ∈ F _2^ n(k) × k , where n(k) denotes the length of the encoded message as a function of the message length k . The code admits deterministic encoding and decoding algorithms, denoted by tt E and tt D respectively. Furthermore, there exists ε ∈ (0, 0.001) , κ, κ' ∈ (0, 1) , and q_ tt L , q_ tt S ∈ Z _+ such that: normal Local Testing: For all n , the code C_n is κ -locally testable with query complexity q_ tt L . That is, there exists a non-adaptive probabilistic polynomial-time oracle machine tt L with query complexity q_ tt L , such that: For any k ∈ Z _+ and x ∈ F _2^k , \[ Pr [tt L ^ tt E (x) (1^k) = 1] = 1. \] For any k ∈ Z _+ and w ∈ F _2^ n(k) , \[ Pr [tt L ^w(1^k) = 1] ≤ 1 - κ · dist (w, C_n). \] normal Self-Correction: For all n , the code C_n is self-correctable with query complexity q_ tt S . There exists a non-adaptive probabilistic polynomial-time oracle machine tt S with query complexity q_ tt S such that for any k ∈ Z _+ and any w ∈ F _2^ n(k) satisfying \[ dist (w, C_n) < κ' · d / 2, \] it holds for all p ∈ [n(k)] that \[ Pr [tt S ^w(1^k, p) = (tt E ∘ tt D (w))_p] ≥ 1 - ε. \]

statement_tex:
\label{def:mqdef}
Let $p, q$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:clifford_ham}, and let $s, N$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:c_ham_amp}. 
Let $H = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i \in [m]} H_i \in \mathbb{C}^{2^n} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{2^n}$ be a $5$-local Clifford Hamiltonian, where $m = \mathrm{poly}(n)$, and either $\lambda_{\min}(H) \leq 2^{-p(n)}$ or $\lambda_{\min}(H) \geq 1/q(n)$. 

For each $i \in [m]$, let
\begin{align*}
H_i =&~ \left(C_i^\dagger (\ketbra{0}{0})^{\otimes 5} C_i \right) \otimes I,\\
O_{i,j} =&~ \left(C_i^\dagger (I^{\otimes (j-1)} \otimes Z \otimes I^{\otimes (5-j)}) C_i\right) \otimes I.    \end{align*}
Each $O_{i,j}$ admits a Pauli representation
\[
O_{i,j} = (-1)^{d_{i,j}} X(a_{i,j}) Z(b_{i,j}) Y(c_{i,j}),
\]
as described in Lemma~\ref{lem:clifford_pauli}.
Let $t \in \mathbb{F}_2^{5N}$ and $l \in [m]^N$. Define
\[
O(t, l) = \bigotimes_{i \in [N]} \prod_{j \in [5]} O_{l_i, j}^{t_{i, j}},
\]
which has Pauli representation:
\[
O(t, l) = (-1)^{d(t, l)} X(a(t, l)) Z(b(t, l)) Y(c(t, l)).
\]
Define the measurement distributions used in the test as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item Sample $ t \in_R \mathbb{F}_2^{5N}$, $r\in_R \mathbb{F}_2^{Nn}$, and $l_i \in_R [m]$ for each $i \in [N]$.
\item Define $\mu_1$ as the distribution over the pair $(b(t, l) + c(t, l), a(t, l) + c(t, l))$.
\item Define $\mu_2$ as the distribution over the pair $(b(t, l) + c(t, l) + r, a(t, l) + c(t, l))$.
\end{itemize}

Each O_ i,j admits a Pauli representation \[ O_ i,j = (-1)^ d_ i,j X(a_ i,j ) Z(b_ i,j ) Y(c_ i,j ), \] as described in Lemma . Let t ∈ F _2^ 5N and l ∈ [m]^N . Define \[ O(t, l) = otimes_ i ∈ [N] Π _ j ∈ [5] O_ l_i, j ^ t_ i, j , \] which has Pauli representation: \[ O(t, l) = (-1)^ d(t, l) X(a(t, l)) Z(b(t, l)) Y(c(t, l)). \] Define the measurement distributions used in the test as follows: Sample t ∈ _R F _2^ 5N , r ∈ _R F _2^ Nn , and l_i ∈ _R [m] for each i ∈ [N] . Define μ_1 as the distribution over the pair (b(t, l) + c(t, l), a(t, l) + c(t, l)) . Define μ_2 as the distribution over the pair (b(t, l) + c(t, l) + r, a(t, l) + c(t, l)) .

statement_tex:
\label{thm:mqt}
Let $ \texttt{V}$ be the verifier defined in Definition \ref{def:mqt:verifier}. Then, 

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textnormal{Completeness:} $ \texttt{V}$ accepts the prover in Definition \ref{def:mqt:honest_prover}  with probability $1$.
\item \textnormal{Soundness:} Let $ \texttt{P}$ be the prover defined in Definition \ref{def:mqt:canonical_prover}.  Let $ O'_{1}(\cdot),O'_{2}(\cdot)$ be defined as in Definition \ref{def:hermitian_prover}. 
If $ \texttt{V}$ accepts $ \texttt{P}$ with probability greater than $ 1- \delta$, then approximate anti-commuting / commuting relationships of $ O'_{1}(a),O'_{2}(b)$ hold under the state 
$$\rho ={U}_{0\rightarrow 2}\ket{000}_{\mathsf{PRD}}\bra{000}_{\mathsf{PRD}}{U}_{0\rightarrow 2}^\dagger. $$
More specifically,
$$\E_{(a,b)\sim \mu_1}\| O'_{1}(a)O'_{2}(b)-(-1)^{a\cdot b}O'_{2}(b)O'_{1}(a)\|^2_\rho =  \Theta(\delta),$$
and 
$$\E_{(a,b)\sim \mu_2}\| O'_{1}(a)O'_{2}(b)-(-1)^{a\cdot b}O'_{2}(b)O'_{1}(a)\|^2_\rho =  \Theta(\delta).$$
\end{enumerate}

[Properties of the prover's hermitian forms]
Let $O'_{q'}(a)$ for $q'\in [2], a\in \F_2^k$ be as in Definition \ref{def:hermitian_prover}. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item For $q'\in [2], a\in \F_2^k$,  $$O'_{q'}(a) = (O'_{q'}(a))^\dagger,$$
\item For $q'\in [2], a\in \F_2^k$,  $$(O'_{q'}(a))^2 = I,$$
\item For $q'\in [2], a,b\in \F_2^k$,   $$[O'_{q'}(a), O'_{q'}(b)]=0,$$
\item For $q'\in [2], a,b\in \F_2^k$,   $$O'_{q'}(a)\cdot O'_{q'}(b)=O'_{q'}(a\oplus b).$$
\end{enumerate}

label: Def: translation
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Def: translation}
Fix formulas $D,N \in \mathcal{L}_!$ and define the translation functions $(\cdot)^t:\mathcal{L}_! \to \mathcal{L}_!$ and $(\cdot)^s: \mathcal{L}_! \to \mathcal{L}_!$ simultaneously and inductively as follows:\medskip

\noindent $\circ$ Translation $(\cdot)^t$:
\begin{itemize}
\item 
$p^t:=p$ \quad where $p$ is an atom
\item 
$1^t:=1$ \qquad $0^t:=D$ \qquad $\top^t:=\top$ \qquad $\bot^t:=\bot$
\item 
$(A \circ B)^t:=A^t \circ B^t$  for $\circ \in \{\wedge, \vee, *\}$
\item 
$(A \to B)^t:=(A^t \to B^t) \wedge (B^s \to A^s)$
\item 
$(!A)^t:=!A^t$ 
\end{itemize}

\noindent $\circ$ Translation $(\cdot)^s$:
\begin{itemize}
\item 

$p^s:= N$ \quad where $p$ is an atom 
\item 
$1^s:= D$ \qquad $0^s:= 1$ \qquad $\top^s:= \bot$ \qquad $\bot^s:= \top$ 
\item 
$(A \wedge B)^s:= A^s \vee B^s$ \qquad $(A \vee B)^s:= A^s \wedge B^s$
\item
$(A * B)^s:= (A^t \to B^s) \wedge (B^t \to A^s)$ 
\item 
$(A \to B)^s:= A^t \st B^s$ \qquad $(!A)^s:= !A^t \to D$
\end{itemize}
For any $\mathcal{L} \in \{\mathcal{L}_u, \mathcal{L}_b\}$, if $N, D \in \mathcal{L}$, the translations can be defined analogously over $\mathcal{L}$ by replacing $\mathcal{L}_!$ with $\mathcal{L}$ and restricting to formulas in $\mathcal{L}$.
statement_text: Fix formulas D,N ∈ L _! and define the translation functions ( · )^t: L _! → L _! and ( · )^s: L _! → L _! simultaneously and inductively as follows: ∘ Translation ( · )^t : p^t:=p quad where p is an atom 1^t:=1 qquad 0^t:=D qquad top ^t:=top qquad bot ^t:=bot (A ∘ B)^t:=A^t ∘ B^t for ∘ ∈ {wedge , vee , *} (A → B)^t:=(A^t → B^t) wedge (B^s → A^s) (!A)^t:=!A^t ∘ Translation ( · )^s : p^s:= N quad where p is an atom 1^s:= D qquad 0^s:= 1 qquad top ^s:= bot qquad bot ^s:= top (A wedge B)^s:= A^s vee B^s qquad (A vee B)^s:= A^s wedge B^s (A * B)^s:= (A^t → B^s) wedge (B^t → A^s) (A → B)^s:= A^t * B^s qquad (!A)^s:= !A^t → D For any L ∈ { L _u, L _b} , if N, D ∈ L , the translations can be defined analogously over L by replacing L _! with L and restricting to formulas in L .

label: Def: Conservative formulas
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define the following sets of L _! -formulas simultaneously: ( Fully conservative ) B:= p mid 1 mid top mid B wedge B mid B vee B mid C → B , where p is an atom and C is conservative ( Conservative ) C := bot mid B mid C wedge C mid C vee C mid C * C mid !C , where B is fully conservative. A formula in the languages L _b is called fully conservative or conservative if it is so in the extended language L _! .

label: Exam: conservative
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Exam: conservative}
The formulas $p \wedge q$, $p \vee q$, and $p \to q$, where $p$ and $q$ are atoms, are all fully conservative, while $p * q$ and $!p$ are conservative but not fully conservative. Note that $(p * q) \to r$ and $!p \to r$ are fully conservative. Moreover, $0$ is neither conservative nor fully conservative and $\bot$ is conservative but not fully conservative.
statement_text: The formulas p wedge q , p vee q , and p → q , where p and q are atoms, are all fully conservative, while p * q and !p are conservative but not fully conservative. Note that (p * q) → r and !p → r are fully conservative. Moreover, 0 is neither conservative nor fully conservative and bot is conservative but not fully conservative.

label: lem: basic conservative
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{lem: basic conservative}
Fix $D=N=\bot$ and let $B$ be a fully conservative and $C$ be a conservative $\calL_b$-formula. Then, there are $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$, $\sigma$, $\tau_1$, and $\tau_2$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
    \item 
$\BIMALL \vdash^{\pi_1} B^t \Rightarrow B$ and $\BIMALL \vdash^{\pi_2} B \Rightarrow B^t$,
\item 
$\BIMALL \vdash^{\sigma} B^s \Rightarrow \bot$,
\item 
$\BIMALL \vdash^{\tau_1} C^t \Rightarrow C$ and $\BIMALL \vdash^{\tau_2} C \Rightarrow C^t$, and
\end{itemize}
$l(\pi_i) \leq O(|B|^2)$, $ l(\sigma) \leq O(|B|)$, and $l(\tau_i) \leq O(|C|^2)$, for any $i \in \{1, 2\}$.
If $B$ and $C$ are $\calL_!$-formulas, then the same results hold when replacing $\BIMALL$ by $\BILL$.

Then, there are π_1 , π_2 , σ , τ_1 , and τ_2 such that: IMALL vdash ^ π_1 B^t ⇒ B and IMALL vdash ^ π_2 B ⇒ B^t , IMALL vdash ^ σ B^s ⇒ bot , IMALL vdash ^ τ_1 C^t ⇒ C and IMALL vdash ^ τ_2 C ⇒ C^t , and l(π_i) ≤ O(|B|^2) , l(σ) ≤ O(|B|) , and l(τ_i) ≤ O(|C|^2) , for any i ∈ {1, 2} . label: Def: Lnn
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Def: Lnn}
    An $\mathcal{L}_p$-formula $F$ is in \emph{negation normal form} (\emph{nnf}, in short), if it is defined by the following grammar:
\[
F:= p \mid \neg p \mid F_1 \wedge F_2 \mid F_1 \vee F_2
\]
Similarly, an $\calL_u$-formula $F$ is in \emph{$*$-negation normal form} (\emph{$*$-nnf}, in short), if it is defined by the grammar:
\[
F:= p \mid \neg p \mid F_1 \wedge F_2 \mid F_1 \vee F_2 \mid  F_1 \st F_2
\]
We write $\calL_{nn}$ and $\calL^*_{nn}$ for the sets of nnf- and $*$-nnf-formulas.
statement_text: An L _p -formula F is in negation normal form ( nnf , in short), if it is defined by the following grammar: \[ F:= p mid ¬ p mid F_1 wedge F_2 mid F_1 vee F_2 \] Similarly, an L _u -formula F is in * -negation normal form ( * -nnf , in short), if it is defined by the grammar: \[ F:= p mid ¬ p mid F_1 wedge F_2 mid F_1 vee F_2 mid F_1 * F_2 \] We write L _ nn and L ^*_ nn for the sets of nnf- and * -nnf-formulas.

label: Def: Calculus G
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define the single-conclusion sequent calculus G over L _u as FL_e plus the following initial sequents: ⇒ p vee ¬ p qquad p ⇒ 1 qquad ¬ p ⇒ 1 qquad 0 ⇒ p qquad 0 ⇒ ¬ p qquad 0 ⇒ 0*0 , where p is an atom. Note that these initial sequents are not meant to be used as axioms and hence using their substitutions are not allowed in G . Moreover, G includes the cut rule.

label: lem: law of excluded middle
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{lem: law of excluded middle}
For any $A \in \calL^*_{nn}$, the following sequents have tree-like $G$-proofs of size $|A|^{O(1)}$:
\[
A \Rightarrow 1 \qquad 0 \Rightarrow A \qquad \Rightarrow A \vee \neg A \qquad A \Rightarrow A * A.
\]
statement_text: For any A ∈ L ^*_ nn , the following sequents have tree-like G -proofs of size |A|^ O(1) : \[ A ⇒ 1 qquad 0 ⇒ A qquad ⇒ A vee ¬ A qquad A ⇒ A * A. \]

label: Def: Calculus LKnn
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define LK_ nn over L _ nn as the single-conclusion sequent calculus consisting of the following axioms: p ⇒ p qquad ¬ p ⇒ ¬ p qquad p, ¬ p ⇒ qquad ⇒ p vee ¬ p along with the structural rules (including cut), conjunction and disjunction rules of LJ .

label: Lem: LKnn to G
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Lem: LKnn to G}
Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where $\Delta$ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like $\LKnn$-proof $\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, there is a tree-like $G$-proof $\sigma_\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$ such that $|\sigma_\pi| \leq |\pi|^{O(1)}$.
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where Δ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like LK_ nn -proof π of Γ ⇒ Δ , there is a tree-like G -proof σ_π of Γ ⇒ Δ such that |σ_π| ≤ |π|^ O(1) .

label: Cor: LK to G
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Cor: LK to G}
Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where $\Delta$ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like $\LK$-proof $\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, there exists a tree-like $G$-proof $\sigma_\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$ such that $|\sigma_\pi| \leq |\pi|^{O(1)}$.
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where Δ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like LK -proof π of Γ ⇒ Δ , there exists a tree-like G -proof σ_π of Γ ⇒ Δ such that |σ_π| ≤ |π|^ O(1) .

label: Def: forgetful
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define the forgetful function ( · )^f: L _! → L _p as: p^f:=p qquad 0^f:= bot qquad 1^f:= top qquad (A * B)^f:= A^f wedge B^f (A ∘ B)^f:= A^f ∘ B^f for ∘ ∈ {wedge , vee , → } qquad (!A)^f:=A^f Define Γ^f:= {A^f mid A ∈ Γ} and S^f:= Γ^f ⇒ Δ^f , for any multisets Γ and Δ and any sequent S of the form Γ ⇒ Δ .

label: Thm: G to FLe
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Thm: G to FLe}
Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be multisets of $\calL_u$-formulas, where $\Delta$ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like $G$-proof $\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, there exists a multiset $\Sigma_{\pi}$ of single-variable $\calL_u$-formulas and an $\BFL$-proof $\sigma_\pi$ of $\Sigma_\pi, \Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, such that $|\Sigma_\pi| \leq O(|\pi|)$, $|\sigma_\pi| \leq O(|\pi|^3)$, and $\LK \vdash \, \Rightarrow \bigwedge \Sigma_\pi^f$.
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be multisets of L _u -formulas, where Δ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like G -proof π of Γ ⇒ Δ , there exists a multiset Σ_ π of single-variable L _u -formulas and an FL_e -proof σ_π of Σ_π, Γ ⇒ Δ , such that |Σ_π| ≤ O(|π|) , |σ_π| ≤ O(|π|^3) , and LK vdash ⇒ wedge Σ_π^f .
title: Feasible Deduction Theorem

paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Cor: LK to FLe}
There exist a sequence $\{\Sigma_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of multisets of single-variable $\calL_u$-formulas and a sequence $\{\sigma_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that each $\sigma_n$ is an $\BFL$-proof for
\[
\Sigma_{n},\; Clique_n(\bar{p}, \bar{r}) \Rightarrow \overline{Color}_n(\bar{p}, \bar{s}),
\]
$|\Sigma_{n}|,|\sigma_{n}| \leq n^{O(1)}$ and $\LK \vdash \, \Rightarrow \bigwedge \Sigma_{n}^f$.
statement_text: There exist a sequence {Σ_n}_ n=1 ^ ∞ of multisets of single-variable L _u -formulas and a sequence {σ_n}_ n=1 ^ ∞ such that each σ_n is an FL_e -proof for \[ Σ_ n , Clique_n(bar p , bar r ) ⇒ overline Color _n(bar p , bar s ), \] |Σ_ n |,|σ_ n | ≤ n^ O(1) and LK vdash ⇒ wedge Σ_ n ^f .

S_n := Clique_n(\bar{p}, \bar{r}),\; \Pi_n \;\Rightarrow\; \bigast \Sigma_n^{\bar{p}, \bar{s}} \to \overline{Color}_n(\bar{p}, \bar{s})
\]
have $\BFL$-proofs of size $n^{O(1)}$, but any $\mathbf{LK^-_!}$-proof of $S_n$ has size $2^{n^{\Omega(1)}}$.
statement_text: The sequents \[ S_n := Clique_n(bar p , bar r ), Π_n ⇒ mathop scalebox 1.5 raisebox -0.2ex ast Σ_n^ bar p , bar s → overline Color _n(bar p , bar s ) \] have FL_e -proofs of size n^ O(1) , but any LK^-_! -proof of S_n has size 2^ n^ Ω(1) .

\label{defvc}
A set $S \subseteq V(G)$ is a \emph{vertex cover} of $G$ if  every edge in $E(G)$ has at least one  endpoint in $S$. The \emph{size} of a smallest vertex cover of  $G$ is the \emph{vertex cover number} of $G$.
statement_text: A set S ⊆ V(G) is a vertex cover of G if every edge in E(G) has at least one endpoint in S . The size of a smallest vertex cover of G is the vertex cover number of G .

statement_tex:
A {\it tree decomposition} of a 
graph~$G=(V,E)$  is a tree $T$ together with a 
collection of subsets $X_t$ (called \emph{bags}) of $V$ labeled by the nodes $t$ of $T$ such that 
$\bigcup_{t\in T}X_t=V $ and (1) and (2) below hold:
\begin{enumerate}
			\item For every edge $uv \in E(G)$, there  is some $t$ such that $\{u,v\}\subseteq X_t$.
			\item  (Interpolation Property) If $t$ is a node on the unique path in $T$ from $t_1$ to $t_2$, then 
			$X_{t_1}\cap X_{t_2}\subseteq X_t$.
		\end{enumerate}

statement_tex:
{\cite{and_zero_decision_trees}}
    Given a deterministic decision-tree $T$ over $\{0, 1\}^p$ , the 0-depth (or 1-depth resp.) of $T$ is the maximum number of queries which are answered 0 (or 1 resp.), in any root-to-leaf path of $T$. The 0-query complexity of a Boolean function $f$, denoted by $\dqcs{0}(f)$, is the smallest 0-depth of $T$, taken over deterministic decision-trees $T$ which compute $f$.

statement_tex: An \textbf{$\fand$-Decision Tree} is a deterministic query model that generalizes the classical decision tree. While a classical tree queries individual input bits $x_i\in \{0, 1\}$, each internal node in an $\mathsf{AND}$-decision tree queries a conjunction of a subset of input bits. Formally, a node $v$ computes a function $f_v(x) = \bigwedge\limits_{i\in S_v} x_i$ for some $S_v\subseteq [n]$, the decision to which child to choose is based on the binary outcome of this query.

statement_tex: A strategy $\lambda_i$ is a {\em best response} to a profile $\vlambda_{-i}$ if $u_i(s_i, \vlambda_{-i}) \le u_i(\vlambda)$ for every possible strategy $s_i \in \cS_i$. A strategy profile $\vlambda$ is a {\em Nash equilibrium} if every player's strategy is a best response.

paper_title: The Complexity of Proper Equilibrium in Extensive-Form and Polytope Games
statement_tex: A strategy $\lambda_i$ is an $\eps$-{\em perfect best response} to a profile $\vlambda_{-i}$ if it is fully mixed, and for all pairs of pure strategies $s_i, s_i' \in \cS_i$, we have $$u_i(s_i, \vlambda_{-i}) < u_i(s_i', \vlambda) \qq{$\Rightarrow$} \lambda_i(s_i) \le \eps.$$ That is, every suboptimal strategy is played with probability at most $\eps$.

paper_title: The Complexity of Proper Equilibrium in Extensive-Form and Polytope Games
statement_tex:
An {\em $\eps$-perfect equilibrium} is a fully-mixed profile $\vlambda$ such that every player is playing an $\eps$-perfect best response. A {\em perfect equilibrium} is a limit point of $\eps$-perfect equilibria as $\eps \to 0$. Formally, $\vlambda^*$ is a perfect equilibrium if there are infinite sequences $\{ \vlambda^{(t)}\}_{t=1}^\infty \to \vlambda^*$ and $\{ \eps^{(t)} \}_{t=1}^\infty \to 0$ such that $\vlambda^{(t)}$ is a $\eps^{(t)}$-perfect equilibrium for every $t$.

    We define {\em ($\eps$-)proper equilibria} identically, by replacing every instance of {\em perfect} with {\em proper}.
statement_text: An em eps -perfect equilibrium is a fully-mixed profile bm λ such that every player is playing an eps -perfect best response. A em perfect equilibrium is a limit point of eps -perfect equilibria as eps → 0 . label: thm:main-1conn
paper_title: Independence-Number Parameterized Space Complexity for Directed Connectivity Certificate
statement_text: Let G=(V,A) be an n -node digraph with independence number at most α . For p ∈ N , there exist p -pass deterministic algorithm for computing a 1 -strong connectivity certificate of G with arboricity at most α+2 using O(α n^ 1+1/p ) space in the insertion-only model; O(α n^ 1+O(1/ sqrt p ) ) space in the turnstile model.

label: thm:main-kconn
paper_title: Independence-Number Parameterized Space Complexity for Directed Connectivity Certificate
statement_text: Let G=(V,A) be an n -node digraph with independence number at most α . For p ∈ N and k ≥ 2 , there exist p -pass randomized algorithm such that with probability 1 - 1/n^ Ω(1) , a k -strong connectivity certificate of G of size O(k α n log n) is computed using: O(k^ 1-1/p α n^ 1+1/p log n) space in the insertion-only model; and O(k^ 1- O(1/ sqrt p ) α n^ 1+ O(1/ sqrt p ) log n) space in the turnstile model.

label: thm:ConnCert-intro
paper_title: Independence-Number Parameterized Space Complexity for Directed Connectivity Certificate
statement_tex:
\label{thm:ConnCert-intro}
    For the class of digraphs with $n$ nodes and independence number at most $\alpha$, 
    any $p$-pass streaming algorithm in the insertion-only model for computing a $1$-node or $1$-arc strong connectivity certificate requires $\Omega(\alpha n/p)$ space. 

    Consequently, in both insertion-only and turnstile models, any $p$-pass streaming algorithm for computing a $k$-node or $k$-arc strong connectivity certificate requires $\Omega(\alpha n/p)$ space.
statement_text: For the class of digraphs with n nodes and independence number at most α , any p -pass streaming algorithm in the insertion-only model for computing a 1 -node or 1 -arc strong connectivity certificate requires Ω(α n/p) space. Consequently, in both insertion-only and turnstile models, any p -pass streaming algorithm for computing a k -node or k -arc strong connectivity certificate requires Ω(α n/p) space.

label: prop:Chernoff
paper_title: Independence-Number Parameterized Space Complexity for Directed Connectivity Certificate
statement_tex:
\label{prop:Chernoff}
    Suppose $X_1,\ldots,X_k$ are independent $0/1$-random variables. Let $X = \sum_{i=1}^k X_i$ and $\mu = \Ex[X]$. For any $\delta>0$,
    \[
        \Pr[X\leq (1-\delta)\mu] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{\delta^2 \mu}{2}\right) 
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        \Pr[X\geq (1+\delta)\mu] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{\delta^2 \mu}{2+\delta}\right).
    \]
statement_text: Suppose X_1, ... ,X_k are independent 0/1 -random variables. Let X = Σ _ i=1 ^k X_i and μ = E [X] . For any δ>0 , \[ Pr [X ≤ (1-δ)μ] ≤ exp (-frac δ^2 μ 2 ) qquad and qquad Pr [X ≥ (1+δ)μ] ≤ exp (-frac δ^2 μ 2+δ ). \]
title: Chernoff bound

label: thm:edmond
paper_title: Independence-Number Parameterized Space Complexity for Directed Connectivity Certificate
statement_tex:
\label{thm:edmond}
    A digraph $G = (V, A)$ contains $k$ arc-disjoint spanning out-branchings rooted at a node $r \in V$ if and only if 
    \(
      |\delta^+_G(S)| \ge k
    \)
    for every cut $(S, V \setminus S)$ with $r \in S$.
statement_text: A digraph G = (V, A) contains k arc-disjoint spanning out-branchings rooted at a node r ∈ V if and only if \( |δ^+_G(S)| ≥ k \) for every cut (S, V \ S) with r ∈ S .
title: Edmonds’ branching theorem

\label{lem:kvc-main}
Let $k\geq 2$, $\rho\in (0,1/k]$ and $n$ be sufficiently large. Write $r=\frac{192\lambda}{\rho^2}\log n$ for some $\lambda\geq 1$.
With probability $1 - n^{-\lambda}$, 
\(

\)
forms a $k$-node strong connectivity certificate of $G$.

paper_title: Catalytic Tree Evaluation From Matching Vectors
statement_tex: A \textit{catalytic machine} $M$ is defined as a Turing machine in the usual sense---i.e.,~a read-only input tape, a write-only output tape, and a (space-bounded) read-write work tape---with an additional read-write tape known as the \textit{catalytic tape}. Unlike the ordinary work tape, the catalytic tape is initialized to hold an arbitrary string $\tau$, and $M$ has the restriction that for any initial setting of the catalytic tape, at the end of its computation the catalytic tape must be returned to the original state $\tau$.
statement_text: A it catalytic machine M is defined as a Turing machine in the usual sense---i.e., a read-only input tape, a write-only output tape, and a (space-bounded) read-write work tape---with an additional read-write tape known as the it catalytic tape . Unlike the ordinary work tape, the catalytic tape is initialized to hold an arbitrary string τ , and M has the restriction that for any initial setting of the catalytic tape, at the end of its computation the catalytic tape must be returned to the original state τ .

label: thm:TEPonelevel

statement_tex:
\label{thm:TEPonelevel}
    Let $m = p_1p_2\ldots p_t$ be a product of $t$ distinct odd primes that are given as input.
    Suppose there exists an $O(\ell)$-space uniform
    matching vector family $\{\uv_x, \vecv_x \in \Z_m^d: x \in \zo^\ell\}$ of size $2^\ell$ over $\Z_m^d$.
    Additionally, let $\left\{\wv_s: s \in \zo^\ell\right\}$ be any $O(\ell)$-space uniform collection of vectors in $\Z_m^{d}$.
    Suppose our algorithm is given the following resources:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item global space 
        comprising three 
        registers $\xv, \yv,\zv \in \Z_m^d$;
        \item the truth table of a function $f: \zo^\ell \times \zo^\ell \to \zo^\ell$ on the input tape; and
        \item an oracle $\calO$ that takes as input a scalar $\gamma \in \Z_m$ and bits $\ctrl, \sigma \in \zo$ in local space and updates the registers as follows.
        In the below, $a, b \in \zo^\ell$ are some bitstrings.
        \begin{itemize}
            \item if $\sigma = 0$, let $\Delta$ denote $\uv_a$ if $\mathsf{ctrl} = 0$ and $\vecv_a$ otherwise.
            The oracle will update $\xv \gets \xv + \gamma \Delta$ and leave all other registers unchanged.
            (Here, by $\xv$ we mean the first of the three catalytic registers, and $\yv$ refers to the second catalytic register.)

            \item if $\sigma = 1$, let $\Delta$ denote $\uv_b$ if $\mathsf{ctrl} = 0$ and $\vecv_b$ otherwise.
            The oracle will update $\yv \gets \yv + \gamma \Delta$ and leave all other registers unchanged.
        \end{itemize}
    \end{itemize}
    Then, there exists an algorithm that takes as input a scalar $\gamma \in \Z_m$ in local space and updates $\zv \gets \zv + \gamma \wv_{f(a, b)}$ (while leaving the $\xv$ and $\yv$ registers unchanged). Moreover, the algorithm uses $O(\ell + \log m + \log(d \cdot \log m))$ local space, and before making all oracle calls erases all but $O(\log m)$ bits of this space. The algorithm runs in time $\poly(2^{\ell+t} \cdot d \cdot \log m)$ and makes $2^{O(t)}$ queries to $\calO$.

Suppose our algorithm is given the following resources: global space comprising three registers x , y , z ∈ Z _m^d ; the truth table of a function f: {0,1} ^ell × {0,1} ^ell → {0,1} ^ell on the input tape; and an oracle O that takes as input a scalar γ ∈ Z _m and bits ctrl , σ ∈ {0,1} in local space and updates the registers as follows. In the below, a, b ∈ {0,1} ^ell are some bitstrings. if σ = 0 , let Δ denote u _a if ctrl = 0 and v _a otherwise. The oracle will update x gets x + γ Δ and leave all other registers unchanged. (Here, by x we mean the first of the three catalytic registers, and y refers to the second catalytic register.) if σ = 1 , let Δ denote u _b if ctrl = 0 and v _b otherwise. The oracle will update y gets y + γ Δ and leave all other registers unchanged. Then, there exists an algorithm that takes as input a scalar γ ∈ Z _m in local space and updates z gets z + γ w _ f(a, b) (while leaving the x and y registers unchanged). Moreover, the algorithm uses O(ell + log m + log (d · log m)) local space, and before making all oracle calls erases all but O( log m) bits of this space.
