label: ass:boundary-calibration-main
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{ass:boundary-calibration-main}
The ensemble $\mathcal D$, the threshold $N(n)$, and the time bound $t$ are chosen so that two conditions hold. First, on $\mathcal D$ the boundary-exposure predicate $E_{\mathcal S}(\cdot,N(n))$ tracks $t$-time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity up to a polynomial-time computable reindexing. Second, this correspondence bridges $\mathcal D$ to the uniform distribution on which Liu--Pass operates: any average-case algorithm computing $\Kt$ over the uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^n$ that is strong enough to violate the Liu--Pass hardness condition yields, through the reindexing, a $1{-}o(1)$-success heuristic for $E_{\mathcal S}(\cdot,N(n))$ on $x{\sim}D_n$.
statement_text: The ensemble D , the threshold N(n) , and the time bound t are chosen so that two conditions hold. First, on D the boundary-exposure predicate E_ S ( · ,N(n)) tracks t -time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity up to a polynomial-time computable reindexing. Second, this correspondence bridges D to the uniform distribution on which Liu--Pass operates: any average-case algorithm computing K^ t over the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n that is strong enough to violate the Liu--Pass hardness condition yields, through the reindexing, a 1 - o(1) -success heuristic for E_ S ( · ,N(n)) on x D_n .

paper_title: Towards Worst-case Hardness for Low-Noise LPN
statement_tex:
Let $n,m \in \mathbb{Z}$, and $\eta \in [0, 1]$. For sample count $m$, secret dimension $n$, and noise parameter $\eta$, algorithms $\Slpn$ and $\Dlpn$ are said to have advantage $\eps \in [0, 1]$ in solving the \emph{Search LPN} and \emph{Decision LPN} problems, respectively, if they satisfy the following conditions:
    \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
        \item \emph{Search LPN:} $\Slpn$ recovers the secret $s$ with probability at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ s \gets \Field{2}^n \\ e \gets \mathrm{Ber}(\eta)^m}}[\Slpn(A, As + e) = s] \geq \eps
       . \]
        
        \item \emph{Decision LPN:} $\Dlpn$ distinguishes LPN samples from uniform with advantage at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \abs{\Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ s \gets \Field{2}^n \\ e \gets \mathrm{Ber}(\eta)^m}}[\Dlpn(A, As + e) = 1] - \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ b \gets \Field{2}^m}}[\Dlpn(A, b) = 1]} \geq \eps.
        \]
    \end{itemize}
statement_text: Let n,m ∈ Z , and η ∈ [0, 1] . For sample count m , secret dimension n , and noise parameter η , algorithms algS _ LPN and algD _ LPN are said to have advantage ε ∈ [0, 1] in solving the Search LPN and Decision LPN problems, respectively, if they satisfy the following conditions: Search LPN: algS _ LPN recovers the secret s with probability at least ε : \[ Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n s gets F _ 2 ^n e gets Ber (η)^m [ algS _ LPN (A, As + e) = s] ≥ ε . \] Decision LPN: algD _ LPN distinguishes LPN samples from uniform with advantage at least ε : \[ abs Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n s gets F _ 2 ^n e gets Ber (η)^m [ algD _ LPN (A, As + e) = 1] - Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n b gets F _ 2 ^m [ algD _ LPN (A, b) = 1] ≥ ε. \]

paper_title: Towards Worst-case Hardness for Low-Noise LPN
statement_tex:
Let $n,m \in \mathbb{Z}$, and $\theta \in [0, 1]$. For code length $m$, code dimension $n$, and noise parameter $\theta$, algorithms $\Ssd$ and $\Dsd$ are said to have advantage $\eps \in [0, 1]$ in solving the \emph{Search SD} and \emph{Decision SD} problems, respectively, if they satisfy the following conditions:
    \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
        \item \emph{Search SD:} $\Ssd$ decodes a syndrome with probability at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n}\\ r \gets \mathcal{W}(m, \theta \cdot m)}}[\Ssd(A, r^TA) = r] \geq \eps.
        \]
        
        \item \emph{Decision SD:} $\Dsd$ distinguishes a syndrome from uniform with advantage at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \abs{\Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n}\\ r \gets \mathcal{W}(m, \theta \cdot m)}}[\Dsd(A, r^TA) = 1] - \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ c \gets \Field{2}^n}}[\Dsd(A, c^T) = 1]} \geq \eps.

label: thm:main

statement_tex:
\label{thm:main}
  Consider $n, m, t \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\eta, \theta \in (0,1)$ such that $t^2\theta^2m < 1$. Suppose there exists an algorithm for Search LPN with sample count $t$, secret dimension $n$, and noise parameter $\tau =  (1 - (1-2\eta)^{\theta \cdot m})/2$, which runs in time $T$ and has advantage $\eps$. Then there exist algorithms $\algD$ and $\algS$ such that for every matrix $A \in \Field{2}^{m \times n}$, at least one of the following is true:
  \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
    \item $\algS$ runs in  time $\poly\left(n, m, T, (1/\eps)^{\log_m(m/\eps)}\right)$ and decodes codewords of $A$ from random noise such that, \[\Pr_{\substack{s \gets \Field{2}^n\\ e \gets Ber(\eta)^m}}[\algS(A, As+e) = s^\prime\  \mathrm{and}\  \wt(As^\prime - (As + e)) \leq 2\eta m] \geq \eps/2 - o(\eps).
    \]
    \item $\algD$ runs in time $\poly(n,m) + T$ and distinguishes a sparse combination of rows of $A$ from a uniform string such that,
    \[
    \Pr_{c \gets \Field{2}^n}[\algD(A, c^T) = 1] - \Pr_{r \gets {\cW(m,\theta \cdot m)}}[\algD(A, r^TA) = 1]  \geq \eps/2t.
    \]
  \end{itemize}

Suppose there exists an algorithm for Search LPN with sample count t , secret dimension n , and noise parameter τ = (1 - (1-2η)^ θ · m )/2 , which runs in time T and has advantage ε . statement_tex:
\label{cor:lpnmain}
    Consider any polynomial $t(n) \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $t(n) > n$, constants $\alpha, \beta \in (0.01, 0.99)$ with $\alpha + \beta \in (0.01, 0.99)$, and $m(n) = \ceil{2t^2n^{2\beta}}$. Suppose that for every pair of PPT algorithms $(\algS, \algD)$, there exists a negligible function $negl$ such that, for all large enough $n$, there exists an $\F_2$-matrix $A$ of dimension $m \times n$ for which both of these conditions are true: 
    \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
        \item $\Pr[\algS(A, As+e) = s^\prime\  \mathrm{and}\  \wt(As^\prime - (As + e)) \leq 2 m/n^{\alpha+\beta}]  \leq negl(n)$, where $s \gets \Field{2}^n$, $e \gets Ber(n^{-(\alpha + \beta)})^{m}$.
        \item $\abs{\Pr[\algD(A, c^T) = 1] - \Pr[\algD(A, r^TA) = 1]} \leq negl(n)$, where $c \gets \Field{2}^n, r \gets \cW(m,n^{\beta})$.
    \end{itemize}    
    Then, for the Search LPN problem with sample count $t(n)$, secret dimension $n$, and noise parameter $n^{-\alpha}$, no PPT algorithm has non-negligible advantage.

Suppose that for every pair of PPT algorithms (algS , algD ) , there exists a negligible function negl such that, for all large enough n , there exists an F _2 -matrix A of dimension m × n for which both of these conditions are true: Pr [algS (A, As+e) = s^prime \ and \ wt (As^prime - (As + e)) ≤ 2 m/n^ α+β ] ≤ negl(n) , where s gets F _ 2 ^n , e gets Ber(n^ -(α + β) )^ m . abs Pr [algD (A, c^T) = 1] - Pr [algD (A, r^TA) = 1] ≤ negl(n) , where c gets F _ 2 ^n, r gets cW (m,n^ β ) . Then, for the Search LPN problem with sample count t(n) , secret dimension n , and noise parameter n^ -α , no PPT algorithm has non-negligible advantage.

label: lem:merge_reduce
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_tex:
\label{lem:merge_reduce}
   Fix $n, \gamma, U, V$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an offline algorithm which receives $K \subset U$  as input, and outputs $\widetilde{K} \subset K$ such that $|\widetilde{K}| \leq |K|/2$ and for any $q \in V$, with probability $1 - \frac{1}{\poly n}$, 
   \begin{equation*}
       \left|\gamma(K, q) - 2\gamma(\widetilde{K}, q)\right| \leq \eta
   \end{equation*}
   for some error bound $\eta =  \eta(|K|)$.
   Let $T = T(|K|)$ be a deterministic upper bound on the runtime of $\mathcal{A}$. 
   Then for every block size $b \geq 1$, there is a streaming algorithm that processes a stream $k_1,  \cdots, k_n$ and, at every time step $j$, maintains a weighted coreset $C_j$ for the prefix $K_j = (k_1, \cdots, k_j)$ such that the following holds: 
    
    For any $q \in U$, with probability $1-\frac{1}{\poly n}$,
   \[\left|
  \gamma(K_j,q)-\gamma(C_j,q)\right|
   \leq O\qty(\eta(b) \cdot \frac{j}{b} \log\frac{j}{b}), \]
   where $\gamma(C_j,q) := \sum_{x \in C_j} w_x \gamma(x,q)$
   for $w_x$ denoting the weight of $x$ in the coreset $C_j$.
   
Moreover, $|C_j|  = O\left(b\log\frac{j}{b}\right)$. The streaming algorithm uses $\tilde{O}\left(b\log\frac{j}{b}\right )$ bits of storage space and $O\left(T(b)\cdot \log\frac{j}{b}\right)$ update time.
statement_text: Fix n, γ, U, V . Let A be an offline algorithm which receives K ⊂ U as input, and outputs widetilde K ⊂ K such that |widetilde K | ≤ |K|/2 and for any q ∈ V , with probability 1 - frac 1 poly n , |γ(K, q) - 2γ(widetilde K , q) | ≤ η for some error bound η = η(|K|) . Let T = T(|K|) be a deterministic upper bound on the runtime of A . Then for every block size b ≥ 1 , there is a streaming algorithm that processes a stream k_1, ... , k_n and, at every time step j , maintains a weighted coreset C_j for the prefix K_j = (k_1, ... , k_j) such that the following holds: For any q ∈ U , with probability 1-frac 1 poly n , \[ | γ(K_j,q)-γ(C_j,q) | ≤ Oqty (η(b) · frac j b log frac j b ), \] where γ(C_j,q) := Σ _ x ∈ C_j w_x γ(x,q) for w_x denoting the weight of x in the coreset C_j . Moreover, |C_j| = O (b log frac j b ) . The streaming algorithm uses tilde O (b log frac j b ) bits of storage space and O (T(b) · log frac j b ) update time.

{lemma}{certifyball}[Certify]\label{cor:certify-ball}
There is a randomized procedure that, given a set
\(K \subseteq B(c,r)\) and parameters \(\Delta,\tau,\delta \in \left(0,\tfrac13\right)\), runs in time
\[
O\!\left(\frac{d}{\Delta^{2}\tau}\log\!\left(\frac{2|K|}{\delta}\right)\cdot |K|\right)
\]
and, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), does one of the following:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item returns a point \(k^* \in B(c,r)\) such that
    \[
    \left|B\!\left(k^*, \sqrt{1-\Delta^4}\,r\right)\cap K\right|
    \;\ge\;
    \Omega(\Delta^2)\cdot \tau |K|,
    \]
    \item certifies that \(K\) is \((\Delta',\tau)\)-pseudo-random, where \(\Delta'=\Theta(\Delta)\).
\end{enumerate}
We refer to this procedure as \(\Certify_{\Delta,\tau,\delta}\).

label: lem:merge-reduce-w

statement_tex:
\label{lem:merge-reduce-w}    Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a black-box offline algorithm which takes as input a dataset $K \subset B(0,r)$, $|K| \leq n$,  and returns $\widetilde{K} \subset K$, $|\widetilde{K}| \leq 3|K|/4$, weight function $\alpha_x \in \{1, 2\}$ such that with probability $1 - \frac{1}{\poly n}$, for any fixed $q \in B(0, r)$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:error_bound-mr}
\left|\exp(K, q) - \exp(\tilde{K}, \alpha,  q)\right| \leq O\left(e^{r^2(1 + o(1))}\cdot n^{o(1)}\cdot \frac{\exp(K, q)}{|K|}\right).
\end{align}
   
   Let $T(m)$ denote the runtime $\mathcal{A}$ on inputs of size $m$. Assume that the space complexity of $\mathcal{A}$ is $O(m)$.

   Algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ can be adapted to process $K$ as a stream. At every step $j$ of the stream, it maintains a weighted coreset $C_j$ of the $j$ first elements of the stream $K_j$. Let $w_x^j$ denote the weight of a point $x \in C_j$ and $w^j$~-- the weight function. We have with probability $1-\frac{1}{\poly (n)}$, for any fixed $q \in U$ and desired error $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$,
   \[\left|
  \exp(K_j,q)-\exp(C_j, w^j, q)\right|
   \leq \epsilon \cdot \exp(K_j, q).
   \]
The size of the coreset, runtime and memory are defined in terms of the \textit{block size} of the algorithm $b$
\[
|C_j| \leq O\left(b\log^2\left(\frac{|K_j|}{b}\right)\right), \quad \text{ runtime} =  O\left(T(b)\cdot \log^2\left(\frac{|K_j|}{b}\right)\right), \quad \text{ space}=
   O\left(b\log^2\left(\frac{|K_j|}{b}\right)\right),
   \]
and the block size $b$ is defined by the desired error $\epsilon$ 
   \[
   b = \frac{e^{r^2(1 + o(1))}\cdot n^{o(1)}}{\epsilon}.
   \]

Assume that $d = \omega(\log n), r^2 = \Theta(\log n)$, $ n < \frac{\exp(r^2 \p{1 - C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{d}}})}{16\eps}$ for some constant $C$, there exists a communication protocol with a message size $S_{n, d, r, \eps} + o(n)$ which solves the $\texttt{INDEX}_{2n, n}$ problem with probability at least $9/10$.
statement_text: Let S_ n, d, r, ε denote a deterministic upper bound on the space, measured in bits, of a (randomized) data structure for the Streaming KDE problem with parameters n, d, r, ε and a failure probability 1/100 . Assume that d = ω( log n), r^2 = Θ( log n) , n < frac exp (r^2 p 1 - C sqrt frac log n d ) 16 ε for some constant C , there exists a communication protocol with a message size S_ n, d, r, ε + o(n) which solves the tt INDEX _ 2n, n problem with probability at least 9/10 .

label: lem:taylor_embed_memory
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_tex:
\label{lem:taylor_embed_memory}

    \]

statement_text: For any t < r^2 and any k_j from a sphere of radius r , we have exp _ >t (k_j, k_j) ≥ frac 1 2 e^ r^2 .

statement_text: Assume that r = log ^ o(1) n , log n ≤ d ≤ log ^a n for some constant a > 1 and n^ -100 < ε < n^ -c for any constant c > 0 . label: def:weighted-kde
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_text: The algorithm receives key-weight pairs (k_1, w(k_1)) ... , (k_n, w(k_n)) ∈ R ^d × R in a stream and at every point j = 1, ... , n , given any fixed q ∈ R ^d , outputs an estimate widehat exp (K_ j , w_j, q) of exp (K_ j , w_j, q) that satisfies |widehat exp (K_ j , w_j, q) - exp (K_ j , w_j, q)| ≤ ε · exp (K_ j , q) with probability at least 1-δ for some δ ∈ (0, 1) for any fixed query q . Here K_ j =(k_1, ... , k_ j ) is the sequence of keys received by time j , w_ j =(w(k_1), ... , w(k_ j )) is the sequence of weights received by time j , |w(k)| ≤ 1 for all k ∈ K , and exp (K, w, q) := Σ _ k ∈ K w(k) exp (k, q).

label: lem:weighted_embed_memory
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_text: Let γ(k, q) := Σ _ l = 0 ^ t a_l \<k, q>^l for some t and a_l . Then there exist embeddings ψ_1, ψ_2 such that for any K ⊂ R ^d with |k|_2 ≤ r for all k ∈ K , any q ∈ R ^d with |q|_2 ≤ r , and any weights {w(k)}_ k ∈ K with |w(k)| ≤ 1 for all k ∈ K , we guarantee \[qty | l le Σ _ k ∈ K w(k) ψ_1(k), ψ_2(q) r rangle - Σ _ k ∈ K w(k)γ(k, q)| < δ,\] and the weighted aggregate Σ _ k ∈ K w(k)ψ_1(k) can be stored in O l(frac (d+t)^ t t! log frac |K| · (d+t)^ t · max _l |a_l| · max {r, 1}^t δ r) bits of space.

label: lem:weighted_streaming_coreset
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_tex:
\label{lem:weighted_streaming_coreset}
    Let $U \times V\subset   \R^d \times \R^d $ be a predefined subset of the domain. There is a randomized algorithm $\BaseCompress'$ which receives as inputs $K \subset U$ and any weights $\{w(k)\}_{k\in K}$ with $|w(k)| \leq 1$ . $\BaseCompress'(K, \{w(k)\}_{k\in K})$ outputs $\widetilde{K} \subset K$ such that $|\widetilde{K}| \leq |K|/2$ and for any $q \in V$, with probability $1 - \delta$,
           \[\left|\expker(K, w, q) - 2\expker(\widetilde{K}, w, q)\right| \leq O\left(\sqrt{\max_{u \in U}\expker(u, u)\cdot \max_{v \in V}\expker(v, v)}\cdot \log (|K|/\delta)\right).\]
    $\BaseCompress'(K,w)$ runs in $O(|K|^2 \cdot T)$ time, where $T$ is the maximum time to access $\expker(k,q)$.
statement_text: Let U × V ⊂ R ^d × R ^d be a predefined subset of the domain. There is a randomized algorithm sc BaseCompress ' which receives as inputs K ⊂ U and any weights {w(k)}_ k ∈ K with |w(k)| ≤ 1 . sc BaseCompress '(K, {w(k)}_ k ∈ K ) outputs widetilde K ⊂ K such that |widetilde K | ≤ |K|/2 and for any q ∈ V , with probability 1 - δ , \[ | exp (K, w, q) - 2 exp (widetilde K , w, q) | ≤ O ( sqrt max _ u ∈ U exp (u, u) · max _ v ∈ V exp (v, v) · log (|K|/δ) ).\] sc BaseCompress '(K,w) runs in O(|K|^2 · T) time, where T is the maximum time to access exp (k,q) .

paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_text: Assume that r = log ^ o(1) n , log n ≤ d ≤ log ^a n for some constant a > 1 and ε < n^ -c for any constant c > 0 . label: l:tokde
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_tex:

label: def:random-kde-instance
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_text: Let x ∈ {0,1}^ 2n be a binary vector with exactly n ones. Let K ⊂ R ^d be a set of 2n points drawn i.i.d.\ from a rotationally invariant distribution, independently of x . Let K_ x be the set of points indexed by the ones of x . A random KDE instance is an instance of the streaming KDE problem (cref def:streaming-kde ) in which the keys k_1, ... , k_n are the points in K and the query q is chosen from K . Vector q is chosen to be one of the keys k_i ∈ K ; the position in the dataset i is independent of the randomness of K .
title: Random KDE Instance

label: l:fromkde

label: lemma:certify
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:certify}
There is a randomized procedure that, given a set
$K \subseteq S^{d-1}$ and parameters $\Delta,\tau,\delta \in \left(0,\tfrac13\right)$, runs in time
\[
O\!\left(\frac{d}{\Delta^{2}\tau}\log\!\left(\frac{2|K|}{\delta}\right)\cdot |K|\right)
\]
and, with probability at least $1-\delta$, does one of the following:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item returns a point $k^* \in S^{d-1}$ such that
    \[
    \left|B\!\left(k^*, \sqrt{2(1 - \Delta^2)}\right)\cap K\right|
    \;\ge\;
    \Omega(\Delta^2)\cdot \tau |K|
    \]
    \item or certifies that the set $K$ is $(\Delta',\tau)$-pseudo-random, where $\Delta' = \Theta(\Delta)$.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: There is a randomized procedure that, given a set K ⊆ S^ d-1 and parameters Δ,τ,δ ∈ (0,tfrac 13 ) , runs in time \[ O (frac d Δ^ 2 τ log (frac 2|K| δ ) · |K| ) \] and, with probability at least 1-δ , does one of the following: returns a point k^* ∈ S^ d-1 such that \[ |B (k^*, sqrt 2(1 - Δ^2) ) ∩ K | ≥ Ω(Δ^2) · τ |K| \] or certifies that the set K is (Δ',τ) -pseudo-random, where Δ' = Θ(Δ) .
title: , Lemma 58

statement_text: If none of X_1, X_2, Y_1 is empty, where X_1 and Y_1 are not consecutive (i.e. (X_1,X_2,Y_1)=(A_1,A_2,C_1) then X_2=X^1_2 ∪ X^2_2 so that X^2_2 is complete to X_1 and independent from Y_1 , and X^1_2 is complete to Y_1 and independent from X_1 .

statement_text: Let G be a connected (P_6, C_3) -free graph. If G contains two vertex-disjoint induced 5-cycles C^1 and C^2 , then there exists at least one edge with one endpoint in V(C^1) and the other in V(C^2) .

label: A1-C2
paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
statement_tex:
\label{A1-C2}

statement_text: Suppose X_1 and Y_2 are not empty where X_1,Y_1 are not consecutive (i.e. A_1 and C_2 are not empty or A_1 and D_2 are not empty). Then for every two vertices x_1,x'_1 ∈ X_1 , N(x_1) ∩ Y_2 = N(x'_1) ∩ Y_2 .

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
statement_tex:
\label{A1~C2_2}
    Suppose $X_1$ and $Y_2$ are not empty where $X_1$ and $Y_1$ are not consecutive (e.g. $A_1$ and $C_2$). Then $Y_2= Y^1_2 \cup Y^2_2$ so that $X_1$ and $Y_2^2$ forms a clique and $X_1 \cup Y^1_2$ is independent.

Then Y_2=Y^2_2 ∪ Y^1_2 , and Z_2=Z^1_2 ∪ Z^2_2 so that : X_1 is complete to Y^2_2 and Z^2_2 . X_1 is independent of Y^1_2 and Z^1_2 . Z^1_2 and Y^2_2 form a complete bipartite graph. Y^1_2 and Z^2_2 form a complete bipartite graph.

For every two vertices a_0,a'_0 ∈ X_0 with a common neighbor in X_2 , N(a_0) ∩ Y_2 = N(a'_0) ∩ Y_2 . statement_text: Let a_1, a_2 ∈ V_j and b_1, b_2 ∈ V_ j+1 . Suppose that a_1b_1 ∈ E(H) , a_2b_2 ∈ E(H) , and b_1a_2 ∈ E(H) , but a_1b_2 ∉ E(H) (a `Z' shape). Then: N(b_2) ∩ V_ j+2 ⊆ N(b_1) ∩ V_ j+2 , N(a_1) ∩ V_ j-1 ⊆ N(a_2) ∩ V_ j-1 .

\qquad\text{and}\qquad

\]
statement_text: Let a_1, a_2 ∈ V_j and b_1, b_2 ∈ V_ j+1 . Suppose a_1b_1 ∈ E(H) and a_2b_2 ∈ E(H) form an induced 2K_2 (i.e., a_1b_2 ∉ E(H) and a_2b_1 ∉ E(H) ). Then \[ N(a_1) ∩ V_ j-1 =N(a_2) ∩ V_ j-1 qquad and qquad N(b_1) ∩ V_ j+2 =N(b_2) ∩ V_ j+2 . \]

statement_text: Suppose H_j , H_ j+1 , and H_ j+2 are proper chain graphs with alternating inclusion directions ( L → R , R → L , and L → R respectively). Then the adjacent bipartite graphs H_ j-1 and H_ j+3 must be complete bipartite graphs.

statement_text: Suppose H_j is not connected. Then H_ j-1 and H_ j+1 are both complete bipartite graphs.

label: 2K2-structure
paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
statement_tex:
\label{2K2-structure}
Suppose $H_j$ is connected and contains two independent edges $a_1b_1$ and $a_2b_2$. Then $H_j$ is partitioned into $A_1, A_2, A_3$ where $A_1$ and $A_2$ are connected and contain $a_1b_1$ and $a_2b_2$ (respectively), and $A_1$ and $A_2$ are independent. $A_3$ is complete to both $A_1$ and $A_2$. Furthermore, $N(A_1) \cap V_{j-1} = N(A_2) \cap V_{j-1} \subseteq N(A_3) \cap V_{j-1}$ and $N(A_1) \cap V_{j+2} = N(A_2) \cap V_{j+2} \subseteq N(A_3) \cap V_{j+2}$.
statement_text: Suppose H_j is connected and contains two independent edges a_1b_1 and a_2b_2 . Then H_j is partitioned into A_1, A_2, A_3 where A_1 and A_2 are connected and contain a_1b_1 and a_2b_2 (respectively), and A_1 and A_2 are independent. A_3 is complete to both A_1 and A_2 . Furthermore, N(A_1) ∩ V_ j-1 = N(A_2) ∩ V_ j-1 ⊆ N(A_3) ∩ V_ j-1 and N(A_1) ∩ V_ j+2 = N(A_2) ∩ V_ j+2 ⊆ N(A_3) ∩ V_ j+2 .

label: OCT-chain-chain-chain
paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs

paper_title: Odd Cycle Transversal in $P_k$-Free Graphs
statement_tex:
The OCT problem on $G$ reduces to breaking the odd-length macroscopic ring $H$. Because $k-1$ is odd, any valid odd cycle transversal must remove all vertices from at least one partition $V_j$, or sever the connections between $V_j$ and $V_{j+1}$. 
    Since $V_j$ and $V_{j+1}$ are independent sets, the subgraph $H[V_j \cup V_{j+1}]$ is bipartite. Breaking the ring optimally is equivalent to computing the Minimum Vertex Cover for the bipartite graph $H[V_j \cup V_{j+1}]$ for each $j \in \{0, \dots, k-2\}$, and taking the global minimum. This can be computed exactly in polynomial time.

Since V_j and V_ j+1 are independent sets, the subgraph H[V_j ∪ V_ j+1 ] is bipartite. Breaking the ring optimally is equivalent to computing the Minimum Vertex Cover for the bipartite graph H[V_j ∪ V_ j+1 ] for each j ∈ {0, ... , k-2} , and taking the global minimum. This can be computed exactly in polynomial time.

label: def:ltc
paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
statement_tex:
\label{def:ltc}
Let $C = \ker(H)$ be a classical code, where $H\in\mathbb{F}_2^{m\times n}$ is a parity-check matrix. We say that $C$ is \emph{locally testable} with soundness $\rho$ if for all $x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, it holds that
\[
\frac{1}{m} |Hx| \geq \rho \frac{d_H(x, C)}{n}\;,
\]
where $|x|$ denotes the Hamming weight (number of nonzero coordinates) of $x$ and $d_H(x, C)$ denotes the Hamming distance between $x$ and the code $C$.
statement_text: Let C = ker (H) be a classical code, where H ∈ F _2^ m × n is a parity-check matrix. We say that C is locally testable with soundness ρ if for all x ∈ F _2^n , it holds that \[ frac 1 m |Hx| ≥ ρ frac d_H(x, C) n , \] where |x| denotes the Hamming weight (number of nonzero coordinates) of x and d_H(x, C) denotes the Hamming distance between x and the code C .
title: Classical locally testable codes

label: def:local-tester

Define the local tester tt T for the code C as the following procedure: Given input w ∈ F _2^n , Randomly sample i_1, ... , i_c ∈ _R [m] , Compute r = H_ i_1 vdots H_ i_c · w ∈ F _2^c, Reject if \( vee_ j ∈ [c] r_j = 1 \) (i.e., any parity constraint is violated).

label: lem:ltc_amp
paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
statement_tex:
\label{lem:ltc_amp}
Let $C = \ker(H)$ be a locally testable code with soundness $\rho$, where each row of $H$ has weight at most $R$.
Let $\kappa > \rho $.

Then, there exists a code tester for $C$ with query complexity $Q$ such that for all $x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$,
\[
\Pr[\text{verifier rejects } x] \geq 1 - \left(1 - \rho \cdot \frac{d_H(x, C)}{n}\right)^{Q/R} \;.
\]

Furthermore, there exists a code tester for $C$ with query complexity
\[
Q = R \cdot \frac{\kappa}{\rho} \cdot \frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{1 - \varepsilon}
\]
such that for all $x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, it holds that
\[
\Pr[\text{verifier rejects } x] \geq \min\left\{\kappa \cdot \frac{d_H(x, C)}{n},\, 1 - \varepsilon \right\} \;.
\]
statement_text: Let C = ker (H) be a locally testable code with soundness ρ , where each row of H has weight at most R . Let κ > ρ . Then, there exists a code tester for C with query complexity Q such that for all x ∈ F _2^n , \[ Pr [ verifier rejects x] ≥ 1 - (1 - ρ · frac d_H(x, C) n )^ Q/R . \] Furthermore, there exists a code tester for C with query complexity \[ Q = R · frac κ ρ · frac log (1/ε) 1 - ε \] such that for all x ∈ F _2^n , it holds that \[ Pr [ verifier rejects x] ≥ min {κ · frac d_H(x, C) n , 1 - ε } . \]

Then, for a ∈ F _2 , w ∈ F _2^q , and r ∈ F _2^ l_r , define the local tester operator as L_r(ket a ket w ) = ket a ⊕ tt T (w; r) ket w .

label: def:css
paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
statement_tex:
\label{def:css}

An $[n, k, d]$ quantum CSS code on $n$ qubits is a subspace $C \subseteq \mathcal{H} = (\mathbb{C}^2)^{\otimes n}$.
It is defined by a pair of parity-check matrices $H_X, H_Z$ such that $\operatorname{Im}(H_X^\top) \perp \operatorname{Im}(H_Z^\top)$.
We denote the code as $C = CSS(H_X, H_Z)$.
Explicitly, the code subspace is given by
\[
CSS(H_X, H_Z) = \left\{ \ket{\psi} \in (\mathbb{C}^2)^{\otimes n} : X(x) \ket{\psi} = \ket{\psi} \, \forall x \in H_X, \, Z(z) \ket{\psi} = \ket{\psi} \, \forall z \in H_Z \right\},
\]
which can also be written as
\[
CSS(H_X, H_Z) = \text{Span}\Big\{ \frac{1}{\sqrt{|H_X|}} \sum_{x \in H_X} \ket{z + x} : z \in \ker(H_Z) \Big\}\;.
\]
The code encodes $k = \log_2\left( |\ker(H_X) / \Im(H_Z^T)| \right)$ logical qubits and has distance
\[
d = \min\big\{ |w| : w \in (\ker(H_X) \setminus \Im(H_Z^T)) \cup (\ker(H_Z) \setminus \Im(H_X^T)) \big\}\;.
\]
statement_text: An [n, k, d] quantum CSS code on n qubits is a subspace C ⊆ H = ( C ^2)^ ⊗ n . It is defined by a pair of parity-check matrices H_X, H_Z such that Im (H_X^top ) perp Im (H_Z^top ) . We denote the code as C = CSS(H_X, H_Z) . Explicitly, the code subspace is given by \[ CSS(H_X, H_Z) = { ket ψ ∈ ( C ^2)^ ⊗ n : X(x) ket ψ = ket ψ ∀ x ∈ H_X, Z(z) ket ψ = ket ψ ∀ z ∈ H_Z }, \] which can also be written as \[ CSS(H_X, H_Z) = Span { frac 1 sqrt |H_X| Σ _ x ∈ H_X ket z + x : z ∈ ker (H_Z) } . \] The code encodes k = log _2 ( |ker (H_X) / Im (H_Z^T)| ) logical qubits and has distance \[ d = min { |w| : w ∈ (ker (H_X) \ Im (H_Z^T)) ∪ (ker (H_Z) \ Im (H_X^T)) } . \]
title: CSS Code

statement_text: Let C be an [M, B_q, d_q] CSS code. Then there exist F, G ∈ F _2^ B_q × M such that X(F_1), ... , X(F_ B_q ) are B_q linearly independent logical operators composed only of X and identity operators, and Z(G_1), ... , Z(G_ B_q ) are B_q linearly independent logical operators composed only of Z and identity operators. Moreover, for each i, j ∈ {1, ... , B_q} , these operators satisfy \[ X(F_i) Z(G_j) = (-1)^ 1(i=j) Z(G_j) X(F_i). \] Finally, it holds that F H_Z^T = G H_X^T = 0 .

label: lem:stabilizer-decomposition
paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
statement_tex:
\label{lem:stabilizer-decomposition}
Let $C=CSS(H_X, H_Z)$ be a stabilizer code on $n$ qubits.
Let
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{S} = \Big\{ (a, b) \,\Big|\, a, b \in \mathbb{F}_2^n,\, \exists r,s \text{ s.t. } & |a \vee b| \text{ is minimized, and } (a, b) \text{ is lex smallest }\\
&~\text{ among all } (a', b') \text{ with } H_X b' = r \text{ and } H_Z a' = s \Big\}\;.
\end{align*}
Then any $n$-qubit state $\ket{\psi}$ has a decomposition of the form
\[
\ket{\psi} = \sum_{(a,b)\in \mathcal{S}} \alpha_{a,b} X(a)Z(b)  \ket{\eta_{a,b}}\;,
\]
where $\|\ket{\eta_{a,b}}\|=1$, $\ket{\eta_{a,b}} \in C$, the terms $X(a)Z(b)  \ket{\eta_{a,b}}$ are pairwise othogonal, and $\sum_{a,b}|\alpha_{a,b}|^2=1$.

Then any n -qubit state ket ψ has a decomposition of the form \[ ket ψ = Σ _ (a,b) ∈ S α_ a,b X(a)Z(b) ket η_ a,b , \] where |ket η_ a,b |=1 , ket η_ a,b ∈ C , the terms X(a)Z(b) ket η_ a,b are pairwise othogonal, and Σ _ a,b |α_ a,b |^2=1 .
title: Stabilizer decomposition,

\label{def:d_qltc}

Let $ {\cal S}$ be defined as in Lemma \ref{lem:stabilizer-decomposition}.
Any $n$-qubit quantum state $\ket{\psi}$ decomposes as
\[
\ket{\psi} = \sum_{(a,b)\in {\cal S}} \alpha_{a,b} X(a)Z(b)  \ket{\eta_{a,b}},

statement_tex:
\label{fact:decoder}
Let $C_q$ be the qLTC family from Theorem~\ref{thm:qltc}. Then $C_q$ admits an efficient (in fact, linear time) decoder $\tD_q$ for errors of weight up to $\eta_q d_q$, where $d_q$ is the quantum distance of the code and $\eta_q$ is a constant.
Furthermore, let $\tD_{W}$ be the decoder in basis $W\in\{X,Z\}$. We take this to be the map $\texttt{D}_W: \F_2^{M} \rightarrow \F_2^{B_W}$ that to a noisy vector returns the ``closest'' element of the code $H_W$
\footnote{Sometimes, the decoder is taken to be a map $\tD'_W: \F_2^{c_W} \rightarrow \F_2^{M}$ that to a syndrome returns an associated error vector, where $c_W$ would be the number of parity checks.
With our notation,  $\tD_W(x)= (E_W)^{-1}(x+\tD'_W(H_W x))$
where (provided the decoder succeeds) $x+\tD'_W(H_W x)\in \ker H_W$
so it is indeed possible to efficiently find a unique preimage of it under the generator matrix $E_W$.}

Then $\tD_W$ is local in the sense that there exists $\eta_W=\Omega(1/\poly\log M)$ such that  for any $e\in\{0,1\}^M$ such that $|e|<\eta_W d_{q,W}$ and any $z\in\{0,1\}^{B_W}$,  then $|\tE_Wz+\tE_W\tD_W(E_W z +e )| \leq (1/\eta_W)  |e|$.

label: def:qiop
paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
statement_tex:
\label{def:qiop}
Let $n \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ denote the instance size, and let
$m : \mathbb{Z}_+ \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_+$ be a non-decreasing, even-valued function representing the total number of messages as a function of the instance size. Define $h(n) := m(n)/2$.

An $m$-message \emph{quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof system} (qIPCP) is specified by a tuple of quantum algorithms
$\texttt{V} = (\texttt{V}_1, \texttt{V}_2, \ldots, \texttt{V}_{h+1})$.

For each $i \in [h+1]$, the verifier’s algorithm $\texttt{V}_i$ takes $x$ as input and acts on registers as follows:
\begin{align*}
\big((\mathsf{R}_{i-1}), (\mathsf{R}_1, \ldots, \mathsf{R}_{i-2}, \mathsf{W}_i, \ldots, \mathsf{W}_h)\big)
\longrightarrow
\big((\mathsf{W}_i, \mathsf{J}_i), (\mathsf{R}_1, \ldots, \mathsf{R}_{i-1}, \mathsf{W}_{i+1}, \ldots, \mathsf{W}_h)\big),
\end{align*}
where
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathsf{R}_i$ is the quantum prover’s message register, for each $i \in \{-1, 0, \ldots, h\}$,
\item $\mathsf{W}_i$ is the quantum witness register, for each $i \in \{1, \ldots, h+1\}$,
\item $\mathsf{J}_i$ is the verifier’s classical message register, for each $i \in \{1, \ldots, h+1\}$.
\item $\mathsf{R}_{-1}$, $\mathsf{R}_0$, and $\mathsf{W}_{h+1}$  are all empty registers.
\item The register $\mathsf{J}$ is initialized to the all-zero classical string.
\item The register $\mathsf{W}=(\mathsf{W}_i)_{i\in[h]}$ is initialized to a quantum witness for the input $x$.
\end{itemize}

Each verifier algorithm $\texttt{V}_i$ must be implementable in polynomial time.

Let $I = \{1, \ldots, h\}$.
A \emph{prover strategy} is defined by a collection of quantum channels $\{\mathbb{P}_i\}_{i \in I}$ (possibly depending on $x$) and a private quantum register $\mathsf{P}$ initialized with an quantum state, where each $\mathbb{P}_i$ acts as:
\[
((\mathsf{W}_i, \mathsf{J}_i), \mathsf{P}) \longrightarrow (\mathsf{R}_i, \mathsf{P}).
\]

The first (classical) bit of the register $\mathsf{J}_{h+1}$ in the output of $\texttt{V}_{h+1}$ represents the verifier’s final decision to accept or reject.
Let $\omega(\texttt{V}, \ket{\phi})$ denote the value of the interactive game defined by $\texttt{V}_x$ when the initial state of the entire system is $\ket{\phi}$. That is, $\omega(\texttt{V}, \ket{\phi})$ is the maximum acceptance probability of $\texttt{V}$ over all prover strategies $\{\mathbb{P}_i\}_{i \in I}$, where $\ket{\phi}$ is defined on the joint quantum register $\mathsf{WP}$.

\paragraph{Resource bounds.}
We define the resource complexity of the system as follows:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Communication complexity:} The verifier $\texttt{V}$ has communication complexity $l : \mathbb{Z}_+ \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_+$ if
    \[
    l(n) \geq \sum_{i \in [h(n)]} l_i(n),
    \]
    where $l_i(n)$ is the total size (in qubits) of the registers $\mathsf{R}_i, \mathsf{J}_i, \mathsf{W}_i$.

    \item \textbf{Query complexity:} The verifier $\texttt{V}$ has query complexity $q : \mathbb{Z}_+ \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_+$ if
    \[
    q(n) \geq \sum_{i \in [h(n)+1]} q_i(n),
    \]
    where $q_i(n)$ is the number of qubits accessed by $\texttt{V}_i$ in the registers $(\mathsf{R}_1, \ldots, \mathsf{R}_{i-1}, \mathsf{W}_i, \ldots, \mathsf{W}_h)$.
\end{itemize}
statement_text: Let n ∈ Z _+ denote the instance size, and let m : Z _+ → Z _+ be a non-decreasing, even-valued function representing the total number of messages as a function of the instance size. Define h(n) := m(n)/2 . An m -message quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof system (qIPCP) is specified by a tuple of quantum algorithms tt V = (tt V _1, tt V _2, ... , tt V _ h+1 ) . For each i ∈ [h+1] , the verifier’s algorithm tt V _i takes x as input and acts on registers as follows: (( R _ i-1 ), ( R _1, ... , R _ i-2 , W _i, ... , W _h) ) longrightarrow (( W _i, J _i), ( R _1, ... , R _ i-1 , W _ i+1 , ... , W _h) ), where R _i is the quantum prover’s message register, for each i ∈ {-1, 0, ... , h} , W _i is the quantum witness register, for each i ∈ {1, ... , h+1} , J _i is the verifier’s classical message register, for each i ∈ {1, ... , h+1} . R _ -1 , R _0 , and W _ h+1 are all empty registers. The register J is initialized to the all-zero classical string. The register W =( W _i)_ i ∈ [h] is initialized to a quantum witness for the input x . Each verifier algorithm tt V _i must be implementable in polynomial time. Let I = {1, ... , h} . A prover strategy is defined by a collection of quantum channels { P _i}_ i ∈ I (possibly depending on x ) and a private quantum register P initialized with an quantum state, where each P _i acts as: \[ (( W _i, J _i), P ) longrightarrow ( R _i, P ). \] The first (classical) bit of the register J _ h+1 in the output of tt V _ h+1 represents the verifier’s final decision to accept or reject. Let ω(tt V , ket φ ) denote the value of the interactive game defined by tt V _x when the initial state of the entire system is ket φ . That is, ω(tt V , ket φ ) is the maximum acceptance probability of tt V over all prover strategies { P _i}_ i ∈ I , where ket φ is defined on the joint quantum register WP . paragraph Resource bounds. We define the resource complexity of the system as follows: bf Communication complexity: The verifier tt V has communication complexity l : Z _+ → Z _+ if \[ l(n) ≥ Σ _ i ∈ [h(n)] l_i(n), \] where l_i(n) is the total size (in qubits) of the registers R _i, J _i, W _i . bf Query complexity: The verifier tt V has query complexity q : Z _+ → Z _+ if \[ q(n) ≥ Σ _ i ∈ [h(n)+1] q_i(n), \] where q_i(n) is the number of qubits accessed by tt V _i in the registers ( R _1, ... , R _ i-1 , W _i, ... , W _h) .
title: Quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof system

paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
statement_text: A quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof system for a promise problem (S_ yes , S_ no ) satisfies the following: Let ω(tt V , ket φ _ WP ) be defined as in Definition . The system must satisfy: normal Completeness: There exists a constant c ∈ (0,1] such that for all x ∈ S_ yes , the maximum acceptance probability satisfies max _ ket ψ ω(tt V , ket ψ _ W ket 0 _ P ) ≥ c . That is, there exists a quantum witness ket ψ and an honest prover strategy under which the verifier accepts with probability at least c . normal Soundness: There exists a constant s ∈ [0, c) such that for all x ∈ S_ no , the maximum acceptance probability satisfies max _ ket φ ω(tt V , ket φ _ WP ) ≤ s . That is, no combination of prover strategy, prover's initial state, and jointly entangled quantum witness can cause the verifier to accept a no-instance with probability greater than s .
title: Quantum interactive probabilistically checkable proof systems for a promise problem

label: def:amplified-hamiltonian
paper_title: Probabilistically Checking Quantum Proofs, with Interaction
statement_tex:
\label{def:amplified-hamiltonian}
Let $H$ be a $k$-local Hamiltonian on $n$ qubits expressed as an expectation over $m$ projection terms,
\[
H = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i\in[m]} \Pi_i.
\]
where the local terms of $H$ can be efficiently and equitably partitioned into
$g=O(1)$ commuting layers, indexed by $\chi\in[g]$.
We denote
\[
H_\chi = \mathbb{E}_{i\in[m_\chi]}[\Pi_i^{\chi}],
\quad
w_\chi = \frac{m_\chi}{m} = \Omega(g^{-1}),
\]
where $w_\chi$ represents the relative weight of clauses assigned to layer~$\chi$, $ H = \E_{\chi} H_\chi$.

For any integer parameter $t\ge 1$, we define the \emph{amplified Hamiltonian} as
\begin{align}
H^{(t)}
=
I - \mathbb{E}_{\chi}
\bigotimes_{j\in [t]}\!\Big(
\prod_{i\in[m_\chi]} (I - \Pi_i^{\chi})
\Big)
,
\end{align}
where, $\mathbb{E}_{\chi}$ indicates sampling $\chi$ from the distribution $(w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_g)$ over $[g]$.

\item The verifier samples queries $(j_1,\ldots,j_Q)\in [M]^Q$ for the code tester $\texttt{L}_W$, where $Q$ is the query complexity.
\item The verifier initializes a single-qubit register $\mathsf{T}'$ and a $Q$-qubit register $\mathsf{T}$ in state $\ket{0}$.

Let $G = (V, E)$ be an undirected graph.  
    A \emph{tree decomposition} of $G$ is a pair $(T, \{X_t\}_{t \in V(T)})$, 
    where $T$ is a tree and each bag $X_t \subseteq V(G)$ is such that
    (i) $\cup_t X_t = V(G)$, 
    (ii) for every $\{u, v\} \in E(G)$, there is an $X_t$ such that $u, v \in X_t$, and 
    (iii) for every $u \in V(G)$, the set of nodes $\{ t \in V(T) \mid u \in X_t \}$ 
        is a connected subtree in $T$.  
    The \emph{width} of the tree decomposition is $\max_t |X_t|-1$.  
    The \emph{treewidth} of $G$ is the minimum width tree decomposition of $G$.

We say that a tree decomposition $(T,\{X_t\}_{t\in V(T)})$ is \emph{nice} if it is a rooted tree with root $r$; $X_r=\emptyset$ and $X_\ell=\emptyset$ for every leaf $\ell$ of $T$; and every non-leaf node $t\in V(T)$ is one of the following three types:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
        \item \textsl{Introduce node:} a node $t$ with exactly one child $t'$ such that $X_t=X_{t'}\cup\{v\}$ for some $v\notin X_{t'}$; in this case, we say that $v$ is \emph{introduced} at $t$.
        \item \textsl{Forget node:} a node $t$ with exactly one child $t'$ such that $X_t=X_{t'}\setminus\{v\}$ for some $v\in X_{t'}$; in this case, we say $v$ is \emph{forgotten} at $t$.
        \item \textsl{Join node:} a node $t$ with exactly two children $t_1,t_2$ such that $X_t=X_{t_1}=X_{t_2}$.
    \end{itemize}
statement_text: We say that a tree decomposition (T,{X_t}_ t ∈ V(T) ) is nice if it is a rooted tree with root r ; X_r= ∅ and X_ell = ∅ for every leaf ell of T ; and every non-leaf node t ∈ V(T) is one of the following three types: sl Introduce node: a node t with exactly one child t' such that X_t=X_ t' ∪ {v} for some v ∉ X_ t' ; in this case, we say that v is introduced at t . sl Forget node: a node t with exactly one child t' such that X_t=X_ t' smallsetminus {v} for some v ∈ X_ t' ; in this case, we say v is forgotten at t . sl Join node: a node t with exactly two children t_1,t_2 such that X_t=X_ t_1 =X_ t_2 .

Then, for any class $\cF$ of VC dimension $d$, there is a $\poly(n,T)$-time algorithm that, given an agnostic ERM oracle for $\cF$, achieves sublinear expected regret in the agnostic setting for all $\dist^\star$ evolving according to~\cref{eq:lds} with $A^\star \in [-B,B]^{n \times n}$ with $\rho(A^\star) \le 1$.
statement_text: Let B>0 be arbitrary, and let ρ( · ) denote the spectral radius of a matrix. Then, for any class cF of VC dimension d , there is a poly (n,T) -time algorithm that, given an agnostic ERM oracle for cF , achieves sublinear expected regret in the agnostic setting for all P^star evolving according to cref eq:lds with A^star ∈ [-B,B]^ n × n with ρ(A^star ) ≤ 1 .
title: cref thm:lds

label: assumption:p-star-cond
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{assumption:p-star-cond}
    The learner has access to a conditionally simulatable process $\dist$ that approximates $\dist^\star$. That is, the learner has access to an oracle $\condoracle_{\dist}$ that, when queried on a prefix $\seq x_{1:t} \in \cX^t$, returns an independent sample from $\dist(\cdot\mid \seq x_{1:t})$.
statement_text: The learner has access to a conditionally simulatable process P that approximates P^star . That is, the learner has access to an oracle O ^ cond _ P that, when queried on a prefix x_ 1:t ∈ cX ^t , returns an independent sample from P( · mid x_ 1:t ) .

label: thm:informal-efficient
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{thm:informal-efficient}
    Assume conditional sampling access to simulator $\dist$. Then, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for the class $\cF$ of VC dimension $d$, there exists an algorithm running in $\poly(T)$ time, with regret in the agnostic setting
    \[
    \En \reg(\cF,T) \lesssim \sqrt{d T (1 +\KL{\dist^\star}{\dist})}.

statement_text: Assume conditional sampling access to simulator P . Then, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for the class cF of VC dimension d , there exists an algorithm running in poly (T) time, with regret in the agnostic setting \[ E Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt d T (1 + KL dvr * P^star P ) . \]

label: thm:stat-dist-trans
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem StatDistTrans Let cF be a VC dimension d class, and let P^star be an arbitrary distribution in Δ(cX ^T) . Let N ∈ bbN be arbitrary. Then, there exists an algorithm that makes at most N oracle calls to O _ P , at most N^ O(d) calls to a realizable ERM oracle w.r.t. cF , and achieves regret \[ E Reg lesssim d log T + frac dT N + d · KL dvr * P^star P + frac T log (1 + N/T ) · KL dvr * P^star P . \]

label: lemma:cover-analysis
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: lemma CoverAnalysis Let Z = (Z_1, ... ,Z_N ) bar P^ ⊗ N , and cG (Z) be an improper cover of cF constructed as follows cG (Z) := { Alg _ M3 ((Z_i,y_i)_ i ∈ [N] ) colon (y_i )_ i ∈ [N] ∈ .cF vert _ Z }. Then, for any f ∈ cF , we have \[ E _ Z E _ X P min _ g ∈ cG (Z) | f-g |_ X lesssim frac d N .\]

label: thm:realizable-lb
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem RealizableLB For any d ∈ bbN , N ≥ 2 , and D ∈ bbN ∪ {0} , there exists a class cF of VC dimension d , such that, for any learning algorithm that draws at most N unconditional samples from O _P , there exists a choice of distributions (P, P^star ) with KL dvr * P^star P ≤ D and f^star ∈ cF such that \[ E Reg (cF , T) gtrsim (d + frac d T N + D + D frac T log N ) ∧ T \]

label: thm:realizable-erm-oracle-lb
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem RealizableERMOracleLB There is a sufficiently small constant c so that the following holds. For any d, N, T ∈ bbN satisfying TN ≤ 2^ cd , and any learning algorithm Alg that draws at most N unconditional samples from P^star and makes at most N agnostic ERM oracle queries, there exists a class cF of VC dimension at most d and a distribution P^star so that Alg suffers regret E Reg (cF , T) gtrsim T .

label: thm:agnostic-impossibility
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem AgnosticImpossibility Let cF be the class of thresholds on the [0,1] interval. label: thm:cond-oracle-eff
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem CondOracleEff Let cF be a VC dimension d class. Then, there exists an algorithm that runs in poly (T) time and, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle over cF and a conditional sampling oracle O ^ cond _ P , achieves the following expected regret bound in the agnostic setting: \[ E Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT (1 + KL dvr * P^star P ) . \]

label: lemma:rel-admissibility
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{lemma}{RelAdmissibility}
    \label{lemma:rel-admissibility}
    Let $\cF$ be an arbitrary function class, and consider any $t \le T$. Suppose the simulator is exact, that is $\dist = \dist^\star$, and let $q_t$ be as in~\cref{eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy}. Then, for any history $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, we have
\[
\En_{X_t \sim \dist_t^\star(\cdot \mid \seq X_{1:t-1})} \exp\left( \sup_{Y_t}\left[\eta \En_{\hat  Y_t \sim  q_t} \ind\{ \hat Y_t  \neq Y_t\} + \eta \rel(\seq S_{1:t})\right] \right) \le \exp\left( \eta \rel(\seq S_{1:t-1}) \right).
\]
Thus, conditioned on $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, $\En_{X_t} \sup_{Y_t} \Phi_t \le \Phi_{t-1}$, and therefore, $\{\Phi_t\}_{t \le T}$ is a supermartingale.
statement_text: lemma RelAdmissibility Let cF be an arbitrary function class, and consider any t ≤ T . Suppose the simulator is exact, that is P = P^star , and let q_t be as in cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy . Then, for any history S_ 1:t-1 , we have \[ E _ X_t P_t^star ( · mid X_ 1:t-1 ) exp ( sup _ Y_t [η E _ hat Y_t q_t m 1 { hat Y_t ≠ Y_t} + η Rel (S_ 1:t ) ] ) ≤ exp ( η Rel (S_ 1:t-1 ) ). \] Thus, conditioned on S_ 1:t-1 , E _ X_t sup _ Y_t Φ_t ≤ Φ_ t-1 , and therefore, {Φ_t}_ t ≤ T is a supermartingale.

label: lemma:idealized-regret
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: lemma IdealizedRegret Let cF be a VC dimension d class. Then, for every η > 0 , an algorithm that plays according to cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy achieves the following expected regret bound in the agnostic setting: \[ E _ P^star Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT + frac 1 η KL dvr * P^star P + η T. \]

label: prop:closed-form
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: proposition ClosedFormStrategy For a history S_ 1:t and a covariate X_t , let G _ y (W^t) := sup _ f ∈ cF [ Σ _ s=t+1 ^T ε_s frac 2f(X_s)-1 2 - L_ t-1 (f) - m 1 {f(X_t) ≠ y} ]. Then, q_t as in cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy can be written as \[ q_t(S_ 1:t-1 , X_t) = frac 1 2 + frac 1 2η log (frac E exp (η G _ 1 (W^t)) E exp (η G _ 0 (W^t)) ) \]

label: lemma:mse-bound
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{lemma}{MSEBound}
    \label{lemma:mse-bound}
    For an arbitrary history $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, an arbitrary covariate $X_t$, and $\eta\le 1$, we have
    \[
    \En\left[(\hat q_t - q_t)^2\right] \lesssim \frac{\nvar}{N},
    \quad \text{where} \quad
    \nvar := \max_{y \in \{0,1\}} \frac{\En \exp(2\eta \off{y}(\seq W^t))}{\left(\En \exp(\eta \off{y}(\seq W^t))\right)^2},
    \]
    is the normalized variance of the exponential moment.
statement_text: lemma MSEBound For an arbitrary history S_ 1:t-1 , an arbitrary covariate X_t , and η ≤ 1 , we have \[ E [(hat q_t - q_t)^2 ] lesssim frac v_t N , quad where quad v_t := max _ y ∈ {0,1} frac E exp (2η G _ y (W^t)) ( E exp (η G _ y (W^t)) )^2 , \] is the normalized variance of the exponential moment.

label: lemma:v-eta
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{lemma}{VEtaBound}
\label{lemma:v-eta}
    For an arbitrary history $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, an arbitrary covariate $X_t$, and $\eta\le 1$, we have
    \[
    \nvar \le \exp(2\eta) \En \exp\left(2\eta \sup_{f} \sum_{s= t+1}^T \varepsilon_s \frac{2f(X_s) - 1}{2}\right) \lesssim 
    \exp\left(O(\eta \sqrt{dT} + \eta^2 T)\right).
    \]
statement_text: lemma VEtaBound For an arbitrary history S_ 1:t-1 , an arbitrary covariate X_t , and η ≤ 1 , we have \[ v_t ≤ exp (2η) E exp (2η sup _ f Σ _ s= t+1 ^T ε_s frac 2f(X_s) - 1 2 ) lesssim exp (O(η sqrt dT + η^2 T) ). \]

label: lemma:reg-mgf-intermediate
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: lemma RegMGFIntermediate Let cF be a VC dimension d class. Then, an algorithm that plays according to cref eq:plug-in with N samples per step and inverse temperature η achieves the following regret bound E _ P^star Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT + η T + frac 1 η KL dvr * P^star P + T sqrt frac exp (O(η sqrt dT + η^2 T)) N .

label: cor:sim-families
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: corollary LearnabilitySublinearKL Let cP be a family of processes with cR (cP ) ≤ o(T) , and cF a bounded VC dimension class. Then, there exists a (possibly inefficient) algorithm that achieves sublinear agnostic regret for every P^star ∈ cP . Moreover, for every D ∈ bbN , there exists cP with cR (cP ) ≤ D ∧ T and a VC class of dimension 1 , such that any algorithm suffers regret Ω(D ∧ T) even in the realizable setting.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label[definition]{def:samplable}
    Let $p \colon \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$ be a time bound. Then, distribution $P \in \Delta(\Sigma^\infty)$ is $p$-time samplable iff there exists a program $\pi$ such that, for every $t \ge 1$ and $s \sim \Unif(\{0,1\}^{p(t)})$, we have $ U^{p(t)}(\pi, 1^{t}\# s) \sim P_{1:t}.$
    For a distribution $P \in \Delta(\Sigma^\infty)$, let
    \[
    K^p(P) = \min\left\{|\pi| \colon U^{p(t)}(\pi, 1^{t}\# s) \sim P_{1:t} \text{ for every } t \ge 1, \text{ where } s \sim \Unif(\{0,1\}^{p(t)}) \right\}
    \]
    be the (time-bounded) Kolmogorov complexity of $P$ if $P$ is $p$-time samplable.
statement_text: Let p colon N → N be a time bound. Then, distribution P ∈ Δ(Σ^ ∞ ) is p -time samplable iff there exists a program π such that, for every t ≥ 1 and s Unif ({0,1}^ p(t) ) , we have U^ p(t) (π, 1^ t \# s) P_ 1:t . For a distribution P ∈ Δ(Σ^ ∞ ) , let \[ K^p(P) = min {|π| colon U^ p(t) (π, 1^ t \# s) P_ 1:t for every t ≥ 1, where s Unif ({0,1}^ p(t) ) } \] be the (time-bounded) Kolmogorov complexity of P if P is p -time samplable.
title: Time-bounded samplable distribution

label: thm:universal-dist
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem UniversalDist Let p colon N → N be a time-constructible bound. There exists a time bound p'(t) = poly (p(t)) and a sequence of measures {μ^t}_ t ≥ 1 , with each μ^t ∈ Δ (Σ^*) samplable in time p'(t) that satisfy the following. For any p -time samplable distribution P and any x ∈ cX ^t we have \[ log frac P_ 1:t (le x rangle ) μ^t(le xrangle ) ≤ K^p(P) + 2 log K^p(P) + O(1). \]
title: Universal samplable distribution

label: thm:samplable-nature
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem SamplableNature Suppose the distribution P^star of nature is p -time samplable (as per Cref def:samplable ). Let cF be any class of VC dimension d . Then, there exists an algorithm that, given access to a realizable ERM oracle w.r.t. cF , runs in time poly (T^d, p(T)) and for any f^star ∈ cF , achieves regret \[ E Reg (cF , T ) lesssim d log (T) + d · 2^ K^p(P^star ) + 2 log K^p(P^star ) . \]

label: thm:lds
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{theorem}{ThmLDS}
\label{thm:lds}
    Let $\cF$ be a class of VC dimension $d$, and let $R, B \ge 1$ and $\sigma > 0$ be arbitrary. There is a $\poly(n, T)$-time algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for $\cF$, the noise scale $\sigma$, and the magnitude bound $B$, achieves expected regret
    \[
    \En \reg(\cF, T) \lesssim \sqrt{dT} \left(1 + \sqrt{n^3 \log\left(nBT(R/\sigma + 1)\right)}\right)
    \]
    in the agnostic setting, simultaneously for every $\dist^\star = \dist^{A^\star}$ with $A^\star \in \Theta$ satisfying $\rho(A^\star) \le 1$ and initial state $X_0 \in \ball(0,R)$.
statement_text: theorem ThmLDS Let cF be a class of VC dimension d , and let R, B ≥ 1 and σ > 0 be arbitrary. There is a poly (n, T) -time algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for cF , the noise scale σ , and the magnitude bound B , achieves expected regret \[ E Reg (cF , T) lesssim sqrt dT (1 + sqrt n^3 log (nBT(R/σ + 1) ) ) \] in the agnostic setting, simultaneously for every P^star = P^ A^star with A^star ∈ Θ satisfying ρ(A^star ) ≤ 1 and initial state X_0 ∈ cB (0,R) .

label: thm:glauber
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{theorem}{ThmGlauber}
\label{thm:glauber}
    Let $\cF$ be a class of VC dimension $d$, and let $B \ge 1$. There is a $\poly(n, T, B)$-time algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for $\cF$, achieves expected regret
    \[
    \En \reg(\cF, T) \lesssim \sqrt{dT} \cdot \left(1 + \sqrt{n^2 \log(BTn)}\right)
    \]
    in the agnostic setting, simultaneously for every $\dist^\star = \dist^{\theta^\star}$ with $\theta^\star \in \Theta$ and initial state $X_0 \in \{0,1\}^n$.
statement_text: theorem ThmGlauber Let cF be a class of VC dimension d , and let B ≥ 1 . There is a poly (n, T, B) -time algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle for cF , achieves expected regret \[ E Reg (cF , T) lesssim sqrt dT · (1 + sqrt n^2 log (BTn) ) \] in the agnostic setting, simultaneously for every P^star = P^ θ^star with θ^star ∈ Θ and initial state X_0 ∈ {0,1}^n .

label: def:vc
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{def:vc}
For a binary class $\cF \subset \{0,1\}^{\cX}$, the VC dimension of $\cF$ is the largest integer $d$ for which there exists a subset $\{x_1,\ldots,x_d\} \subset \cX$ such that, for any labels $y_1,\ldots,y_d \in \{0,1\}$, there exists $f \in \cF$ such that $f(x_t) = y_t$ for every $t \in [d]$.
statement_text: For a binary class cF ⊂ {0,1}^ cX , the VC dimension of cF is the largest integer d for which there exists a subset {x_1, ... ,x_d} ⊂ cX such that, for any labels y_1, ... ,y_d ∈ {0,1} , there exists f ∈ cF such that f(x_t) = y_t for every t ∈ [d] .
title: VC dimension

label: lemma:sauer-shelah
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:sauer-shelah}
    For a binary class $\cF$ with VC dimension $d$, and any finite set $S \subset \cX$, the number of distinct labelings of $S$ by functions in $\cF$ is at most \[
    \sum_{i=0}^d \binom{|S|}{i} \leq \left(\frac{e |S|}{d}\right)^d.
    \]
statement_text: For a binary class cF with VC dimension d , and any finite set S ⊂ cX , the number of distinct labelings of S by functions in cF is at most \[ Σ _ i=0 ^d binom |S| i ≤ (frac e |S| d )^d. \]
title: Sauer--Shelah Lemma

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
Let $\cF \subset \{0,1\}^\cX$ be a binary class of functions. The Littlestone dimension is the largest integer $d$ such that the following holds. There exists a tree $\mathbf x$ such that, for any choice of signs $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_d \in\{\pm 1\}$ there exists a function $f \in \cF$ such that
        \[
        f(\tree x_t(\varepsilon_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_{t-1})) = \frac{\varepsilon_t + 1}{2},
        \]
        for every $t \in [d]$.
statement_text: Let cF ⊂ {0,1}^cX be a binary class of functions. The Littlestone dimension is the largest integer d such that the following holds. There exists a tree x such that, for any choice of signs ε_1, ... ,ε_d ∈ {pm 1} there exists a function f ∈ cF such that \[ f(x_t(ε_ 1 , ... ,ε_ t-1 )) = frac ε_t + 1 2 , \] for every t ∈ [d] .
title: Littlestone Dimension

label: prop:littlestone-hardness
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{prop:littlestone-hardness}
        Let $\cF \subset \{0,1\}^\cX$ be a class of infinite Littlestone dimension, and let $\tree x$ be a depth-$T$ Littlestone tree. Consider nature's strategy that first samples $\varepsilon_t \sim \Unif(\{\pm 1\})$ independently for each $t \in [T]$. Then, at step $t \in [T]$, the nature presents the learner with $X_t = \tree x_t(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_{t-1})$ labeled by $Y_t := (\varepsilon_t + 1)/2$. Then, any learner suffers $T/2$ regret in this setting.
statement_text: Let cF ⊂ {0,1}^cX be a class of infinite Littlestone dimension, and let x be a depth- T Littlestone tree. Consider nature's strategy that first samples ε_t Unif ({pm 1}) independently for each t ∈ [T] . Then, at step t ∈ [T] , the nature presents the learner with X_t = x_t(ε_1, ... ,ε_ t-1 ) labeled by Y_t := (ε_t + 1)/2 . Then, any learner suffers T/2 regret in this setting.

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label[definition]{def:littlestone-consistent-function}
        Let $\tree x$ be a depth-$T$ tree. We say that a function $f$ is consistent with the path $(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_T)$ in $\tree x$ iff
        \[
        f(\tree x_t(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_{t-1})) = \frac{\varepsilon_t + 1}{2}.
        \]
statement_text: Let x be a depth- T tree. We say that a function f is consistent with the path (ε_1, ... ,ε_T) in x iff \[ f(x_t(ε_1, ... ,ε_ t-1 )) = frac ε_t + 1 2 . \]

label: lemma:mult-pinkser
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:mult-pinkser}
        For any $P, Q\in\Delta([0,1])$, we have
        \[

        \]
statement_text: For any P, Q ∈ Δ([0,1]) , we have \[ E _ Q X ≤ 3 E _P X + 4 KL dvr * P Q . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: For any P,Q , λ > e we have \[ P_ P [frac d P d Q > λ ] ≤ frac KL dvr * P Q log (λ/e) \]

\label{lemma:log-plus}
        For any $P,Q$ we have

statement_text: For any P,Q we have \[ E _ P log ^+ (frac d P d Q ) ≤ KL dvr * P Q + 1. \]

label: lemma:price-of-sampling
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:price-of-sampling}
    Let $\cF_d$ be the class as defined in~\cref{eq:d-dim-thresholds}. For any $N \in \mathbb N$ and for any learning algorithm that draws at most $N$ unconditional samples from $\dist^\star$, there exists a choice of $\dist^\star$ and $f^\star \in \cF_d$ such that
    \[
    \En \reg(\cF_d, T) \gtrsim \frac{T (d \land N)}{N}.
    \]
statement_text: Let cF _d be the class as defined in cref eq:d-dim-thresholds . For any N ∈ N and for any learning algorithm that draws at most N unconditional samples from P^star , there exists a choice of P^star and f^star ∈ cF _d such that \[ E Reg (cF _d, T) gtrsim frac T (d ∧ N) N . \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label[lemma]{lemma:linear-kl-lb}
    Let $\cF_1$ be as in~\cref{eq:d-dim-thresholds}. For every $D \in \mathbb N$, there exist a family $\cP_D$ of distributions over $\cX^T$ and a simulator $\dist$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]

        \[
        \En \reg(\cF_1, T) \ge \frac{D \land T}{2}.
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
statement_text: Let cF _1 be as in cref eq:d-dim-thresholds . For every D ∈ N , there exist a family cP _D of distributions over cX ^T and a simulator P such that: max _ P^star ∈ cP _D KL dvr * P^star P ≤ D ∧ T . For any learning algorithm, even one granted full knowledge of P , there exists P^star ∈ cP _D and a labeling f^star ∈ cF _1 for which \[ E Reg (cF _1, T) ≥ frac D ∧ T 2 . \]

label: lemma:kl-sampling-lb
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:kl-sampling-lb}
    Let $\cF_1$ be as in~\cref{eq:d-dim-thresholds}. For any $N \ge 2$, $D \in \mathbb N$, and for any learning algorithm that draws at most $N$ unconditional samples from $\dist$, there exists a choice of $(\dist, \dist^\star)$ with $\KL{\dist^\star}{\dist} \le D$ and $f^\star \in \cF_1$ such that

For any N ≥ 2 , D ∈ N , and for any learning algorithm that draws at most N unconditional samples from P , there exists a choice of (P, P^star ) with KL dvr * P^star P ≤ D and f^star ∈ cF _1 such that \[ E Reg (cF _1, T) gtrsim T ( frac D log (N) ∧ 1 ) \]

label: lem:close-uniform
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lem:close-uniform}
Fix any subset $\cK \subset [K]$ and step $j \in [J]$, and set $\eps= \frac{2j |\cK|}{K}$. Then with probability at least $1-\sqrt{\eps}$ over the execution of $\tAlg$ up to step $j$ and the choice of $\cF$, the distribution of the tuple of functions $(h_k)_{k \in \cK}$ conditioned on $\scrF\^j$ is $\sqrt{\eps}$-close to uniform in total variation distance.
statement_text: Fix any subset cK ⊂ [K] and step j ∈ [J] , and set ε= frac 2j |cK | K . Then with probability at least 1- sqrt ε over the execution of widetilde Alg up to step j and the choice of cF , the distribution of the tuple of functions (h_k)_ k ∈ cK conditioned on scrF \^j is sqrt ε -close to uniform in total variation distance.

label: prop:approx-agnostic-lb
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: proposition ApproxAgnosticLB Consider the class cF of thresholds on the unit interval [0,1] . Then, for any D ∈ [T] , and for any algorithm, there exists a pair (P, P^star ) such that KL dvr * P^star P = D , and the algorithm suffers regret ≥ sqrt D T in the agnostic setting.

label: lemma:lds-compressor
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:lds-compressor}
    Let $\dist$ be as defined in~\cref{eq:universal-dist-lds}. Then, for any $A^\star \in \Theta$ with $\rho(A^\star) \le 1$ and $X_0 \in \ball(0, R)$, we have
    \[
    \KL{\dist^{A^\star} (\cdot \mid X_0)}{\dist(\cdot \mid X_0)} \le O\left(n^3 \log\left(nBT(R/\sigma + 1)\right)\right).
    \]
statement_text: Let P be as defined in cref eq:universal-dist-lds . Then, for any A^star ∈ Θ with ρ(A^star ) ≤ 1 and X_0 ∈ cB (0, R) , we have \[ KL dvr * P^ A^star ( · mid X_0) P( · mid X_0) ≤ O (n^3 log (nBT(R/σ + 1) ) ). \]

label: lemma:matrix-power-growth
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:matrix-power-growth}
For any $A \in \bbR^{n \times n}$ with $\rho(A) \le 1$ and any $s \ge 1$,
\[
\norm{A^s}_{\mathrm{op}} \le n \cdot (\norm{A}_{\mathrm{op}} + 1)^{n-1} \cdot s^{n-1}.
\]
statement_text: For any A ∈ bbR ^ n × n with ρ(A) ≤ 1 and any s ≥ 1 , \[ | A^s |_ op ≤ n · ( | A |_ op + 1)^ n-1 · s^ n-1 . \]

label: prop:lds-cond-sampler
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{prop:lds-cond-sampler}
    For any $X_0, \seq X_{1:t}$, exact conditional sampling from $\dist(\cdot \mid \seq X_{1:t}, X_0)$, where $\dist$ is as in~\cref{lemma:lds-compressor}, can be implemented in $\poly(n, T)$ time per sample.
statement_text: For any X_0, X_ 1:t , exact conditional sampling from P( · mid X_ 1:t , X_0) , where P is as in cref lemma:lds-compressor , can be implemented in poly (n, T) time per sample.

label: lemma:glauber-compressor
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:glauber-compressor}
    For any $T \ge 2$, $\theta^\star \in \Theta$, and $X_0 \in \{0,1\}^n$, we have
    \[
    \KL{\dist^{\theta^\star}(\cdot \mid X_0)}{\dist(\cdot \mid X_0)} \lesssim p \log(BTn).
    \]
statement_text: For any T ≥ 2 , θ^star ∈ Θ , and X_0 ∈ {0,1}^n , we have \[ KL dvr * P^ θ^star ( · mid X_0) P( · mid X_0) lesssim p log (BTn). \]

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World

statement_text: For any X_0 ∈ {0,1}^n , conditional sampling from P( · mid I_ 1:t , X_ 1:t , X_0) , where P is as in cref lemma:glauber-compressor , can be implemented in poly (n, T, B, 1/δ) time per sample, to within total-variation error δ .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex: Consider any class $\cF$ with infinite Littlestone dimension, and consider the Littlestone tree of depth $T$. Let $\dist^\star$ be a distribution that samples a uniform path $\seq X$ in the Littlestone tree, and, for each $t \le T-1$, set $Y_t := 1$ iff $X_{t+1}$ is the right child of its parent (and sample $Y_T$ randomly). This strategy of nature forces any learner to have $\ge T/2$ regret.
statement_text: Consider any class cF with infinite Littlestone dimension, and consider the Littlestone tree of depth T . Let P^star be a distribution that samples a uniform path X in the Littlestone tree, and, for each t ≤ T-1 , set Y_t := 1 iff X_ t+1 is the right child of its parent (and sample Y_T randomly). This strategy of nature forces any learner to have ≥ T/2 regret.

label: assumption:adaptive-labels
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{assumption:adaptive-labels}
    For every $t \in [T]$, the distribution $\seq X_{t+1:T} \mid (\cH_t, Y_t, \hat Y_t)$ is given by $\dist^\star(\cdot \mid \seq X_{1:t})$.
statement_text: For every t ∈ [T] , the distribution X_ t+1:T mid (cH _t, Y_t, hat Y_t) is given by P^star ( · mid X_ 1:t ) .

paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label[proposition]{prop:adaptive-labels-impossibility}
    Let $\cF$ be the class of thresholds on the $[0,1]$ interval. For any $N \ge 1$, and for any learning algorithm that draws at most $N$ unconditional samples, there exists a choice of a distribution $\dist^\star$, a choice of realizable labels satisfying~\cref{assumption:adaptive-labels} such that
    \[
    \En \left[\sum_{t=1}^T \ind\{f^{\star}(X_t) \neq \hat{y}_t\} - \inf_{f \in\cF} \sum_{t=1}^T  \ind\{f^{\star}(X_t) \neq f(X_t) \} \right] \ge T/8.
    \]
statement_text: Let cF be the class of thresholds on the [0,1] interval. For any N ≥ 1 , and for any learning algorithm that draws at most N unconditional samples, there exists a choice of a distribution P^star , a choice of realizable labels satisfying cref assumption:adaptive-labels such that \[ E [ Σ _ t=1 ^T m 1 {f^ star (X_t) ≠ hat y _t} - inf _ f ∈ cF Σ _ t=1 ^T m 1 {f^ star (X_t) ≠ f(X_t) } ] ≥ T/8. \]

label: thm:cond-oracle-eff-adaptive-labels
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label{thm:cond-oracle-eff-adaptive-labels}
Let $\cF$ be a class of VC dimension $d$. Suppose the labels satisfy~\cref{assumption:adaptive-labels}. Then, there exists an algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle over $\cF$ and a conditional sampling oracle $\condoracle_{\dist}$, achieves expected regret bound:
    \[
    \En \reg(\cF,T) \lesssim \sqrt{dT (1 + \KL{\dist^\star}{\dist})},
    \]
    in both realizable and agnostic settings. Moreover, the algorithm runs in $\poly(T)$ time.
statement_text: Let cF be a class of VC dimension d . Suppose the labels satisfy cref assumption:adaptive-labels . Then, there exists an algorithm that, given access to an agnostic ERM oracle over cF and a conditional sampling oracle O ^ cond _ P , achieves expected regret bound: \[ E Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT (1 + KL dvr * P^star P ) , \] in both realizable and agnostic settings. Moreover, the algorithm runs in poly (T) time.

label: def:noninteracting
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{def:noninteracting}
A coalition $C\subseteq N$ is \emph{non‑interacting} if, for every $i\in C$, the payoff $u_i$
does not depend on $\sigma_{i'}$ for any $i'\in C\setminus\{i\}$ (equivalently, in a polymatrix
game, $C$ is an independent set of the interaction graph). For a non‑interacting coalition,
$u_i(y_i,\sigma_{-i}^t)=u_i(y_C,\sigma_{-C}^t)$ for all $i\in C$, so the aggregate
deviation--regret $\CDR{C}{y_C}$ coincides with the \emph{joint} coalitional deviation--regret
$\sum_t\sum_{i\in C}\big(u_i(y_C,\sigma_{-C}^t)-u_i(\sigma^t)\big)$ in which the whole coalition
deviates simultaneously.
statement_text: A coalition C ⊆ N is non‑interacting if, for every i ∈ C , the payoff u_i does not depend on σ_ i' for any i' ∈ C \ {i} (equivalently, in a polymatrix game, C is an independent set of the interaction graph). For a non‑interacting coalition, u_i(y_i,σ_ -i ^t)=u_i(y_C,σ_ -C ^t) for all i ∈ C , so the aggregate deviation--regret R ^ y_C _ C coincides with the joint coalitional deviation--regret Σ _t Σ _ i ∈ C (u_i(y_C,σ_ -C ^t)-u_i(σ^t) ) in which the whole coalition deviates simultaneously.
title: Non‑interacting coalition

label: def:edre
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{def:edre}
A profile $\sigma^\star$ is a static $(\varepsilon)$‑EDRE if
\[
\max_{a_i} u_i(a_i,\sigma^\star_{-i}) \ \le \ u_i(\sigma^\star)+\varepsilon
\quad\text{for all }i.
\]
A \emph{strict} EDRE sets $\varepsilon=0$.
statement_text: A profile σ^star is a static (ε) ‑EDRE if \[ max _ a_i u_i(a_i,σ^star _ -i ) \ ≤ \ u_i(σ^star )+ε quad for all i. \] A strict EDRE sets ε=0 .
title: Static EDRE

label: def:dynamic-edre
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{def:dynamic-edre}
Fix $L>0$ and consider entropic MD with either:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item[(A)] constant steps $0<\eta\le 1/L$ (Lyapunov monotonicity and selection to the fixed‑point set; when that set is a singleton, pointwise convergence holds for $0<\eta<1/L$), or
\item[(B)] diminishing steps $\eta_t=\eta_0/\sqrt{t}$ with $\eta_0>0$ (deviation‑regret).
\end{itemize}
We say that a static EDRE $\sigma^\star$ satisfies the dynamic properties if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{(Deviation–regret)} Under (B), for \emph{each} fixed coalition $C$ and fixed deviation $y_C$, from any interior initial condition (or under fixed exploration), for each horizon $T\ge1$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cdr-bound}
\begin{aligned}
\max_{1\le \tau\le T}\ \CDR{C}{y_C}(\tau)
&\ \le\
2|C|\sqrt{\,2T\ln\!\frac{4T}{\delta}\,}
\\[-1mm]&\quad
+\ \sqrt{T}\Bigg[
\frac{1}{\eta_0}\sum_{i\in C} D_{\!KL}(y_i\Vert \sigma_i^1)
\;+\;\eta_0\,|C|
\Bigg].
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
\item \textbf{(MD selection / invariance)} Under (A), for any interior start,
\[
\mathrm{dist}\bigl(\sigma^{t},\Fix(\mathrm{MD}_\eta)\bigr)\ \longrightarrow\ 0,
\qquad \text{and we require } \sigma^\star\in\Fix(\mathrm{MD}_\eta).
\]
If the fixed‑point set is a singleton, then for $0<\eta<1/L$ we have $\sigma^t\to\sigma^\star$.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: Fix L>0 and consider entropic MD with either: constant steps 0<η ≤ 1/L (Lyapunov monotonicity and selection to the fixed‑point set; when that set is a singleton, pointwise convergence holds for 0<η<1/L ), or diminishing steps η_t=η_0/ sqrt t with η_0>0 (deviation‑regret). We say that a static EDRE σ^star satisfies the dynamic properties if: bf (Deviation–regret) Under (B), for each fixed coalition C and fixed deviation y_C , from any interior initial condition (or under fixed exploration), for each horizon T ≥ 1 , with probability at least 1-δ , max _ 1 ≤ τ ≤ T \ R ^ y_C _ C (τ) &\ ≤ \ 2|C| sqrt 2Tln frac 4T δ [-1mm]&quad +\ sqrt T g[ frac 1 η_0 Σ _ i ∈ C D_ KL (y_iVert σ_i^1) + η_0 |C| g]. bf (MD selection / invariance) Under (A), for any interior start, \[ dist l(σ^ t , Fix ( MD _η) r)\ longrightarrow \ 0, qquad and we require σ^star ∈ Fix ( MD _η). \] If the fixed‑point set is a singleton, then for 0<η<1/L we have σ^t → σ^star .
title: Dynamic EDRE properties

label: prop:strict-edre-subset-ne
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{prop:strict-edre-subset-ne}
A profile is a strict EDRE if and only if it is a mixed Nash equilibrium.
statement_text: A profile is a strict EDRE if and only if it is a mixed Nash equilibrium.
title: Strict EDRE ⟺ NE

label: lem:eq-iter2
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_text: The game admits pure Nash equilibria (1,1) and (2,2) (both weak ), and (3,3) is a strict pure Nash equilibrium.

label: lem:sep-conv-iter2
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{lem:sep-conv-iter2}
Entropic MD on an $L$‑smooth cost potential satisfies
\[
\Psi(\sigma^{t+1})-\Psi(\sigma^t)
\;\le\;
\bigl(-\tfrac{1}{\eta}+L\bigr)\,D_{\!KL}(\sigma^{t+1}\Vert\sigma^t).
\]
Hence for $0<\eta\le 1/L$, the potential $\Psi(\sigma^t)$ is non‑increasing. If
$0<\eta<1/L$, then also $\sum_{t}D_{\!KL}(\sigma^{t+1}\Vert\sigma^t)<\infty$, so
$\|\sigma^{t+1}-\sigma^{t}\|_1\to 0$ and every $\omega$–limit point of $\{\sigma^t\}$
is a fixed point of the MD map. If the fixed‑point set is a singleton, convergence is
pointwise for $0<\eta<1/L$.
statement_text: Entropic MD on an L ‑smooth cost potential satisfies \[ Ψ(σ^ t+1 )-Ψ(σ^t) ≤ l(-tfrac 1 η +L r) D_ KL (σ^ t+1 Vert σ^t). \] Hence for 0<η ≤ 1/L , the potential Ψ(σ^t) is non‑increasing. If 0<η<1/L , then also Σ _ t D_ KL (σ^ t+1 Vert σ^t)< ∞ , so |σ^ t+1 -σ^ t |_1 → 0 and every ω –limit point of {σ^t} is a fixed point of the MD map. If the fixed‑point set is a singleton, convergence is pointwise for 0<η<1/L .
title: Potential descent and fixed points

label: lem:sep-regret-iter2
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{lem:sep-regret-iter2}
Suppose play is \emph{held} at the fixed point $(2,2)$ for $T$ rounds. The (interacting)
coalition $C=\{1,2\}$ with fixed deviation $y_C=(3,3)$ accrues \emph{joint} coalitional
deviation--regret $\sum_t\sum_{i\in C}\big(u_i(y_C,\sigma_{-C}^t)-u_i(\sigma^t)\big)=T$, which
exceeds the bound of Definition~\ref{def:dynamic-edre}(i) for large $T$.
statement_text: Suppose play is held at the fixed point (2,2) for T rounds. The (interacting) coalition C={1,2} with fixed deviation y_C=(3,3) accrues joint coalitional deviation--regret Σ _t Σ _ i ∈ C (u_i(y_C,σ_ -C ^t)-u_i(σ^t) )=T , which exceeds the bound of Definition (i) for large T .
title: Joint coalitional regret at a held profile

label: cor:sep-edre-iter2
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{cor:sep-edre-iter2}
In the congestion game above, the MD fixed‑point set contains multiple pure points (e.g., $(1,1)$ and $(2,2)$; in fact $(3,3)$ is also a NE). Unless the potential is strictly concave (it is not here), Definition~\ref{def:dynamic-edre}(ii) yields set‑valued (Cesàro) selection rather than a singleton. Hence a given NE (e.g., $(2,2)$) need not be the \emph{uniquely selected} outcome from all interior initials; Nash equilibria need not coincide with EDRE under singleton‑selection.
statement_text: In the congestion game above, the MD fixed‑point set contains multiple pure points (e.g., (1,1) and (2,2) ; in fact (3,3) is also a NE). Unless the potential is strictly concave (it is not here), Definition (ii) yields set‑valued (Cesàro) selection rather than a singleton. Hence a given NE (e.g., (2,2) ) need not be the uniquely selected outcome from all interior initials; Nash equilibria need not coincide with EDRE under singleton‑selection.
