label: lem:regret
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{lem:regret}
Assume utilities in $[0,1]$. Let players run entropic mirror descent with steps $\eta_t=\eta_0/\sqrt{t}$ for any $\eta_0>0$. From any interior initial state 
($\min_a\sigma_i^1(a)>0$ for all $i$), for any fixed coalition $C$ and deviation $y_C$,
\[
\max_{1\le \tau\le T}\ \CDR{C}{y_C}(\tau)
\;\le\;
2|C|\sqrt{2T\ln\frac{4T}{\delta}}
\;+\;\sqrt{T}\Bigg[
\frac{1}{\eta_0}\sum_{i\in C} D_{\!KL}(y_i\Vert \sigma_i^1)
\;+\;\eta_0\,|C|
\Bigg]
\quad\text{with probability }1-\delta.
\]
The same bound holds under a fixed exploration mixture $p_i^t=(1-\gamma)\sigma_i^t+\gamma\,\mathbf u_i$ with $\gamma>0$.
statement_text: Assume utilities in [0,1] . Let players run entropic mirror descent with steps η_t=η_0/ sqrt t for any η_0>0 . From any interior initial state ( min _aσ_i^1(a)>0 for all i ), for any fixed coalition C and deviation y_C , \[ max _ 1 ≤ τ ≤ T \ R ^ y_C _ C (τ) ≤ 2|C| sqrt 2Tln frac 4T δ + sqrt T g[ frac 1 η_0 Σ _ i ∈ C D_ KL (y_iVert σ_i^1) + η_0 |C| g] quad with probability 1-δ. \] The same bound holds under a fixed exploration mixture p_i^t=(1-γ)σ_i^t+γ u_i with γ>0 .
title: High‑probability, all prefixes with diminishing steps

label: lem:tight
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{lem:tight}
For every constant $c<1$ there is a sequence of payoff (gradient) vectors in $[0,1]$, realizable
within a two‑player zero‑sum interaction, against which entropic MD with steps $\eta_t=\eta_0/\sqrt t$
incurs unilateral deviation--regret at least $c\sqrt{T}$ with probability $1-\delta$ for all large
$T$. Hence the $\Theta(\sqrt T)$ rate of Lemma~\ref{lem:regret} cannot be improved in general by
the OMD analysis.
statement_text: For every constant c<1 there is a sequence of payoff (gradient) vectors in [0,1] , realizable within a two‑player zero‑sum interaction, against which entropic MD with steps η_t=η_0/ sqrt t incurs unilateral deviation--regret at least c sqrt T with probability 1-δ for all large T . Hence the Θ( sqrt T) rate of Lemma cannot be improved in general by the OMD analysis.
title: Order‑tightness of the template

label: def:exact-pot
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{def:exact-pot}
A finite game admits an \emph{exact potential} $\Phi$ if
\[
u_i(a'_i,a_{-i})-u_i(a)
   \;=\;
\Phi(a'_i,a_{-i})-\Phi(a)
\quad\forall i,a_i',a.
\]
statement_text: A finite game admits an exact potential Φ if \[ u_i(a'_i,a_ -i )-u_i(a) = Φ(a'_i,a_ -i )-Φ(a) quad ∀ i,a_i',a. \]
title: Exact potential game

label: def:strict-concave
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{def:strict-concave}
A differentiable $\Phi$ on $\Delta(\mathcal A)$ is \emph{strictly
concave} if  
$\Phi(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)>
 \lambda\Phi(x)+(1-\lambda)\Phi(y)$
for all $x\neq y$ and $\lambda\in(0,1)$.
statement_text: A differentiable Φ on Δ(A) is strictly concave if Φ(λ x+(1-λ)y)> λΦ(x)+(1-λ)Φ(y) for all x ≠ y and λ ∈ (0,1) .
title: Strict concavity

label: lem:uhc
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{lem:uhc}
Assume the payoff potential $\Phi$ is concave on $\Delta(\mathcal A)$ and fix $\lambda>0$.
For each $\sigma$, the problem
\[
\mathcal{T}_\lambda(\sigma)=
\argmax_{\sigma'\in \Delta(\mathcal A)}\Bigl[\Phi(\sigma')-\lambda
                       D_{\!KL}(\sigma'\!\|\sigma)\Bigr]
\]
has a \emph{unique} maximizer (since $-D_{\!KL}(\cdot\|\sigma)$ is strictly concave), hence
$\mathcal T_\lambda$ is a single‑valued map. Moreover, $\mathcal T_\lambda$ is continuous by Berge's Maximum Theorem~\citep{berge1963}
(strict concavity yields continuity of the argmax map).
statement_text: Assume the payoff potential Φ is concave on Δ(A) and fix λ>0 . For each σ , the problem \[ T _λ(σ)= arg max _ σ' ∈ Δ(A) l[Φ(σ')-λ D_ KL (σ' |σ) r] \] has a unique maximizer (since -D_ KL ( · |σ) is strictly concave), hence T_λ is a single‑valued map. Moreover, T_λ is continuous by Berge's Maximum Theorem (strict concavity yields continuity of the argmax map).
title: Well‑defined proximal map

label: lem:kakutani-to-NE
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{lem:kakutani-to-NE}
Let $\Gamma$ be an exact‑potential game with concave multilinear extension $\Phi$.
If $\sigma^\star\in\mathcal{T}_\lambda(\sigma^\star)$ for some $\lambda>0$ and $\sigma^\star$ lies
in the relative interior of $\Delta(\mathcal A)$, then $\sigma^\star$ is a constrained stationary
point of $\Phi$ on $\Delta(\mathcal A)$; in particular, for every player $i$, all actions in
$\mathrm{supp}(\sigma_i^\star)$ have equal payoff and no unilateral deviation yields a higher
payoff, so EDRE(i) holds with $\varepsilon=0$. For a \emph{boundary} (e.g.\ pure) fixed point of
$\mathrm{MD}_\eta$, optimality is checked directly: a pure profile is a fixed point of the
multiplicative‑weights map iff the played action is a best response, which is exactly the Nash
condition.
statement_text: Let Γ be an exact‑potential game with concave multilinear extension Φ . If σ^star ∈ T _λ(σ^star ) for some λ>0 and σ^star lies in the relative interior of Δ(A) , then σ^star is a constrained stationary point of Φ on Δ(A) ; in particular, for every player i , all actions in supp (σ_i^star ) have equal payoff and no unilateral deviation yields a higher payoff, so EDRE(i) holds with ε=0 . For a boundary (e.g.\ pure) fixed point of MD _η , optimality is checked directly: a pure profile is a fixed point of the multiplicative‑weights map iff the played action is a best response, which is exactly the Nash condition.
title: Interior proximal fixed point ⇒ unilateral optimality

label: thm:exist-edre
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{thm:exist-edre}
Every finite exact‑potential game admits at least one profile satisfying Definition~\ref{def:edre} with $\varepsilon=0$
(a Nash equilibrium). Under the step‑size regimes in Definition~\ref{def:dynamic-edre}, item (i)
holds, and item (ii) holds relative to the fixed‑point set as stated therein. When that fixed‑point
set is a singleton, EMD converges pointwise for $0<\eta<1/L$.
statement_text: Every finite exact‑potential game admits at least one profile satisfying Definition with ε=0 (a Nash equilibrium). Under the step‑size regimes in Definition , item (i) holds, and item (ii) holds relative to the fixed‑point set as stated therein. When that fixed‑point set is a singleton, EMD converges pointwise for 0<η<1/L .
title: Existence

label: thm:global-md
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{thm:global-md}
With constant step $0<\eta\le 1/L$ and an interior initialization, EMD on an $L$‑smooth
cost potential $\Psi$ satisfies
\[
\Psi(\sigma^{t+1})-\Psi(\sigma^{t})\ \le\ \bigl(-\tfrac{1}{\eta}+L\bigr)D_{\!KL}(\sigma^{t+1}\|\sigma^{t}),
\]
so $\{\Psi(\sigma^{t})\}$ is non‑increasing (strictly decreasing when $\eta<1/L$). For $0<\eta<1/L$,
every $\omega$–limit point of $\{\sigma^t\}$ is a fixed point of the MD map, and
$\mathrm{dist}(\sigma^t,\Fix(\mathrm{MD}_\eta))\to0$. If the fixed‑point set
is a singleton, then $\sigma^t$ converges to it. (Pure strategies are fixed points of the
multiplicative‑weights map; from interior starts they are not attained in finite time but can
arise as limits.)

payoff potential $\Phi$.

label: thm:flip-bifurcation
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{thm:flip-bifurcation}
For the map \eqref{eq:1d-map}, the interior equilibrium $p^\star=G_0/G_1$ has multiplier
\[
T_\eta'(p^\star)\;=\;1-\eta\,G_1\,p^\star(1-p^\star),
\]
which decreases monotonically in $\eta$ and equals $-1$ at the threshold
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{PD}}\;=\;\frac{2}{G_1\,p^\star(1-p^\star)} .
\]
Hence $p^\star$ is linearly stable for $\eta<\eta_{\mathrm{PD}}$ and loses stability through a
\emph{period‑doubling} (flip) bifurcation at $\eta=\eta_{\mathrm{PD}}$, after which a stable
$2$‑cycle appears. This is a one‑dimensional codimension‑one bifurcation; it is \emph{not} a
Neimark--Sacker bifurcation (the state space is one‑dimensional, so there is no complex
multiplier pair and no invariant circle).

This is a one‑dimensional codimension‑one bifurcation; it is not a Neimark--Sacker bifurcation (the state space is one‑dimensional, so there is no complex multiplier pair and no invariant circle).

label: thm:liyorke-chaos
paper_title: Ergodic Deviation-Robust Equilibrium under Mirror Descent Learning in Finite Games
statement_tex:
\label{thm:liyorke-chaos}
Fix the congestion game with $G_0=0.7$, $G_1=3$ (so $p^\star=7/30$ and
$\eta_{\mathrm{PD}}=2/(3\cdot\tfrac{7}{30}\cdot\tfrac{23}{30})=3.7267\ldots$), and take step
$\eta=7$. Then the map $T_\eta$ of \eqref{eq:1d-map} possesses a period‑three orbit
\[
x_1\;\xrightarrow{\,T_\eta\,}\;x_2\;\xrightarrow{\,T_\eta\,}\;x_3\;\xrightarrow{\,T_\eta\,}\;x_1,
\qquad
\begin{aligned}
x_1&=0.000197784073392\ldots,\\
x_2&=0.025773667425\ldots,\\
x_3&=0.674028548501\ldots,
\end{aligned}
\]
with $x_1<x_2<x_3$ (verified: $|T_\eta^3(x_1)-x_1|<10^{-30}$ and $|T_\eta(x_1)-x_1|>2\times10^{-2}$,
so the period is exactly three). Consequently, by the theorem of \citet{liyorke1975}, $T_\eta$
exhibits \emph{Li--Yorke chaos}: it has periodic points of every period and an uncountable
``scrambled'' set $S$ on which no two distinct points are asymptotic. Moreover $T_\eta$ has
positive topological entropy \citep{blockcoppel1992}. The conclusion is robust: a period‑three
orbit persists for all $\eta$ in an interval containing $[6.4,7.6]$.

Moreover T_η has positive topological entropy . The conclusion is robust: a period‑three orbit persists for all η in an interval containing [6.4,7.6] .

label: lem:feedback-intractability

statement_tex:
\label{lem:feedback-intractability}
Fix a loss family
\[
L(t)=\sum_{a=1}^m c_a(t)P_a,\qquad m=O(\mathrm{poly}(n)),
\]
where each $P_a$ is an $O(1)$-local Pauli string with
$\|L(t)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1$. Suppose
Assumptions~\ref{ass:gibbs-mapping} and~\ref{ass:bcl-realizable} hold, so that for
every $t\in\mathcal{W}$ with $t\ge t_0$, the steady state $\rGibbs(t)$ prepared
by the Davies generator~\eqref{eq:davies-generator} is within trace distance
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{prep}}$ of a BCL-hard Gibbs state whose
computational-basis measurement distribution $\mu^\star$ is classically hard to
sample. Let $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{class}}$ be any randomized classical algorithm
that, given only the classical description of the loss $L(t)$ at some round
$t\in\mathcal{W}$ with $t\ge t_0$, outputs in polynomial time a sample whose
distribution is within total-variation distance
$\tau<\tfrac12-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{prep}}$ of the distribution from which
DQMW-Sample draws its round-$t$ sample. Then the existence of such a
polynomial-time $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{class}}$ would yield a polynomial-time
classical sampler for the BCL distribution $\mu^\star$ to within total-variation
distance $\tau+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{prep}}<\tfrac12$. Under the standard hardness
assumption that no such efficient classical sampler for $\mu^\star$ exists (on
pain of collapsing the polynomial hierarchy), no such classical algorithm
$\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{class}}$ can exist. Consequently, there is no efficient
classical algorithm that can simulate the sampling step that supplies the loss
feedback to the multiplicative-weights update of DQMW-Sample in the hard window
$\mathcal{W}$.

label: thm:robust
paper_title: Dissipative Quantum Multiplicative Weights with Sampling Feedback: A Classically Hard Primitive Realized via Engineered Open-System Dynamics
statement_tex:
\label{thm:robust}
Let the physical evolution be governed by
$\mathcal{L}_t^{\mathrm{phys}}=\mathcal{D}_t+\mathcal{H}_t+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{hw}}$,
where $\mathcal{D}_t$ is the Davies dissipator with spectral gap bounded below by
$\gamma_0>0$ and unique attracting state $\rGibbs(t)$,
$\mathcal{H}_t(\rho)=-i[H_{\mathrm{drift}}(t),\rho]$ is the coherent part, and
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{hw}}$ is an unstructured-noise perturbation with
$\|\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{hw}}\|_{\diamond}\le\delta$. Assume:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[(R1)] the gap lower bound $\gamma_0$ holds uniformly in $t$ along the
trajectory;
\item[(R2)] \emph{(noise--dissipation independence)} the noise strength $\delta$
does not grow with the engineered dissipation strength $\gamma_0$; equivalently,
$\delta$ and $\gamma_0$ are independently controllable;
\item[(R3)] \emph{(controlled coherent driving)} the coherent generator acts
tangentially to the Gibbs manifold up to a residual of order the target motion,
$\|\mathcal{H}_t(\rGibbs(t))\|_1=O(\eta)$, so that coherent driving does not by
itself set a noise-independent floor.
\end{itemize}
Then the additional regret attributable to hardware noise satisfies
\begin{equation}
\Delta\mathrm{Regret}_{\mathrm{noise}}(T)\;\le\;\frac{C\,\delta}{\gamma_0}\,T,
\label{eq:noise-regret-general}
\end{equation}
where $C=C(d)$ depends on the Hilbert-space dimension $d=2^n$ only through the
norm-equivalence constant relating the trace norm to the loss functional
[see~\eqref{eq:lipschitz} below]; in particular $C$ is dimension-free whenever
the losses satisfy $\|L(t)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1$. Under the balanced schedule
$\gamma_0(T)=\Theta(\sqrt{T})$,
\begin{equation}
\Delta\mathrm{Regret}_{\mathrm{noise}}(T)\;=\;O\!\bigl(\delta\sqrt{T}\bigr),
\label{eq:noise-regret-sublinear}
\end{equation}
so the noise-induced regret is sublinear in $T$ and DQMW-Sample remains
asymptotically no-regret for any fixed $\delta>0$.

Assume: the gap lower bound γ_0 holds uniformly in t along the trajectory; (noise--dissipation independence) the noise strength δ does not grow with the engineered dissipation strength γ_0 ; equivalently, δ and γ_0 are independently controllable; (controlled coherent driving) the coherent generator acts tangentially to the Gibbs manifold up to a residual of order the target motion, | H _t(ρ_ Gibbs (t))|_1=O(η) , so that coherent driving does not by itself set a noise-independent floor. Then the additional regret attributable to hardware noise satisfies Δ Regret _ noise (T) ≤ frac C δ γ_0 T, where C=C(d) depends on the Hilbert-space dimension d=2^n only through the norm-equivalence constant relating the trace norm to the loss functional [see below]; in particular C is dimension-free whenever the losses satisfy |L(t)|_ op ≤ 1 . Under the balanced schedule γ_0(T)=Θ( sqrt T ) , Δ Regret _ noise (T) = O l(δ sqrt T r), so the noise-induced regret is sublinear in T and DQMW-Sample remains asymptotically no-regret for any fixed δ>0 .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
A \emph{propositional proof system} $P$ is given by a polynomial-time algorithm $V: \{0,1\}^* \times \{0,1\}^* \rightarrow \{0,1\}$, known as its verifier, such that for every CNF formula $F$, \[\exists\, \Pi\colon\, \,V(F,\Pi) = 1 \iff F \text{ is unsatisfiable}.\]
Given two propositional proof systems $P$, $Q$, with verifiers $V_P$ and $V_Q$, we say that $P$ \emph{polynomially-simulates} $Q$, written $P \geq_p Q$, if there is a polynomial-time computable function $f$ such that $V_Q(F, \Pi) \implies V_P(F, f(F, \Pi))$ for all $F$ and $\Pi$.
statement_text: A propositional proof system P is given by a polynomial-time algorithm V: {0,1}^* × {0,1}^* → {0,1} , known as its verifier, such that for every CNF formula F , \[ ∃ Πcolon V(F,Π) = 1 ⟺ F is unsatisfiable .\] Given two propositional proof systems P , Q , with verifiers V_P and V_Q , we say that P polynomially-simulates Q , written P ≥ _p Q , if there is a polynomial-time computable function f such that V_Q(F, Π) ⇒ V_P(F, f(F, Π)) for all F and Π .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
Let $C_1, \dots C_m, D$ be a collection of clauses.
    A \emph{Resolution} proof of $D$ from $C_1, \dots, C_m$ is a sequence of clauses \[\Pi = (D_1, D_2, \ldots, D_s)\] where $D_s = D$ and, for each $i \leq s$, either $D_i = C_j$ for some $j$, or $D_i$ is derived from earlier clauses in the sequence by one of the following two rules:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item {\emph{Resolution}} $C \lor x, D \lor \neg x \vdash C \lor D$
        \item {\emph{Weakening}} $C \vdash C \lor D$
    \end{itemize}
    The proof is a \emph{refutation} if $D = \bot$ (the empty clause).
statement_text: Let C_1, ... C_m, D be a collection of clauses. A Resolution proof of D from C_1, ... , C_m is a sequence of clauses \[Π = (D_1, D_2, ... , D_s)\] where D_s = D and, for each i ≤ s , either D_i = C_j for some j , or D_i is derived from earlier clauses in the sequence by one of the following two rules: Resolution C ∨ x, D ∨ ¬ x vdash C ∨ D Weakening C vdash C ∨ D The proof is a refutation if D = bot (the empty clause).

label: def:reflection
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
\label{def:reflection}
    For a proof system $P$ with verifier $V$, its \emph{reflection principle} is the family of tautologies 
    \[\refl_{P,n,m,s}(F,\Pi,x) := \neg\mathrm{Proof}_{n,m,s}(F,\Pi) \vee \mathrm{SAT}_{n,m}(F,x)\]
    where $\mathrm{Proof}_{n,m,s}$ is a formula (using the definition of $V_{n,m,s}$) asserting that $\Pi$ is a $P$-proof that $F$ is a tautology, and $\mathrm{SAT}_{n,m}$ is the CNF formula claiming that $x$ is a satisfying assignment to $F$. This captures the soundness of the proof system $P$: it asserts that if $\Pi$ is a $P$-proof of $F$ then every assignment satisfies $F$. 
    If the parameters $n, m, s$ are clear from context, then we will suppress the subscripts and call the formula $\refl_P$.

    A $\Sigma^q_1$-formula is a quantified boolean formula of the form $\exists \vec y G(x, y)$, where $G$ is unquantified.
    The reflection principle for $\Sigma^q_1$-formulas is defined similarly by changing $\mathrm{SAT}(F,x)$ to $\mathrm{SAT}_{\Sigma^q_1}(F,x)$, asserting that $F$, a $\Sigma^q_1$-formula, is satisfied by assignment $x$. 
    The formula $\mathrm{SAT}_{\Sigma^q_1}(F,x)$ may itself be written as a $\Sigma^q_1$-formula in the natural way. 
    We will denote this version of reflection as $\Sigma^q_1$-$\refl_P$.
statement_text: For a proof system P with verifier V , its reflection principle is the family of tautologies \[ Refl _ P,n,m,s (F,Π,x) := ¬ Proof _ n,m,s (F,Π) vee SAT _ n,m (F,x)\] where Proof _ n,m,s is a formula (using the definition of V_ n,m,s ) asserting that Π is a P -proof that F is a tautology, and SAT _ n,m is the CNF formula claiming that x is a satisfying assignment to F . This captures the soundness of the proof system P : it asserts that if Π is a P -proof of F then every assignment satisfies F . If the parameters n, m, s are clear from context, then we will suppress the subscripts and call the formula Refl _P . A Σ^q_1 -formula is a quantified boolean formula of the form ∃ vec y G(x, y) , where G is unquantified. The reflection principle for Σ^q_1 -formulas is defined similarly by changing SAT (F,x) to SAT _ Σ^q_1 (F,x) , asserting that F , a Σ^q_1 -formula, is satisfied by assignment x . The formula SAT _ Σ^q_1 (F,x) may itself be written as a Σ^q_1 -formula in the natural way. We will denote this version of reflection as Σ^q_1 - Refl _P .

statement_tex:
The proof system $[EF, \Resolution]$ is defined as follows.
    If $F(x_1, \dots, x_n) = C_1 \land \cdots \land C_m$ is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, then a refutation in $[EF, \Resolution]$ of $F$ is given by a pair $(C, \Pi)$, where $C$ is an implicit encoding of a Resolution refutation of $F$, and $\Pi$ is an Extended Frege proof that $C$ is correctly encoded.
statement_text: The proof system [EF, Resolution ] is defined as follows. If F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, then a refutation in [EF, Resolution ] of F is given by a pair (C, Π) , where C is an implicit encoding of a Resolution refutation of F , and Π is an Extended Frege proof that C is correctly encoded.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
A relation $R \subseteq \bits^* \times \bits^*$ is 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{Total}, if for all $x \in \bits^*$ there is a $y \in \bits^*$ such that $(x, y) \in R$. 
        \item \emph{Polynomially bounded}, if there is a polynomial $\ell(n)$ such that for all $(x, y) \in R$, $|y| \leq \ell(n)$.
    \end{itemize} 
    An \emph{$\NP$ search problem} is a polynomial-time computable, polynomially bounded relation $R \subseteq \bits^* \times \bits^*$.
    The class of all total $\NP$ search problems is denoted $\TFNP$.
statement_text: A relation R ⊆ { 0,1 } ^* × { 0,1 } ^* is Total , if for all x ∈ { 0,1 } ^* there is a y ∈ { 0,1 } ^* such that (x, y) ∈ R . Polynomially bounded , if there is a polynomial ell (n) such that for all (x, y) ∈ R , |y| ≤ ell (n) . An NP search problem is a polynomial-time computable, polynomially bounded relation R ⊆ { 0,1 } ^* × { 0,1 } ^* . The class of all total NP search problems is denoted TFNP .

label: def:tfnp-cnf-encoding
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
\label{def:tfnp-cnf-encoding}
    Let $R \in \TFNP$ and let $n, \ell$ be positive integers.
    Define $V_{R, n, \ell}$ to be a polynomial-size circuit such that $V_{R, n, \ell}(x, y) = R(x, y)$.
    If the parameters $n$ and $\ell$ are clear from context, then we will omit them and write $V_R(x, y)$.
statement_text: Let R ∈ TFNP and let n, ell be positive integers. Define V_ R, n, ell to be a polynomial-size circuit such that V_ R, n, ell (x, y) = R(x, y) . If the parameters n and ell are clear from context, then we will omit them and write V_R(x, y) .

label: def:mapping-reduction
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
\label{def:mapping-reduction}
    Let $R, S \in \TFNP$.
    A \emph{mapping reduction}\footnote{In this paper, all mapping reductions will be polynomial-time computable.} from $R$ to $S$ is given by two polynomial-time computable functions $f$ and $g$ such that for all $x, y \in \bits^*$, 
    \[S(f(x), y) \implies R(x, g(y)).\]
    If $R$ is mapping reducible to $S$ we write $R \leq_m S$.
statement_text: Let R, S ∈ TFNP . A mapping reduction from R to S is given by two polynomial-time computable functions f and g such that for all x, y ∈ { 0,1 } ^* , \[S(f(x), y) ⇒ R(x, g(y)).\] If R is mapping reducible to S we write R ≤ _m S .

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
The $\iterlong$ problem, also denoted $\iter$, is defined as follows.
    For any positive integer $n$, 
    
    let $\ell(n) = n^{O(1)}$ be a  polynomially-bounded input parameter.
    The input to the problem is a size parameter $1^n$ and a circuit $S: \bits^n \times \bits^\ell \rightarrow \bits^\ell$ of size polynomial in $n$.
    Given $n$ and $S$, a string $y \in \bits^\ell$ is a valid solution if either
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $y = 0^\ell$, if $S(x, 0^\ell) = 0^\ell$, or
        \item $y \neq 0^\ell$, if $S(x, y) <_{lex} y$, or 
        \item $y \neq 0^\ell$, if $S(x, y) >_{lex} y$ and $S(x, S(x, y)) = S(x, y)$.
    \end{itemize}
    Above $<_{lex}$ denotes the usual lexicographic ordering on strings. 
    The class of all search problems mapping reducible to $\iterlong$ is denoted by $\PLS$.
statement_text: The iterlong problem, also denoted iter , is defined as follows. For any positive integer n , let ell (n) = n^ O(1) be a polynomially-bounded input parameter. The input to the problem is a size parameter 1^n and a circuit S: { 0,1 } ^n × { 0,1 } ^ell → { 0,1 } ^ell of size polynomial in n . Given n and S , a string y ∈ { 0,1 } ^ell is a valid solution if either y = 0^ell , if S(x, 0^ell ) = 0^ell , or y ≠ 0^ell , if S(x, y) <_ lex y , or y ≠ 0^ell , if S(x, y) >_ lex y and S(x, S(x, y)) = S(x, y) . Above <_ lex denotes the usual lexicographic ordering on strings. The class of all search problems mapping reducible to iterlong is denoted by PLS .

statement_tex: If $F(x_1, \dots, x_n) = C_1 \land \cdots \land C_m$ is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, the \emph{false-clause search problem} $\search_F$ associated with $F$ is the total relation \[\search_F := \set{(x, i) \in \{0,1\}^n \times [m]: C_i(x) = 0}.\]
statement_text: If F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m is an unsatisfiable CNF formula, the false-clause search problem Search _F associated with F is the total relation \[ Search _F := { (x, i) ∈ {0,1}^n × [m]: C_i(x) = 0 }.\]

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. 
    A \emph{black-box search problem} is any total relation \[\dtR_n \subseteq \set{0,1}^{n} \times O_n,\] where $O_n$ is a polynomial-sized set of feasible solutions.
    The class $\TFNP^{dt}$ contains all sequences $\dtR = \set{\dtR_n}_n$ of black-box search problems such that the following holds: there is a universal constant $c$ such that for each input length $n$, and each $o \in O_n$, there is a $O((\log n)^c)$-depth decision tree $T_o$ satisfying $T_o(x) = \dtR_n(x,o)$.
statement_text: Let n be a positive integer. A black-box search problem is any total relation \[R^ dt _n ⊆ { 0,1 }^ n × O_n,\] where O_n is a polynomial-sized set of feasible solutions. The class TFNP ^ dt contains all sequences R^ dt = { R^ dt _n }_n of black-box search problems such that the following holds: there is a universal constant c such that for each input length n , and each o ∈ O_n , there is a O(( log n)^c) -depth decision tree T_o satisfying T_o(x) = R^ dt _n(x,o) .

label: def:formulation
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
\label{def:formulation}  
	Let $\dtS_m \subseteq \{0,1\}^m \times O_S, \dtR_n \subseteq \{0,1\}^n \times O_S$ be black-box search problems.
	A \emph{decision-tree reduction} from $\dtS_m$ to $\dtR_n$ is given by functions $f = \{f_i: \bits^m \rightarrow
    \{0,1\}\}_{i \in [n]}$ and $g = \{g_o: \bits^n \rightarrow O_S\}_{o \in O_R}$ 
    
    each computable by decision trees $T_{f_i}, T_{g_o}$, such that for every $x \in \{0,1\}^m$ and $o \in O_R$,
	\begin{equation*}\label{eqn:mapping-reduction}
		(T_f(x), o) \in \dtR \implies (x, T_{g_o}(x)) \in \dtS. 
	\end{equation*} 
    where $T_f(x)$ denotes the $n$-bit string obtained by evaluating $T_{f_1}(x),\ldots,T_{f_n}(x)$.
    
    The \emph{depth} of the reduction is the maximum depth of any of the decision trees $\set{T_{f_i}}_i \cup \set{T_{g_o}}_o$.
    The \emph{complexity} of the reduction to be: \[\sum_{i=1}^n |T_{f_i}| + \sum_{o \in O_S} |T_{g_o}|.\] 
    
    
    
	We extend this definition to sequences as follows. 
	If $\mathsf{R}^{dt} = \{\dtR_n\}$ is a sequence of search problems, then $R^{dt}(\dtS_m)$ is the minimum complexity of a reduction from $\dtS_m$ to any problem in $R^{dt}$. 
	If $S^{dt} = \{\dtS_m\}$ is also a sequence of search problems, then we write $S^{dt} \leq^{dt}_m \mathsf{R}^{dt}$ if $\mathsf{R}^{dt}(\dtS_m)$ is polynomially-bounded in $m$.
statement_text: Let S^ dt _m ⊆ {0,1}^m × O_S, R^ dt _n ⊆ {0,1}^n × O_S be black-box search problems. A decision-tree reduction from S^ dt _m to R^ dt _n is given by functions f = {f_i: { 0,1 } ^m → {0,1}}_ i ∈ [n] and g = {g_o: { 0,1 } ^n → O_S}_ o ∈ O_R each computable by decision trees T_ f_i , T_ g_o , such that for every x ∈ {0,1}^m and o ∈ O_R , (T_f(x), o) ∈ R^ dt ⇒ (x, T_ g_o (x)) ∈ S^ dt . where T_f(x) denotes the n -bit string obtained by evaluating T_ f_1 (x), ... ,T_ f_n (x) . The depth of the reduction is the maximum depth of any of the decision trees { T_ f_i }_i ∪ { T_ g_o }_o . The complexity of the reduction to be: \[ Σ _ i=1 ^n |T_ f_i | + Σ _ o ∈ O_S |T_ g_o |.\] We extend this definition to sequences as follows. If R ^ dt = {R^ dt _n} is a sequence of search problems, then R^ dt (S^ dt _m) is the minimum complexity of a reduction from S^ dt _m to any problem in R^ dt . If S^ dt = {S^ dt _m} is also a sequence of search problems, then we write S^ dt ≤ ^ dt _m R ^ dt if R ^ dt (S^ dt _m) is polynomially-bounded in m .

statement_text: Let N = 2^k be a positive integer. The problem iter _N^ dt is defined as follows. As input, for each element u ∈ [N] , we are given a successor s_u ∈ [N] , interpreted as naming the successor node of u , and which we can think of as being encoded by a string of k bits. The goal of the search problem is to output any of the following 1 if s_1 = 1 hfill (inactive distinguished source) u ≠ 1 , if s_u < u , hfill (decreasing successor) u , if u is active and s_u is a proper sink. hfill (proper sink)

label: def:unsat-cnf
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
\label{def:unsat-cnf}
    Let $F(x_1, \dots, x_n) = C_1 \land C_2 \land \cdots \land C_m$ be a CNF formula.
    The formula $\unsat_F(x_1, \dots, x_n, z_1, \dots, z_m)$ is defined to be \[\unsat_F(x, z) := \left(\bigvee_{i=1}^m z_i\right) \land \bigwedge_{i=1}^m (\neg z_i \lor \neg C_i).\]
    If $\mathcal{F} = \set{F_i}_i$ is a sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then let $\unsat_{\mathcal{F}} = \set{\unsat_{F_i}}_i$ be the corresponding sequence of formulas.
statement_text: Let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ C_2 ∧ ... ∧ C_m be a CNF formula. The formula UNSAT _F(x_1, ... , x_n, z_1, ... , z_m) is defined to be \[ UNSAT _F(x, z) := ( vee_ i=1 ^m z_i ) ∧ wedge_ i=1 ^m ( ¬ z_i ∨ ¬ C_i).\] If F = { F_i }_i is a sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then let UNSAT _ F = { UNSAT _ F_i }_i be the corresponding sequence of formulas.

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex: If $\mathcal{F}$ is a polynomial-time uniform sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then $\unsat_{\mathcal{F}}$, interpreted as a total search problem, is in $\FP$.
statement_text: If F is a polynomial-time uniform sequence of unsatisfiable CNF formulas, then UNSAT _ F , interpreted as a total search problem, is in FP .

label: def:non-uniform mapping reduction
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: Let R ∈ TFNP and let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = C_1 ∧ ... ∧ C_m be an unsatisfiable CNF formula. Let ell (n) denote the polynomial upper bound on the length of any solution to R on inputs of length n . A non-uniform mapping reduction from Search _F to R is given by two circuits C : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^s, D : { 0,1 } ^n × { 0,1 } ^ ell (s) → { 0,1 } ^m , such that R(C(x), y) ⇒ UNSAT _F(x, D(x, y)).

paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
Let $n, m$ be positive integers, let $R \in \TFNP$, and let $F(x_1, \dots, x_n) = \wedge_{i=1}^m C_i$ be a CNF formula.
    Let $\ell$ be a polynomial bound on the certificate length of $R$.
    If $R \in \TFNP$ and $F(x_1, \dots, x_n) = \wedge_{i=1}^m C_i$, then $\Reduction_{R, n, m, S, s}(C, D, F)$ is the boolean formula defined as follows.
    We introduce several helper formulas which can easily be represented in CNF.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\isCkt_S(C)$ is satisfied iff the variables in $C$ encode a valid boolean circuit with $S$ gates.
        \item $\Eval_{n, S, s}(C, x, t)$ is satisfied iff $C$ encodes a boolean circuit with $n$ inputs, $S$ gates, and $s$ outputs, and $t \in \bits^s$ is the output of $C$ on input $x \in \bits^n$.
    \end{itemize}
    Then $\Reduction_{R, n, m, S, s}(C, D, F):=$ \[\isCkt(C) \land \isCkt(D) \land \Eval(C, x, x') \land \Eval(D, (x, y), z) \land \Eval(V_R, x', y) \rightarrow \unsat_F(x, z).\]
    For readability, we have omitted parameter subscripts above, and we will continue to do so when those parameters are clear from context. 
    The circuit $C$ has $n$ inputs, $S$ gates, and $s$ outputs, and the circuit $D$ has $n+\ell(s)$ inputs, $S$ gates, and $m$ outputs.
statement_text: Let n, m be positive integers, let R ∈ TFNP , and let F(x_1, ... , x_n) = wedge _ i=1 ^m C_i be a CNF formula. Let ell be a polynomial bound on the certificate length of R . If R ∈ TFNP and F(x_1, ... , x_n) = wedge _ i=1 ^m C_i , then Reduction _ R, n, m, S, s (C, D, F) is the boolean formula defined as follows. We introduce several helper formulas which can easily be represented in CNF. isCkt _S(C) is satisfied iff the variables in C encode a valid boolean circuit with S gates. Eval _ n, S, s (C, x, t) is satisfied iff C encodes a boolean circuit with n inputs, S gates, and s outputs, and t ∈ { 0,1 } ^s is the output of C on input x ∈ { 0,1 } ^n . Then Reduction _ R, n, m, S, s (C, D, F):= \[ isCkt (C) ∧ isCkt (D) ∧ Eval (C, x, x') ∧ Eval (D, (x, y), z) ∧ Eval (V_R, x', y) → UNSAT _F(x, z).\] For readability, we have omitted parameter subscripts above, and we will continue to do so when those parameters are clear from context. The circuit C has n inputs, S gates, and s outputs, and the circuit D has n+ell (s) inputs, S gates, and m outputs.

label: def:ef-mapping-r
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_tex:
\label{def:ef-mapping-r} (Defining $\langle EF,R\rangle$)
    For any $R \in \TFNP$, the propositional proof system $\langle EF, R \rangle$ is defined as follows.
    For any unsatisfiable CNF formula $F(x_1, \dots, x_n) = C_1 \land \cdots \land C_m$, a refutation of $F$ in $\langle EF, R \rangle$ is given by an \emph{$EF$-provable reduction from $\search_F$ to $R$}.

label: def:G
paper_title: Provable Reductions in TFNP
statement_text: We adapt Frege to allow quantified formulas introduced by the following rules: \[ l l ( ∀ -left ) inferrule * A(B), Γ → Δ ∀ x A(x), Γ → Δ & ( ∀ -right ) inferrule * Γ → Δ, A(p) Γ → Δ, ∀ x A(x) ( ∃ -left ) inferrule * A(p), Γ → Δ ∃ x A(x), Γ → Δ & ( ∃ -right ) inferrule * Γ → Δ, A(p) Γ → Δ, ∃ x A(x) \] For the ∀ -right and ∃ -left rules, the variable p is called an eigenvariable and cannot appear in the bottom sequent. The G proof system is simply PK with these additional rules. For i ≥ 0 , G_i is a restriction of G to only allow cuts on (Σ^q_i ∪ Π^q_i ) -formulas. (That is, the cut rule for G_i can only be applied to formulas with at most i alternations of ∀ and ∃ quantifiers.) While the G systems can prove validity of general QBF formulas, it is also interesting to understand their strength with respect to Boolean formulas. Since G (and even G_1 ) has all of EF rules plus additional rules, G can trivially p-simulate EF (with respect to Boolean formulas). And it is known that the tree-like version of G_1 , called G_1^* is p-equivalent to EF. On the other hand, it is unknown whether or not G_1 is stronger than EF (with respect to Boolean formulas), and it is generally conjectured to be more powerful wrt p-simulations.

statement_tex:
For a proof system $P$ (a polynomial-time verifier) and parameters $n,m,s$, a reflection principle for $P$ is a CNF formula 
    \[ \text{Refl}_P:=  \text{Proof}_P(F,\Pi, s) \supset \text{SAT}(F,X), \]
    where $\text{SAT}$ is the $\VPV$-predicate stating that $F$ is a formula satisfied by the truth assignment $X$. As well, $\text{Proof}_P$ is a $\VPV$-predicate which is true iff $\Pi$ is a $P$-proof of $F$. Such a formula can be obtained, for example, by taking the Cook-Reckhow translation of the verifying Turing Machine for $P$-proofs. Reflection principles establish the \emph{soundness} of a proof system.

    The satisfiability predicate and reflection principles may be generalized to quantified boolean formulas in the natural way, by changing the $\text{SAT}$ predicate to be $\text{SAT}_{\Sigma^q_1} \equiv \exists |W| < |F|\, \text{SAT}(F,X,W)$, where values for $W$ are substituted into existentially quantified variables of $F$. We refer to this reflection as $\Sigma^q_1$-reflection.
statement_text: For a proof system P (a polynomial-time verifier) and parameters n,m,s , a reflection principle for P is a CNF formula \[ Refl _P:= Proof _P(F,Π, s) ⊃ SAT (F,X), \] where SAT is the VPV -predicate stating that F is a formula satisfied by the truth assignment X . As well, Proof _P is a VPV -predicate which is true iff Π is a P -proof of F . Such a formula can be obtained, for example, by taking the Cook-Reckhow translation of the verifying Turing Machine for P -proofs. Reflection principles establish the soundness of a proof system. The satisfiability predicate and reflection principles may be generalized to quantified boolean formulas in the natural way, by changing the SAT predicate to be SAT _ Σ^q_1 equiv ∃ |W| < |F| SAT (F,X,W) , where values for W are substituted into existentially quantified variables of F . We refer to this reflection as Σ^q_1 -reflection.

statement_tex:
A \textsc{Pure-Circuit} instance consists of a node set $\NodeSet$ and a gate set $\GateSet$ 




of types \NOT, \OR, and \PURIFY. 

Each node is the output node of at most one gate. A solution is an assignment
$
x\in\BoolOrUnknown^V
$
satisfying:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=7mm]
\item $\NOT(u,v)$:
\[
x[u]=0\Rightarrow x[v]=1,
\qquad
x[u]=1\Rightarrow x[v]=0.
\]
\item $\OR(u_0,u_1,w)$:
\[
x[u_0]=x[u_1]=0\Rightarrow x[w]=0,
\]
and
\[
x[u_0]=1\ \text{or}\ x[u_1]=1\Rightarrow x[w]=1.
\]
\item $\PURIFY(u,v_0,v_1)$:
\[
\{x[v_0],x[v_1]\}\cap\Bits\neq\emptyset,
\]
and if $x[u]\in\Bits$, then
\[
x[v_0]=x[v_1]=x[u].
\]
\end{itemize}

label: def:tasks
paper_title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
statement_tex:
\label{def:tasks}
\begin{enumerate}
\item An algorithm achieves \emph{strong detection} if it outputs a value
in $\{\textsf{planted},\textsf{null}\}$ whose total error,
$P_m(\textsf{null})+Q_m(\textsf{planted})$, tends to $0$.
\item An algorithm achieves \emph{weak recovery} if, under
$\mathbf P_m$, it outputs $\widehat x\in\{\pm1\}^n$ with
$|\ip{\widehat x}{\xstar}|\ge c_kn$ with probability $1-o(1)$, for a
constant $c_k>0$; it achieves \emph{$\vartheta$-accurate recovery} if
$\err_k(\widehat x,\xstar)\le\vartheta$ with probability $1-o(1)$, and
\emph{exact recovery} if $\vartheta<1/n$.  For odd $k$ the orientation
of $\xstar$ is identifiable, and our algorithms achieve the oriented
guarantee $\ip{\widehat x}{\xstar}\ge c_kn$.
\item An algorithm achieves \emph{two-sided strong refutation at
advantage $\eps$} if, on \emph{every} input $I$, it outputs a value
$\Cert(I)\ge\sup_x|V_I(x)|$, and under $Q_m$ it outputs
$\Cert(I)\le\eps$ with probability $1-o(1)$.  Strong refutation
ordinarily asks only for a certified upper bound on $\sup_xV_I(x)$;
controlling $\sup_x|V_I(x)|$ is the stronger two-sided statement, and
the two coincide at odd $k$, where $V_I(-x)=-V_I(x)$.
\end{enumerate}




All probabilities above are over the instance
and the internal randomness jointly.
statement_text: An algorithm achieves strong detection if it outputs a value in {sf planted ,sf null } whose total error, P_m(sf null )+Q_m(sf planted ) , tends to 0 . An algorithm achieves weak recovery if, under P_m , it outputs widehat x ∈ {pm 1}^n with | le widehat x, x^star rangle | ≥ c_kn with probability 1-o(1) , for a constant c_k>0 ; it achieves vartheta -accurate recovery if err _k(widehat x, x^star ) ≤ vartheta with probability 1-o(1) , and exact recovery if vartheta <1/n . For odd k the orientation of x^star is identifiable, and our algorithms achieve the oriented guarantee le widehat x, x^star rangle ≥ c_kn . An algorithm achieves two-sided strong refutation at advantage ε if, on every input I , it outputs a value Cert (I) ≥ sup _x|V_I(x)| , and under Q_m it outputs Cert (I) ≤ ε with probability 1-o(1) . Strong refutation ordinarily asks only for a certified upper bound on sup _xV_I(x) ; controlling sup _x|V_I(x)| is the stronger two-sided statement, and the two coincide at odd k , where V_I(-x)=-V_I(x) . All probabilities above are over the instance and the internal randomness jointly.
title: Detection, recovery, refutation

label: thm:main-boost

statement_tex:
\label{thm:main-boost}
Let $\widetilde x$ satisfy $|\ip{\widetilde x}{\xstar}|\ge cn$ for a
constant $c>0$.  There is a constant $\vartheta_0(k)\in(0,1)$ such
that, for every $1/(2n)\le\vartheta\le\vartheta_0(k)$, an
independent sample of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cleanup-curve}
 m_{\rm c}\ge C_{k,c}\frac n{\rho^2}\log\frac1\vartheta
\end{equation}
clauses suffices for an $O(km_{\rm c}+n)$-time majority vote to output
$\widehat x$ with $\err_k(\widehat x,\xstar)\le\vartheta$ with
probability $1-o(1)$.  Taking $\vartheta=1/(2n)$ gives exact recovery.

There is a constant vartheta _0(k) ∈ (0,1) such that, for every 1/(2n) ≤ vartheta ≤ vartheta _0(k) , an independent sample of m_ rm c ≥ C_ k,c frac n ρ^2 log frac 1vartheta clauses suffices for an O(km_ rm c +n) -time majority vote to output widehat x with err _k(widehat x, x^star ) ≤ vartheta with probability 1-o(1) . Taking vartheta =1/(2n) gives exact recovery.

label: thm:main-refutation
paper_title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
statement_tex:
\label{thm:main-refutation}
Fix $\eps\in(0,1)$ and a level satisfying \cref{eq:range}.  There is an
algorithm which, on every input,
outputs a bound satisfying with certainty
\[
 \Cert(I)\ge\sup_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}|V_I(x)|.
\]
For a random null instance,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:refutation-threshold}
 m\ge C_{k,\delta}\frac{\Dkl}{\eps^2}
\end{equation}
implies $\Cert(I)\le\eps$ with probability $1-o(1)$.  The even
algorithm is deterministic.  The odd algorithm uses a random rooting, but
soundness holds for every rooting.  In the standard explicit-input regime
$m=n^{O_k(1)}$, deterministically sound exact evaluation takes
$n^{O_k(\ell)}$ bit
operations and yields a degree-$O_k(\ell)$ SoS proof.
statement_text: Fix ε ∈ (0,1) and a level satisfying cref eq:range . There is an algorithm which, on every input, outputs a bound satisfying with certainty \[ Cert (I) ≥ sup _ x ∈ {pm 1}^n |V_I(x)|. \] For a random null instance, m ≥ C_ k,δ frac D_ k,ell ε^2 implies Cert (I) ≤ ε with probability 1-o(1) . The even algorithm is deterministic. The odd algorithm uses a random rooting, but soundness holds for every rooting. In the standard explicit-input regime m=n^ O_k(1) , deterministically sound exact evaluation takes n^ O_k(ell ) bit operations and yields a degree- O_k(ell ) SoS proof.
title: Two-sided strong refutation at level ell

label: thm:main-lower
paper_title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
statement_tex:
\label{thm:main-lower}
For every $k\ge2$, there are constants $c_k,C_k>0$ such that, in the same
fixed-$m$ model:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $D\le n/(2k)$ and
$m\rho^2D^{k/2-1}/n^{k/2}\le c_k$, every positive-variance sign-degree-$D$
statistic $g$ satisfies
\[
 \frac{|\E_Pg-\E_Qg|}{\sqrt{\Var_Q(g)}}
 \le C_k\frac{m\rho^2D^{k/2-1}}{n^{k/2}},
\]
where $Q=Q_m$ and $P=P_m$ is the planted mixture
(\cref{thm:ld-detection}).
\item If $d\le n/(4k)$ and
$m\rho^2(2d)^{k/2-1}/n^{k/2}\le c_k$, every estimator
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ with pointwise bounds $|f_i|\le1$ and sign degree at
most $d$ in each coordinate satisfies
\[
 \E\left(\frac1n\sum_i x_i^\star f_i(I)\right)^2
 \le \frac1n+C_k\sqrt{\frac dn}.
\]
Here the expectation is over a uniform planted assignment and its planted
instance.  Thus such estimators have vanishing overlap for $d=o(n)$ below the
same curve (\cref{thm:ld-recovery}).
\end{enumerate}
Together with the unconditional cleanup converse of
\cref{rem:cleanup-converse}, this matches every upper bound of
\cref{thm:main-inference,thm:main-boost} within its class.
statement_text: For every k ≥ 2 , there are constants c_k,C_k>0 such that, in the same fixed- m model: If D ≤ n/(2k) and mρ^2D^ k/2-1 /n^ k/2 ≤ c_k , every positive-variance sign-degree- D statistic g satisfies \[ frac |E_Pg-E_Qg| sqrt Var _Q(g) ≤ C_kfrac mρ^2D^ k/2-1 n^ k/2 , \] where Q=Q_m and P=P_m is the planted mixture (cref thm:ld-detection ). If d ≤ n/(4k) and mρ^2(2d)^ k/2-1 /n^ k/2 ≤ c_k , every estimator f=(f_1, ... ,f_n) with pointwise bounds |f_i| ≤ 1 and sign degree at most d in each coordinate satisfies \[ E (frac 1n Σ _i x_i^star f_i(I) )^2 ≤ frac 1n+C_k sqrt frac dn . \] Here the expectation is over a uniform planted assignment and its planted instance. Thus such estimators have vanishing overlap for d=o(n) below the same curve (cref thm:ld-recovery ). Together with the unconditional cleanup converse of cref rem:cleanup-converse , this matches every upper bound of cref thm:main-inference,thm:main-boost within its class.
title: Matching inference lower bounds

label: cor:curve
paper_title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
statement_tex:
\label{cor:curve}
For $k>2$ and clause density $\Delta=m/n$, the inference threshold is,
up to constants depending on $(k,\delta)$,
\[
 \ell\gtrsim \frac{n}{(\rho^2\Delta)^{2/(k-2)}}.
\]
Together with \cref{thm:main-lower}, this shows that the spectral upper
curve agrees, up to constants, with the sign-degree
obstruction in the same fixed-sample model.  Replacing $\rho$ by $\eps$
gives the refutation upper curve; the best canonical sum-of-squares
converse there still has polylogarithmic slack.
statement_text: For k>2 and clause density Δ=m/n , the inference threshold is, up to constants depending on (k,δ) , \[ ell gtrsim frac n (ρ^2Δ)^ 2/(k-2) . \] Together with cref thm:main-lower , this shows that the spectral upper curve agrees, up to constants, with the sign-degree obstruction in the same fixed-sample model. Replacing ρ by ε gives the refutation upper curve; the best canonical sum-of-squares converse there still has polylogarithmic slack.
title: The matched inference curve

label: lem:subsample
paper_title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
statement_tex:
\label{lem:subsample}
Let $I$ consist of $m$ i.i.d.\ clauses from the null or a planted law, and
let $0<\mu\le m/2$.  Draw $M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\mu)$ independently of
$I$; declare failure if $M>m$, and otherwise retain the first $M$
clauses.  Failure has probability at most $e^{-\mu/8}$.  There is a
coupling to an ideal Poisson clause process of total intensity $\mu$,
with atoms i.i.d.\ from the same one-clause law, under which, on the
event $M\le m$, the retained collection agrees with the ideal process
\emph{pathwise}.  Moreover, assigning
each retained clause independently to one of finitely many pools with
fixed probabilities produces independent Poisson pools with the
corresponding sub-intensities.
statement_text: Let I consist of m i.i.d.\ clauses from the null or a planted law, and let 0<μ ≤ m/2 . Draw M Pois (μ) independently of I ; declare failure if M>m , and otherwise retain the first M clauses. Failure has probability at most e^ -μ/8 . There is a coupling to an ideal Poisson clause process of total intensity μ , with atoms i.i.d.\ from the same one-clause law, under which, on the event M ≤ m , the retained collection agrees with the ideal process pathwise . Moreover, assigning each retained clause independently to one of finitely many pools with fixed probabilities produces independent Poisson pools with the corresponding sub-intensities.

label: lem:branch-recursion
paper_title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
statement_tex:
\label{lem:branch-recursion}
Let $\Xi$ be a marked Poisson process of finite intensity $\nu$, and let
$\mathfrak T$ be a finite rooted tree of chronological prefixes.  At a node
$P$, a finite list of atoms has been exposed explicitly and the remaining
background is an independent copy of $\Xi$.  Every node functional below is
evaluated on this residual background; the explicitly exposed atoms are
part of the recorded prefix rather than arguments of $\Xi$.  Let
$\Phi_P(\Xi)\ge0$ be an insertion-nonincreasing prefix weight.  A child is of one of two types.
\begin{enumerate}
\item An \emph{old} child introduces no atom and multiplies by a nonnegative
factor $\psi_{P,j}(\Xi)$ such that $\Phi_P\psi_{P,j}$ remains
insertion-nonincreasing.
\item A \emph{fresh} child of type $\beta$ selects an ordered tuple of
$s_\beta$ distinct background atoms, where $s_\beta\in\{1,2\}$ (this
range suffices for all our applications).  Its transition factor
satisfies
\[
 0\le\psi_{P,\beta}(\Xi;z_1,\ldots,z_{s_\beta})
 \le h_{P,\beta}(z_1,\ldots,z_{s_\beta})/d,
\]
where $h_{P,\beta}\ge0$ is deterministic, and after the selected atoms are
moved to the explicit list the child prefix weight is
insertion-nonincreasing in the residual background.
\end{enumerate}
Let $T_P$ be the sum of the products of all future transition factors below
$P$, with $T_P=1$ at leaves.  Suppose deterministic bounds $B_P$ are chosen
backwards, with $B_P=1$ at leaves, so that pointwise at every internal node
\begin{equation}\label{eq:branch-recursion}
\begin{aligned}
 B_P\ge{}&\sum_{j\text{ old}}\psi_{P,j}(\Xi)B_{P,j}\\
 &+\sum_{\beta\text{ fresh}}
 \int \frac{h_{P,\beta}(\mathbf z)}d
 B_{P,\beta,\mathbf z}\,d\nu^{s_\beta}(\mathbf z).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here a deterministic uniform bound may replace
$B_{P,\beta,\mathbf z}$ for all atoms of one combinatorial branch type.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:branch-conclusion}
 \E[\Phi_P(\Xi)T_P(\Xi)]\le B_P\,\E\Phi_P(\Xi)
\end{equation}
at every node.
statement_text: Let Xi be a marked Poisson process of finite intensity ν , and let T be a finite rooted tree of chronological prefixes. At a node P , a finite list of atoms has been exposed explicitly and the remaining background is an independent copy of Xi . Every node functional below is evaluated on this residual background; the explicitly exposed atoms are part of the recorded prefix rather than arguments of Xi . Let Φ_P(Xi ) ≥ 0 be an insertion-nonincreasing prefix weight. A child is of one of two types. An old child introduces no atom and multiplies by a nonnegative factor ψ_ P,j (Xi ) such that Φ_Pψ_ P,j remains insertion-nonincreasing. A fresh child of type β selects an ordered tuple of s_β distinct background atoms, where s_β ∈ {1,2} (this range suffices for all our applications). Its transition factor satisfies \[ 0 ≤ ψ_ P,β (Xi ;z_1, ... ,z_ s_β ) ≤ h_ P,β (z_1, ... ,z_ s_β )/d, \] where h_ P,β ≥ 0 is deterministic, and after the selected atoms are moved to the explicit list the child prefix weight is insertion-nonincreasing in the residual background. Let T_P be the sum of the products of all future transition factors below P , with T_P=1 at leaves. Suppose deterministic bounds B_P are chosen backwards, with B_P=1 at leaves, so that pointwise at every internal node B_P ≥ & Σ _ j old ψ_ P,j (Xi )B_ P,j &+ Σ _ β fresh int frac h_ P,β (z) d B_ P,β,z dν^ s_β (z). Here a deterministic uniform bound may replace B_ P,β,z for all atoms of one combinatorial branch type. Then E[Φ_P(Xi )T_P(Xi )] ≤ B_P EΦ_P(Xi ) at every node.
title: Branch recursion

label: lem:rounding

statement_tex:
\label{lem:rounding}
Let $\sigma\succeq0$ have trace one, put $\bar x:=\xstar/\sqrt n$, and
assume $\bar x^{\mathsf T}\sigma\bar x\ge c$, $0<c\le1$.  Let $P$
be the spectral projector of $\sigma$ onto eigenvalues at least $c/4$.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rounding-projector}
 \rank P\le\frac4c,
 \qquad
 \|P\bar x\|^2\ge\frac c2.
\end{equation}

the basis vectors and their negatives, repeated $O_c(\log n)$ times,

$1-o(1)$, contains one with
$|\ip z{\xstar}|\ge c'_cn$ for a constant $c'_c>0$.

\label{lem:validation}

label: lem:blocking
paper_title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
statement_tex:
\label{lem:blocking}
Fix $\eps\in(0,1)$ and a certificate procedure $\Cert_0$ that, on
instances whose size lies in $[m_0,2m_0]$, is pointwise sound and satisfies
$\Cert_0\le\eps/4$ under the null with probability $1-o(1)$, uniformly in
that window.  Then for every $m\ge m_0$ the following is pointwise sound
and at most $\eps$ under the null with probability $1-o(1)$: partition the
clause indices into deterministic blocks $I_j$ of sizes
$m_j\in[m_0,2m_0]$ and output
\[
 \Cert(I):=\sum_j\frac{m_j}m\min\{1,\Cert_0(I_j)\}.
\]

label: lem:rational-psd

statement_tex:
\label{lem:rational-psd}
Every rational positive semidefinite matrix $M$ admits a permutation
$\Pi$, a rational unit lower-triangular matrix $L$, and a diagonal matrix
$\Lambda$ with nonnegative rational entries such that
\[
 \Pi^{\mathsf T}M\Pi=L\Lambda L^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Consequently every rational quadratic form defined by a positive
semidefinite matrix is a sum of squares of rational linear forms.

statement_tex:
\label{lem:degree-one-channel}
Let $(I_a,Y_a)_{a=1}^m$ be the derived degree-one channel of fixed bias
$\beta>0$, so $I_a$ is uniform on $[n]$ and under planting
$Y_a=x_{I_a}^\star\eta_a$ with $\E\eta_a=\beta$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The collision statistic
\[
 T:=\sum_{1\le a<b\le m}\1\{I_a=I_b\}Y_aY_b
\]
has null mean zero and variance $\binom m2/n$, while under planting
\[
 \E T=\beta^2\binom m2/n,
 \qquad
 \Var T\le C\left(m^2/n+\beta^2m^3/n^2\right).
\]
Consequently $m=\Theta(\beta^{-2}\sqrt n)$ gives constant statistical
advantage, and $\beta^2m/\sqrt n\to\infty$ gives strong detection.
\item The coordinatewise majority estimator
\[
 \widehat x_i:=\sign\!\left(\sum_{a:I_a=i}Y_a\right)
\]
(with fair tie breaking) has constant overlap with $x^\star$ with
probability $1-o(1)$ once $m\ge C\beta^{-2}n$.
\item On every input,
\[
 \sup_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}
 \left|\frac1m\sum_aY_ax_{I_a}\right|
 =\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^n
 \left|\sum_{a:I_a=i}Y_a\right|.
\]
Under the null, this quantity is $O(\sqrt{n/m})$ with probability
$1-o(1)$.
\end{enumerate}

label: def:ex_post_PE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:ex_post_PE}


Fix bidders $[n]$ and divisible items $[q]$. Bidder $i$ has budget $B_i$, value $v_{ij}$ for item $j$, and paced bid $b_{ij}(\alpha) := \alpha_i v_{ij}$ under multiplier $\alpha_i \in [0,1]$. Let $H_j(\alpha) := \arg\max_{k \in [n]} b_{kj}(\alpha)$ be the highest paced bidders for item $j$. 

A \emph{pacing equilibrium} consists of multipliers $\alpha \in [0,1]^n$, allocation $x \in [0,1]^{n \times q}$, and prices $p \in \mathbb{R}_+^q$ such that, for all $i \in [n]$ and $j \in [q]$:

\squishlist
    \item \emph{Market clearing.} Each item is fully allocated: $\sum_{i=1}^n x_{ij} = 1$. Moreover, only highest paced bidders receive positive allocation: $x_{ij} > 0 \implies i \in H_j(\alpha)$.

    \item \emph{Auction pricing.} If $x_{ij} > 0$, then the price of item $j$ is determined by the auction format: $p_j = b_{ij}(\alpha)$ for \emph{first-price} auctions, and $p_j = \max_{k \neq i} b_{kj}(\alpha)$ for \emph{second-price} auctions.

    \item \emph{Budget feasibility} Each bidder respects their budget: $\sum_{j=1}^q p_j x_{ij} \leq B_i$. If bidder $i$ does not exhaust their budget, then they are unpaced: $\sum_{j=1}^q p_j x_{ij} < B_i \implies \alpha_i = 1$.
\squishend

label: def:ex_post_TE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:ex_post_TE}
Fix bidders $[n]$ and divisible items $[q]$. Bidder $i$ has budget $B_i$, value $v_{ij}$ for item $j$, and enters each auction independently with throttling probability $\theta_i \in [0,1]$, bidding $v_{ij}$ upon entry. A $\pi_S(\theta) := \prod_{k \in S} \theta_k \prod_{k \notin S} (1 - \theta_k)$ fraction of each item is thus contested by entrant set $S \subseteq [n]$; the $\pi_\emptyset(\theta)$ fraction is unsold. Let $H_j(S) := \arg\max_{k \in S} v_{kj}$ be the highest entrants for item $j$.
A \emph{throttling equilibrium} consists of $\theta \in [0,1]^n$, allocations $x^S \in [0,1]^{n \times q}$, and prices $p^S \in \mathbb{R}_+^q$ such that, for all $i \in [n]$, $j \in [q]$, and nonempty $S \subseteq [n]$:
\squishlist
    \item \emph{Market clearing.} Each contested fraction is fully allocated, and only to highest entrants: $\sum_{i=1}^n x^S_{ij} = 1$ and $x^S_{ij} > 0 \implies i \in H_j(S)$.
    \item \emph{Auction pricing.} If $x^S_{ij} > 0$, the auction format sets the price: $p^S_j = v_{ij}$ for \emph{first price}, and $p^S_j = \max_{k \in S \setminus \{i\}} v_{kj}$ for \emph{second price}, with $\max_\emptyset := 0$.
    \item \emph{Budget feasibility.} Each bidder spends within budget: $\sum_{j=1}^q \sum_{S \ni i} \pi_S(\theta)\, p^S_j x^S_{ij} \leq B_i$, with equality whenever $\theta_i < 1$.
\squishend

label: def:GNE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:GNE}
For each player $i \in [n]$, let $\X_i$ be a nonempty, convex, compact private strategy set. Given $\alpha_{-i}$, player $i$ solves $\min_{\alpha_i \in \X_i} l_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i})$ subject to $g_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i}) \leq 0$. Define $\Fe_i(\alpha_{-i}) := {\alpha_i \in \X_i : g_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i}) \leq 0}$. A strategy profile $\alpha^* = (\alpha_1^*,\ldots,\alpha_n^*)$ is a generalized Nash equilibrium if, for every $i \in [n]$, $l_i(\alpha_i^*,\alpha_{-i}^*) \leq l_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i}^*)$ for all $\alpha_i \in \Fe_i(\alpha_{-i}^*)$.
statement_text: For each player i ∈ [n] , let X _i be a nonempty, convex, compact private strategy set. Given α_ -i , player i solves min _ α_i ∈ X _i l_i(α_i,α_ -i ) subject to g_i(α_i,α_ -i ) ≤ 0 . Define F _i(α_ -i ) := α_i ∈ X _i : g_i(α_i,α_ -i ) ≤ 0 . A strategy profile α^* = (α_1^*, ... ,α_n^*) is a generalized Nash equilibrium if, for every i ∈ [n] , l_i(α_i^*,α_ -i ^*) ≤ l_i(α_i,α_ -i ^*) for all α_i ∈ F _i(α_ -i ^*) .
title: Generalized Nash Equilibrium

label: prob:Bayesian_SPTE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{prob:Bayesian_SPTE}
Consider a set of $n$ bidders, where each bidder $i$ has per iteration budget
constraint $\rho_i$ and value distribution $v_i \sim \mathcal{D}_i$. Under
throttling, each bidder $i$ participates in the auction independently with
probability $\alpha_i \in [0,1]$ and, upon participating, submits her truthful
bid $v_i$; let $s_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\alpha_i)$ denote the participation
coin. The ex ante SPTE for the value maximizing bidder setting is a strategy
profile $\alpha^*$ such that each bidder $i \in [n]$'s strategy $\alpha_i^*$
attains the minimum of her optimization problem given the others' strategy
$\alpha_{-i}^*$, i.e.,
\begin{align*}
  l_i(\alpha)
  &:= \min_{\alpha_i \in [0,1]}
  \mathbb{E}_{v \sim \mathcal{D},\, s \sim \mathrm{Ber}(\alpha)}
    \!\big[-\,x_i(\alpha)\, v_i\big] \\
  \text{s.t.}\quad
  g_i(\alpha)
  &:= \mathbb{E}_{v \sim \mathcal{D},\, s \sim \mathrm{Ber}(\alpha)}
    \!\Big[\, x_i(\alpha)\, \max_{j \neq i:\, s_j = 1} v_j \,\Big] - \rho_i
  \;\le\; 0
  \qquad \text{budget constraint} .
\end{align*}
where $x_i(\alpha) := s_i \cdot \mathbbm{1} \{\, v_i \ge \max_{j:\, s_j = 1} v_j \,\}$
is the throttled allocation, $\alpha = (\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$, and
$\mathcal{D} = \prod_{i \in [n]} \mathcal{D}_i$ denotes the (independent) product
Gaussian distribution over bidders' values.

label: thm:condition_autobid_diffuse_model
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{thm:condition_autobid_diffuse_model}

Under the diffuse analysis with value distribution satisfying the distributional regularity condition (Ass.~\ref{ass:dist_regular}), for both second price pacing equilibrium and second price throttling equlibriums, the following properties hold: For every $i \in [n]$, given $1>\underline{\alpha} > 0$.

\squishlist
    \item \textbf{Continuously Differentiability}. the loss function $\ell_i$ and the constraint function $g_i$ are contiunously differentiable for all $\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_j, j \neq i$.
    \item \textbf{Bounded Hessian}. 
    
    The functions \(\ell_i\) and \(g_i\) have bounded Hessians. More precisely, for every \(f_i\in\{\ell_i,g_i\}\) and every \(j,k\in[n]\), \[ \left| \frac{\partial^2 f_i} {\partial\alpha_j\,\partial\alpha_k} \right| = \begin{cases} O(n^2), & j=k=i,\\ O(n), & \lvert\{j,k\}\cap\{i\}\rvert=1,\\ O(1), & j\neq i \text{ and } k\neq i. \end{cases} \]
    \item \textbf{Monotonicity}. $\ell_i$ is monotonically decreasing, and $g_i$ is monotonically increasing with $\alpha_i$.
    \item \textbf{P\L{}}. There exist $\mu_l^i, \mu_g^i$, such that $\ell_i$ satisfies $\mu_l^i$-P\L{}, and $g_i$ satisfies $\mu_g^i$-P\L{} for $\alpha_i \in [\underline{\alpha}, 1]$.

    \item \textbf{Relative Lipschitzness}. There exist an $L_c >0$, such that $\ell_i$ is relative $L_c$ Lipschitz with $g_i$ for any $\alpha_i \in [\underline{\alpha}, 1]$.
    

\squishend

statement_tex:
\label{def:aug_lagrangian} 
Given the local optimization problem defined in Def.~\ref{def:GNE}, we define the the augmented Lagrangian function of every bidder $i \in [n]$ as follows:$
\lag^i(\alpha_i, \alpha_{-i},\lambda_i) = l_i(\alpha) + \frac{\lambda_i}{2} (g_i(\alpha) + |g_i (\alpha)|)$,
where $l_i$ is the loss function, $\lambda_i \geq 0$ is the Lagrangian dual multipliers for the constraint. Here we use $g_i(x) + |g_i(x)| = \max\{0, g_i(x)\}$ as a substitute for the original constraint function $g_i (x)$.

label: def:app: ex_post_PE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:app: ex_post_PE}

Fix bidders $[n]$ and divisible items $[q]$. Bidder $i$ has budget $B_i$, value $v_{ij}$ for item $j$, and paced bid $b_{ij}(\alpha) := \alpha_i v_{ij}$ under multiplier $\alpha_i \in [0,1]$. Let $H_j(\alpha) := \arg\max_{k \in [n]} b_{kj}(\alpha)$ be the highest paced bidders for item $j$. 

A \emph{pacing equilibrium} consists of multipliers $\alpha \in [0,1]^n$, allocation $x \in [0,1]^{n \times q}$, and prices $p \in \mathbb{R}_+^q$ such that, for all $i \in [n]$ and $j \in [q]$:


\squishlist
    \item \emph{Market clearing.} Each item is fully allocated: $\sum_{i=1}^n x_{ij} = 1$. Moreover, only highest paced bidders receive positive allocation: $x_{ij} > 0 \implies i \in H_j(\alpha)$.

    \item \emph{Auction pricing.} If $x_{ij} > 0$, then the price of item $j$ is determined by the auction format: $p_j = b_{ij}(\alpha)$ for \emph{first-price} auctions, and $p_j = \max_{k \neq i} b_{kj}(\alpha)$ for \emph{second-price} auctions.

    \item \emph{Budget feasibility} Each bidder respects their budget: $\sum_{j=1}^q p_j x_{ij} \leq B_i$. If bidder $i$ does not exhaust their budget, then they are unpaced: $\sum_{j=1}^q p_j x_{ij} < B_i \implies \alpha_i = 1$.
\squishend

label: def:app:ex_post_TE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:app:ex_post_TE}
Fix bidders $[n]$ and divisible items $[q]$. Bidder $i$ has budget $B_i$, value $v_{ij}$ for item $j$, and throttling parameter $\theta_i \in [0,1]$: with probability $\theta_i$, bidder $i$ enters the auction and submits the truthful bid $b_{ij} := v_{ij}$, independently across bidders. Thus a $\pi_S(\theta) := \prod_{k \in S} \theta_k \prod_{k \notin S} (1 - \theta_k)$ fraction of each item is contested by exactly the entrants $S \subseteq [n]$; the $\pi_\emptyset(\theta)$ fraction goes unsold. Let $H_j(S) := \arg\max_{k \in S} b_{kj}$ be the highest entrants for item $j$.
A \emph{throttling equilibrium} consists of parameters $\theta \in [0,1]^n$ together with allocations $x^S \in [0,1]^{n \times q}$ and prices $p^S \in \mathbb{R}_+^q$ for each nonempty $S \subseteq [n]$ such that, for all $i \in [n]$, $j \in [q]$, and nonempty $S \subseteq [n]$:
\squishlist
    \item \emph{Market clearing.} Each contested fraction is fully allocated: $\sum_{i=1}^n x^S_{ij} = 1$. Moreover, only highest entrants receive positive allocation: $x^S_{ij} > 0 \implies i \in H_j(S)$.
    \item \emph{Auction pricing.} If $x^S_{ij} > 0$, then the price of item $j$ on fraction $S$ is determined by the auction format: $p^S_j = b_{ij}$ for \emph{first price} auctions, and $p^S_j = \max_{k \in S \setminus \{i\}} b_{kj}$ for \emph{second price} auctions, with $\max_\emptyset := 0$.
    \item \emph{Budget feasibility.} Each bidder respects their budget in aggregate: $\sum_{j=1}^q \sum_{S \ni i} \pi_S(\theta)\, p^S_j x^S_{ij} \leq B_i$. If bidder $i$ does not exhaust their budget, then they are unthrottled: $\sum_{j=1}^q \sum_{S \ni i} \pi_S(\theta)\, p^S_j x^S_{ij} < B_i \implies \theta_i = 1$.
\squishend

statement_text: Given a set of n players where each player i ∈ [n] deploys strategy α_i and optimizes the objective function l_i subject to the constraints g_i below: min _ α_i ∈ X _i l_i (α_i, α_ -i ) quad s.t. quad &quad g_i (α_i, α_ -i ) ≤ 0 where X _i is a nonempty, convex, closed and bounded "private" strategy set of player i . label: def:powerlaw
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:powerlaw}
A probability distribution supported on $[0,\infty)$ is a \emph{power law distribution} with tail exponent $\gamma>0$ if it admits a density $p$ of the form
\[
p(x)=\gamma(1+x)^{-(\gamma+1)},
\qquad x\ge 0.
\]
Equivalently, a random variable $V$ with this distribution has survival function
\[
\Pr[V>x]=(1+x)^{-\gamma},
\qquad x\ge 0.
\]
statement_text: A probability distribution supported on [0, ∞ ) is a power law distribution with tail exponent γ>0 if it admits a density p of the form \[ p(x)=γ(1+x)^ -(γ+1) , qquad x ≥ 0. \] Equivalently, a random variable V with this distribution has survival function \[ Pr [V>x]=(1+x)^ -γ , qquad x ≥ 0. \]
title: Power law distribution

\qquad x\ge 0,
\]
where $\gamma_i>3$ is the tail exponent. Equivalently, its survival function satisfies
\[
\Pr[V_i>x]=(1+x)^{-\gamma_i},
\qquad x\ge 0.
\]
statement_text: For each bidder i ∈ [n] , the value distribution has a density p_i supported on [0, ∞ ) of the form \[ p_i(x)=γ_i(1+x)^ -(γ_i+1) , qquad x ≥ 0, \] where γ_i>3 is the tail exponent. Equivalently, its survival function satisfies \[ Pr [V_i>x]=(1+x)^ -γ_i , qquad x ≥ 0. \]
title: Smooth power-law Distribution

paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
A distribution \(F\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) is sub-Gaussian if there exist constants \(C,c>0\) such that, for \(V\sim F\),
\[
\Pr\!\left(\left|V-\mathbb{E}[V]\right|\ge t\right)
\le C e^{-ct^2},
\qquad t\ge 0.
\]
statement_text: A distribution \(F\) on \( R \) is sub-Gaussian if there exist constants \(C,c>0\) such that, for \(V F\), \[ Pr ( |V- E [V] | ≥ t ) ≤ C e^ -ct^2 , qquad t ≥ 0. \]
title: Sub-Gaussian Distribution

label: ass:app:smooth_subgaussian
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{ass:app:smooth_subgaussian}
For each bidder $i\in[n]$, the value distribution is supported on
$[0,\infty)$ and has a positive density $p_i$ on $[0,\infty)$. Moreover,
$p_i$ is continuously differentiable, and both $p_i$ and $p_i'$ are
uniformly bounded: there exist constants $P_i,Q_i<\infty$ such that
\[
        \sup_{x\ge 0} p_i(x)\le P_i,
        \qquad
        \sup_{x\ge 0} |p_i'(x)|\le Q_i .
\]
In addition, the distribution has a sub-Gaussian tail: there exist constants
$C_i,c_i>0$ such that
\[
        \Pr[V_i>x]\le C_i e^{-c_i x^2},
        \qquad x\ge 0 .
\]
statement_text: For each bidder i ∈ [n] , the value distribution is supported on [0, ∞ ) and has a positive density p_i on [0, ∞ ) . Moreover, p_i is continuously differentiable, and both p_i and p_i' are uniformly bounded: there exist constants P_i,Q_i< ∞ such that \[ sup _ x ≥ 0 p_i(x) ≤ P_i, qquad sup _ x ≥ 0 |p_i'(x)| ≤ Q_i . \] In addition, the distribution has a sub-Gaussian tail: there exist constants C_i,c_i>0 such that \[ Pr [V_i>x] ≤ C_i e^ -c_i x^2 , qquad x ≥ 0 . \]
title: Smooth sub-Gaussian distribution

statement_text: The Beta function, denoted by B(a,b) , is defined for all a,b>0 as B(a,b) &= int _0^1 t^ a-1 (1-t)^ b-1 dt. The Beta function is related to the Gamma function through the identity B(a,b) &= frac Γ(a)Γ(b) Γ(a+b) .

label: prob:app:local-opt-bayesian-sppe
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{prob:app:local-opt-bayesian-sppe}
For $\alpha \in \A$, bidder $i$'s allocation indicator in the second-price pacing auction is $x_i(\alpha,V)=\1{\alpha_iV_i\ge \max_{j\ne i}\alpha_jV_j}$. Define the loss and payment-surplus functions by $l_i(\alpha):=-\E[V_i x_i(\alpha,V)]$ and $g_i(\alpha):=\E[x_i(\alpha,V)\max_{j\ne i}\alpha_jV_j]-\rho_i$. At a fixed rival profile $\alpha_{-i}$, bidder $i$ solves $\min_{\alpha_i\in[\underline\alpha,1]} l_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i})$ subject to $g_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i})\le0$.
statement_text: For α ∈ X _α , bidder i 's allocation indicator in the second-price pacing auction is x_i(α,V)=\1 α_iV_i ≥ max _ j ≠ i α_jV_j . Define the loss and payment-surplus functions by l_i(α):=- E [V_i x_i(α,V)] and g_i(α):= E [x_i(α,V)max _ j ≠ i α_jV_j]-ρ_i . At a fixed rival profile α_ -i , bidder i solves min _ α_i ∈ [underline α,1] l_i(α_i,α_ -i ) subject to g_i(α_i,α_ -i ) ≤ 0 .

label: lem:dist_comp_bid_SPPE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:dist_comp_bid_SPPE}
For fixed \(\alpha_{-i}\), the random variable
\[
        Y_i:=\max_{j\ne i}\alpha_jV_j
\]
has CDF \(H_i(\cdot;\alpha_{-i})\).  Moreover \(H_i\) is continuously
differentiable on \([0,\infty)\), with
\[
        h_i(t;\alpha_{-i})
        =
        \sum_{j\ne i}
        {p_j(t/\alpha_j)\over \alpha_j}
        \prod_{k\ne i,j}F_k(t/\alpha_k).
\]
statement_text: For fixed \(α_ -i \), the random variable \[ Y_i:=max _ j ≠ i α_jV_j \] has CDF \(H_i( · ;α_ -i )\). Moreover \(H_i\) is continuously differentiable on \([0, ∞ )\), with \[ h_i(t;α_ -i ) = Σ _ j ≠ i p_j(t/α_j)over α_j Π _ k ≠ i,j F_k(t/α_k). \]

label: lem:sppe-integral-formulas_SPPE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:sppe-integral-formulas_SPPE}
For every \(\alpha\in\A\),
\[
        -l_i(\alpha)
        =
        \int_0^\infty v p_i(v)H_i(\alpha_i v;\alpha_{-i})\dd v,
\]
and
\[
        g_i(\alpha)+\rho_i
        =
        \int_0^\infty p_i(v)
        \left[
        \alpha_i vH_i(\alpha_i v;\alpha_{-i})
        -
        \int_0^{\alpha_i v}H_i(t;\alpha_{-i})\dd t
        \right]\dd v .
\]
statement_text: For every \(α ∈ X _α\), \[ -l_i(α) = int _0^ ∞ v p_i(v)H_i(α_i v;α_ -i ) d v, \] and \[ g_i(α)+ρ_i = int _0^ ∞ p_i(v) [ α_i vH_i(α_i v;α_ -i ) - int _0^ α_i v H_i(t;α_ -i ) d t ] d v . \]

\label{prop:sppe-hessian-bounds}

\]
for all distinct \(j,k\ne i\).
statement_text: For every bidder \(i\), there are finite constants \[ L_ i,ii ^g,\ L_ i,jj ^g,\ L_ i,jk ^g,\ L_ i,ij ^g, qquad L_ i,ii ^ell ,\ L_ i,jj ^ell ,\ L_ i,jk ^ell ,\ L_ i,ij ^ell , \] depending only on \(underline α,n\) and the constants in Assumption , such that for all \(α ∈ X _α\), \[ |partial _ α_iα_i ^2g_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,ii ^g, qquad |partial _ α_jα_j ^2g_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,jj ^g, \] \[ |partial _ α_jα_k ^2g_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,jk ^g, qquad |partial _ α_iα_j ^2g_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,ij ^g, \] and \[ |partial _ α_iα_i ^2l_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,ii ^ell , qquad |partial _ α_jα_j ^2l_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,jj ^ell , \] \[ |partial _ α_jα_k ^2l_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,jk ^ell , qquad |partial _ α_iα_j ^2l_i(α)| ≤ L_ i,ij ^ell , \] for all distinct \(j,k ≠ i\).

For every \(i\) and every \(\alpha\in\A\),
