        \partial_{\alpha_i}g_i(\alpha)\ge m_i^g>0.
\]
statement_text: For every \(i\) and every \(α ∈ X _α\), \[ partial _ α_i g_i(α) ≥ m_i^g>0. \]
title: Self-gradient lower bound, constraint

label: lem:PL_obj_constraint_SPPE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:PL_obj_constraint_SPPE}
\label{lem:app:PL_obj_constraint_SPPE}
Fix bidder \(i\) and a rival profile
\(\alpha_{-i}\in[\underline\alpha,1]^{n-1}\).  The one-dimensional function
\[
        x\mapsto l_i(x,\alpha_{-i})
\]
satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality on
\([\underline\alpha,1]\) with parameter
\[
        \mu_i^\ell=
        {(m_i^\ell)^2\over 2U_i^\ell(1-\underline\alpha)}.
\]
The one-dimensional function
\[
        x\mapsto g_i(x,\alpha_{-i})
\]
satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality on
\([\underline\alpha,1]\) with parameter
\[
        \mu_i^g=
        {(m_i^g)^2\over 2U_i^g(1-\underline\alpha)}.
\]
statement_text: Fix bidder \(i\) and a rival profile \(α_ -i ∈ [underline α,1]^ n-1 \). The one-dimensional function \[ xmapsto l_i(x,α_ -i ) \] satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality on \([underline α,1]\) with parameter \[ μ_i^ell = (m_i^ell )^2over 2U_i^ell (1-underline α) . \] The one-dimensional function \[ xmapsto g_i(x,α_ -i ) \] satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality on \([underline α,1]\) with parameter \[ μ_i^g= (m_i^g)^2over 2U_i^g(1-underline α) . \]
title: PL condition for objective and constraint

label: lem:relative_lipschitzness
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:relative_lipschitzness}
\label{lem:app:relative_lipschitzness}
For every \(i\), every \(\alpha_{-i}\in[\underline\alpha,1]^{n-1}\), and all
\(x,y\in[\underline\alpha,1]\),
\[
        {m_i^g\over U_i^\ell}
        |l_i(x,\alpha_{-i})-l_i(y,\alpha_{-i})|
        \le
        |g_i(x,\alpha_{-i})-g_i(y,\alpha_{-i})|.
\]
Thus \(x\mapsto l_i(x,\alpha_{-i})\) is relative
\(m_i^g/U_i^\ell\)-Lipschitz (Def.~\ref{def:compare_lipschitz}) with respect to
\(x\mapsto g_i(x,\alpha_{-i})\).
statement_text: For every \(i\), every \(α_ -i ∈ [underline α,1]^ n-1 \), and all \(x,y ∈ [underline α,1]\), \[ m_i^gover U_i^ell |l_i(x,α_ -i )-l_i(y,α_ -i )| ≤ |g_i(x,α_ -i )-g_i(y,α_ -i )|. \] Thus \(xmapsto l_i(x,α_ -i )\) is relative \(m_i^g/U_i^ell \)-Lipschitz (Def. ) with respect to \(xmapsto g_i(x,α_ -i )\).
title: Coordinatewise relative Lipschitzness, SPPE

label: lem:app:bounded_0_th_SPPE
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:app:bounded_0_th_SPPE}
For every bidder \(i\) and every \(\alpha\in\A\),
\[
        |l_i(\alpha)|\le \E[V_i],
        \qquad
        |g_i(\alpha)|\le \E[V_i]+\rho_i .
\]
Consequently, with
\[
        C_\ell:=\max_i\E[V_i],
        \qquad
        C_g:=\max_i(\E[V_i]+\rho_i),
\]
we have uniformly over all bidders and all \(\alpha\in\A\),
\[
        |l_i(\alpha)|\le C_\ell,
        \qquad
        |g_i(\alpha)|\le C_g.
\]
statement_text: For every bidder \(i\) and every \(α ∈ X _α\), \[ |l_i(α)| ≤ E [V_i], qquad |g_i(α)| ≤ E [V_i]+ρ_i . \] Consequently, with \[ C_ell :=max _i E [V_i], qquad C_g:=max _i( E [V_i]+ρ_i), \] we have uniformly over all bidders and all \(α ∈ X _α\), \[ |l_i(α)| ≤ C_ell , qquad |g_i(α)| ≤ C_g. \]
title: Bounded function values

label: prob:app:local-opt-bayesian-spte
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex: \label{prob:app:local-opt-bayesian-spte} For $\alpha\in{\A}$, let $S_i\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\alpha_i)$ denote bidder $i$'s participation indicator, independently across bidders and independently of the values. Bidder $i$'s allocation indicator in the second-price throttling auction is \[ \widehat x_i(\alpha,V,S) := S_i\1\left\{V_i\ge \max_{j\ne i:S_j=1}V_j\right\}, \] where ties occur with probability zero and the maximum over an empty set is defined as zero. Define the throttling loss and payment-surplus functions by \[ \widehat l_i(\alpha) := -\E[V_i\widehat x_i(\alpha,V,S)] \] and \[ \widehat g_i(\alpha) := \E\left[ \widehat x_i(\alpha,V,S) \max_{j\ne i:S_j=1}V_j \right]-\rho_i. \] At a fixed rival profile $\alpha_{-i}$, bidder $i$ solves \[ \min_{\alpha_i\in[\underline\alpha,1]} \widehat l_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i}) \qquad \text{subject to} \qquad \widehat g_i(\alpha_i,\alpha_{-i})\le 0. \]
statement_text: For α ∈ X _α , let S_i Bernoulli (α_i) denote bidder i 's participation indicator, independently across bidders and independently of the values. Bidder i 's allocation indicator in the second-price throttling auction is \[ widehat x_i(α,V,S) := S_i\1 {V_i ≥ max _ j ≠ i:S_j=1 V_j }, \] where ties occur with probability zero and the maximum over an empty set is defined as zero. Define the throttling loss and payment-surplus functions by \[ widehat l_i(α) := - E [V_iwidehat x_i(α,V,S)] \] and \[ widehat g_i(α) := E [ widehat x_i(α,V,S) max _ j ≠ i:S_j=1 V_j ]-ρ_i. \] At a fixed rival profile α_ -i , bidder i solves \[ min _ α_i ∈ [underline α,1] widehat l_i(α_i,α_ -i ) qquad subject to qquad widehat g_i(α_i,α_ -i ) ≤ 0. \]
title: Local Optimization Problem, Bayesian SPTE

label: ass:spte-regular
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{ass:spte-regular}
For each bidder \(i\), \(p_i\) is positive and \(C^1\) on \((0,\infty)\), and
\[
        P_i:=\sup_{x\ge0}p_i(x)<\infty,\qquad
        Q_i:=\sup_{x\ge0}|p_i'(x)|<\infty,
\]
\[
        \int_0^\infty (1+x^3)p_i(x)\dd x<\infty .
\]
statement_text: For each bidder \(i\), \(p_i\) is positive and \(C^1\) on \((0, ∞ )\), and \[ P_i:=sup _ x ≥ 0 p_i(x)< ∞ ,qquad Q_i:=sup _ x ≥ 0 |p_i'(x)|< ∞ , \] \[ int _0^ ∞ (1+x^3)p_i(x) d x< ∞ . \]
title: Distributional Regularity

label: lem:throttle-cdf
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:throttle-cdf}
For fixed \(\alpha_{-i}\), the random variable
\[
        \widehat Y_i:=\max_{j\ne i:S_j=1}V_j
\]
has CDF \(\widehat H_i(\cdot;\alpha_{-i})\).
statement_text: For fixed \(α_ -i \), the random variable \[ widehat Y_i:=max _ j ≠ i:S_j=1 V_j \] has CDF \(widehat H_i( · ;α_ -i )\).
title: Active-rival maximum

label: lem:throttle-formulas
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:throttle-formulas}
For every \(\alpha\in{\A}\),
\[
        \widehat l_i(\alpha)
        =
        -\alpha_i
        \int_0^\infty v p_i(v)\widehat H_i(v;\alpha_{-i})\dd v,
\]
and
\[
        \widehat g_i(\alpha)+\rho_i
        =
        \alpha_i
        \int_0^\infty p_i(v)
        \left[
        v\widehat H_i(v;\alpha_{-i})
        -
        \int_0^v\widehat H_i(t;\alpha_{-i})\dd t
        \right]\dd v .
\]
statement_text: For every \(α ∈ X _α \), \[ widehat l_i(α) = -α_i int _0^ ∞ v p_i(v)widehat H_i(v;α_ -i ) d v, \] and \[ widehat g_i(α)+ρ_i = α_i int _0^ ∞ p_i(v) [ vwidehat H_i(v;α_ -i ) - int _0^vwidehat H_i(t;α_ -i ) d t ] d v . \]
title: Throttling integral formulas

label: lem:throttle-smooth
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:throttle-smooth}
Let \(a=\underline\alpha\) and \(U=(a/2,1+a/2)^n\).  Under
Assumption~\ref{ass:spte-regular}, each \(\widehat l_i\) and \(\widehat g_i\)
extends to a \(C^2\) function on \(U\).  All first and second partial
derivatives are bounded on \({\A}\).
statement_text: Let \(a=underline α\) and \(U=(a/2,1+a/2)^n\). Under Assumption , each \(widehat l_i\) and \(widehat g_i\) extends to a \(C^2\) function on \(U\). All first and second partial derivatives are bounded on \( X _α \).
title: Throttling smoothness

label: lem:throttle-monotone
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:throttle-monotone}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:spte-regular}, for every \(i\) and every \(\alpha\in{\A}\),
\[
        \partial_{\alpha_i}\widehat l_i(\alpha)<0,
        \qquad
        \partial_{\alpha_i}\widehat g_i(\alpha)>0.
\]
Moreover the quantities
\[
        \widehat m_i^\ell:=\inf_{\alpha_{-i}}\widehat A_i(\alpha_{-i}),
        \qquad
        \widehat U_i^\ell:=\sup_{\alpha_{-i}}\widehat A_i(\alpha_{-i}),
\]
\[
        \widehat m_i:=\inf_{\alpha_{-i}}\widehat C_i(\alpha_{-i}),
        \qquad
        \widehat U_i^g:=\sup_{\alpha_{-i}}\widehat C_i(\alpha_{-i})
\]
are finite and strictly positive, where the infima and suprema range over
\([\underline\alpha,1]^{n-1}\).
statement_text: Under Assumption , for every \(i\) and every \(α ∈ X _α \), \[ partial _ α_i widehat l_i(α)<0, qquad partial _ α_i widehat g_i(α)>0. \] Moreover the quantities \[ widehat m_i^ell :=inf _ α_ -i widehat A_i(α_ -i ), qquad widehat U_i^ell :=sup _ α_ -i widehat A_i(α_ -i ), \] \[ widehat m_i:=inf _ α_ -i widehat C_i(α_ -i ), qquad widehat U_i^g:=sup _ α_ -i widehat C_i(α_ -i ) \] are finite and strictly positive, where the infima and suprema range over \([underline α,1]^ n-1 \).
title: Throttling own-coordinate monotonicity

label: prop:throttle-pl
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{prop:throttle-pl}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:spte-regular}, fix \(i\) and
\(\alpha_{-i}\in[\underline\alpha,1]^{n-1}\).  The one-dimensional maps
\[
        x\mapsto \widehat l_i(x,\alpha_{-i}),
        \qquad
        x\mapsto \widehat g_i(x,\alpha_{-i})
\]
satisfy the following uniform properties on \([\underline\alpha,1]\):
\[
        |\partial_x\widehat l_i(x,\alpha_{-i})|
        \ge \widehat m_i^\ell,
        \qquad
        \partial_x\widehat g_i(x,\alpha_{-i})\ge \widehat m_i.
\]
The loss satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality with parameter
\[
        \widehat\mu_i^\ell=
        {\widehat m_i^\ell\over 2(1-\underline\alpha)},
\]
and the constraint function satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality with
parameter
\[
        \widehat\mu_i^g=
        {\widehat m_i\over 2(1-\underline\alpha)}.
\]
Moreover \(x\mapsto \widehat l_i(x,\alpha_{-i})\) is relative
\(\widehat L_i\)-Lipschitz with respect to
\(x\mapsto \widehat g_i(x,\alpha_{-i})\), where
\[
        \widehat L_i={\widehat m_i\over \widehat U_i^\ell}.
\]
Finally, for every \(\alpha\in{\A}\),
\[
        |\widehat l_i(\alpha)|\le \E[V_i],
        \qquad
        |\widehat g_i(\alpha)|\le \E[V_i]+\rho_i .
\]
statement_text: Under Assumption , fix \(i\) and \(α_ -i ∈ [underline α,1]^ n-1 \). The one-dimensional maps \[ xmapsto widehat l_i(x,α_ -i ), qquad xmapsto widehat g_i(x,α_ -i ) \] satisfy the following uniform properties on \([underline α,1]\): \[ |partial _xwidehat l_i(x,α_ -i )| ≥ widehat m_i^ell , qquad partial _xwidehat g_i(x,α_ -i ) ≥ widehat m_i. \] The loss satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality with parameter \[ widehat μ_i^ell = widehat m_i^ell over 2(1-underline α) , \] and the constraint function satisfies the Polyak--Lojasiewicz inequality with parameter \[ widehat μ_i^g= widehat m_iover 2(1-underline α) . \] Moreover \(xmapsto widehat l_i(x,α_ -i )\) is relative \(widehat L_i\)-Lipschitz with respect to \(xmapsto widehat g_i(x,α_ -i )\), where \[ widehat L_i= widehat m_iover widehat U_i^ell . \] Finally, for every \(α ∈ X _α \), \[ |widehat l_i(α)| ≤ E [V_i], qquad |widehat g_i(α)| ≤ E [V_i]+ρ_i . \]
title: PL , self-gradient, relative-Lipschitz, and bounded-value bounds

label: def:app:weak_convexity
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:app:weak_convexity}
A function $f: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be 
\emph{$\rho_{\textsc{wc}}$-weakly convex} if 
$
    f(x) + \frac{\rho_{\textsc{wc}}}{2}\|x\|^2
$
is convex in $x$. Equivalently, $f$ has curvature bounded below by 
$-\rho_{\textsc{wc}}$.
statement_text: A function f: X → R is said to be ρ_ sc wc -weakly convex if f(x) + frac ρ_ sc wc 2 |x|^2 is convex in x . Equivalently, f has curvature bounded below by -ρ_ sc wc .
title: Weak Convexity

label: def:app:weak_concave_convex
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{def:app:weak_concave_convex}
Consider a minimax saddle-point problem of the form, where $\X_x$ and $\X_y$ are convex: $\min_{x \in \X_x} \max_{y \in \X_y} f(x, y).
$ The function $ f: \X_x \times \X_y \to \mathbb{R} $ is said to be \emph{\((\rho_x, \rho_y)\)-weakly convex–concave} if: 
\squishlist
    \item For any fixed \( y \in \mathcal{Y} \), the function \( f(\cdot, y) \) is \( \rho_x \)-weakly convex, i.e., $f(x, y) + \frac{\rho_x}{2} \|x\|^2$ is convex in $x$. 
    \item For any fixed \( x \in \mathcal{X} \), the function \(f(x, \cdot) \) is \( \rho_y \)-weakly concave, i.e., $-f(x, y) + \frac{\rho_y}{2} \|y\|^2$ is convex in $ y$.  
\squishend
statement_text: Consider a minimax saddle-point problem of the form, where X _x and X _y are convex: min _ x ∈ X _x max _ y ∈ X _y f(x, y). The function f: X _x × X _y → R is said to be \((ρ_x, ρ_y)\)-weakly convex–concave if: bullet setlength sep 0pt setlength parsep 3pt setlength topsep 3pt setlength partopsep 0pt setlength margin 1em setlength width 1em setlength sep 0.5em For any fixed \( y ∈ Y \), the function \( f( · , y) \) is \( ρ_x \)-weakly convex, i.e., f(x, y) + frac ρ_x 2 |x|^2 is convex in x . For any fixed \( x ∈ X \), the function \(f(x, · ) \) is \( ρ_y \)-weakly concave, i.e., -f(x, y) + frac ρ_y 2 |y|^2 is convex in y .
title: Weakly Convex Weakly Concave

label: def:app:moreau_envelope
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_text: Let f: R ^d → (- ∞ ,+ ∞ ] be a proper, lower semicontinuous function and let \(η>0\). The Moreau envelope of \(f\) with parameter \(η\) is defined by \[ f_η(x) := inf _ y ∈ R ^d { f(y) + frac η 2 |x-y|^2 }, qquad x ∈ R ^d. \] The associated proximal operator is well-defined and unique, as defined below: \[ prox _ η f (x) := arg min _ y ∈ R ^d { f(y) + frac η 2 |x-y|^2 }. \]
title: Moreau Envelope

label: lem:app:grad_moreau
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_text: Let f: R ^n → R be ρ_sc wc -weakly convex and let η > ρ_sc wc . Let \[ x_+ = arg min _ u { f(u) + frac η 2 |u - x|^2 } \] be the proximal point. Then nabla f_η(x) = η(x - x_+) = nabla f(x_+). Moreover, if f is twice differentiable, then the Hessian of the Moreau envelope is nabla ^2 f_η(x) &= η I - η^2 (η I + nabla ^2 f(x_+) )^ -1 .
title: Gradient of the Moreau Envelope

label: lem:app:grad_moreau_constr
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_tex:
\label{lem:app:grad_moreau_constr}
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\eta>\rho_\textsc{wc}$-weakly convex and $C^1$, let $\X_x \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty closed convex, and let $\eta > \rho_\textsc{wc}$. Let
\[
x_+ = \arg\min_{u \in \X_x} \left\{ f(u) + \frac{\eta}{2}\|u - x\|^2 \right\}
\]
be the constrained proximal point. Then $f_\eta\in C^1$ with $\nabla f_\eta(x)=\eta(x-x_+)$, and for $x\in\X_x$,
\[
\|\nabla f(x_+)\| \;\ge\; \eta\,\|x - x_+\| .
\]
statement_text: Let f: R ^n → R be η>ρ_sc wc -weakly convex and C^1 , let X _x ⊆ R ^n be nonempty closed convex, and let η > ρ_sc wc . Let \[ x_+ = arg min _ u ∈ X _x { f(u) + frac η 2 |u - x|^2 } \] be the constrained proximal point. Then f_η ∈ C^1 with nabla f_η(x)=η(x-x_+) , and for x ∈ X _x , \[ |nabla f(x_+)| ≥ η |x - x_+| . \]
title: Gradient of the constrained Moreau Envelope

label: def:saddle_env
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_text: Given a saddle point optimization problem min _ x ∈ X _x max _ y ∈ X _y L (x, y) , with X _x, X _y convex, its saddle envelope is defined as: L _ η (x,y) = min _ u ∈ X _x max _ v ∈ X _y L_sc Saddle (u,v):= L (u, v) + η_1/2 |u - x|^2 - η_2/2 |v - y|^2
title: Saddle Envelope

label: lem:app:saddle_env_grad
paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_text: Let z = (x, y) , and let z_ + = (x_ + , y_ + ) = prox _η(z) denote the proximal update. Then the gradient of the saddle envelope L _η(x, y) satisfies: |nabla _x L (z_ + )|_2 ≥ η_1 |x - x_ + |_2, quad |nabla _y L (z_ + )|_2 ≥ η_2 |y_ + - y|_2. nabla _x L _η(x) = η_1 (x - x_ + ), quad nabla _y L _η(y) = -η_2 (y - y_ + ) where the first (resp., second) equality holds if and only if x_ + (resp., y_ + ) is not on the boundary of X _x (resp., X _y ).
title: Gradient of Saddle Envelope

paper_title: Beyond the PPAD hardness of Auto-bidding Auctions
statement_text: Consider the saddle envelope L_η(z) , where z = (α, λ) . Its Hessian satisfies the following: nabla _ λ λ ^2 L_η(z) &= -η_2 I + η_2^2 ( η_2 I + nabla _ λ λ ^2 L(z_+) + nabla _ λ α ^2 L(z_+) ( η_1 I + nabla _ α α ^2 L(z_+) )^ -1 nabla _ α λ ^2 L(z_+) )^ -1 .

Given the GNE setting (Def.~\ref{def:SM_GNE}) with $\X_\alpha = (0,1]$, there exists a finite global saddle point (Def.~\ref{def:saddle_point}) of its Lagrangian function as in Def.~\ref{def:aug_lagrangian}. Each saddle point corresponds to a GNE.

    Let $C_\lambda := L_c + 1$. Then for $(\alpha, \lambda)$ such that $\lag_\eta (\alpha, \lambda) = \min_{\alpha_{+}} \lag_\lambda $ (Case (ii)), $\lag_\eta (\alpha, \lambda)$ satisfies primal side PL with parameter $\nicefrac{\mu_2 \eta}{(\mu_2 + \eta)}.$

label: lem:prop_m

statement_tex:
\label{lem:spectral_norm}
The \textbf{spectral norm} of a matrix $L \in \R^{n \times n}$, denoted as $\|L\|_2$, is defined as $\|L\|_2 = \sup_{\|x\|_2 = 1} \|Lx\|_2$.

For a \textbf{symmetric} matrix $L$ (i.e., $L = L^T$), the spectral norm simplifies to the \textbf{largest absolute eigenvalue}: $\|L\|_2 = \max |\lambda_i(L)|$, where $\lambda_i(L)$ are the eigenvalues of $L$.

The spectral norm of a matrix is bounded by its row sum norm (maximum absolute row sum): $\|L\|_2 \leq \|L\|_{\infty} = \max_{i} \sum_{j=1}^{n} |L_{ij}|$, where $\|L\|_{\infty}$ denote the infinity norm of the matrix $L$.

paper_title: Optimal Time-Space Tradeoff for Dynamic Difference-Encoded Dictionaries
statement_text: theorem MainDict Let U be an integer. Let Ω( log log U/ log U) ≤ ε<1/4 be a parameter The constraint on ε may seem strange. However, it turns out that Ω( log log U/ log U) ≤ ε<1/4 is the only interesting regime. Indeed, the data structure constructed for ε= log log U/ log U also satisfies the time and space constraints for any ε< log log U/ log U : For the time constraint, this is straightforward because log ε^ -1 / log log ε^ -1 is decreasing in ε for ε=o(1) . For the space constraint, when ε=O( log log U/ log U) , we have that |S| log ( gap (S)/|S|)=Ω(ε · gap (S)) , so the actual value of ε does not affect the space bound . To see this, note that gap (S)/|S| ≤ log U , which implies that log ( gap (S)/|S|)/ log log ( gap (S)/|S|)=O( log log U/ log log log U) by monotonicity of log x/ log log x . . There exists a data structure in the word RAM model with word size w=Θ( log U) that maintains a key set S ⊆ [U] . In O( log ε^ -1 / log log ε^ -1 ) expected amortized time, the data structure supports the following operations: bf Insertion : Insert a key x to S . bf Deletion : Delete a key x from S . bf Membership : Given x ∈ [U] , output whether x ∈ S . The data structure uses gap (S)+O(ε · gap (S))+Obk * |S| log frac gap (S) |S| +Obk * U^ δ bits of space, where δ>0 is a small constant parameter of our choice.

label: thm:retrieval
paper_title: Optimal Time-Space Tradeoff for Dynamic Difference-Encoded Dictionaries
statement_text: Let U and V be parameters with log V ≤ O( log U) . In the word RAM model with word size w=Ω( log U+ log V) , there is a fully dynamic retrieval data structure maintaining a set S ⊆ [U] for which poly log U ≤ |S| ≤ U/2 , where each key is associated with a value in [V] . In O(1) time, the data structure supports insertion, deletion and value queries. In particular, when answering a value query on key x ∈ [U] , the data structure returns the value associated with x if x ∈ S , and an arbitrary value otherwise. At any time, the data structure uses |S| · log V+O(|S| log log (U/|S|)) bits of space. The data structure assumes access to lookup tables and hash functions of total size at most U^ δ bits, where δ>0 is an arbitrary parameter. At any given moment, the space and time bounds hold with high probability in |S| . Upon close inspection, when given an arbitrarily long sequence of operations, the data structure of cref thm:retrieval is always guaranteed to return the correct answer for each query. Furthermore, the worst-case time and space bounds are O(|S|) and O(|S| log U) , respectively.

label: def:vl_word_RAM
paper_title: Optimal Time-Space Tradeoff for Dynamic Difference-Encoded Dictionaries
statement_text: In the variable-length word RAM model with boldmathbf word size w , the memory is a collection of 2^w words. At any point in time, each word is either boldmathbf idle or boldmathbf active . When a word is active, it can store as its boldmathbf content a bit string of length at most w . In unit time, an algorithm in the variable-length word RAM model can perform the following operations: Activate a word and set its content to be empty. Deactivate a word. Write to/Read the content of an active word. When we read an active word, the memory returns the length of its content as well as the content itself. Perform arithmetic or bitwise operations on two w -bit integers. Note that the memory is not responsible for remembering which words are active. If the queried word of some type 1 (resp. 2, 3) operation is currently active (resp. idle), the behaviour of the memory is undefined. We say that a data structure in the variable-length word RAM model is boldmathbf legitimate if it never causes undefined behavior. The boldmathbf space usage of the memory in the variable-length word RAM model with word size w is defined to be (total length of word contents) +C_ retr · log w · (\# of active words) , where C_ retr is a sufficiently large constant. We say that a data structure has boldmathbf address limit M , if it only ever accesses the first M words, regardless of its input.
title: Variable-Length Word RAM Model

statement_text: Let U be an integer. There is a data structure in the word RAM model with word size w=Θ( log U) that maintains two sets P,S ⊂ [U] , where 0 ∈ P always holds. For each key x ∈ [U] , its boldmathbf pivot is defined as the largest key in P smaller than or equal to x (denoted as p_x ). Our data structure supports the following operations in expected amortized time: bf Insertion/Deletion on P : Insert a key to or delete a key from P in O( log U) time. It is guaranteed that this operation would not change the pivot of any key in S , and that for each insertion (resp. deletion), the given key did not exist (resp. did exist) in P . bf Insertion on S with advice : Given a key x ∉ S and its pivot p_x ∈ P , insert x to S in O(1) time. bf Deletion on S : Given a key x ∈ S , delete x from S in O(1) time. bf Pivot : Given a key x ∈ S , return its pivot p_x in O(1) time. If the given key is not in S , the distributor may return anything. The data structure uses O(|P| · log ^2U+|S| · log log U) bits of space with high probability in |S| when |S| ≥ ( log U)^c for a sufficiently large constant c . The data structure assumes access to lookup tables and hash functions of total size at most U^ δ bits, where δ>0 is an arbitrary parameter.

Let $\tweak{\cal K}$ be any class of sets.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The {\em Boolean (``alternating sums'') hierarchy over} ${\cal K}$:
$$\c{1}({\cal K})\equalsdef{\cal K},\ \ 
\c{k}({\cal K})\equalsdef\left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
  \c{k-1}({\cal K})\union {\cal K}      & \mbox{if $k$ odd}\\
  \c{k-1}({\cal K})\inter \co{\cal K} & \mbox{if $k$ even}
\end{array}
\right.
,\ k\geq 2,\ \ 
\ch({\cal K})\equalsdef\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\c{k}({\cal K}).$$

\item The {\em nested difference hierarchy over} ${\cal K}$:
$$\d{1}({\cal K})\equalsdef{\cal K},\ \ 
  \d{k}({\cal K})\equalsdef{\cal K} \minus 
                                        \d{k-1}({\cal K}),\ k\geq 2,\ \ 
  \newdh({\cal K})\equalsdef\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\d{k}({\cal K}).$$

\item 
The {\em Hausdorff (``union of differences'') hierarchy over} 
${\cal K}$:\footnote{
\protect\singlespacing
Hausdorff hierarchies~(\protect\cite{hau:b:sets}, see
\protect\cite{cai-gun-har-hem-sew-wag-wec:j:bh1,ber-bru-jos-sit-you:c:gen,gun-nas-wec:c:counting-survey},
respectively, for applications to NP, R, and
$\mbox{C}\!\!\!\!=\!\!\!\mbox{P}$) are interesting both in the case
where, as in the definition here, the sets are arbitrary sets from
$\tweak\cal K$, and, as is sometimes used in definitions, the sets from
$\tweak\cal K$ are required to satisfy additional containment conditions.
For classes closed under union and intersection, such as NP, the two
definitions are identical, level by level (\protect\cite{hau:b:sets},
see also~\protect\cite{cai-gun-har-hem-sew-wag-wec:j:bh1}).  In this
paper, as, e.g., UP, is not known to be closed under union, the
distinction is nontrivial.
}
$$\e{1}({\cal K}) \equalsdef {\cal K},\ \ 
\e{2}({\cal K}) \equalsdef {\cal K} \minus {\cal K},\ \ 





\e{k}({\cal K}) \equalsdef \e{2}({\cal K}) \union 
                                        \e{k-2}({\cal K}),\ \ k > 2,\ \
\eh({\cal K}) \equalsdef \bigcup_{k\geq 1}\e{k}({\cal K}).$$

\item The {\em symmetric difference hierarchy over} ${\cal K}$:
$$\sd{1}({\cal K})\equalsdef{\cal K},\ \ 
  \sd{k}({\cal K})\equalsdef\sd{k-1}({\cal K})\XOR {\cal K},\ k\geq 2,\ \ 
  \sdh({\cal K})\equalsdef\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\sd{k}({\cal K}).$$
\end{enumerate}

$\delp{0}\equalsdef\p$, \

$\ph \equalsdef\bigcup_{k\geq 0}\sigp{k}$.

hierarchy}~\cite{nie-ros:c:up-hierarchy} is defined as follows:\\
$\u\sigp{0}\equalsdef\p$, 
$\u\delp{0}\equalsdef\p$,
$\u\sigp{k}\equalsdef\up^{\protect\scriptsize \u\sigp{k-1}}$, 
$\u\pip{k}\equalsdef\co\u\sigp{k}$,

and $\u\ph \equalsdef\bigcup_{k\geq 0}\u\sigp{k}$.

\item \label{def-part:promise}
The {\em promise unambiguous polynomial 
hierarchy}~(\cite{lan-ros:c:up-circuit-and-hierarchy}\cite[p.~483]{nie-ros:c:up-hierarchy}) 
is defined as follows:
$\pru\sigp{0}\equalsdef\p$, $\pru\sigp{1}\equalsdef\up$, and 
for $k\geq 2$, $L\in \pru\sigp{k}$ if and only if 
$L\in \sigp{k}$ via NPOMs $N_1,\ldots ,N_k$ satisfying for all 
inputs $x$ and every $i$, $1\leq i\leq k-1$, that if $N_i$ asks some 
query $q$ during the computation of $N_1(x)$, 
then $N_{i+1}(q)$ with oracle $L(N_{i+2}^{L(N_{i+3}^{\.^{\.^{L(N_{k})}}})})$
has at most one accepting path.
$\pruph\equalsdef\bigcup_{k\geq 0}\pru\sigp{k}$.
The classes $\pru\delp{k}$ and $\pru\pip{k}$, $k\geq 0$, are defined
analogously.  As a notational shorthand, we often use 
$\p^\smallprup$ to represent
$\pru\delp{2}$;  we stress that both notations 
are used here to represent the class of sets accepted via {\em guardedly 
unambiguous\/} access to an NP oracle (that is, the class
of sets accepted by some P machine with an NP machine's language 
as its oracle
such that on no input does the P machine ask its oracle machine
any question on which the oracle machine has more than one accepting
path).









\item For each of the above hierarchies, we use 
${\rm \Sigma}_k^{p,A}$ (respectively, $\u{\rm \Sigma}_k^{p,A}$ and

(respectively, $\u{\rm \Sigma}_k^{p}$ and
$\pru{\rm \Sigma}_k^{p}$) 
computation is performed relative to oracle $A$; similar notation
is used for the $\Pi$ and $\Delta$ classes of the hierarchies.
\end{enumerate}

statement_tex:
\label{l:klaus}

{\bf \cite{wag:j:more-on-bh}}~
Let $A$ be some $\np$-complete set, and let $B$ be any set. If
there exists a polynomial-time computable function $g$ such that,
for all $k \geq 1$ and all 
strings $x_1, \ldots, x_{2k} \in \sigmastar$ satisfying
$\chi_A(x_1) \geq \chi_A(x_2) \geq \cdots \geq \chi_A(x_{2k})$, it 
holds that
\[||\{i\condition x_i \in A\}|| \mbox{ is odd }
\Longleftrightarrow g(x_1, \ldots,
x_{2k}) \in B,\]
then $B$ is $\thetatwo$-hard.\footnote{\protect\label{f:arity}
Recall 
the comments/conventions
of Section~\ref{s:prelims} regarding the handling 
of the arguments of variable-arity functions.  Wagner did not 
discuss this issue, but we note that his proof remains valid under 
the conventions 
of Section~\ref{s:prelims}.  These conventions
have been adopted as they shield Wagner's theorem from
a pathological type of counterexample 
(involving large, variable numbers of length zero 
inputs~($\epsilon$) followed by one other constant-length string)
noted by a referee
that, without the conventions, could render Wagner's theorem
true but never applicable.

Another difference in our statement of the theorem 
relative to Wagner's is that 
though we state the theorem for the class~$\thetatwo$, Wagner
used the class ``$\p_{\rm bf}^{\rm NP}$.''  However, this 
is legal as 
$\p_{\rm bf}^{\rm NP}$ is now
known to be equal to~$\thetatwo$

paper_title: Lower bounds for randomized and quantum query complexity using Kolmogorov arguments
statement_tex:
Fix $n$ and a quantum algorithm $A$ for Grover search for instances of length $n$.
Let $z$ be a binary string of
length $\log n$, with $\K(z \given A) \geq \log n$.
Let $j$ be the integer between $0$ and $n-1$ whose binary expansion is  $z$.
Consider $x$, the all $0$'s string, and let $y$ be everywhere 
$0$ except at position $i=j+1$, where it is $1$.
Then $\K(i \given x,A) \geq \log n -O(1)$ and $\K(i \given y,A) = O(1)$,
therefore,
$\qqc(\textsc{Search})=\Omega(\sqrt{n})$.

Let j be the integer between 0 and n-1 whose binary expansion is z . Consider x , the all 0 's string, and let y be everywhere 0 except at position i=j+1 , where it is 1 . Then K (i | x,A) ≥ log n -O(1) and K (i | y,A) = O(1) , therefore, QQC (sc Search )=Ω( sqrt n ) .

paper_title: Lower bounds for randomized and quantum query complexity using Kolmogorov arguments
statement_tex:
Let $M$ be a Turing machine.
Let $x$ and $y$ be finite strings.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
The {\em Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ given $y$ with respect to $M$} is
denoted $\C_{M}(x \given y)$,  and defined as follows:
$$\C_{M}(x \given y)=
    \min (\mbox{$\length{P}$ such that $M(P,y)= x$}).$$
\item A set of strings is {\em prefix-free} if no string is a prefix of another 
in the set.
\item The {\em prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ given $y$ 
with respect to $M$} is
denoted $\K_{M}(x \given y)$, and defined as follows:
$$\K_{M}(x \given y)=\min(\mbox{$\length{P}$ such that $M(P,y)= x$}),$$
where $P$ is taken in some fixed prefix-free set.

label: thm:ambainis+weights

statement_tex:
\label{thm:ambainis+weights}
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite set, let $n\geq 1$ be an integer,
and let $S\subseteq\Sigma^n$ and $S'$ be sets.
Let $f:S\rightarrow S'$.
Consider a weight scheme as follows:
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}
\item Every pair $(x,y)\in S^2$ is assigned a non-negative weight $w(x,y)$
such that $w(x,y)=0$ whenever $f(x)=f(y)$.
\item Every triple $(x,y,i)$ is assigned
a non-negative weight $w'(x,y,i)$ such that
$w'(x,y,i)=0$ whenever $x_i=y_i$ or $f(x)=f(y)$.
\end{itemize}
For all $x,i$, let
$wt(x) {=} \sum_{y}w(x,y)$ and
$v(x,i){=} \sum_{y}w(x,y,i)$.
If $w'(x,y,i) w'(y,x,i) \geq w^{2}(x,y)$ 
for all $x,y,i$ such that $x_i \neq y_i$, 
then
$$\qqc(f)=\Omega\left(
\min_{\stackrel{x,y,i}{w(x,y)\neq 0, x_i\neq y_i}}\left(\sqrt{\frac{wt(x)wt(y)}{v(x,i)v(y,i)}}\right)
\right).$$

Furthermore, if 
$w'(x,y,i),w'(y,x,i) \geq w(x,y)$
for all $x,y,i$ such that $x_i \neq y_i$, 
then
$$\rqc(f)=\Omega\left(\min_{\stackrel{x,y,i}{w(x,y)\neq 0, x_i\neq y_i}}\left(
\max\left(\frac{wt(x)}{v(x,i)},\frac{wt(y)}{v(y,i)}
\right)\right)\right).$$

\label{df:prob_formula_size}
Let $\{f_j\}_{j \in J}$ be a set of functions with $f_j:S \rightarrow \{0,1\}$
for each $j \in J$.  For a function $f:S\rightarrow \{0,1\}$, we say that $f$ is
$\epsilon$-approximated by $\{f_j\}_{j \in J}$ if there is a probability
distribution $\alpha=\{\alpha_j\}_{j \in J}$ over $J$ such that for every
$x \in S$,
$$
\Pr_{\alpha}[f(x)=f_j(x)] \ge 1- \epsilon.
$$
In particular, if $\max_j \L(f_j) \le s$, then we say that $f$ is
$\epsilon$-approximated by formulas of size $s$, denoted
$\L^{\epsilon}(f) \le s$.
statement_text: Let {f_j}_ j ∈ J be a set of functions with f_j:S → {0,1} for each j ∈ J . In particular, if max _j L (f_j) ≤ s , then we say that f is ε -approximated by formulas of size s , denoted L ^ ε (f) ≤ s .

$$

$$

statement_tex:
Let $S \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ and
$f: S \rightarrow \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and $X=f^{-1}(0), 
Y=f^{-1}(1)$.  Let $q$ be a probability distribution
on $X{\times} Y$, and $p_A,p_B$ be probability distributions on $X,Y$ 
respectively.  Finally let $\{p_{x,i}': x \in X, i \in [n]\}$ and 
$\{p_{y,i}': y \in Y, i \in [n]\}$ be families of probability distributions
on $X,Y$ respectively.  Assume that $q(x,y) = 0$ when $f(x)=f(y)$.  Let 
$P$ range over all possible tuples $(q,p_A, p_B, \{p_{x,i}'\}_{x,i})$ of 
distributions as above. Then
$$
\PA(f)= \max_{P} \min_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{x,y,i}{f(x)\not=f(y), x_i \not = y_i}} 
\frac{\sqrt{p_A(x)p_B(y)p_{x,i}'(y)p_{y,i}'(x)}}{q(x,y)}
$$
\label{df:prob_scheme}
statement_text: Let S ⊆ {0,1}^n and f: S → {0,1} be a Boolean function, and X=f^ -1 (0), Y=f^ -1 (1) . Let q be a probability distribution on X × Y , and p_A,p_B be probability distributions on X,Y respectively. Finally let {p_ x,i ': x ∈ X, i ∈ [n]} and {p_ y,i ': y ∈ Y, i ∈ [n]} be families of probability distributions on X,Y respectively. Assume that q(x,y) = 0 when f(x)=f(y) . Let $S \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ and 
$f: S \rightarrow \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function.  Let 
$X=f^{-1}(0), Y=f^{-1}(1)$.  Let $\Gamma \ne 0$ be 
an arbitrary $|X| {\times} |Y|$ non-negative symmetric matrix that satisfies 
$\Gamma[x,y]=0$ whenever $f(x)=f(y)$.  For $i \in [n]$, let $\Gamma_i$ be the

$$

\begin{array}{ll}
0 & \mbox{ if } x_i=y_i \\

\right.
$$
Then
$$

$$

statement_tex:
For any function $f:\{0,1\}^n\rightarrow \{0,1\}$,

\begin{enumerate}
\addtolength{\itemsep}{-0.5\baselineskip} 
\item A {\em restriction} is a string in $\{0,1,\star\}^n$ 
where $\star$ means the
variable is left free, and~0 or~1 mean the variable
is set to the constant~0 or~1, respectively.
\item The restricted function $f|_\rho$ is the 
function that remains after the non-$\star$ variables in $\rho$
are fixed.
\item $R_p$ is the distribution on random restrictions to the variables of
$f$ obtained by setting each variable, independently, to $\star$
with probability $p$, and to~0 or~1 each with probability $\frac{(1-p)}{2}$.
\item A {\em filter} $\Delta$ is a set of restrictions which has
the property that if $\rho\in \Delta$, then every $\rho'$
obtained by fixing one of the $\star$s to a constant is also
in $\Delta$.
\item When $p$ is known from the context, and for any event $E$, and any filter $\Delta$,
we write $\Pr[E|\Delta]$ to mean $\Pr_{\rho\in R_p}[E|\rho\in \Delta]$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{thm:hastad}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\rightarrow\{0,1\}$.

\label{thm:mwum}
Fix $\gamma\in(0,1/2)$ and $\alpha>0$.
Let $M^{(1)},\dots,M^{(T)}$ be arbitrary $d\times d$ ``loss'' matrices with $0\preceq M^{(t)}\preceq \alpha I$.
Let $W^{(1)},\dots,W^{(T)}$ be $d\times d$ ``weight'' matrices given by
\begin{align*}
  W^{(1)} &= I &
  W^{(t+1)} &= \exp\Pa{-\gamma \Pa{M^{(1)} + \cdots + M^{(t)}} }.
\end{align*}
Let $\rho^{(1)},\dots,\rho^{(T)}$ be density operators obtained by normalizing each $W^{(1)},\dots,W^{(T)}$ so that $\rho^{(t)}=W^{(t)}/\ptr{}{W^{(t)}}$.
For all density operators $\rho$ it holds that
\[
  \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \Inner{\rho^{(t)}}{M^{(t)}} \leq
  \Inner{\rho}{\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T M^{(t)}} + \alpha\Pa{\gamma + \frac{\ln d}{\gamma T}}.
\]
statement_text: Fix γ ∈ (0,1/2) and α>0 . Let M^ (1) , ... ,M^ (T) be arbitrary d × d ``loss'' matrices with 0preceq M^ (t) preceq α I . Let W^ (1) , ... ,W^ (T) be d × d ``weight'' matrices given by W^ (1) &= I & W^ (t+1) &= exp (-γ (M^ (1) + ... + M^ (t) ) ). Let ρ^ (1) , ... ,ρ^ (T) be density operators obtained by normalizing each W^ (1) , ... ,W^ (T) so that ρ^ (t) =W^ (t) / Tr _ (W^ (t) ) . For all density operators ρ it holds that \[ frac 1 T Σ _ t=1 ^T le ρ^ (t) , M^ (t) rangle ≤ le ρ , frac 1 T Σ _ t=1 ^T M^ (t) rangle + α (γ + frac ln d γ T ). \]

label: obs:not
paper_title: Quantum generalizations of the polynomial hierarchy with applications to QMA(2)
statement_tex: \label{obs:not} The proof of the Cleaning Lemma uses a $\Po^{\PrBQP}$ machine. Let us highlight a subtle reason why using a weaker $\BQP$ oracle instead might be difficult (indeed, in Section~\ref{sscn:ppcomp} we show that the task we use the $\PrBQP$ oracle for is $\PP$-complete).   Let $M$ denote the trivially \BQP-complete problem of determining whether a given polynomial-sized quantum circuit $Q$ accepts with probability at least $2/3$, or accepts with probability at most $1/3$, with the promise that one of the two is the case. Now consider the following polynomial time computation, $\Pi$, which is given access to an oracle $O_M$ for $M$: $\Pi$ inputs the Hadamard gate $H$ into $O_M$ and outputs $O_M$'s answer. Does it hold that $\Pi\in \Po^{\BQP}$? No. Since $H$ violates the promise of BQP, i.e. measuring the output of $H$ yields $0$ or $1$ with equal probability, the oracle $O_M$ can answer $0$ or $1$ arbitrarily, and so the output of $\Pi$ is not well-defined. Having a well-defined output, however, is required for a $\Po^{O_K}$ computation, where $K$ is any promise class~\cite{G06}.
statement_text: The proof of the Cleaning Lemma uses a up P ^ up Precise - up BQP machine. Let us highlight a subtle reason why using a weaker up BQP oracle instead might be difficult (indeed, in Section we show that the task we use the up Precise - up BQP oracle for is up PP -complete). Let M denote the trivially up BQP -complete problem of determining whether a given polynomial-sized quantum circuit Q accepts with probability at least 2/3 , or accepts with probability at most 1/3 , with the promise that one of the two is the case. Now consider the following polynomial time computation, Π , which is given access to an oracle O_M for M : Π inputs the Hadamard gate H into O_M and outputs O_M 's answer. Does it hold that Π ∈ up P ^ up BQP ? No. Since H violates the promise of BQP, i.e. measuring the output of H yields 0 or 1 with equal probability, the oracle O_M can answer 0 or 1 arbitrarily, and so the output of Π is not well-defined. Having a well-defined output, however, is required for a up P ^ O_K computation, where K is any promise class .
title: When a up P \ machine querying a up BQP \ oracle is not a up P ^ up BQP machine

label: thm:inEXP
paper_title: Quantum generalizations of the polynomial hierarchy with applications to QMA(2)
statement_text: For any polynomial r and input size n , if c - s ≥ 1/ 2^ 2^ r(n) , then Q Σ_2(c,s) ⊆ up EXP quad and quad Q Π_2(c,s) ⊆ up EXP when c and s are computable in exponential time in n . (Note for classes with small completeness-soundness gaps such as these, a gate set must be fixed The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm (see e.g. ) allows one to convert between gate sets in time scaling polylogarithmically in 1/ε per gate, where ε is the desired approximation precision per gate. Thus, the setting of doubly exponentially small precision takes superpolynomial overhead to convert between gate sets, which is problematic for promise classes involving polynomial -time uniform circuit families (such as Q Σ_2 and Q Π_2 ). For this reason, in the small gap regime, one can ``circumvent'' the problem by fixing a gate set when defining the class. . However, this result is independent of a fixed gate set.)

\label{def:QJS}
	The quantum Jensen-Shannon divergence between two quantum states $\rho_0$ and $\rho_1$ is defined by

	Here, $\S(\rho) \coloneqq -{\rm Tr}(\rho \ln \rho)$ denotes the von Neumann entropy of the quantum state $\rho$, and $\D(\rho_0 \| \rho_1)$ denotes the quantum relative entropy between $\rho_0$ and $\rho_1$.
statement_text: The quantum Jensen-Shannon divergence between two quantum states ρ_0 and ρ_1 is defined by \[normal rm QJS xspace (ρ_0,ρ_1) coloneqq S rbra * frac ρ_0+ρ_1 2 -frac S (ρ_0)+ S (ρ_1) 2 =frac 1 2 sbra * D rbra [ g] ρ_0 g| frac ρ_0+ρ_1 2 + D rbra [ g] ρ_1 g| frac ρ_0+ρ_1 2 .\] Here, S (ρ) coloneqq - rm Tr (ρ ln ρ) denotes the von Neumann entropy of the quantum state ρ , and D (ρ_0 | ρ_1) denotes the quantum relative entropy between ρ_0 and ρ_1 .

[Exact amplitude amplification, adapted from {\cite[Equation 8]{BHMT02}}]
\label{lemma:exact-amplitude-amplification}
    Suppose $U$ is a unitary operator such that $U\ket{\bar 0} = \sin(\theta) \ket{\psi_0} + \cos(\theta) \ket{\psi_1}$, where $\ket{\psi_0}$ and $\ket{\psi_1}$ are normalized pure states and $\innerprod{\psi_0}{\psi_1} = 0$.
    Let $G  \coloneqq  - U (I - 2\ket{\bar 0}\bra{\bar 0}) U^\dag (I - 2\ket{\psi_0}\bra{\psi_0})$ be the Grover operator. Then, for every integer $j \geq 0$, we have

    Specifically, with a single iteration of $G$, we get $G U \ket{\bar 0} = \sin(3\theta) \ket{\psi_0} + \cos(3\theta) \ket{\psi_1}$.

label: def:QIP(3)

statement_tex:
[\textsf{QIP(3)}]\label{def:QIP(3)}Let $A=(A_{\text{yes}},A_{\text{no}})$ be a
promise problem, and let $c,s:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\left[  0,1\right]  $ be
polynomial-time computable functions such that the gap $c-s$ is at least an
inverse polynomial in the input size. Then $A\in\ $\textsf{QIP}$\left(
3,c,s\right)  $ if there exists a three-message quantum interactive proof
system with the following properties:

\begin{enumerate}
\item Completeness:\ For all input strings $x\in A_{\text{yes}}$, there exists
a prover that causes the verifier to accept with probability at least
$c\left(  \left\vert x\right\vert \right)  $.

\item Soundness:\ For all input strings $x\in A_{\text{no}}$, every prover
causes the verifier to accept with probability at most $s\left(  \left\vert
x\right\vert \right)  $.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: [sf QIP(3) ] Let A=(A_ yes ,A_ no ) be a promise problem, and let c,s: N → [ 0,1 ] be polynomial-time computable functions such that the gap c-s is at least an inverse polynomial in the input size. Then A ∈ \ sf QIP ( 3,c,s ) if there exists a three-message quantum interactive proof system with the following properties: Completeness:\ For all input strings x ∈ A_ yes , there exists a prover that causes the verifier to accept with probability at least c ( vert x vert ) . Soundness:\ For all input strings x ∈ A_ no , every prover causes the verifier to accept with probability at most s ( vert x vert ) .

Assume that $\ket \psi = (\ket{\psi_T}, \ket{\psi_U}) \in \C^T \oplus \C^U$ is an eigenvalue-$\rho$ eigenvector of $A_G$, for some $\rho \neq 0$.  Then $(\ket{\psi_T}, -\ket{\psi_U})$ is an eigenvector of $A_G$ with eigenvalue $-\rho$.  Moreover, $\ket{\psi_T} = \frac{1}{\rho} \biadj_G \ket{\psi_U}$ is an eigenvector of $\biadj_G \biadj_G^\dagger$ and $\ket{\psi_U} = \frac{1}{\rho} \biadj_G^\dagger \ket{\psi_T}$ is an eigenvector of $\biadj_G^\dagger \biadj_G$, both with corresponding eigenvalues $\rho^2$.

statement_tex:
\label{lem:conditional}
    Let $\Pi$ and $\Pi'$ two distributions taking output in a common
    universe. Let $F$ and $H$ be two events in
    the underlying probability space of $\Pi'$. Finally, we let $\Pi'_E$ denote the distribution $\Pi'$ conditioned on $E=H\setminus F$, and assume that $|\Pi'_E - \Pi| \leq c$.









  Then it holds that $|\Pi'_H - \Pi| \leq c + \frac{\Pr_{\Pi'}[F]}{\Pr_{\Pi'}[H]}$.
statement_text: Let Π and Π' two distributions taking output in a common universe. Let F and H be two events in the underlying probability space of Π' . Finally, we let Π'_E denote the distribution Π' conditioned on E=H \ F , and assume that |Π'_E - Π| ≤ c . Then it holds that |Π'_H - Π| ≤ c + frac mathop Pr _ Π' [F] mathop Pr _ Π' [H] .

label: thm:OW
paper_title: An Average-Case Depth Hierarchy Theorem for Boolean Circuits
statement_tex:
\label{thm:OW}
For $w \in \N$ and $n := w2^w$, let $\Tribes : \zo^n\to\zo$ be the function computed by a $2^w$-term read-once monotone DNF formula where every term has width exactly $w$. Let $\Tribes^\dagger$ denote its Boolean dual, the function computed by a $2^w$-clause read-once monotone CNF formula where every clause has width exactly $w$, and define
the $2n$-variable function $F: \{0,1\}^{2n} \to \{0,1\}$ as
\[ F(x) = \Tribes(x_1,\ldots,x_n) \vee \Tribes^\dagger(x_{n+1},\ldots,x_{2n}). \]
Then any depth-$2$ circuit $C$ on $2n$ variables that has size $2^{O(n/\log n)}$ agrees with $F$ on at most a $0.99$-fraction of the $2^{2n}$ inputs.  (Note that $F$ is computed by a
linear-size depth-3 circuit.)
statement_text: For w ∈ m N and n := w2^w , let sf Tribes : {0,1}^n → {0,1} be the function computed by a 2^w -term read-once monotone DNF formula where every term has width exactly w . (Note that F is computed by a linear-size depth-3 circuit.)

\[

\ast & \text{if~} \tau_a \in \{\ast,\circ\}^{w_{k-1}} \setminus \{\circ\}^{w_{k-1}}.

statement_text: Let G : {0,1}^ A × [w] → {0,1} be a DNF over X , where we assume a fixed but arbitrary ordering on its terms, and likewise on the literals within each term. The canonical projection decision tree ProjDT (G) : {0,1}^A → {0,1} associated with G is defined recursively as follows: If G equiv 1 (i.e. if G(X) = 1 for all X ∈ {0,1}^ A × [w] ) output the trivial decision tree ProjDT (G) equiv 1 , and likewise, if G equiv 0 output ProjDT (G) equiv 0 . Otherwise, let T be the first term in G such that T not equiv 0 , and let \[ η = { y_a colon x_ a,i occurs in T for some i ∈ [w] } ⊆ Y \] ProjDT (G) queries all the variables in η in its first |η| levels. paper_title: Zero-knowledge proof systems for QMA
statement_tex:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $C$ be a Clifford operation on $k$
  qubits, and let $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$.
  There exists a string $t\in\{0,+,\circlearrowright\}^k$, a bit
  $a\in\{0,1\}$, and pure states $\ket{\phi_0}$ and $\ket{\phi_1}$ on
  $j-1$ qubits and $k - j$ qubits, respectively, so that
  \begin{equation}
    C \ket{t} = \ket{\phi_0} \ket{a} \ket{\phi_1}.
  \end{equation}
  Equivalently, there is a choice of $t$ so that the $j$-th qubit of
  $C\ket{t}$ is left in a standard basis state.
statement_text: Let k be a positive integer, let C be a Clifford operation on k qubits, and let j ∈ {1, ... ,k} . There exists a string t ∈ {0,+,circlearrowright }^k , a bit a ∈ {0,1} , and pure states lvert φ_0 rangle and lvert φ_1 rangle on j-1 qubits and k - j qubits, respectively, so that C lvert t rangle = lvert φ_0 rangle lvert a rangle lvert φ_1 rangle . Equivalently, there is a choice of t so that the j -th qubit of C lvert t rangle is left in a standard basis state.

paper_title: Zero-knowledge proof systems for QMA
statement_tex:
A promise problem $A = (A_{\yes},A_{\no})$ is contained in the complexity
  class $\class{QMA}_{\alpha,\beta}$ if there exists a polynomial-time generated
  collection
  \begin{equation}
    \bigl\{V_x\,:\,x\in A_{\yes} \cup A_{\no}\bigr\}
  \end{equation}
  of quantum circuits and a polynomially bounded function $p$ possessing the
  following properties:
  \begin{mylist}{\parindent}
  \item[1.]
    For every string $x\in A_{\yes}\cup A_{\no}$, one has that $V_x$ is a
    measurement circuit taking $p(\abs{x})$ input qubits and outputting
    a single bit.
  \item[2.]
    \emph{Completeness}.
    For all $x\in A_{\yes}$, there exists a $p(\abs{x})$-qubit state $\rho$
    such that $\Pr(V_x(\rho) = 1) \geq \alpha$.
  \item[3.]
    \emph{Soundness}.
    For all $x\in A_{\no}$, and every $p(\abs{x})$-qubit state
    $\rho$, it holds that $\Pr(V_x(\rho) = 1) \leq \beta$.
  \end{mylist}
statement_text: A promise problem A = (A_ yes ,A_ no ) is contained in the complexity class up QMA _ α,β if there exists a polynomial-time generated collection l{V_x : x ∈ A_ yes ∪ A_ no r} of quantum circuits and a polynomially bounded function p possessing the following properties: parindent For every string x ∈ A_ yes ∪ A_ no , one has that V_x is a measurement circuit taking p( lvert x rvert ) input qubits and outputting a single bit. Completeness . For all x ∈ A_ yes , there exists a p( lvert x rvert ) -qubit state ρ such that Pr (V_x(ρ) = 1) ≥ α . Soundness . For all x ∈ A_ no , and every p( lvert x rvert ) -qubit state ρ , it holds that Pr (V_x(ρ) = 1) ≤ β .

label: def_ind_states
paper_title: Zero-knowledge proof systems for QMA
statement_tex:
\label{def_ind_states}
  Suppose that $S\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\ast}$ is an infinite set of binary strings,
  $r$ is a polynomially bounded function, and $\rho_x$ and $\xi_x$ are states on
  $r(\abs{x})$ qubits for each $x\in S$.
  The collections $\{\rho_x\,:\,x\in S\}$ and $\{\xi_x\,:\,x\in S\}$ are
  \emph{quantum computationally indistinguishable} if, for every choice of
  polynomially bounded functions $s$ and $k$, any measurement circuit $Q$ of
  size $s(\abs{x})$, and any choice of a $k(\abs{x})$-qubit state $\sigma$, it
  holds that
  \begin{equation}
    \abs{\Pr[Q(\rho_x \otimes\sigma) = 1] -
      \Pr[Q(\xi_x \otimes\sigma) = 1]} \leq \varepsilon(\abs{x})
  \end{equation}
  for all $x\in S$, for a negligible function $\varepsilon$.
statement_text: Suppose that S ⊆ {0,1}^ ast is an infinite set of binary strings, r is a polynomially bounded function, and ρ_x and ξ_x are states on r( lvert x rvert ) qubits for each x ∈ S . label: def_qczk
paper_title: Zero-knowledge proof systems for QMA
statement_tex:
An interactive proof system $(P, V)$ for a promise problem $A$ is
  \emph{quantum computational zero-knowledge} if, for every polynomial-time
  generated quantum verifier $V'$, there exists a polynomial-time generated
  quantum simulator $S$ that satisfies the following requirements.
  \begin{mylist}{\parindent}
  \item[1.]
    The verifier $V'$ and simulator $S$ agree on the polynomially bounded
    functions $q$ and $r$ that specify the number of auxiliary input qubits and
    output qubits, respectively.
  \item[2.]
    Let $\Phi_x$ be the channel that results from the interaction between $V'$
    and $P$ on input~$x$, and let $\Psi_x$ be the channel induced by the
    simulator $S$ on input~$x$, both as described above.
    Then the collections $\{\Phi_x: x\in A_{\yes}\}$ and
    $\{\Psi_x: x \in A_{\yes}\}$ are quantum computationally
    indistinguishable.
  \end{mylist}
  \label{def_qczk}
statement_text: An interactive proof system (P, V) for a promise problem A is quantum computational zero-knowledge if, for every polynomial-time generated quantum verifier V' , there exists a polynomial-time generated quantum simulator S that satisfies the following requirements. parindent The verifier V' and simulator S agree on the polynomially bounded functions q and r that specify the number of auxiliary input qubits and output qubits, respectively. Let Φ_x be the channel that results from the interaction between V' and P on input x , and let Ψ_x be the channel induced by the simulator S on input x , both as described above. Then the collections {Φ_x: x ∈ A_ yes } and {Ψ_x: x ∈ A_ yes } are quantum computationally indistinguishable.
title: Quantum computational zero-knowledge

For every choice of n ∈ N , a,b ∈ Γ , and r,s ∈ {0,1}^ p(n) , one has that f_n(a,r) = f_n(b,s) implies a=b . Quantum computationally concealing property. For every a ∈ Γ and n ∈ N , define ρ_ a,n = frac 1 2^ p(n) Σ _ r ∈ {0,1}^ p(n) lvert f_n(a,r) rangle le f_n(a,r) rvert . For every choice of a,b ∈ Γ the ensembles {ρ_ a,n : n ∈ N } and {ρ_ b,n : n ∈ N } are quantum computationally indistinguishable.

label: fact:equiv
paper_title: Separations in communication complexity using cheat sheets and information complexity
statement_tex:
\label{fact:equiv}
Let $F\colon\X \times \Y \rightarrow \{0,1,*\}$ be a partial function.
Fix an error parameter $\eps \in (0,1/2)$ and an information bound $I \geq 0$.
Suppose $\mathcal{P}$ is a family of protocols such that for every distribution $\mu$ on $\dom(F)$ there exists a protocol $\Pi \in \mathcal{P}$ such that $$\err^\mu(\Pi) \leq \eps \quad \mathrm{and} \quad \IC^\mu(\Pi)\leq I.$$
Then for any $\alpha \in (0,1)$ there exists a protocol $\Pi'$ such that $$\err(\Pi')\leq \eps/\alpha \quad \mathrm{and} \quad \IC(\Pi') \leq I/(1-\alpha).$$
Moreover, $\Pi'$ is a probability distribution over protocols in $\mathcal{P}$, and hence $\CC(\Pi') \leq \max_{\Pi\in \mathcal{P}} \CC(\Pi)$.
statement_text: Let Fcolon X × Y → {0,1,*} be a partial function. Fix an error parameter ε ∈ (0,1/2) and an information bound I ≥ 0 . Suppose P is a family of protocols such that for every distribution μ on dom (F) there exists a protocol Π ∈ P such that err ^μ(Π) ≤ ε quad and quad IC ^μ(Π) ≤ I. Then for any α ∈ (0,1) there exists a protocol Π' such that err (Π') ≤ ε/α quad and quad IC (Π') ≤ I/(1-α). Moreover, Π' is a probability distribution over protocols in P , and hence CC (Π') ≤ max _ Π ∈ P CC (Π) .
title: Minimax principle

label: def:lookup
paper_title: Separations in communication complexity using cheat sheets and information complexity
statement_tex:
\label{def:lookup}
Let $F\colon \X \times \Y \to \{0,1,*\}$ be a (partial) communication function and $\mathcal{G}=\{G_0, \ldots, G_{2^c-1}\}$ a 
family of communication functions, where each $G_i \colon (\X^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \times (\Y^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \to \B$.  
A $(F, \mathcal{G})$-lookup function, denoted $F_\mathcal{G}$, is a total communication function 
$F_\G \colon (\X^c \times \B^{m2^c}) \times \Y^c \times \B^{m2^c}$ defined as follows.
Let $\x=(x_1, \ldots, x_c) \in \X^c, \y =(y_1, \ldots, y_c) \in \Y^c, 
\fu=(u_0, \ldots, u_{2^c-1}) \in \B^{m2^c}, \fv=(v_0, \ldots, v_{2^c-1}) \in \B^{m2^c}$.  Then
\[
F_{\G}(\x, \fu, \y, \fv) = 
\begin{cases}
G_\ell(\mathbf{x}, u_\ell, \mathbf{y}, v_\ell) & \text{if } \ell = F^c(\x,\y) \in \B^c \\
G_0(\x, u_0, \y, v_0) & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]
statement_text: Let Fcolon X × Y → {0,1,*} be a (partial) communication function and G ={G_0, ... , G_ 2^c-1 } a family of communication functions, where each G_i colon ( X ^c × {0,1}^m) × ( Y ^c × {0,1}^m) → {0,1} . A (F, G ) -lookup function, denoted F_ G , is a total communication function F_ G colon ( X ^c × {0,1}^ m2^c ) × Y ^c × {0,1}^ m2^c defined as follows. Let x =(x_1, ... , x_c) ∈ X ^c, y =(y_1, ... , y_c) ∈ Y ^c, u =(u_0, ... , u_ 2^c-1 ) ∈ {0,1}^ m2^c , v =(v_0, ... , v_ 2^c-1 ) ∈ {0,1}^ m2^c . Then \[ F_ G ( x , u , y , v ) = G_ell ( x , u_ell , y , v_ell ) & if ell = F^c( x , y ) ∈ {0,1}^c G_0( x , u_0, y , v_0) & otherwise. \]
title: (F, G ) -lookup function

label: def:consistency
paper_title: Separations in communication complexity using cheat sheets and information complexity
statement_tex:
\label{def:consistency}
Let $F\colon \X \times \Y \to \{0,1,*\}$ be a (partial) communication function and $\mathcal{G}=\{G_0, \ldots, G_{2^c-1}\}$ a 
family of communication functions, where each $G_i \colon (\X^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \times (\Y^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \to \B$.  We 
say that $\G$ is \emph{consistent} outside $F$ if for all $i \in \{0, \ldots, 2^c-1\}, u,v,u',v' \in \B^m$ and 
$\x=(x_1, \ldots, x_c) \in \X^c, \y =(y_1, \ldots, y_c) \in \Y^c$ with $\ell=F^c(\x,\y) \not \in \B^c$
we have $G_0(\x, u, \y, v) = G_i(\x, u', \y, v')$.
statement_text: Let Fcolon X × Y → {0,1,*} be a (partial) communication function and G ={G_0, ... , G_ 2^c-1 } a family of communication functions, where each G_i colon ( X ^c × {0,1}^m) × ( Y ^c × {0,1}^m) → {0,1} . label: def:xor
paper_title: Separations in communication complexity using cheat sheets and information complexity
statement_tex:
\label{def:xor}
Let $\mathcal{G}=\{G_0, \ldots, G_{2^c-1}\}$ a 
family of communication functions, where each $G_i \colon (\X^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \times (\Y^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \to \B$. We 
say that $\G$ is a nontrivial XOR family if the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Nontriviality) For all $\x=(x_1, \ldots, x_c) \in \X^c$ and $\y =(y_1, \ldots, y_c) \in \Y^c$, if we have 
$\ell = F^c(\x,\y) \in \B^c$ 
then for every $i \in \{0,\ldots,2^c-1\}$ there exists $u,v,u', v' \in \B^m$ such that 
$G_i(\x, u, \y, v) \ne G_i(\x, u', \y, v')$.
\item (XOR function) For all $i \in \{0,\ldots,2^c-1\}, u,u',v,v' \in \B^m$ and $\x=(x_1, \ldots, x_c) \in \X^c, 
\y=(y_1, \ldots, y_c) \in \Y^c$ 
if $u \oplus v = u' \oplus v'$ then $G_i(\x, u, \y, v) = G_i(\x, u', \y, v')$.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: Let G ={G_0, ... , G_ 2^c-1 } a family of communication functions, where each G_i colon ( X ^c × {0,1}^m) × ( Y ^c × {0,1}^m) → {0,1} . We say that G is a nontrivial XOR family if the following conditions hold. (Nontriviality) For all x =(x_1, ... , x_c) ∈ X ^c and y =(y_1, ... , y_c) ∈ Y ^c , if we have ell = F^c( x , y ) ∈ {0,1}^c then for every i ∈ {0, ... ,2^c-1} there exists u,v,u', v' ∈ {0,1}^m such that G_i( x , u, y , v) ≠ G_i( x , u', y , v') . (XOR function) For all i ∈ {0, ... ,2^c-1}, u,u',v,v' ∈ {0,1}^m and x =(x_1, ... , x_c) ∈ X ^c, y =(y_1, ... , y_c) ∈ Y ^c if u ⊕ v = u' ⊕ v' then G_i( x , u, y , v) = G_i( x , u', y , v') .

label: thm:ICCS
paper_title: Separations in communication complexity using cheat sheets and information complexity
statement_tex:
\label{thm:ICCS}
Let $F\colon\X \times \Y \to \{0,1,*\}$ be a (partial) function and let $c\geq \log \R(F)$. Let $\G=\{G_0, \ldots, G_{2^c-1}\}$ 
be a nontrivial family of XOR functions (\defn{xor}) where each $G_i \colon (\X^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \times (\Y^c \times \{0,1\}^m) \to \B$, and 
let $F_\G$ be the $(F, \G)$-lookup function.  For any $1/3$-error protocol $\Pi$ for $F_\G$, there exists a $1/3$-error protocol $\Pi'$ for $F$ such that 
$$\IC(\Pi') \leq O(c^3\IC(\Pi)) \quad \text{and} \quad  \CC(\Pi') \leq O(c^2 \CC(\Pi)).$$
In particular,
$\R(F_\G)= \Omega(\R(F)/c^2)$ and $\IC(F_\G)= \Omega(\IC(F)/c^3)$.
statement_text: Let Fcolon X × Y → {0,1,*} be a (partial) function and let c ≥ log R (F) . Let G ={G_0, ... , G_ 2^c-1 } be a nontrivial family of XOR functions (hyperref [def:xor] Definition ) where each G_i colon ( X ^c × {0,1}^m) × ( Y ^c × {0,1}^m) → {0,1} , and let F_ G be the (F, G ) -lookup function. For any 1/3 -error protocol Π for F_ G , there exists a 1/3 -error protocol Π' for F such that IC (Π') ≤ O(c^3 IC (Π)) quad and quad CC (Π') ≤ O(c^2 CC (Π)). In particular, R (F_ G )= Ω( R (F)/c^2) and IC (F_ G )= Ω( IC (F)/c^3) .

label: def:cheat
paper_title: Separations in communication complexity using cheat sheets and information complexity
statement_tex:
\label{def:cheat}
	Let $F\colon\X \times \Y \to \B$ be a total function.  Fix a cover $\mathcal{R}=\{R_0, \ldots, R_{2^{N(F)}-1}\}$ 
	of $\X \times \Y$ by rectangles monochromatic for $F$.  Let $N=\min\{\log |\X|, \log |\Y|\}$ and $c=10\log N$.  
	Define a function 
	\[
	G: (\X^c \times \B^{cN(F)}) \times (\Y^c \times \B^{cN(F)}) \rightarrow \B
	\]
	where
     	$G(x_1,\ldots, x_c, a_1, \ldots, a_c, y_1, \ldots, y_c, b_1, \ldots, b_c) = 1$ if and only if 
	$(x_i, y_i) \in R_{a_i \oplus b_i}$ 
	for all $i=1,\ldots, c$.  The \emph{cheat sheet} function $F_\CS$ of $F$ is the $(F, \{G_0, \ldots, G_{2^c-1}\})$ 
	lookup function where $G_i=G$ for all $i$.  In other words, 
	$F_\CS(x_1, \ldots, x_c, u_0, \ldots, u_{2^c-1}, y_1, \ldots, y_c, v_0, \ldots, v_{2^c-1})$ evaluates to 
	$G(x_1, \ldots, x_c, u_\ell, y_1,\ldots, y_c, v_\ell)$, where $\ell = (F(x_1, y_1), \ldots, F(x_c,y_c))$.
statement_text: Let Fcolon X × Y → {0,1} be a total function. Fix a cover R ={R_0, ... , R_ 2^ N(F) -1 } of X × Y by rectangles monochromatic for F . Let N=min { log | X |, log | Y |} and c=10 log N . Define a function \[ G: ( X ^c × {0,1}^ cN(F) ) × ( Y ^c × {0,1}^ cN(F) ) → {0,1} \] where G(x_1, ... , x_c, a_1, ... , a_c, y_1, ... , y_c, b_1, ... , b_c) = 1 if and only if (x_i, y_i) ∈ R_ a_i ⊕ b_i for all i=1, ... , c . The cheat sheet function F_ CS of F is the (F, {G_0, ... , G_ 2^c-1 }) lookup function where G_i=G for all i . In other words, F_ CS (x_1, ... , x_c, u_0, ... , u_ 2^c-1 , y_1, ... , y_c, v_0, ... , v_ 2^c-1 ) evaluates to G(x_1, ... , x_c, u_ell , y_1, ... , y_c, v_ell ) , where ell = (F(x_1, y_1), ... , F(x_c,y_c)) .
title: Cheat sheets for total functions

statement_tex:
\label{fact:AND}
	Let $F\colon \X \times \Y \rightarrow \{0,1,*\}$
	be a (partial) function, and let $\eps\in(0,1/2)$ be a constant.
	For any protocol $\Pi$ for $\OR_n\circ F$ with
	worst case error at most $\eps$, there is a protocol $\Pi^\prime$
	for $F$ with worst error at most $\eps$ such that
	\[\IC^0(\Pi^\prime)=O(\IC^0(\Pi)/n)\quad \textrm{and} \quad

	worst case error at most $\eps$,
	there is a protocol $\Pi^\prime$ for $F$ with
	worst case error at most $\eps$, such that
	\[\IC^1(\Pi^\prime)=O(\IC^1(\Pi)/n)\quad \textrm{and} \quad
	\CC(\Pi^\prime)=O(\CC(\Pi)).\]
statement_text: Let Fcolon X × Y → {0,1,*} be a (partial) function, and let ε ∈ (0,1/2) be a constant. For any protocol Π for sc Or _n ∘ F with worst case error at most ε , there is a protocol Π^prime for F with worst error at most ε such that \[ IC ^0(Π^prime )=O( IC ^0(Π)/n)quad rm and quad CC (Π^prime )=O( CC (Π)).\] Similarly, if Π is a protocol for sc And _n ∘ F with worst case error at most ε , there is a protocol Π^prime for F with worst case error at most ε , such that \[ IC ^1(Π^prime )=O( IC ^1(Π)/n)quad rm and quad CC (Π^prime )=O( CC (Π)).\]

\textbf{No Low-Energy Trivial States (NLTS)} 

\noindent
Let $\{H_n\}_{n\in \mathbf{N}}$ be a family of $k$-local Hamiltonians
for $k=O(1)$. 
We say that $\{H_n\}_{n\in \mathbf{N}}$ is $\eps$-NLTS if 
there exists a constant $\eps>0$ such that
for any $d$ and all sufficiently large $n$, 
the following holds: 
if $\{\rho_n\}$ is any family of $d$-trivial states then
\be \tr[\rho_n H_n] >\lambda_{\min}(H_n) + \eps.
\ee
statement_text: bf No Low-Energy Trivial States (NLTS) Let {H_n}_ n ∈ N be a family of k -local Hamiltonians for k=O(1) . We say that {H_n}_ n ∈ N is ε -NLTS if there exists a constant ε>0 such that for any d and all sufficiently large n , the following holds: if {ρ_n} is any family of d -trivial states then tr [ρ_n H_n] >λ_ min (H_n) + ε.

statement_tex:
\textbf{CSS code}

\noindent
A $[[n,k,d]]$ quantum CSS code on $n$ qubits 
is a subspace ${\cal C}\subseteq {\cal H} = (\bbC^2)^{\ot n}$ of $n$ qubits. 
It is defined by a pair of  linear subspaces of $S_x, S_z \subseteq
\bbF_2^n$ such that $S_x \perp S_z$.
It is thus denoted  ${\cal C} = {\cal C}(S_x,S_z)$. 
Explicitly the subspace is given by
\ba
\calC(S_x, S_z) &=
\left\{\ket\psi\in (\bbC^2)^{\ot n} : X^x\ket\psi = \ket\psi \,\forall
x\in S_x,
Z^z\ket\psi = \ket\psi \,\forall z\in S_z\right\}
\\ & 
=\Span\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{|S_x|}} 
\sum_{x \in S_x} \ket{z+x} : z \in S_z^{\perp}\right\}.\ea
The code has $k = \log(|S_x^{\perp}/S_z|)$ logical qubits and distance $d = \min_{w\in S_x^{\perp}
  - S_z, S_z^{\perp} - S_x} |w|$.
statement_text: bf CSS code A [[n,k,d]] quantum CSS code on n qubits is a subspace cal C ⊆ cal H = ( C ^2)^ ot n of n qubits. It is defined by a pair of linear subspaces of S_x, S_z ⊆ F _2^n such that S_x perp S_z . It is thus denoted cal C = cal C (S_x,S_z) . Explicitly the subspace is given by ba cal C (S_x, S_z) &= { | ψ rangle ∈ ( C ^2)^ ot n : X^x | ψ rangle = | ψ rangle ∀ x ∈ S_x, Z^z | ψ rangle = | ψ rangle ∀ z ∈ S_z } & = Span {frac 1 sqrt |S_x| Σ _ x ∈ S_x | z+x rangle : z ∈ S_z^ perp }.ea The code has k = rm log (|S_x^ perp /S_z|) logical qubits and distance d = min _ w ∈ S_x^ perp - S_z, S_z^ perp - S_x |w| .

statement_tex:
\label{def:lh}

\textbf{$k$-local Hamiltonian}

\noindent
A $k$-local $n$-qubit Hamiltonian $H\succeq 0$
is a positive semidefinite operator on the $n$-qubit space $(\bbC^2)^{\otimes n}$,
that can be written as a sum $H = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m H_i$, where each $H_i$ is a positive-semidefinite matrix,
$0\preceq H_i \preceq I$, and each $H_i$ may be written as $H_i = h_i \otimes
I$, where $h_i \succeq 0$ is a $2^k \times 2^k$ PSD matrix.
statement_text: bf k -local Hamiltonian A k -local n -qubit Hamiltonian Hsucceq 0 is a positive semidefinite operator on the n -qubit space ( C ^2)^ ⊗ n , that can be written as a sum H = frac 1 m Σ _ i=1 ^m H_i , where each H_i is a positive-semidefinite matrix, 0preceq H_i preceq I , and each H_i may be written as H_i = h_i ⊗ I , where h_i succeq 0 is a 2^k × 2^k PSD matrix.

label: eq:code-Ham
paper_title: Local Hamiltonians Whose Ground States are Hard to Approximate
statement_tex:
\textbf{The Hamiltonian of the code} 

\noindent
Suppose ${\cal C} = \calC(S_x, S_z)$ is a CSS code and
$H_x,H_z$ are subsets of $\bbF_2^n$ that generate
$S_x,S_z$.
Then we can define a Hamiltonian $H({\cal C})$, 
whose terms correspond to the 
generators of the CSS code in the following way.
\be
H = H({\cal C})
= \frac{1}{2|H_x|} \sum_{e\in H_x} \frac{I+X^e}{2}
+ \frac{1}{2|H_z|} \sum_{e\in H_z} \frac{I+Z^e}{2}
\label{eq:code-Ham}.\ee
statement_text: bf The Hamiltonian of the code Suppose cal C = cal C (S_x, S_z) is a CSS code and H_x,H_z are subsets of F _2^n that generate S_x,S_z . Then we can define a Hamiltonian H( cal C ) , whose terms correspond to the generators of the CSS code in the following way. H = H( cal C ) = frac 1 2|H_x| Σ _ e ∈ H_x frac I+X^e 2 + frac 1 2|H_z| Σ _ e ∈ H_z frac I+Z^e 2 .

statement_tex:
\label{def:ltc}
\textbf{Classical locally testable code}

\noindent
A code $C\subseteq \bbF_2^n$ is said to be locally testable with
soundness $\rho$ and query $q$, if there exists a set of $q$-local check terms
$\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}$, such that
$$
\Prob_{i\sim U[m]} \left[C_i(w) = 1\right] \geq \rho \cdot \frac{\dist(w, C)}{n}.
$$
In particular $w\in C$ iff $C_i(w)=0$ for all $i$.

In particular w ∈ C iff C_i(w)=0 for all i .

statement_tex:
\label{def:subspace-distance}
If $V$ is a subspace of $(\bbC^2)^{\ot n}$ then define its
$t$-fattening to be 
\be V_t := \Span \{ (A_1 \ot \cdots \ot A_n)\ket\psi : \ket\psi \in V,
\# \{i : A_i \neq I\}\leq t\}.\ee
Let $\Pi_{V_t}$ project onto $V_t$.  Then define the distance operator
\be D_V := \sum_{t\geq 1} t (\Pi_{V_t} - \Pi_{V_{t-1}}).\ee
statement_text: If V is a subspace of ( C ^2)^ ot n then define its t -fattening to be V_t := Span { (A_1 ot ... ot A_n) | ψ rangle : | ψ rangle ∈ V, \# {i : A_i ≠ I} ≤ t}. Let Π_ V_t project onto V_t . Then define the distance operator D_V := Σ _ t ≥ 1 t (Π_ V_t - Π_ V_ t-1 ).

statement_tex:
\label{fact:CSS}
\textbf{Classical codes comprising a $\qLTC$ CSS code must also be locally testable}

\noindent
Let ${\cal C}(S_x,S_z)$ be a quantum CSS code corresponding to two linear codes
$S_x^\perp,S_z^\perp \subseteq \bbF_2^n$.  If ${\cal C}$ is a $(q,\rho)$-$\qLTC$
then $S_x^\perp$ and $S_z^\perp$ are each
$q$-$\LTC$s with soundness at least $\rho/2$.  Conversely, if
$S_x^\perp$ and $S_z^\perp$ are each
$q$-$\LTC$s with soundness parameter $\rho$ with $S_x\subseteq S_z^\perp$ then
$\calC(S_x,S_z)$ is a $(q,\rho)$-$\qLTC$.
statement_text: bf Classical codes comprising a sf qLTC CSS code must also be locally testable Let cal C (S_x,S_z) be a quantum CSS code corresponding to two linear codes S_x^perp ,S_z^perp ⊆ F _2^n . If cal C is a (q,ρ) - sf qLTC then S_x^perp and S_z^perp are each q - sf LTC s with soundness at least ρ/2 . Conversely, if S_x^perp and S_z^perp are each q - sf LTC s with soundness parameter ρ with S_x ⊆ S_z^perp then cal C (S_x,S_z) is a (q,ρ) - sf qLTC .

\textbf{Maximal-connected residual graph}

A (unitary) quantum circuit $C$ on $n$ qubits of depth $d$
is a product of $d$ layers $U_1,\hdots, U_d$,
where each layer $U_i$ can be written as a tensor-product

$N\geq n$) and tracing out $N-n$ qubits.

statement_tex:
\label{def:nlts}

\textbf{No Low-Energy Trivial States (NLTS) (restated)}  

\noindent
An infinite family of local Hamiltonians $\{H_n\}_{n\in \mathbf{N}}$ 
is $\eps$-NLTS if for any $d$ and 
a depth-$d$ trivial state family ${\cal F}$
and all sufficiently large $n$
\be \tr[\rho_n H_n] >\lambda_{\min}(H_n)+ \eps.\ee
We say that $\{H_n\}_{n\in \mathbf{N}}$ is NLTS if it is $\eps$-NLTS
for some constant $\eps>0$.
statement_text: bf No Low-Energy Trivial States (NLTS) (restated) An infinite family of local Hamiltonians {H_n}_ n ∈ N is ε -NLTS if for any d and a depth- d trivial state family cal F and all sufficiently large n tr [ρ_n H_n] >λ_ min (H_n)+ ε. We say that {H_n}_ n ∈ N is NLTS if it is ε -NLTS for some constant ε>0 .

\textbf{$\QNC^1$-hard distribution}

\noindent
A family of  distributions $\{\calD_n\}$ on $n$ bits is said to be
$\QNC^1$-hard if there exist constants $a,c>0$ such that for
sufficiently large $n$ any $n$-qubit
depth-$c\cdot\log(n)$ trivial state $\rho_n$ satisfies
\be \| \calD_n  - \diag(\rho_n) \|_1 = \Omega(n^{-a}).

statement_tex:
\label{prop:hbar1}

\textbf{Uncertainty for code-states in at least one basis}

\noindent
Let $(S_x,S_z)$ be a CSS code with $\calB_x,\calB_z$ as in \factref{basis}.  Let
$\ket{\psi}$ be a quantum code-state, and $D_{\psi}^X,D_{\psi}^Z$ be the distribution of
the measurement of $\ket{\psi}$ in the Pauli-$X$ or Pauli-$Z$ basis, respectively.  Then
at least one of the following equations must hold:
\begsub{uncertainty-code-state}
D_{\psi}^Z(C_0^Z)
&\in \left[\frac{1}{2} -\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}},  \frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right]
\\
D_{\psi}^X(C_0^X)
&\in \left[\frac{1}{2} -\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}},  \frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right]
\endsub
Since $D_\psi^P(C_0^P)+D_\psi^P(C_1^P)=1$ for $P=X,Z$ we could equivalently state
\eq{uncertainty-code-state} in terms of $C_1^Z$ and $C_1^X$.

paper_title: Local Hamiltonians Whose Ground States are Hard to Approximate
statement_tex:
Given a depth-$d$ quantum circuit $C$ on $n$ qubits 

we define a directed acyclic graph $G=(V,E)$ by considering
$d+1$ layers of $n$ vertices, 
\be
V = \{V_0,\hdots, V_{d}\},  |V_i| = n\ \  \forall t\in \{0,\ldots,d\},
\ee 
where $V_0$ is the set of input qubits, and $V_{d}$
is the set of output qubits.
Recall from \defref{circuits} that the set of two-qubit gates at time $t$ defines a partition
$P_t$.  Then 
define the edge set $E$ by
connecting for all $t\in [d], k,l\in [n]$ the vertex $V_{t-1,k}$ to $V_{t,l}$ if 
$(k,l)\in P_t$. 
For a subset $S\subseteq V_{d}$ of output qubits, the {\em light cone} of $S$ 
is defined as the set 
$L(S)\subseteq V_0$ of input qubits from which there exists a directed
path in $G$ to some vertex in $S$.  The ``blow-up'' $B = B(C)$ of the circuit $C$
is defined as:
$$
B = B(C) = \max_{v\in V} L(v).
$$
statement_text: Given a depth- d quantum circuit C on n qubits we define a directed acyclic graph G=(V,E) by considering d+1 layers of n vertices, V = {V_0,hdots , V_ d }, |V_i| = n\ \ ∀ t ∈ {0, ... ,d}, where V_0 is the set of input qubits, and V_ d is the set of output qubits. Recall from Definition that the set of two-qubit gates at time t defines a partition P_t . Then define the edge set E by connecting for all t ∈ [d], k,l ∈ [n] the vertex V_ t-1,k to V_ t,l if (k,l) ∈ P_t . For a subset S ⊆ V_ d of output qubits, the em light cone of S is defined as the set L(S) ⊆ V_0 of input qubits from which there exists a directed path in G to some vertex in S . The ``blow-up'' B = B(C) of the circuit C is defined as: B = B(C) = max _ v ∈ V L(v).
title: Light cone

label: def:TZ

statement_tex:
\label{def:TZ}

\textbf{The Hypergraph Product}

\noindent
Let $(V_1,E_1),(V_2,E_2)$ be two constraint hypergraphs with
corresponding edge-vertex incidence
operators $\partial_1,\partial_2$ and codes $\calC_1=\ker\partial_1,
\calC_2=\ker\partial_2$.
Then the Tillich-Z\'{e}mor hypergraph product 
of these codes, denoted by 
\be
\calC_{\times} = {\cal C}_1 \times_{TZ} {\cal C}_2,
\label{eq:TZ-notation}\ee
is defined by the hypergraph product of the corresponding graphs.
Specifically, its Hilbert space is comprised of qubits corresponding to
$$\left(V_1\times V_2\right) \cup \left(E_1\times E_2\right),$$
and check matrices are
\be  H_x = \left( \partial_1 \otimes I_{V_2} \middle| I_{E_1} \otimes \partial_2^T \right)
\qquad
 H_z = \left( I_{V_1} \otimes \partial_2 \middle| \partial_1^T \otimes I_{E_2}\right)
\ee
statement_text: bf The Hypergraph Product Let (V_1,E_1),(V_2,E_2) be two constraint hypergraphs with corresponding edge-vertex incidence operators partial _1,partial _2 and codes cal C _1=ker partial _1, cal C _2=ker partial _2 . Then the Tillich-Z\' e mor hypergraph product of these codes, denoted by cal C _ × = cal C _1 × _ TZ cal C _2, is defined by the hypergraph product of the corresponding graphs. Specifically, its Hilbert space is comprised of qubits corresponding to (V_1 × V_2 ) ∪ (E_1 × E_2 ), and check matrices are H_x = ( partial _1 ⊗ I_ V_2 middle | I_ E_1 ⊗ partial _2^T ) qquad H_z = ( I_ V_1 ⊗ partial _2 middle | partial _1^T ⊗ I_ E_2 )

label: fact:TZ
paper_title: Local Hamiltonians Whose Ground States are Hard to Approximate
statement_tex:
\label{fact:TZ}

\textbf{Basic Properties of the hypergraph product}\cite{TZ09}

\noindent
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If $C_1,C_2$ have locality parameters $l_1,l_2,l_1^T,l_2^T$, respectively, 
($l_i^T$ is the maximum number of checks incident upon any bit in code $C_i$)
then
$\calC_{\times}$ has locality parameter $l_1 + l_2^T$ for $H_x$, and $l_2 + l_1^T$ for $H_z$.
\item
$
\delta_{\min}({\cal C}_{\times})
\geq
\min \left\{ \delta_{\min}({\cal C}_1),\delta_{\min}({\cal C}_2),\delta_{\min}({\cal C}_1^T),\delta_{\min}({\cal C}_2^T)\right\}
$
\item Let $r(\calC)$ denote the number of qubits in a code $\calC$.
Then
$
r({\cal C}_{\times}) = r({\cal C}_1) \cdot r({\cal C}_2) + r({\cal C}_1^T) \cdot r({\cal C}_2^T).
$
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: bf Basic Properties of the hypergraph product If C_1,C_2 have locality parameters l_1,l_2,l_1^T,l_2^T , respectively, ( l_i^T is the maximum number of checks incident upon any bit in code C_i ) then cal C _ × has locality parameter l_1 + l_2^T for H_x , and l_2 + l_1^T for H_z . δ_ min ( cal C _ × ) ≥ min { δ_ min ( cal C _1),δ_ min ( cal C _2),δ_ min ( cal C _1^T),δ_ min ( cal C _2^T) } Let r( cal C ) denote the number of qubits in a code cal C . Then r( cal C _ × ) = r( cal C _1) · r( cal C _2) + r( cal C _1^T) · r( cal C _2^T).

statement_tex:
\label{fact:logicalshape}


\textbf{Group of logical operators isomorphic to the original code}

\noindent
For any $x\in {\cal C}_1$, and $y\notin {\cal C}_2^{\perp}$, the word 
\be
\left(\left(x \ot y\right)_{V_1\times V_2} , \mathbf{0}_{E_1\times E_2}\right)
 \in S_x^\perp - S_z
\ee
Similarly, for $x\notin \calC_1^\perp, y\in\calC_2$, 
\be\left(\left(x \ot y\right)_{V_1\times V_2} , \mathbf{0}_{E_1\times E_2}\right)
 \in S_z^\perp - S_x.
\ee
One can also show that
\begsub{cycles}
 (\mathbf{0}_{V_1\times V_2}, \calC_2^T \ot (\calC_1^{T\perp})^c) & \subset

statement_tex:
\label{prop:prodexp}

\textbf{The hypergraph product of a connected graph}

\noindent
Let $G = (V,E)$ denote a $d$-regular connected graph on $n$ vertices.
Let ${\cal C} = {\cal C}(G)$ denote the repetition code on $n$ bits defined by treating the edges of $G$ as equality constraints.
Let ${\cal C}_{\times}(G)$ denote the hypergraph product of ${\cal C} \times_{TZ} {\cal C}$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Denote $|V| = n$, $|E| = m = dn/2$, and so
$|V\times V| = n^2, |E\times E| = d^2n^2/4, |V\times E| = |E\times V| = dn^2/2$.
The number of qubits is $N = (1+d^2/4)n^2$ and the number of checks is $dn^2$.
\item
${\cal C}_{\times}$ is a quantum code 
on the space of $\bbF_2^{V\times V}\oplus\bbF_2^{ E\times E} = \F_2^{N}$,
constrained by the $d+2$-local checks from the columns of $\{H_x,H_z\}$.
\item
The following set of vectors, indexed by $v\in V,e\in E$,  generates $S_z$, 
\be\label{eq:sz}
s_z(v,e) =  H_z^T(v\ot e) = v \otimes \partial^Te + \partial v \otimes e
\ee




Likewise $S_x$ is generated by the vectors
\be \label{eq:sx}
s_x(e,v) = H_x^T(e\ot v) = \partial^Te\otimes v + e\ot\partial v. \ee

\item
$\dim(S_x^{\perp} / S_z) = 1 + \dim({\cal C}^T)^2$.

This follows from Proposition 14 in \cite{TZ09}.  

\item
The distance of the code is 
given by the minimum of the distance of the code ${\cal C}$ and the transposed code ${\cal C}^T$.
\end{enumerate}

paper_title: Low-degree testing for quantum states, and a quantum entangled games PCP for QMA
statement_tex:
Let $n$ be an integer and $q = p^t$ a prime power such that $q = \Theta(\frac{\log^2 n}{\log \log n})$.
	Then there exists a two-prover test $\qld$ in which the
        verifier sends questions of length $\poly(\log n,\log q)$ and
        receives answers of length 
        $O(\poly\log\log(n) \cdot \log q)$ such that the following hold: 
	\begin{enumerate}[nolistsep]
	\item \emph{(Completeness:)} There exists a strategy for the provers based on sharing an $n$-qudit maximally entangled state, with qudits of local dimension $q$, and making measurements in the eigenbasis of tensor products of generalized $\qp_X$ or $\qp_Z$ observables over $\Fq$;
	\item \emph{(Soundness:)} For any $\eps \geq 0$, any strategy that is accepted
    with probability at least $1-\eps$ in the test must use an entangled state
    that is (up to local isometries) within distance $\delta =
    \poly(\poly(p)\cdot\poly(\eps) )$ from an $n$-qudit maximally entangled state.\footnote{Here and
      throughout we use the notation $f(X)=\poly(h(X)))$ as an abbreviation for ``there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that $f(X) = O(h(X)^c)$ as $X\to 0$ (if $X=\eps$) or as $X\to\infty$ (if $X=n$); in the theorem $p,t$ and $q$ are all allowed to be implicitly functions of $n$, but not $\eps$.}
\end{enumerate}

statement_tex:
Let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. A \emph{$k$-partite strategy} $S = (\ket{\psi},\mathcal{X},
  \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{M})$ consists of finite question and answer sets $\mathcal{X}=X_1\times\cdots\times X_k$
  and $\mathcal{A}=A_1\times\cdots\times A_k$ respectively, a $k$-partite
   quantum state $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_1\otimes \cdots \otimes\mH_k$, and for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$ a collection of measurement
  operators $\{M^a_x\}_{a \in A_i}$ on $\mathcal{H}_i$ and indexed by $x \in X_i$.\footnote{Although this is left implicit in the notation, the measurement operators associated with different spaces need not be equal.} We say that the strategy is \emph{partial} if it only specifies measurement operators for a subset of the possible questions, or if it does not specify a state $\ket{\psi}$.
