label: thm: generalapproach
paper_title: Plethysm is in #BQP
statement_tex:
\label{thm: generalapproach}
If, given a reductive group $G$ and a representation $V$ as in \cref{eq: Vdecomposition}, there exists a model representation $V_\text{model}$ for $G$ such that:
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
    \item there exists an efficiently-implementable $G$-equivariant isometric embedding $V\hookrightarrow V_{\text{model}}$,
    \item there exists an efficient quantum algorithm to perform strong Fourier sampling on $V_\text{model}$,
\end{itemize}
then the problem of computing the multiplicities $m_\la(V)$ is in $\#\BQP$, and the problem of deciding whether $m_\la(V)>0$ is in $\QMA$ (or in $\QMA_1$ if the above can be implemented exactly).
statement_text: If, given a reductive group G and a representation V as in cref eq: Vdecomposition , there exists a model representation V_ model for G such that: there exists an efficiently-implementable G -equivariant isometric embedding Vhookrightarrow V_ model , there exists an efficient quantum algorithm to perform strong Fourier sampling on V_ model , then the problem of computing the multiplicities m_λ(V) is in \# BQP , and the problem of deciding whether m_λ(V)>0 is in QMA (or in QMA _1 if the above can be implemented exactly).

paper_title: Plethysm is in #BQP
statement_tex:
For the plethysm coefficients in~\cref{prob: plethysm}, the embedding step is
    \[
        V \coloneqq \{\mu\}\restr \hookrightarrow V_\text{model} \coloneqq (\C^n)^{\ot |\mu|\cdot|\nu|},
    \]
    and is implemented via two rounds of inverse Schur transforms (see \cref{eq:pleth emb} and discussion below it).
    Strong Fourier sampling for the model representation becomes in this case strong \emph{Schur} sampling, and can be efficiently implemented by a Schur transform followed by measurements.
statement_text: For the plethysm coefficients in cref prob: plethysm , the embedding step is \[ V coloneqq {μ} downarrow ^G_H hookrightarrow V_ model coloneqq (m C ^n)^ ⊗ |μ| · |ν| , \] and is implemented via two rounds of inverse Schur transforms (see cref eq:pleth emb and discussion below it). Strong Fourier sampling for the model representation becomes in this case strong Schur sampling, and can be efficiently implemented by a Schur transform followed by measurements.

paper_title: Plethysm is in #BQP
statement_tex:
While the Kronecker coefficients~$g_{\lambda,\mu,\nu}$ fall into the general framework of branching multiplicities, they can be directly captured by the above approach.
    Let $\lambda,\mu,\nu$ be partitions of~$n$, each with no more than~$d$ parts.
    Then the Kronecker coefficients are captured by first applying the embedding
    \[
        V \coloneqq [\la]\ot[\mu]\ot[\nu] \hookrightarrow V_\text{model} \coloneqq (\C^d)^{\ot n}\ot(\C^d)^{\ot n}\ot(\C^d)^{\ot n}\cong(\C^{d^3})^{\ot n},
    \]
    using three inverse Schur transforms, and subsequently applying weak Fourier sampling, accepting if the outcome corresponds ot the trivial~$S_n$-representation (as explained in \cref{rem:inv} one could similarly use two inverse Schur transforms and strong Schur sampling).
    Ref.~\cite{christandl2015algcomp} used a close variant of this approach, with the embedding replaced by a projective measurement onto the subspace~$V \subseteq V_\text{model}$.
statement_text: While the Kronecker coefficients g_ λ,μ,ν fall into the general framework of branching multiplicities, they can be directly captured by the above approach. Let λ,μ,ν be partitions of n , each with no more than d parts. Then the Kronecker coefficients are captured by first applying the embedding \[ V coloneqq [λ] ⊗ [μ] ⊗ [ν] hookrightarrow V_ model coloneqq (m C ^d)^ ⊗ n ⊗ (m C ^d)^ ⊗ n ⊗ (m C ^d)^ ⊗ n cong (m C ^ d^3 )^ ⊗ n , \] using three inverse Schur transforms, and subsequently applying weak Fourier sampling, accepting if the outcome corresponds ot the trivial S_n -representation (as explained in cref rem:inv one could similarly use two inverse Schur transforms and strong Schur sampling). Ref. used a close variant of this approach, with the embedding replaced by a projective measurement onto the subspace V ⊆ V_ model .

statement_tex:
\label{cor:gpe bqp}
If, given a finite group~$G$ and a unitary representation~$V$, there exist efficient quantum circuits for the Fourier transform ${\rm QFT}_G$ and for the controlled group action $\mathcal{U}$, then the problem of computing the multiplicities~$m_\la(V)$ is in $\#\BQP$, and the problem of deciding whether $m_\la(V)>0$ is in $\QMA$ (or in $\QMA_1$ if the above can be implemented exactly).

paper_title: Plethysm is in #BQP
statement_tex:
Recall that the restriction coefficients~$r_\lambda^\mu$ are defined as the multiplicities of Specht modules in Weyl modules by embedding $S_n \subset \GL(n)$ as permutation matrices.
    That is, they are defined as the multiplicity of the irreducible $S_n$-representation~$[\la]$ in~$\{\mu\}\!\!\downarrow^{\GL(n)}_{S_n}$.
    We can first embed
    \[
        \irr{\mu}{\GL(n)}\hookrightarrow (\C^n)^{\ot |\mu|},
    \]
    by applying an inverse Schur transform (as in the case of plethysms).
    Since the controlled group action of~$S_n$ on $\C^n$ can be implemented efficiently, and there is an efficient QFT for the symmetric group~$S_n$, we can apply \cref{cor:gpe bqp} to see that the restriction coefficients are in~$\#\BQP$.
statement_text: Recall that the restriction coefficients r_λ^μ are defined as the multiplicities of Specht modules in Weyl modules by embedding S_n ⊂ GL (n) as permutation matrices. That is, they are defined as the multiplicity of the irreducible S_n -representation [λ] in {μ} downarrow ^ GL (n) _ S_n . We can first embed \[ {μ}_ GL (n) hookrightarrow (m C ^n)^ ⊗ |μ| , \] by applying an inverse Schur transform (as in the case of plethysms). Since the controlled group action of S_n on m C ^n can be implemented efficiently, and there is an efficient QFT for the symmetric group S_n , we can apply cref cor:gpe bqp to see that the restriction coefficients are in \# BQP .

label: def:subsetstate
paper_title: Improved Hardness Results for the Guided Local Hamiltonian Problem
statement_tex:
\label{def:subsetstate}
We say that a normalized state $\ket{u} \in \mathbb{C}^{2^n}$ is a semi-classical subset state if there is a subset $S\subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ with $|S|=\poly(n)$ such that
\[
\ket{u}= \frac{1}{\sqrt{|S|}}\sum_{x\in S} \ket{x}.
\]
statement_text: We say that a normalized state ket u ∈ C ^ 2^n is a semi-classical subset state if there is a subset S ⊆ {0,1}^n with |S|= poly (n) such that \[ ket u = frac 1 sqrt |S| Σ _ x ∈ S ket x . \]
title: Semi-classical subset state

label: def:semiclassical
paper_title: Improved Hardness Results for the Guided Local Hamiltonian Problem
statement_tex:
\label{def:semiclassical}
We say that a normalized state $\ket{u} \in \mathbb{C}^{2^m}$, for $n<m \in\mathcal{O}(n)$, is a semi-classical encoded state if there is a subset $S\subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ with $|S|=\poly(n)$ and a set of isometries $V_1, V_2,...,V_n$, where each of $V_i$ maps a $1$-qubit state to an $\mathcal{O}(1)$-qubit state, such that
\[
\ket{u}= \frac{1}{\sqrt{|S|}}\sum_{x\in S} V_1(\ket{x_1})\otimes V_2(\ket{x_2}) \otimes \cdots \otimes V_n(\ket{x_n}).
\]
statement_text: We say that a normalized state ket u ∈ C ^ 2^m , for n<m ∈ O (n) , is a semi-classical encoded state if there is a subset S ⊆ {0,1}^n with |S|= poly (n) and a set of isometries V_1, V_2,...,V_n , where each of V_i maps a 1 -qubit state to an O (1) -qubit state, such that \[ ket u = frac 1 sqrt |S| Σ _ x ∈ S V_1(ket x_1 ) ⊗ V_2(ket x_2 ) ⊗ ... ⊗ V_n(ket x_n ). \]
title: Semi-classical encoded state

label: lemma:sampling
paper_title: Improved Hardness Results for the Guided Local Hamiltonian Problem
statement_text: Given the description of an m -qubit semi-classical encoded state ket u , we can classically efficiently sample from the probability distribution that outputs x ∈ {0,1}^m with probability |le x|urangle |^2 .

label: def:non2sld
paper_title: Improved Hardness Results for the Guided Local Hamiltonian Problem
statement_tex:
\label{def:non2sld}
Suppose $\mathcal{S}$ is a set of interactions at most 2 qubits. We say that $\mathcal{S}$ is 2SLD if there exists $U \in {\rm SU}(2)$, such that for all $h_i \in \mathcal{S}$,
\[
U^{\otimes 2} h_i (U^\dagger)^{\otimes 2} = \alpha_i Z\otimes Z + A_i \otimes I + I \otimes B_i,
\]
where $\alpha_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and $A_i, B_i$ are arbitrary single-qubit Hamiltonians.
statement_text: Suppose S is a set of interactions at most 2 qubits. We say that S is 2SLD if there exists U ∈ rm SU (2) , such that for all h_i ∈ S , \[ U^ ⊗ 2 h_i (U^dagger )^ ⊗ 2 = α_i Z ⊗ Z + A_i ⊗ I + I ⊗ B_i, \] where α_i ∈ R and A_i, B_i are arbitrary single-qubit Hamiltonians.
title: 2SLD interaction

label: proposition:overlap
paper_title: Improved Hardness Results for the Guided Local Hamiltonian Problem
statement_text: For any δ ∈ (0,1-Ω(1/ poly (n))) , there exist a,b ∈ [0,1] with b-a ∈ Ω(1/ poly (n)) such that the problem GLHLE (5,0,a,b,δ) is up BQP -hard. Moreover, it is still up BQP -hard with the additional two promises that H has a non-degenerate ground state separated from the first excited state by a spectral gap γ ∈ Ω(1/ poly (n)) in both the cases λ_0(H) ≤ a and λ_0(H) ≥ b .(We call such instances γ -gapped up GLH (k,a,b,δ) .) The guiding state is restricted to be a semi-classical subset state.

label: prop:locality

statement_tex:
\label{prop:locality}
Any $\gamma$-gapped $\text{GLHLE}(k,c,a,b,\delta)$ with $k\in \mathcal{O}(1)$, $b-a\in \Omega(1/\poly(n))$, $\delta \in (0,1-\Omega(1/\poly(n)))$, $0 \leq c \leq \text{poly}(n)$, and $\gamma \in \Omega(1/\poly(n))$

statement_tex:
\label{cor}
	Let $G$ be a $k$-player game with $\val(G) \leq 1 - \eps$, and let $n \geq \frac{\log 4/\eps}{\eps^5 \lambda^2 }$. If $G$ is:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Free, i.e., $\mu(x) = \mu^1(x^1) \times \cdots \times \mu^k(x^k)$, then
		$$
	\val(G^{\otimes n}) \leq \exp \left(-\frac{c \, \eps^5 \, n}{k^2 \log |\A|}\right).
		$$
		\item $\alpha$-Anchored (see Definition~\ref{def:anchored-game}, and \cite{BavarianVY2015}  for more details), then
		$$ \val(G^{\otimes n}) \leq \exp \left(-\frac{c \, \alpha^{2k} \,\eps^5 \,  n}{64 ~k^2\log |\A|}\right). $$
		\item Connected, i.e., the $(k-1)$-connection graph is connected, then
		$$
		\val(G^{\otimes n}) \leq \exp \left(-\frac{c \,\rho_{min}^2 \,  \eps^5 \,n}{\log |\A|}\right)
		$$
		where $ \rho_{min} = \min_{u,v : \rho(u,v) > 0} \rho(u,v)$. In particular, if the game $G$ is such that $\mu$ is the uniform distribution over some set $S \subseteq \X$, then $\rho_{min} \geq (k|S|^2 )^{-1}$.

	\end{enumerate}
	where $c$ is a universal constant.

label: def:anchored-game
paper_title: Multiplayer parallel repetition for expander games
statement_tex:
\label{def:anchored-game}
Given a $k$-prover game $G$, and a parameter $\alpha < 1$ we define the \emph{$\alpha$ anchored} game $G_{\bot}$ as follows: the referee chooses a question tuple $(x^1, \ldots, x^k)$, according to $G$, and independently, for every $t\in [k]$, replaces $x^t$ by the anchoring symbol $\bot$ with probability $\alpha$ to get the tuple $(x'^1, \ldots x'^k)$. The new domain is thus $\X'^1 \times \X'^2 \ldots \X'^k$, where $X'^i= \X \cup \{\bot\}$. If any of the $x'$'s are $\bot$, the verifier accepts trivially, otherwise the verifier accepts according to the predicate of the game $G$.
statement_text: Given a k -prover game G , and a parameter α < 1 we define the α anchored game G_ bot as follows: the referee chooses a question tuple (x^1, ... , x^k) , according to G , and independently, for every t ∈ [k] , replaces x^t by the anchoring symbol bot with probability α to get the tuple (x'^1, ... x'^k) . The new domain is thus mathscr X '^1 × mathscr X '^2 ... mathscr X '^k , where X'^i= mathscr X ∪ {bot } . If any of the x' 's are bot , the verifier accepts trivially, otherwise the verifier accepts according to the predicate of the game G .

label: def:ds
paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
statement_tex:
\label{def:ds}
Let $Y \in \Ten(n_0,n_1,\ldots,n_d)$ be a tensor and $\rho=YY^\dagger/Y^\dagger Y$, with quantum marginals $\rho_1,\dots,\rho_{d}$ on the last $d$ systems.
Then we define the \emph{distance to $d$-stochasticity} $\ds(Y)$ as the (squared) distance between the marginals and $d$-stochastic marginals,
\[
\ds(Y) := \sum_{i=1}^d \norm{\rho_i - \frac{I_{n_i}}{n_i}}_F^2,
\]
where $\lVert M \rVert_F := (\tr M^\dagger M)^{1/2}$ is the Frobenius norm.
Following \cref{eq:dual-alt-min}, we further define the \emph{minimal distance to $d$-stochasticity} as
\[
\dds(X) := \inf_{A\in G} \, \ds(A\cdot X).
\]
statement_text: Let Y ∈ Ten (n_0,n_1, ... ,n_d) be a tensor and ρ=YY^dagger /Y^dagger Y , with quantum marginals ρ_1, ... ,ρ_ d on the last d systems. Then we define the distance to d -stochasticity ds (Y) as the (squared) distance between the marginals and d -stochastic marginals, \[ ds (Y) := Σ _ i=1 ^d norm ρ_i - frac I_ n_i n_i _F^2, \] where lVert M rVert _F := (tr M^dagger M)^ 1/2 is the Frobenius norm. Following cref eq:dual-alt-min , we further define the minimal distance to d -stochasticity as \[ dds (X) := inf _ A ∈ G ds (A · X). \]
title: Distance to d -stochasticity

statement_tex:
A tensor $X \in \Ten_m^d$ is said to have \emph{slice rank-one} if it decomposes as the tensor product of a vector and a lower-order tensor, i.e., if there exists a $k \in [d]$, a vector $V \in \C^m$, and a tensor $Y \in \Ten_m^{d-1}$ such that
\[
X_{j_1,\dots,j_d} = V_{j_k} \cdot Y_{j_1,\dots,j_{k-1},j_{k+1},\dots,j_d}.
\]
The \emph{slice rank} of a tensor $X$, denoted $\sr(X)$, is defined as the minimum number $r$ of slice rank-one tensors $X_1,\dots,X_r$ such that $X=\sum_{i=1}^r X_i$.
statement_text: A tensor X ∈ Ten _m^d is said to have slice rank-one if it decomposes as the tensor product of a vector and a lower-order tensor, i.e., if there exists a k ∈ [d] , a vector V ∈ C ^m , and a tensor Y ∈ Ten _m^ d-1 such that \[ X_ j_1, ... ,j_d = V_ j_k · Y_ j_1, ... ,j_ k-1 ,j_ k+1 , ... ,j_d . \] The slice rank of a tensor X , denoted slice-rank (X) , is defined as the minimum number r of slice rank-one tensors X_1, ... ,X_r such that X= Σ _ i=1 ^r X_i .
title: Slice rank

label: thm:slice rank1
paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
statement_tex:
{theorem}{slicerank}\label{thm:slice rank1}
Consider a tensor $X \in \Ten_m^d$. If $\sr(X) < m$, then $X$ is in the null cone for $\SL(m)^d$. In fact, $\ins(X) \ge 1/\sqrt{d m^3}$.
statement_text: theorem slicerank Consider a tensor X ∈ Ten _m^d . If slice-rank (X) < m , then X is in the null cone for SL (m)^d . In fact, instability (X) ≥ 1/ sqrt d m^3 .

label: thm:slice rank2
paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
statement_tex:
\label{thm:slice rank2}
Consider a tensor $X \in \Ten_m^d$. If $X$ is in the null cone for $\SL(m)^d$, then $\sr(X^{\otimes k}) < m^k$ for some positive integer $k$.
statement_text: Consider a tensor X ∈ Ten _m^d . If X is in the null cone for SL (m)^d , then slice-rank (X^ ⊗ k ) < m^k for some positive integer k .

label: le:asympt-stab
paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
statement_tex:
{lemma}{asymptstab}\label{le:asympt-stab}
Let $k \ge 1$. Then
$X$ is in the null cone of the action of $\SL(m)^d$ if and only if
$X^{\otimes k}$ is in the null cone of the action of $\SL(m^k)^d$.
statement_text: lemma asymptstab Let k ≥ 1 . Then X is in the null cone of the action of SL (m)^d if and only if X^ ⊗ k is in the null cone of the action of SL (m^k)^d .

label: cor:slice rank null cone
paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
statement_tex:
\label{cor:slice rank null cone}
A tensor $X \in \Ten_m^d$ is in the null cone iff $\sr(X^{\otimes k}) < m^k$ for some positive integer $k$.
statement_text: A tensor X ∈ Ten _m^d is in the null cone iff slice-rank (X^ ⊗ k ) < m^k for some positive integer k .

paper_title: Alternating minimization, scaling algorithms, and the null-cone problem from invariant theory
statement_tex:
There is a deterministic $\poly(m^d, b)$ time algorithm that, given a tensor $X \in \Ten_m^d$,
with entries of bit size bounded by $b$, such that either
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\sr(X^{\otimes k}) = m^k$ for all $k$, or
\item $\sr(X) < m$,
\end{enumerate}
decides which is the case.
statement_text: There is a deterministic poly (m^d, b) time algorithm that, given a tensor X ∈ Ten _m^d , with entries of bit size bounded by b , such that either slice-rank (X^ ⊗ k ) = m^k for all k , or slice-rank (X) < m , decides which is the case.

statement_text: For a reductive group G acting on a vector space V , the Reynolds operator R _G is a G -invariant projection R _G: C [V] → C [V]^G. That is, it is a linear map satisfying the following properties for every polynomial p ∈ C [V] : R _G(p) = p if p ∈ C [V]^G , R _G(g · p) = R _G(p) for all g ∈ G .

statement_tex:
Let $V$ be a representation of $G$ of dimension $n$ and $v \in V$ be a vector with
integral entries that is not in the null cone of the $G$ action.
Then the capacity of $v$ is bounded below by
\begin{align*}
  \capac(v) = \inf_{g\in G} \lVert \rho(g) v\rVert_2^2 \geq
   \exp(-c \left( d\ln(Rn) + d \ell \ln(\ell) \max_{i\ge 1} \ell_i n_i^2 \right) ),
\end{align*}
where $c >0$ is a universal constant.
For the tensor action of $G$ on $\Ten(n_0, \ldots, n_d)$, we have a bound of the form
$\exp\left(-c \; d^2 \ln(d) \max_{i \geq 0} n_i^2 \right)$.

label: thm:traversal

statement_tex:
{theorem}{theoremtraversal}\label{thm:traversal}
    Let $H\in\hermp{\C^d},\,d=2^n$ with $0\preccurlyeq H \preccurlyeq I$, $\ket{\psi},\ket\phi\in\C^d$ with $\braketb\psi H\le \eta$ and $\braketb\phi H\le\eta$.
    For any $\Delta \ge 2^{-\poly(n)}$, there exists a sequence of $2$-local unitary gates $U=U_m\cdots U_1$ with $m\le 2^{\poly(n)}$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
        \item $\enorm{U\ket\psi - \ket\phi}\le \Delta$, and
        \item for all $i\in [m]$, $\braketb{\psi_i} H \le \eta+\Delta$, where $\ket{\psi_i} := U_{i}\cdots U_1\ket\psi$.
    \end{enumerate}

U_1 with m ≤ 2^ poly (n) such that enorm Uket ψ - ket φ ≤ Δ , and for all i ∈ [m] , bra ψ_i Hket ψ_i ≤ η+Δ , where ket ψ_i := U_ i ... U_1ket ψ .

statement_text: Let p,q,r,m,α,β:R mapsto R , where p,q,r are poly-bounded. label: def:stream
paper_title: Quantum space, ground space traversal, and how to embed multi-prover interactive proofs into unentanglement
statement_text: Let U be a quantum circuit acting on an n_1 -qubit input register R_1 , n_2 -qubit ancilla register R_2 , and 1 -qubit proof register R_3 , for some n_1,n_2>0 . Registers R_2 and R_3 are initialized to all zeroes. At a high level, the idea is to stream a classical proof in register R_3 one bit at a time. To do so, we view the entire execution of U as a sequence of 1 - and 2 -qubit gates, but where certain 1 -qubit gates on R_3 are a priori unknown. Formally: There are two main phases in the circuit, which repeat until the circuit completes. In iteration i : (Computation phase) A sequence of 1 - and 2 -qubit gates acts solely on registers R_1 and R_2 . (Proof phase) (Compute) Single-qubit gate W_i ∈ {I,X } is applied to R_3 , for X the Pauli NOT gate. (Copy) R_3 is classically copied into R_2 via CNOT gate (controlled from R_3 onto R_2 ). (Uncompute) W_i is applied to R_3 to return R_3 to ket 0 .
title: Streaming classical proof

label: def:QCMASPACE
paper_title: Quantum space, ground space traversal, and how to embed multi-prover interactive proofs into unentanglement
statement_text: definition definitionQCMASPACE A promise problem A=(A_ up yes ,A_ up no ) is in SQCMASPACE (p,q,r) for polynomially-bounded functions p,q,r , if there exist thresholds α(n),β(n) satisfying α(n)-β(n) ≥ 2^ -r(n) , and a q(n) -space uniform family of quantum circuits {Q_n } with properties as follows. Q_n takes as input a string x ∈ Σ^n , a classical streaming proof y ∈ {0,1 } ^ 2^ p(n) , and q(n) ancilla qubits in state ket 0 ^ ⊗ q(n) . We say Q_n accepts (x,y) with probability p if on input (x,y) , measuring Q_n 's dedicated output wire in the standard basis yields 1 with probability p . Then: (Completeness) If xinA _ up yes , there exists a streaming proof y ∈ {0,1 } ^ 2^ p(n) such that Q_n accepts (x,y) with probability at least α . (Soundness) If xinA _ up no , for all streaming proofs y ∈ {0,1 } ^ 2^ p(n) , Q_n accepts (x, y ) with probability at most β . Finally, let the input, ancilla, and proof registers be denoted R_1 , R_2 , R_3 respectively. To enforce that R_1 and R_3 are not used as ancilla, we require that Q_n only acts on R_1 and R_3 via CNOTs with the control in R_1 or R_3 and the target in R_2 .
title: Streaming- QCMASPACE ( SQCMASPACE (p,q,r) )

label: def:sparse

statement_tex:
\label{def:sparse}
A Hermitian operator $H \in \herm\left((\C^2)^{\otimes n}\right)$ is \emph{row-sparse} if each row of $H$ has at most $\poly(n)$ non-zero entries, and if there exists an efficient classical algorithm mapping row index $i\in[2^n]$ to a sequence of all non-zero entries $H_{ij}$ of $H$.
statement_text: A Hermitian operator H ∈ Herm ((C^2)^ ⊗ n ) is row-sparse if each row of H has at most poly (n) non-zero entries, and if there exists an efficient classical algorithm mapping row index i ∈ [2^n] to a sequence of all non-zero entries H_ ij of H .

label: def:sepsparse

statement_text: Let g:N mapsto R be an efficiently computable function. Given as input a sparse Hamiltonian H , a bipartition L versus R of the n qubits H acts on, and threshold parameters α,β satisfying β-α ≥ 1/g(n) , decide: (YES case) If there exists ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R such that bra ψ_1 _Lbra ψ_2 _R H ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R ≤ α , output YES. (NO case) If for all ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R , bra ψ_1 _Lbra ψ_2 _R H ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R ≥ β , output NO.
title: Separable Sparse Hamiltonian (SSH( g ))

label: def:QMAt

statement_text: A promise problem A=(A_ up yes ,A_ up no ) is in QMA (2,p,q,r) for polynomially bounded functions p,q,r if there exist thresholds α(n),β(n) satisfying α(n)-β(n) ≥ 2^ -r(n) , and a poly-time uniform family of quantum circuits {Q_n } with properties as follows. Q_n takes as input a string x ∈ Σ^n , a quantum proof ket ψ_1 _L ⊗ ket ψ_2 _R ∈ C^ 2^ p(n) ⊗ C^ 2^ p(n) , and q(n) ancilla qubits in state ket 0 ^ ⊗ q(n) . We say Q_n accepts (x,y) with probability p_ up acc if on input (x,ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R) , measuring Q_n 's dedicated output wire in the standard basis yields 1 with probability p_ up acc . Then: (Completeness) If xinA _ up yes , there exists a ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R such that Q_n accepts (x,ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R) with probability at least α . (Soundness) If xinA _ up no , for all ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R , Q_n accepts (x,ket ψ_1 _Lket ψ_2 _R) with probability at most β .
title: QMA (2,p,q,r)

label: def:SQMASPACE
paper_title: Quantum space, ground space traversal, and how to embed multi-prover interactive proofs into unentanglement
statement_text: definition definitionSQMASPACE A promise problem A=(A_ up yes ,allowbreakA _ up no ) is in SQMASPACE (p,q,r) for polynomially-bounded functions p,q,r , if there exist thresholds α(n),β(n) satisfying α(n)-β(n) ≥ 2^ -r(n) , and a q(n) -space uniform family of quantum circuits {Q_n} with properties as follows. Q_n takes as input a string x ∈ Σ^n , a 2^ p(n) -qubit proof ket ψ in register Y , a q(n) -bit ancilla register X initialized to ket 0 ^ ⊗ q(n) , and is of form (see Cref fig:sqma ) Q_n= Π _ i=m ^1 l((V_i)_X · SWAP _ X _1,Y _i r) · (V_0)_X . Then, (Completeness) If xinA _ up yes : ∃ ket ψ ∈ Y :bra 0^q bra ψ l(Q_n^dagger ketbra 11_ X _1 Q_n r)ket 0^q ket ψ ≥ α(n) . (Soundness) If xinA _ up no : ∀ ket ψ ∈ Y :bra 0^q bra ψ l(Q_n^dagger ketbra 11_ X _1 Q_n r)ket 0^q ket ψ ≤ β(n) . As in Cref def:QCMASPACE , we do not allow Q_n to alter the contents of its input register (to avoid using said register as additional ancilla space).
title: Streaming- QMASPACE ( SQMASPACE (p,q,r) )

label: def:QMAEXP

statement_text: A promise problem A=(A_ up yes ,A_ up no ) is in QMAEXP (p(n),q(n)) for polynomially bounded functions p, q if there exists an exponential time uniform family of quantum circuits {Q_n } with properties as follows. Q_n takes as input a string x ∈ Σ^n , a quantum proof ket ψ_1 ∈ (C^2)^ ⊗ 2^ p(n) , and ancilla qubits in state ket 0 ^ ⊗ 2^ q(n) . We say Q_n accepts (x,ket ψ) with probability p_ up acc if on input (x,ket ψ) , measuring Q_n 's dedicated output wire in the standard basis yields 1 with probability p_ up acc . Then: (Completeness) If xinA _ up yes , there exists a ket ψ such that Q_n accepts (x,ket ψ) with probability at least 2/3 . (Soundness) If xinA _ up no , for all ket ψ , Q_n accepts (x,ket ψ) with probability at most 1/3 .
title: QMAEXP (p,q)

statement_text: Fix a constant d . The input is the length of the chain N encoded in binary, a single Hamiltonian constraint H ∈ Herm (C^ d ⊗ C^ d ) specified with a constant number of bits, and polynomials α,β such that β-α ≥ 1/ poly (N) . The full Hamiltonian is thus H^ (N) := Σ _ i=1 ^ N-1 H_ i,i+1 (i.e. H acts on each pair of qudits on a line). Decide: (YES case) If λ_ min (H^ (N) ) ≤ α(N) , output YES. (NO case) If λ_ min (H^ (N) ) ≥ β(N) , output NO.
title: IDTIH

statement_text: A promise problem A=(A_ up yes ,A_ up no ) is in MIP (t,p,r,c,s) if there exist polynomial t and polynomially bounded functions u and v , and a classical verifier V using poly (n) time, u(n) space, v(n) bits of randomness, and interacting with p non-communicating provers via r rounds of interaction, where each round consists of t(n) bits of communication between verifier and provers, and where n=abs x is the size of input x , such that If x ∈ A_ up yes , then there exists a strategy for the provers that is accepted by the verifier with probability at least c . If x ∈ A_ up no , any strategy of the provers is accepted by the verifier with probability at most s .

label: def:pcp
paper_title: Quantum space, ground space traversal, and how to embed multi-prover interactive proofs into unentanglement
statement_text: A language L is in PCP [r(n),q(n)] if there exists verifier Turing machine M that behaves as follows: M receives input x , a proof y ∈ {0,1}^ * , and a random string z ∈ {0,1}^ r(n) on separate tapes. M computes indices i_1, ... ,i_ q(n) without accessing y (it may access z ) in polynomial time. M copies proof bits y_ i_1 , ... ,y_ i_ q(n) to its work tape. M accepts or rejects in polynomial time without accessing y . M must also satisfy the following conditions for all x ∈ {0,1}^n : If x ∈ L , ∃ y:Pr _z[M(x,y,z)=1]=1 , where z ∈ {0,1}^ r(n) is chosen uniformly at random. If x ∉ L , ∀ y:Pr _z[M(x,y,z)=1] ≤ 1/2 .
title: PCP [r(n),q(n)]

statement_tex:
{lemma}{embed}\label{l:embed}
    Let $p,q,r,m,\alpha,\beta:\R\mapsto\R$ be efficiently computable functions, where $p,q,r$ are polynomially bounded. Let $Q_n$ be a quantum circuit consisting of $m(n)$ $1$-and $2$-qubit gates, taking in (1) input $x\in\Sigma^n$, (2) a classical streaming proof ${y}\in \set{0,1}^{2^{p(n)}}$, and (3) $q(n)$ ancilla qubits in state $\ket{0}^{\otimes q(n)}$, such that $m(n)\geq 2^{p(n)}$ and $q(n)\geq p(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Define thresholds $\alpha(n),\beta(n)$ satisfying $\alpha(n)-\beta(n)\geq 2^{-r(n)}$. We are promised that either:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item (YES) There exists\footnote{\label{footnote:embedding-lemma}To clarify, we are slightly abusing notation here for simplicity. Formally, \Cref{def:stream} defines $y$ as being ``part of the circuit'' $Q_n$. Section \ref{sscn:ingredients} will reflect this by using notation $Q_n(y)$ (i.e. the circuit $Q_n$ with proof gates according to $y$). In the statement of the lemma, however, we say for simplicity, in the usual wording, ``there exists a proof $y$ such that$\ldots$''.} a streaming proof $y\in\set{0,1}^{2^{p(n)}}$ such that $Q_n$ accepts $(x,y)$ with probability at least $\alpha$.
        \item (NO) For all streaming proofs ${y}\in \set{0,1}^{2^{p(n)}}$, $Q_n$ accepts $(x,{y})$ with probability at most $\beta$.
    \end{itemize}
    There exists a $\poly(n)$-time mapping from $(Q_n,x)$ to a sparse Hamiltonian $H$ on $O(q(n)+\log(m(n)))$ qubits, partition $(L,R)$ of the qubits $H$ acts on, and threshold parameters $\alpha'(n)$ and $\beta'(n)$ satisfying $\alpha(n)'-\beta(n)'\geq ((m(n)+1)2^{r(n)})^{-1}$ such that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item If $(Q_n,x)$ is a YES case, there exists $\LR$ such that
        $
            \RL H \LR \leq \alpha'.
        $
        \item If $(Q_n,x)$ is a NO case, then for all $\LR$,
        $
            \RL H \LR \geq \beta'.
        $
    \end{itemize}
    The norm of $H$ scales as $\snorm{H}\in\poly(m(n),2^{r(n)})$.

label: FBPPdef
paper_title: A Qubit, a Coin, and an Advice String Walk Into a Relational Problem
statement_tex:
\label{FBPPdef}
$\mathsf{FBPP}$ is the class of polynomially-bounded relations $R\subseteq \bin^* \times \bin^*$ for which there exists a polynomial-time randomized algorithm $A$ such that for all $x$ for which there exists a $y$ with $(x,y)\in R$ and all $\varepsilon > 0$,
$$ \Pr[(x,A(x,0^{1/\varepsilon}))\in R]\ge 1-\varepsilon,$$
where the probability is over $A$'s outputs. \ $\mathsf{FBQP}$ is exactly the same except that $A$ can now be a quantum algorithm.
statement_text: FBPP is the class of polynomially-bounded relations R ⊆ {0,1}^* × {0,1}^* for which there exists a polynomial-time randomized algorithm A such that for all x for which there exists a y with (x,y) ∈ R and all ε > 0 , Pr [(x,A(x,0^ 1/ε )) ∈ R] ≥ 1-ε, where the probability is over A 's outputs. \ FBQP is exactly the same except that A can now be a quantum algorithm.

label: theorem:main-result-agnostic-quantum-fourier-sampling-learning
paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
statement_text: Let D =( U _n, φ) be an unknown probability distribution over {0,1}^n × {0,1} , with (known) uniform marginal over {0,1}^n and with (unknown) conditional label expectation φ:{0,1}^n → [0,1] . bf Distributional agnostic quantum Fourier sampling: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that, given a single copy of ρ_ D , with success probability nicefrac 1 2 outputs a sample from a probability distribution over {0,1}^n that is inverse-exponentially close to the squares of the Fourier coefficients of φ = 1-2φ . bf Distributional agnostic proper quantum parity learning: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that properly 1 -agnostically learns parities from an efficient number of copies of ρ_ D . bf Distributional 2-agnostic improper quantum Fourier-sparse learning: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that improperly 2 -agnostically learns Fourier-sparse functions from an efficient number of copies of ρ_ D .
title: Distributional agnostic approximate quantum Fourier sampling and learning -- Informal

label: theorem:main-result-verification
paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
statement_text: There is a class D of probability distributions over {0,1}^n × {0,1} with (known) uniform marginal over {0,1}^n such that: Distributional 1 -agnostic parity learning is classically hard from SQs or random examples, even if the unknown distribution is promised to lie in D . When promised that the unknown distribution lies in D , there is an efficient interactive verification procedure that allows a classical verifier, with SQ or random example access, to verify a distributional 1 -agnostic quantum parity learner, who has mixture-of-superpositions example or QSQ access. When promised that the unknown distribution lies in D , there is an efficient interactive verification procedure that allows a classical verifier, with SQ or random example access, to verify a distributional 2 -agnostic quantum Fourier-sparse learner, who has mixture-of-superpositions example or QSQ access.
title: Verifying distributional agnostic quantum learning -- Informal

statement_text: We say that a learning algorithm A is an α -agnostic learner for the benchmark class B , via the model class M , with respect to the distribution class D over X _n × {0,1} , from oracle O if: For all D ∈ D , when given access to oracle O ( D ) , as well as some (ε,δ) ∈ (0,1) , algorithm A outputs, with probability at least 1-δ , some model m ∈ M such that err _ D (m) ≤ α · opt _ D ( B ) +ε.

label: definition:noisy-functional-quantum-examples
paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
statement_text: Let D = ( D _ X _n , f) be a probability distribution over X _n × {0,1} with deterministic labeling function f: X _n → {0,1} . Let 0 ≤ η < nicefrac 1 2 be a noise parameter. A mixed η -noisy functional quantum example for D = ( D _ X _n , f) is a copy of the mixed (n+1) -qubit state ρ_ ( D _ X _n , f),η coloneqq (1-η)ket ψ_ ( D _ X _n ,f) bra ψ_ ( D _ X _n ,f) + ηket ψ_ ( D _ X _n ,f ⊕ 1) bra ψ_ ( D _ X _n ,f ⊕ 1) , where ⊕ denotes additional modulo 2 . A pure η -noisy functional quantum example for D = ( D _ X _n , f) is a pure superposition quantum example ket ψ_ D _η according to Cref definition:superposition-quantum-examples , where D _η is the probability distribution over X _n × {0,1} defined as D _η (x,f(x)) = (1-η) D _ X _n (x) , D _η (x,f(x) ⊕ 1) = η D _ X _n (x),quad ∀ x ∈ X _n . That is, such a quantum example is a copy of the pure (n+1) -qubit state ket ψ_ D _η coloneqq frac 1 sqrt 2^n Σ _ x ∈ {0,1}^n ( sqrt 1-η ket x,f(x) + sqrt η ket x,f(x) ⊕ 1 ) , where ⊕ denotes additional modulo 2 . A mixture-of-superpositions η -noisy functional quantum example for D = ( D _ X _n , f) is a copy of the mixed (n+1) -qubit state ρ_ D _η coloneqq E _ {e_x}_ x ∈ X _n [ ket ψ_ ( D _ X _n ,f ⊕ e) bra ψ_ ( D _ X _n ,f ⊕ e) ] , where the e_x , x ∈ X _n , are i.i.d. random variables with P [e_x = 0 ]=1-η=1- P [e_x = 1 ] for all x ∈ X _n .
title: Noisy functional quantum examples

label: definition:superposition-quantum-examples
paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
statement_text: Let D be a probability distribution over X _n × {0,1} . Then, a pure superposition example for D is a copy of the pure (n+1) -qubit state ket ψ_ D = ket ψ_ ( D _ X _n , φ) coloneqq Σ _ x ∈ {0,1}^n Σ _ y ∈ {0,1} sqrt D (x,y) ket x,y = Σ _ x ∈ {0,1}^n sqrt D rvert _ X _n (x) ( sqrt 1-φ(x) ket x,0 + sqrt φ(x) ket x,1 ) . Accordingly, a pure superposition quantum example oracle for D is an oracle that when queried outputs a copy of ket ψ_ D .
title: Pure superposition quantum examples

label: definition:interactive-verification-of-learning
paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
statement_text: Let F ⊆ {0,1}^ X _n be a benchmark class. Let D be a family of probability distributions over X _n × {0,1} . Let α ≥ 1 . We say that F is α -agnostic verifiable with respect to D using classical or quantum oracles O _V and O _P if there exists a pair of classical or quantum algorithms (V,P) that satisfy the following conditions for every input accuracy parameter ε ∈ (0,1) and for every confidence parameter δ ∈ (0,1) : bf Completeness: For any D ∈ D , the random hypothesis h: X _n → {0,1} that V(ε,δ) outputs after interacting with the honest prover P , assuming V(ε,δ) has access to O _V ( D ) and P(ε,δ) has access to O _P ( D ) , satisfies P [h ≠ reject wedge ( err _ D (h) ≤ α · opt _ D ( F ) + ε ) ] ≥ 1-δ . bf Soundness: For any D ∈ D and for any (possibly unbounded) dishonest prover P' , the random hypothesis h: X _n → {0,1} that V(ε,δ) outputs after interacting with P' , assuming V(ε,δ) has access to O _V ( D ) and P'(ε,δ) has access to O _P ( D ) , satisfies P [h ≠ reject wedge ( err _ D (h)> α · opt _ D ( F ) + ε ) ] ≤ δ . Moreover: If the above can be achieved with a pair (V,P) such that V(ε,δ) makes at most O ( poly (n, nicefrac 1 ε , nicefrac 1 δ )) queries to O _V ( D ) , such that P(ε,δ) makes at most O ( poly (n, nicefrac 1 ε , nicefrac 1 δ )) queries to O _P ( D ) , and such that both V(ε,δ) and P(ε,δ) have running time O ( poly (n, nicefrac 1 ε , nicefrac 1 δ )) , then we say that F is efficiently α -agnostic verifiable with respect to D using oracles O _V and O _P . If additionally one can ensure that the random hypothesis h: X _n → {0,1} that V(ε,δ) outputs after interacting with any (possibly unbounded) dishonest prover P' , assuming V(ε,δ) has access to O _V ( D ) and P'(ε,δ) has access to O _P ( D ) , satisfies h ∈ { reject } ∪ F almost surely, then we say that F is proper α -agnostic verifiable with respect to D using oracles O _V and O _P .
title: Interactive verification of α -agnostic learning -- Classical and/or quantum

label: definition:mixture-of-superpositions-quantum-example
paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
statement_text: Let D be a probability distribution over X _n × {0,1} . Let F_ D be the probability distribution over {0,1}^ X _n defined by sampling f(x) from the conditional label distribution independently for each x ∈ X _n . That is, for any Tilde f : X _n → {0,1} , P _ f F_ D [f=Tilde f ] = Π _ z ∈ X _n P _ (x,y) D [ tilde f (z)=y | x=z ] = Π _ z ∈ X _n ( (1-φ(z))(1-tilde f (z)) + φ(z) tilde f (z) ) . Then, a mixture-of-superpositions quantum example for D is a copy of the mixed (n+1) -qubit state ρ_ D = E _ f F_ D [ ket ψ_ ( D _ X _n , f) bra ψ_ ( D _ X _n , f) ] . Accordingly, a mixture-of-superpositions quantum example oracle for D is an oracle that when queried outputs a copy of ρ_ D .
title: Mixture-of-superpositions quantum examples for distributional agnostic learning

label: lemma:functional-quantum-Fourier-sampling
paper_title: Classical Verification of Quantum Learning
statement_text: Let D be a probability distribution over X _n × {0,1} with D =( U _n, f) for some deterministic labeling function f:{0,1}^n → {0,1} . Consider the following quantum algorithm: Given a single copy of ket ψ_ ( U _n, f) , first apply the unitary H^ ⊗ (n+1) , then measure all n+1 qubits in the computational basis. The measurement outcomes of this procedure satisfy the following: The computational basis measurement on the last qubit gives outcome 0 with probability nicefrac 1 2 and outcome 1 with probability nicefrac 1 2 . Conditioned on having observed outcome 1 for the last qubit, the computational basis measurement on the first n qubits outputs a string s ∈ {0,1}^n with probability (hat g (s))^2 , with g=(-1)^f .

\label{theorem:functional-agnostic-quantum-parity-verification-qsq-no-small-non-zero-Fourier-coeff}

    The class of $n$-bit parities is efficiently proper $1$-agnostic verifiable w.r.t.~$\mathfrak{D}_{ \mathcal{U}_n; \geq \vartheta}^{\mathrm{func}}$ by a classical verifier $V$ with classical SQ access interacting with a quantum prover $P$ with QSQ access.

    Moreover, this can be achieved by a pair $(V,P)$ that uses only a single round of communication consisting of at most $\mathcal{O}\left(\tfrac{n}{\vartheta^2}\right)$ classical bits.

\label{proposition:interactive-verification-fourier-approximation}
    Let $\vartheta\in (2^{-(\tfrac{n}{2} - 3)},1)$.
    Let $0\leq a \leq b\leq 1$.
    Let $\delta\in (0,1)$ and $\varepsilon\geq 2\sqrt{b^2-a^2}$.
    There is a classical-quantum verifier-prover pair $(V,P)$ that achieves the following for any $\mathcal{D}=(\mathcal{U}_n, \varphi)\in \mathfrak{D}_{ \mathcal{U}_n; \geq \vartheta} \cap \mathfrak{D}_{ \mathcal{U}_n; [a^2,b^2]}$:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $P$ uses $\mathcal{O}\left(\tfrac{\log(\nicefrac{1}{\delta\vartheta^2})}{\vartheta^4}\right)$ copies of $\rho_{\mathcal{D}}$ , $\mathcal{O}\left(n\tfrac{\log(\nicefrac{1}{\delta\vartheta^2})}{\vartheta^4}\right)$ single-qubit gates, a classical memory of size $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(n\tfrac{\log(\nicefrac{1}{\delta\vartheta^2})}{\vartheta^4}\right)$, and classical running time $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(n\tfrac{\log(\nicefrac{1}{\delta \vartheta^2})}{\vartheta^4}\right)$.
        \item $V$ uses $\mathcal{O}\left(b^4\tfrac{\log(\nicefrac{1}{\delta\vartheta^2})}{\varepsilon^4 \vartheta^4}\right)$ classical random examples, $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(n\tfrac{b^4\log(\nicefrac{1}{\delta\vartheta^2})}{\varepsilon^4 \vartheta^4}\right)$ classical running time, and a classical memory of size $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(n\tfrac{b^4 \log(\nicefrac{1}{\delta\vartheta^2})}{\varepsilon^4 \vartheta^4}\right)$.
        \item $(V,P)$ uses only a single round of communication consisting of at most $\mathcal{O}\left(\tfrac{n}{\vartheta^2}\right)$ classical bits.
        \item Completeness: If $V$ interacts with the honest prover $P$, then, with success probability $\geq 1-\delta$, $V$ accepts the interaction and outputs a succinctly represented $\tilde{\phi}$ such that $\norm{\tilde{\phi}-\hat{\phi}}_1\leq\varepsilon$ and $\norm{\tilde{\phi}}_0 \leq \mathcal{O}(\nicefrac{1}{\vartheta^2})$.
        \item Soundness: If $V$ interacts with any (possibly unbounded) prover $P'$, then, with failure probability at most $\delta$, $V$ accepts the interaction and outputs a $\tilde{\phi}$ such that $\norm{\tilde{\phi}-\hat{\phi}}_1 >\varepsilon$. 
    \end{itemize}
    In that sense, the Fourier spectrum of any distribution in $\mathfrak{D}_{ \mathcal{U}_n; \geq \vartheta} \cap \mathfrak{D}_{ \mathcal{U}_n; [a^2,b^2]}$ is efficiently verifiable through classical-quantum interactions.

    Let $\mathcal{D}=(\mathcal{U}_n, \varphi)$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}_n\times\{0,1\}$ with uniform input marginal.
    Let $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and let $k\in \{1,\ldots, 2^n\}$.
    Let $t_1,\ldots,t_k\in\{0,1\}^n$ be $k$ heaviest Fourier coefficients of $\phi$. That is, let $t_1\in \operatorname{argmax}_{t\in\{0,1\}^n} \lvert \hat{\phi}(t)\rvert$, and for $2\leq \ell\leq k$, let $t_\ell\in \operatorname{argmax}_{t\in\{0,1\}^n\setminus\{t_1,\ldots,t_{\ell -1}\}} \lvert \hat{\phi}(t)\rvert$. 
    Also, let $s_1,\ldots,s_k\in\{0,1\}^n$ be such that $\left\lvert  \lvert\hat{\phi}(t_\ell)\rvert - \lvert\hat{\phi}(s_\ell)\rvert\right\rvert \leq \nicefrac{\varepsilon}{2k} $ holds for every $1\leq \ell\leq k$ and let $\Tilde{\phi}(s_\ell)$ be $(\nicefrac{\varepsilon}{2k})$-accurate estimates of the respective Fourier coefficients, that is $\lvert \Tilde{\phi}(s_\ell) - \hat{\phi}(s_\ell)\rvert\leq \nicefrac{\varepsilon}{2k}$ holds for every $1\leq \ell\leq k$.
    Then, if we define 
    $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x) = \sum_{\ell=1}^k \tilde{\phi}(s_\ell)\chi_{s_\ell}$, and take the randomized hypothesis $h:\{0,1\}^n\to \{0,1\}$ as in \Cref{lemma:misclassification-probability-bound-L2-probabilistic-hypothesis}, 
    \begin{equation}

label: def:hardcomplete
paper_title: Homogeneous Algebraic Complexity Theory and Algebraic Formulas
statement_tex:
\label{def:hardcomplete}
Let $\mathscr C \subseteq \IS^\IN$ be a class of ungraded p-families.
We say that a graded p-family $f$ is \emph{$\mathscr C$-hard}
if for all $g \in \mathscr C$ we have $g \leq_{\textup{p-homlin}}f$.

We say that $f$ is $\mathscr C$-complete
if $f$ is $\mathscr C$-hard and
$\varphi(f) \subseteq \mathscr C$.
statement_text: Let mathscr C ⊆ S ^ N be a class of ungraded p-families. We say that a graded p-family f is mathscr C -hard if for all g ∈ mathscr C we have g ≤ _ up p-homlin f . We say that f is mathscr C -complete if f is mathscr C -hard and φ(f) ⊆ mathscr C .

statement_tex:
We write $p\leq_{\textup{afflin}}q$ if $p$ can be obtained from $q$ by replacing variables in $q$ by affine linear polynomials.
Let $f$ be a graded p-family that is $\mathscr C$-complete under homogeneous linear projections, and assume that
$\forall n,d: f_{n,d-1}\leq_{\textup{afflin}} f_{n,d}$ and $f_{n-1,d}\leq_{\textup{homlin}} f_{n,d}$.
Let $g := \varphi(f,\textup{diag}(1,\ldots,1),\textup{id}_\IN,\textup{id}_\IN)$
with the property that
there exists a bivariately polynomially bounded $q$ such that $\forall n,k$: if $h_1,\ldots,h_k \leq_{\textup{afflin}} g_n$, then $h_1+\ldots+h_k \leq_{\textup{afflin}} g_{q(k,n)}$.
Then $g$ is $\mathscr C$-complete under affine linear projections.

\label{pro:VFKumar}
Fix $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, $i\neq j$. Let $f$ be a polynomial admitting an IHL formula of depth~$\delta$. Then there exist $3 \times 3$ matrices $A_1 \vvirg A_r$ with $r \leq 4^\delta$ having \emph{homogeneous linear entries} such that
\[
f \cdot E_{i,j} \;=\; (\idthree+A_1)(\idthree+A_2)\cdots(\idthree+A_r) - \idthree\;.
\]

label: pro:usethetrace
paper_title: Homogeneous Algebraic Complexity Theory and Algebraic Formulas
statement_tex:
\label{pro:usethetrace}
For every IHL formula of depth $\delta$ there exist $\leq 4^\delta$ many
$3\times 3$ matrices $A_i$ with 
\emph{homogeneous linear entries} over $\IC[\eps,\eps^{-1}]$
and $\alpha \in \IC[\eps,\eps^{-1}]$
such that
\[
E_{1,1} \cdot f = \lim_{\eps\to0} \Big( \alpha \big((\idthree+A_1)(\idthree+A_2)\cdots(\idthree+A_r) - \idthree\big)\Big)
\]
and hence
\[
f = \lim_{\eps\to0} \textup{tr} \Big( \alpha \big((\idthree+A_1)(\idthree+A_2)\cdots(\idthree+A_r) - \idthree\big)\Big).
\]
statement_text: For every IHL formula of depth δ there exist ≤ 4^δ many 3 × 3 matrices A_i with homogeneous linear entries over C [ε,ε^ -1 ] and α ∈ C [ε,ε^ -1 ] such that \[ E_ 1,1 · f = lim _ ε → 0 ( α (( id _3+A_1)( id _3+A_2) ... ( id _3+A_r) - id _3 ) ) \] and hence \[ f = lim _ ε → 0 up tr ( α (( id _3+A_1)( id _3+A_2) ... ( id _3+A_r) - id _3 ) ). \]

label: thm:CM16
paper_title: Complexity Classification of Product State Problems for Local Hamiltonians
statement_tex:
\label{thm:CM16}
	For $\calS$ any fixed set of 2-qubit Hamiltonian terms:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item If every matrix in $\calS$ is 1-local, then \sLH{} is in $\PTIME$.
		\item Otherwise, if there exists a single-qubit unitary $U$ such that $U$
		locally diagonalizes all elements of $\calS$ (i.e.\ $U^{\otimes 2} H
		U^{\dagger \otimes 2}$ is diagonal for each 2-qubit $H \in \calS$), then
		\sLH{} is $\NP$-complete.  \item Otherwise, if there exists a single-qubit
		unitary $U$ such that for each 2-qubit $H \in\calS$, \[
		U^{\otimes 2}H U^{\dagger \otimes 2} = \alpha Z^{\otimes 2}+A \otimes I + I\otimes B
		\]
		for some $\alpha \in \reals$ and 1-local Hermitian matrices $A,B$, then
		\sLH{} is $\class{StoqMA}$-complete.
		\item Otherwise, \sLH{} is $\QMA$-complete.
	\end{itemize}
statement_text: For S any fixed set of 2-qubit Hamiltonian terms: If every matrix in S is 1-local, then S up sc -LH xspace is in P xspace . Otherwise, if there exists a single-qubit unitary U such that U locally diagonalizes all elements of S (i.e.\ U^ ⊗ 2 H U^ dagger ⊗ 2 is diagonal for each 2-qubit H ∈ S ), then S up sc -LH xspace is NP xspace -complete. Otherwise, if there exists a single-qubit unitary U such that for each 2-qubit H ∈ S , \[ U^ ⊗ 2 H U^ dagger ⊗ 2 = α Z^ ⊗ 2 +A ⊗ I + I ⊗ B \] for some α ∈ R and 1-local Hermitian matrices A,B , then S up sc -LH xspace is StoqMA xspace -complete. Otherwise, S up sc -LH xspace is QMA xspace -complete.

label: fact:relabelPaulis
paper_title: Complexity Classification of Product State Problems for Local Hamiltonians
statement_tex:
\label{fact:relabelPaulis}
  For any choice of permutation $\pi$ on $\{1,2,3\}$ and any choice of \emph{two} of $c_1,c_2,c_3=\pm 1$,
  there exists a single-qubit unitary $U$ and corresponding third coefficient such that
  simultaneous conjugation by $U$ maps
  the Pauli matrices $\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\}$ to $\{c_{\pi(1)}\sigma_{\pi(1)},c_{\pi(2)}\sigma_{\pi(2)},c_{\pi(3)}\sigma_{\pi(3)}\}$.
  So, writing every element of $\calS$ in the Pauli basis,
  relabeling all $\sigma_i$ with $c_{\pi(i)} \sigma_{\pi(i)}$ in the decompositions of each
  element of $\calS$ does not change the complexity of $\sLH$ or $\sprodLH$, where $\pi$ and two of the coefficients can be chosen arbitrarily.
statement_text: For any choice of permutation π on {1,2,3} and any choice of two of c_1,c_2,c_3=pm 1 , there exists a single-qubit unitary U and corresponding third coefficient such that simultaneous conjugation by U maps the Pauli matrices {σ_1,σ_2,σ_3} to {c_ π(1) σ_ π(1) ,c_ π(2) σ_ π(2) ,c_ π(3) σ_ π(3) } . So, writing every element of S in the Pauli basis, relabeling all σ_i with c_ π(i) σ_ π(i) in the decompositions of each element of S does not change the complexity of S up sc -LH xspace or S mhyphen up sc prodLH xspace , where π and two of the coefficients can be chosen arbitrarily.

For any single-qubit unitary U , U^ ⊗ 2 H (U^dagger )^ ⊗ 2 = Σ _ i,j=1 ^ 3 (R M R^T)_ ij σ_i σ_j + Σ _ k=1 ^ 3 parend * (Rv)_k σ_k I + (Rw)_k I σ_k for some R ∈ SO(3) . label: remark:symAntiSym
paper_title: Complexity Classification of Product State Problems for Local Hamiltonians
statement_tex:
\label{remark:symAntiSym}
	If a 2-qubit Hamiltonian term $H$ is symmetric, and so the associated correlation matrix $M$ is symmetric, there exists $R\in SO(3)$ which diagonalizes $M$.
	Combining \cref{fact:local_rot,fact:onelocalconjugating},
	for any 2-qubit symmetric term $H$,
	there exists a symmetric term of the form $H'=\sum_{i=1}^3 u_i \sigma_i \sigma_i + \sum_{j=1}^3 v_j (\sigma_j I + I \sigma_j)$ such that
	the complexities of
	$\sLH[\{H\}]$ and $\sprodLH[\{H\}]$ are respectively the same as
	$\sLH[\{H'\}]$ and $\sprodLH[\{H'\}]$.

	If $H$ is a 2-qubit antisymmetric term that is not 1-local, then $M$ is skewsymmetric and nonzero.
	Such an $M$ may be block diagonalized via some $R\in SO(3)$ such that $H$ is mapped to $a\!\left(\sigma_i\sigma_j - \sigma_j\sigma_i\right) + \sum_{k=1}^3 v_k \left(\sigma_k I - I\sigma_k\right)$ \cite{thompson1988normalForm,CM16_hamiltonians}.
        In particular, by \cref{fact:relabelPaulis}, $H$ can be mapped to $a\!\left(XZ-ZX\right) + \sum_{k=1}^3 v'_k \left(\sigma_k I - I\sigma_k\right)$.
	Therefore, the complexities of $\sLH[\{H\}]$ and $\sprodLH[\{H\}]$ are unaffected by assuming $H$ has this form.
statement_text: If a 2-qubit Hamiltonian term H is symmetric, and so the associated correlation matrix M is symmetric, there exists R ∈ SO(3) which diagonalizes M . Combining cref fact:local_rot,fact:onelocalconjugating , for any 2-qubit symmetric term H , there exists a symmetric term of the form H'= Σ _ i=1 ^3 u_i σ_i σ_i + Σ _ j=1 ^3 v_j (σ_j I + I σ_j) such that the complexities of {H} up sc -LH xspace and {H}mhyphen up sc prodLH xspace are respectively the same as {H'} up sc -LH xspace and {H'}mhyphen up sc prodLH xspace . If H is a 2-qubit antisymmetric term that is not 1-local, then M is skewsymmetric and nonzero. Such an M may be block diagonalized via some R ∈ SO(3) such that H is mapped to a (σ_iσ_j - σ_jσ_i ) + Σ _ k=1 ^3 v_k (σ_k I - Iσ_k ) . In particular, by cref fact:relabelPaulis , H can be mapped to a (XZ-ZX ) + Σ _ k=1 ^3 v'_k (σ_k I - Iσ_k ) . Therefore, the complexities of {H} up sc -LH xspace and {H}mhyphen up sc prodLH xspace are unaffected by assuming H has this form.

label: lem:stars

statement_tex:
\label{lem:stars}
	Consider a star graph $S_K$ with center vertex $v$ and $K$ neighbors.
	Consider any $0\leq \eps\leq 1$ and any
	$W=\diag(1,w_2,w_3)$ with $1 \geq w_2 \geq w_3 \geq 0$ and $w_3 < 1$.

	Let $\Pi$ denote the projector onto the axes for which $w_i=1$
	(so the projector onto the $x$-axis or the $xy$-plane).
	Similarly, let $\lambda$ be the largest $w_i$ which is not equal to 1
	(either $w_2$ or $w_3$).
	Let $\widehat{\sgn}(\hat{v}) = \Pi v / \norm{\Pi v}$.

	If vectors are assigned to $S_K$ which achieve at least
	$\Wlinearmaxcutop(S_K) \geq K(1-\eps)$,
	and $\hat{v}$ is the vector assigned to $v$,
	then
	\[
	\norm{W \hat{v} - \widehat{\sgn}(\hat{v})} \leq \delta
	\quad\text{for}\quad
	\delta = 2\sqrt{\eps} \sqrt{\frac{1 + \lambda^2}{1-\lambda^2}} .
	\]

label: defn:instancecomp
paper_title: Instance complexity of Boolean functions
statement_tex:
\label{defn:instancecomp}
    For a Boolean function $f : \zone^n \to \zone$, an input $x \in \zone$ and a decision tree $\T$ that computes $f$, define the \emph{instance complexity of $f$ at input $x$ w.r.t.~$\T$}, which we denote by $\IC(f, x, \T)$, to be
    \[
    \IC(f, x, \T) := \frac{\T(x)}{\C(f, x)}.
    \]
    Define the \emph{instance complexity of $f$ w.r.t.~$T$} to be
    \[
    \IC(f, \T) := \max_{x \in \zone^n}\IC(f, x, \T).
    \]
    Finally, define the \emph{instance complexity of $f$}, which we denote by $\IC(f)$, to be
    \[
    \IC(f) = \min_{\T : \T~\mathrm{computes}~f}\IC(f, \T).
    \]
statement_text: For a Boolean function f : {0,1}^n → {0,1} , an input x ∈ {0,1} and a decision tree T that computes f , define the instance complexity of f at input x w.r.t. T , which we denote by InstC (f, x, T ) , to be \[ InstC (f, x, T ) := frac T (x) C (f, x) . \] Define the instance complexity of f w.r.t. T to be \[ InstC (f, T ) := max _ x ∈ {0,1}^n InstC (f, x, T ). \] Finally, define the instance complexity of f , which we denote by InstC (f) , to be \[ InstC (f) = min _ T : T computes f InstC (f, T ). \]

We extend this definition to randomized refuters as follows: A BPP xspace - refuter for f against A is a randomized polynomial time algorithm R that, given input 1^n , prints a string x ∈ {0,1}^n , such that for infinitely many n , A(x) ≠ f(x) with probability at least 2/3 .protect protect protect protect protect protect A ZPP - refuter for f against A is a randomized polynomial time algorithm R that, given input 1^n , prints x ∈ {0,1}^n ∪ {perp } , such that for infinitely many n , either x= perp or A(x) ≠ f(x) with probability 1 , and x ≠ perp with probability at least 2/3 . For cal D ∈ { P xspace , BPP xspace , ZPP } and a typical complexity class cal C , we say there is a cal D -constructive separation of f ∉ cal C , if for every algorithm A computable in cal C , there is a refuter for f against A that is computable in cal D .

label: lemma:red
paper_title: Constructive Separations and Their Consequences
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:red}
Let $M$ be a $T(n)$-time nondeterministic RAM. There exists a strongly explicit family of $3$-SAT formulas $\{C_n\}_{n \in \N}$ of $T \cdot \polylog(T)$ size, such that for every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, $M(x) = 1$ if and only if there exists $y$ such that $C_n(x,y) = 1$.

[\cite{Nisan91, Viola05}]\label{thm:Nisan}  Let $d,c$ be any positive integers. There is a pseudo-random generator $G =\{G_N\}, G_N\colon \{0,1\}^{\log(N)^{O(d)}} \rightarrow \{0,1\}^N$, such that for each $N$, the PRG $G$ $1/N$-fools depth-$d$ $\AC^0$ circuits of size $N^c$.

label: defn:constsizelistref
paper_title: Constructive Separations and Their Consequences
statement_tex:
\label{defn:constsizelistref}
		For a  function $f \colon \{0,1\}^{\star} \rightarrow \{0,1\}$ and an algorithm $A$, a \emph{constant-size} $\PTIME$-\emph{list-refuter} for $f$ against $A$ is a deterministic polynomial time algorithm $R$ that, given input $1^n$, prints a list of $c$ strings $x_n^{(1)},x_n^{(2)},\dots,x_n^{(c)}\in \{0,1\}^*$ (for a constant~$c$ independent of $n$),  such that for infinitely many $n$,  there exists $i\in [c]$ for which $A(x_n^{(i)})\neq f(x_n^{(i)})$.
	Moreover, for every $i\in [c]$, there is a strictly increasing polynomial $\ell^{(i)}\colon \N \to \N$ such that $|x_n^{(i)}|=\ell^{(i)}(n) \ge n$ for all integers $n$.

  This definition can be generalized to constant-size $\BPP$-list-refuters and constant-size $\ZPP$-list-refuters similarly to \cref{defn:refuter}.
statement_text: For a function f colon {0,1}^ star → {0,1} and an algorithm A , a constant-size P xspace - list-refuter for f against A is a deterministic polynomial time algorithm R that, given input 1^n , prints a list of c strings x_n^ (1) ,x_n^ (2) , ... ,x_n^ (c) ∈ {0,1}^* (for a constant c independent of n ), such that for infinitely many n , there exists i ∈ [c] for which A(x_n^ (i) ) ≠ f(x_n^ (i) ) . Moreover, for every i ∈ [c] , there is a strictly increasing polynomial ell ^ (i) colon N → N such that |x_n^ (i) |=ell ^ (i) (n) ≥ n for all integers n . This definition can be generalized to constant-size BPP xspace -list-refuters and constant-size ZPP -list-refuters similarly to cref defn:refuter .
title: Constant-size list-refuters
